How to find an admin on your Dropbox team

Dropbox teams have one or more admins in their organization who manage the security, integration, and sharing settings for their team. If you’re a member of a Dropbox team and need to change these settings, contact an admin for assistance. 

If you have a personal account and aren’t part of a Dropbox team, you don‘t need to contact an admin. You can update and manage your own account settings or details.

How to find an admin on your team

To find an admin on your Dropbox team:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click View team and groups.
  4. Click the Members tab.  

You’ll see a list with the name and status of everyone on your team. The different types of admins are:

  • Team admins
  • User management admins
  • Support admins
  • Billing admins
  • Content admins
  • Compliance admins
  • Reporting admins
  • Security admins

We recommend contacting the team admin for most requests, as they have the highest level of access to admin settings. Learn more about the different types of admins and their permissions.

How to fix Dropbox Sign Outlook link errors

When receiving an error stating an invitation link or a reset password link is no longer valid after trying to click on the link within the invitation email could be caused by security settings within Outlook. 

Outlook has security features that can sometimes quarantine emails from our noreply domains (noreply@mail.hellofax.com and noreply@mail.hellosign.com).

To add Dropbox Sign and Dropbox Fax to your organization’s allow list, follow the steps with an administrator account (if not the administrator, please involve your administrator to follow the steps below):

  1. Log into the exchange admin center. 
  2. Under Protection, click Spam filter.
  3. On the general page, double-click the default policy in order to start editing it.
  4. Under Allow lists, click Sender allow lists. 
  5. Click Add.
  6. In the selection dialog box, add the recipients you wish to allow. 
  7. Click OK to return to the Allow lists page.
  8. Since the default spam filter policy is applied to every user in your organization, the goal is achieved after this.

Additionally, if you change the spam and bulk actions to move messages to the junk email folder in exchange admin center > protection > spam filter, the message won’t be moved to the quarantine.

Find out more about additional information on releasing messages from quarantine.

How to invite someone to your Dropbox team account

Adding someone to your Dropbox team account helps streamline collaboration and keep your organization’s content in one place. Certain types of admins can invite people to join the team. Team members can also send invites if an admin has enabled that option.

What do I keep?

  • All private files or folders.
  • Shared folders you own.
  • Shared folders owned by people not on the team.
  • Shared folders owned by the team that you were invited to before joining the team.
  • Paper docs.
  • Access to files in shared folders owned by team members you were invited to before joining the team or that don’t have team-only permissions.

What do I lose access to?

  • Team folders.
  • Files in shared folders owned by other team members you were invited to after joining the team or that have team-only permissions.
  • The team’s shared space quota.
  • Dropbox team-only features.

Let people with the same email domain to join your team

Admins can let people with the same verified email domain join the team automatically by using a team invite link. 

For example, if your organization’s verified domain is example.com, people with an @example.com address can join through the invite link without receiving an individual invitation.

To manage this setting:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Members.
  5. Turn Requests to join the team on.
  6. Turn Automatic approval for team join requests from@[Domain] on.

What happens when someone joins automatically?

If automatic approval is turned on and an eligible person joins through a team invite link:

  • They’re added to your Dropbox team automatically.
  • They don’t need an individual invitation.
  • They don’t need admin approval.
  • They use one available license.
  • Additional license charges may apply if no licenses are available.
  • Admins can manage or remove members at any time from the admin console.

How to invite people to your Dropbox team if you’re a team member

How to invite users to your team in Dropbox Sign

If you’re an admin on a Dropbox Sign Standard or Premium plan, you can invite new members to your team and assign them roles based on what you want them to be able to do. Learn more about team roles.

To invite users to your team:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. In the menu on the left, click Users. You can see each each user and their role. You can also see how many people are on your team.
  4. In the upper right hand corner, click the Invite button.
    • If you’re on a Premium plan, you can click Bulk invite to send out multiple invites.
  5. Add the email address of the user and select the role you would like them to have. If you’re on a Premium plan, you can also assign the user to a team.
    • Note: If you’re not sure about the permissions of each role, click Learn more under Role.
  6. Click Invite.

How to resend an invite

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Click Admin console.
  4. Click Users in the left sidebar.
  5. Click “⁝” (vertical ellipsis) next to the user you’d like to resend an invite to.
  6. Click Resend invite.

How to join a Dropbox Dash team account

If you’ve been invited to join a Dropbox Dash team, follow the steps below to connect your apps, review the Privacy Policy, and access the Dash start page.

How to join a Dropbox team

This article explains how to join a Dropbox team. If you’d like to link your team account to your personal Dropbox account instead, learn how to link two Dropbox accounts or switch between accounts.

How to accept a Dropbox team invitation

You may receive a prompt to join a Dropbox team because Dropbox has noticed you frequently collaborate with that team, or because a Dropbox admin has invited you to join their team.

Learn more about how admins invite someone to their Dropbox team account.

If you received an email invitation  from an admin to join their team

To accept an invitation you received in your email:

  1. Open the email invitation you received with the subject line, “You’re invited to join the [Dropbox team name] team on Dropbox”.
  2. Click the team invite link you were sent.
  3. Log in to dropbox.com with your Dropbox account, or create a new account.
    • Note: You may have to verify your email address to continue. 
  4. Click Join team.
  5. Follow the prompts to transfer your existing account to a Dropbox team account or to create a new Dropbox account.
If you received a prompt from Dropbox to request to join a team 

This prompt will appear when you receive a link to open a file or folder a Dropbox admin has sent you.

  1. Click the link you were sent to open the file or folder.
  2. Log in to dropbox.com with your Dropbox account, or create a new account.
    • Note: You may have to verify your email address to continue. 
  3. Click Send request to join the Dropbox team account.
  4. Click Got it in the pop-up window verifying your request was sent. 

Watch this video for more information about how to get started as a Dropbox team member. Learn more about why you are being prompted to join a Dropbox team account.

What happens to my subscription if I join a Dropbox team with an existing Dropbox account?

If you upgrade or transfer from Dropbox Plus or Professional to Dropbox Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise, your Plus or Professional subscription will immediately end. Any remaining credit on the Plus or Professional subscription will be refunded to the original payment method. Each individual Dropbox account owner can track this information on the account payments page.

If the automatic refund does not go through for any reason (such as an expired credit card), we’ll notify the account owner by email.

How to link or unlink two Dropbox accounts

If you’re on Dropbox Basic, Plus, Family, Professional, or Essentials, you can link your account with a Dropbox Standard, Advanced, Business, Business Plus, or Enterprise account, or vice versa. For example, you can link your Dropbox Business to an existing personal account.

If you’re an admin, learn how to manage your team members’ linked accounts and devices.

What does “linking accounts” mean?

When you link two Dropbox accounts, you can easily switch between them anywhere you use Dropbox without logging out of one and into the other every time you want to switch.

You can link your accounts on dropbox.com, the Dropbox desktop app, and the Dropbox iOS app. However, you can unlink only on dropbox.com. Once you link or unlink two accounts, they become linked or unlinked everywhere you use Dropbox.

Although linking your accounts links them everywhere you use Dropbox, it doesn’t log you into both accounts on all devices. It only logs you in where you initiated the link. Your other devices will display the option for you to log into your linked account. After you do, you will remain logged in and can easily switch between your linked accounts on that device.

Personal security when linking a team account

Linking accounts doesn’t share or transfer information between the two accounts.

If you link your accounts and your admin uses the “log in as a team member” feature to log into your team member account, they can’t open or access your linked personal account. They can, however, view the name and email address of your linked personal account.

How to unlink your accounts

You can unlink your accounts only on dropbox.com. Unlinking your accounts unlinks them everywhere. Across all apps and devices, you’ll be logged out of the last account you added to that app, and you’ll stay logged into the first account.

You can always log back into your accounts on any device, as you normally would with any unlinked account.

To unlink your accounts:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with either account.
  2. Click your avatar (photo or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the General tab.
  5. Click Unlink next to Linked accounts.
  6. Click Yes, unlink to confirm.

How to locate Dropbox Sign team admins

If you’re a developer or a member of a Dropbox Sign team, you can locate the email address associated with the admin of the corresponding Dropbox Sign team by completing the following:

  1. Log in to Dropbox Sign.
  2. In the top-right corner of your browser, click your initials.
  3. Click Admin console from the drop-down menu.
  4. Click Team on the left side of your browser.
  5. Locate the admin’s email address, found below Admin.

How to log in to Dropbox with SSO

If your admin has enabled single sign-on (SSO), you’ll be able to access Dropbox in the same way you access other applications for work—by entering your SSO password on your organization’s login page.

Each organization has its own requirements for employees, so check with your admin to see how to use SSO for work. Read on to learn more about using Dropbox with SSO.

How to log in to dropbox.com with SSO

Whenever you need to log in to dropbox.com, enter your email address and click Continue. You’ll be taken to your organization’s login page. Enter your SSO password there (not your Dropbox password).

How to add a computer to your account

If the Dropbox desktop app on your computer is currently logged into your Dropbox account, you don’t need to do anything—the computer has been added to the device list in your account settings and you can keep using the app without having to log in again.

However, if you need to remove your computer and add a new one, you’ll need the latest version of the app to use SSO.

To add a computer to your device list: 

  1. Open the Dropbox desktop app.
  2. Select I already have a Dropbox account and click Continue.
  3. Enter your email address and click Continue.
  4. Click the Get your link code button.
  5. If you haven’t logged in to your organization’s SSO page, you’ll be prompted to do so in your web browser. Enter your email address, SSO password (not your Dropbox password), and any other information your organization requires. If you’ve already logged in, you’ll skip this step.
  6. A page will open in your browser and display a code. Click the Copy link code button, or select and copy the code manually.
  7. Go back to the Dropbox desktop app and click Paste, or manually paste the code into the field and click Continue.
  8. Follow the rest of the setup process to finish adding the computer to your Dropbox account.

How to add a mobile device to your account

If the Dropbox mobile app on your phone or tablet is currently logged into your Dropbox account, you don’t need to do anything—the device has been added to the device list in your account settings and you can keep using the app without having to log in again.

However, if you need to remove your device and add a new one, you’ll need the latest version of the app to use SSO.

To add a phone or tablet to your device list: 

  1. Open the Dropbox mobile app.
  2. Tap I’m Already a Dropbox User.
  3. Enter your email address and tap Sign In to Dropbox.
  4. If you haven’t logged in to your organization’s SSO page on your device, a browser window will open up and prompt you to do so. Enter your email address, SSO password (not your Dropbox password), and any other information your organization requires. If you’ve already logged in on your device, you’ll skip this step.
  5. A page will open in your browser that requests your approval for the app to use SSO. Tap Allow.
  6. In the Dropbox mobile app, follow the rest of the setup process to finish adding the device to your Dropbox account.

Can I still use my Dropbox password?

If your admin has made SSO optional, you’ll be able to use either login method. You can log in to your organization’s page with your SSO password for work, or click Log in with Dropbox credentials to log in with your Dropbox password.

How to log into Dropbox Fax

You have 3 options for logging in: 

  1. Enter your email address and you will be prompted to enter your password once you click Continue.
  2. Log in with Google.
    • This option allows you to log in with your Google account. Please keep in mind that if you choose this log in option, you will be locked into it. You’ll only be able to log in using your Google account, unless you click on “Forgot password?” and set a password to use to log in.
  3. Log in with Dropbox.
    • This option allows you to log in with your Dropbox account. Please keep in mind that if you choose this log in option, you will be locked into it. You’ll only be able to log in using your Dropbox account, unless you click on “Forgot password?” and set a password to use to log in.

How to manage team members and role permissions in Dropbox Forms

How to add new team members

To add team members:   

  1. Log in to Dropbox Forms. 
  2. Click More in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Team. The list of current team members will populate. 
  4. Click Invite in the upper right side of the screen.
  5. Enter the email address of the person you’d like to invite. 
  6. Select their access level from the Team Role section.
  7. Click Save.

How to edit a team member’s role

To edit: 

  1. Log in to Dropbox Forms.
  2. Click More in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Team. The list of current team members will populate. 
  4. Find the name of the team member whose role you’d like to change.
  5. Click the edit icon (pencil) under Actions.
  6. Select their new access level in the Team Role section.
  7. Click Save.  

How to remove team members

  1. Log in to Dropbox Forms.
  2. Click More in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Team. The list of current team members will populate. 
  4. Find the name of the team member you’d like to remove.
  5. Click X under Actions to remove the person from your team.
  6. Click Ok to confirm.

How to merge two Dropbox team accounts

This article discusses merging two Dropbox team accounts. It’s also possible to merge multiple individual Dropbox accounts.  

When you merge two Dropbox team accounts, all members and content from the secondary Dropbox team are imported into the primary Dropbox team. Any primary team settings will override the secondary team settings. 

Will any data be lost when merging accounts?

All data from the secondary team will be transferred to the primary team except:

  • Deleted team member accounts
    • Note: Suspended team member accounts will be transferred
  • Activity logs
  • Admin permissions
  • Team API apps
  • Invoices and receipts

What to do before merging teams

Before a team merge, you should make sure that:

  • The primary team has enough open licenses for the number of users on the secondary team.
  • The primary team has enough free space to accommodate the secondary team’s data.
  • Both teams have already enabled Dropbox Paper in their team settings so both teams can continue using Dropbox Paper after the merge.
  • Both teams are using the same version of Dropbox Paper. Learn how to check your version of Dropbox Paper. If not, see the FAQ below.

If the secondary team has team selective sync enabled, the primary team will also need to enable team selective sync for the merge to complete.

How to initiate a team merge

You must be the admin of a Dropbox team account to initiate a team merge. To initiate a team merge:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Under Account, click Trusted teams.
  5. Click the Add a trusted team button.
  6. You can choose to:
    • Merge into a primary team, which will import all of your members and content into another existing team.
    • Request a secondary team merge into my team, which will import the members and content of another team into your existing team.
  7. If you choose to merge into a primary team, click the checkbox to agree to the terms and click Send request.
  8. If you choose to request a secondary team merge, click Copy link.
  9. Paste the link in an email and send it to the email address of the secondary team’s admin.

Once the merge is complete, which usually happens within 72 hours:

  • Both admins will receive an email that the merge has been successful.
  • Members from the secondary team will receive an email confirming that they’re on a new team.

The secondary team will automatically receive a prorated refund for the remainder of their subscription. The admin of the secondary team will receive an email confirming their refund has been applied.

How to move members to another Dropbox team account

If you’re an admin of a Dropbox team account, you can move team members to another Dropbox team account you manage. 

You can also add an admin from another team to manage your team.

What to know before you move a team member

When you move a team member, they’ll lose access to the original team’s shared folders. They’ll keep access to files and folders in their team member folder, files and folders directly shared with them, and their own Paper docs.

If the member you’d like to move is the owner of a shared folder, that shared folder will move with them to their new team. If you’d like that folder to stay with the original team, change the owner to a member who isn’t moving.

If you’d like the member you move to keep access to shared folders from their original team, set the folder membership of each folder to Anyone. 

If the member you’d like to move has created shared links, those links may stop working once they’re moved to their new team.

Will I come across any issues when moving members?

There are a few reasons why you may encounter an issue when moving members.

License limit

When the team you’d like to move members to exceeds the license limit or doesn’t have enough free licenses you’ll encounter an error. If you’d like to move more members to that team, you‘ll have to add more licenses.

Incompatible version of Dropbox

If the team you’d like to move members to is on an incompatible version of Dropbox team, you’ll need to contact Dropbox support.

Another move is in progress

If you or another admin has initiated a move, you’ll need to wait until that move is complete before starting another one. To check the status of a move, log in to dropbox.com and click View tasks in the upper-right corner.

Legal hold

You can’t move members under a legal hold.

How to remove team members in Dropbox Sign

Admins and team managers on Standard and Premium plans can remove team members.

All templates owned by the removed team member will be transferred to the administrator of the account and the removed user will no longer have access to them. 

Unless you transfer them to another user, all documents and templates owned by the removed team member will remain with the user. Once you remove a user from the team, they’ll be downgraded to their own free account. The account won’t be associated with your team’s account and the user won’t have access to templates, however, you’ll no longer have access to the user’s documents.

How to remove a team member in Dropbox Sign

Only Dropbox Sign team admins can remove team members.

To remove a team member:

  1. Log in to your admin account.
  2. Click your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. When a list pops up, select Admin console.
  4. Click Users in the left sidebar.
  5. Click “⁝” (vertical ellipsis) to the right of the user’s name and click Remove. 
    • Note: If you don’t see the team member you’d like to remove, use the search bar in the upper-right corner.
  6. Choose whether to allow the user to keep their documents and created templates, or transfer them to another user. If you don’t transfer the documents or created templates to another team member, you’ll lose access to them.

How to remove a team member in Dropbox Fax

Only team admins with a Dropbox Fax subscription can remove a team member.

To remove a team member:

  1. Log in to your admin account.
  2. Click Team in the left sidebar.
  3. Hover over the downward arrow next to the correct team member.
  4. Click Remove.
  5. Click OK to confirm the removal of the user. 
  6. Choose whether to allow the user to keep their documents, or transfer them to another user. If you don’t transfer the documents to another team member, you’ll lose access to them.

How to restore deleted users on Dropbox team accounts

If a Dropbox team admin accidentally deleted a team member, they have seven days to restore the user. Restoring a member reactivates the account with the same files and permissions, so the account is exactly as it was before deletion. Team admins and user management admins can restore deleted users.

How to restore a team member

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Members.
  4. Click Removed filter and select Deleted.
  5. Click More  beside the name of the member you want to restore. If you don’t see their name, it means they cannot be restored.
  6. Click Restore.
  7. Click Restore in the pop-up window.

Why am I not seeing the option to restore a team member?

There are a few reasons why an admin may not see the option to restore a team member. These include:

  • The member was deleted more than seven days ago. After seven days, an admin can use account transfer to transfer files to a new team member account.
  • An admin already used account transfer on the deleted member’s account.
  • An admin chose to permanently delete the member.
  • The member was restored by Dropbox Support.
  • The member was invited, but never actually joined your team.
  • The member was deleted by an app that uses the v.1 of the Dropbox API.

What is restored when a team member is restored?

When you restore a deleted team member, their account should be restored to its previous state, including shared folders, files, Paper docs, groups, and all user settings. However, deleted member restoration should only be used as a backup measure. 

If you’re unsure whether to delete a member or not, consider suspending them first.

What is not restored when a team member is restored?

Restored team members won’t be added back to exception lists for some features. For example, if a member was in an exception list for enterprise mobility management (EMM), you’ll need to re-add them to the exception list after restoring their account.

How to restore multiple team members with the Dropbox API

To restore a large number of team members at once, use the Dropbox API. There are two ways to do this:

  • Use your own script to restore members with the Dropbox API
  • Use the Dropbox restoration tool

How to set device approvals for Dropbox team members

Certain types of admins can use device approvals to manage what devices team members use to access their Dropbox team accounts. Learn more about device limits for users on different Dropbox plans.  

How to set up device approvals for your team

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Select the Security tab.
  5. Scroll to the Devices section.
  6. Under Devices, click Device approvals.
  7. In the Computers and Mobile devices sections, use the dropdown menus to choose how many computers and devices each team member can connect to Dropbox.
  8. In the Disconnected devices section, choose what happens when a member disconnects a computer or device from Dropbox:
    • Remove: The device no longer counts toward the limit.
    • Keep: The device counts toward the limit until an admin removes it.
  9. In the Device limit reached section, choose what happens when members are already over the limits (such as when they join the team or when an admin lowers the limit):
    • Remove oldest: Oldest devices (by last activity) are removed and disconnected to meet the limit.
    • Remove all: All devices are disconnected.
    • Make exception: The member is allowed to connect as many devices as they like.
  10. In the Exceptions section, click Add exceptions to choose which members (if any) can connect as many devices as they like. Start typing their name or email address, click the auto-populated name to add it, then click Done.
  11. In the Fixed web session secton, choose how long members can stay logged into their account before they’re automatically logged out. Options range from 1 day to 1 year.
  12. In the Idle web sessions section, choose how long members can stay logged in without activity on dropbox.com before they’re automatically logged out. Options range from None to 48 hours.
  13. Click Save in the bottom-right corner.

How to limit team members to one Dropbox account per computer

If you don’t want your team members to access both a personal and a work Dropbox account on their computers via the desktop app, you can allow only a single account on each computer.

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Select the Security tab.
  5. Under Devices, click Linked accounts.
  6. Toggle Linked accounts to Off.
  7. Click Save in the bottom-right corner.

How to sign up for a Dropbox Sign account

You can sign up for a free Dropbox Sign account at sign.dropbox.com. With a free plan, you can sign or request signatures on 3 documents per month.

  1. Go to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Click Sign up.
  3. Enter your email address or click to sign up with your Google or Dropbox account.
  4. You’ll receive an email to verify and activate your Dropbox Sign account.
  5. Follow the steps in the email to verify your account. Once complete, you can create a password.

Visit our pricing page for information on plans with more documents and features.

How to switch between linked Dropbox accounts

You can switch between two linked Dropbox accounts on dropbox.com, the Dropbox desktop app, and the Dropbox mobile app. Learn how to link or unlink Dropbox accounts.

You must be logged into both linked Dropbox accounts on the web session or the app you’re using to switch between your accounts.

If your accounts aren’t linked, you can still switch to a different Dropbox account on any device by logging out of one account and logging into the other.

If you’d like to change your Dropbox account email address instead, visit this article.

How to switch the email addresses between personal and work accounts

This article explains how to change the email addresses associated with your personal and work Dropbox accounts. If instead you would like to switch between accounts, learn how to link and unlink your Dropbox accounts. Or, learn what you can do if you no longer have access to the email address associated with your Dropbox account.

To switch the email addresses linked to your personal and work Dropbox accounts, you’ll need to use a third email address as a placeholder.

In both sets of instructions, we’ll call the email address linked to your personal account “Email A.” The email linked to your work account will be called “Email B.” The third, placeholder email address you’ll need to use to swap Email A and Email B will be called “Email C.”

How to switch email addresses as a Dropbox team admin

  1. Log in to dropbox.com and change the email linked to your personal account from Email A to the placeholder Email C.
  2. Click your name or avatar at the top of any page.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the Account tab.
  5. Next to Email A, choose Change email.
  6. Enter Email C, confirm the email, and enter your password.
  7. Click Update email.
    • Once you’ve changed the email, Email A will be released.
  8. Following the same steps above, next log into your work account (Email B) and change the email linked to your work account from Email B to Email A.
  9. Log out of your work account and back into your personal account (Email C). From there, you can change the email linked to your personal account from Email C to Email B.

How to switch email addresses as a Dropbox team member

  1. Log in to dropbox.com and with your personal account (Email A).
  2. Click your name or avatar at the top of any page.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the Account tab.
  5. Next to Email A, choose Change email.
  6. Enter Email C, confirm the email, and enter your password.
  7. Click Update email.
    • Once you’ve changed the email, Email A will be released.
  8. Contact your admin to change your work email address from Email B to Email A.
    •   Note: Dropbox team members can’t change email addresses on team accounts.

 

Your admin will need to follow these steps:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Members.
  4. Click the team member’s name.
  5. Click change beside the current email address and enter the new one (Email C).

Once these changes have been made, you can change your personal email address from Email C to Email B by following the instructions above.

How to transfer a deleted team member’s files

Certain types of Dropbox admins can transfer a deleted team member’s files and folders to someone else on their team. This feature allows for a seamless transition of ownership and ensures that important files and folders aren’t lost or inaccessible after a member leaves the team.

You can only transfer a team member’s files and folders to another member after the first member is deleted. Learn how to delete a member from a Dropbox team account.

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox helps you effortlessly share files and folders.

What’s transferred during an account transfer?

  • All existing folders and files.
  • All deleted files.
  • Ownership of shared folders that the former team member owned.
  • Membership to shared folders owned by other members of your Dropbox team.
  • Shared folders owned by someone outside your team that contain fewer than 250,000 items.
    • Note: The recipient receives copies of these folders, not membership.
  • Ownership of Paper docs created by the former team member.
  • A copy of the “Apps” folder containing third-party application data.
  • Existing Signature documents (including Pending Signature, Pending your signature, Declined, and Signed). 
  • Existing Signature templates.
  • Shared links created by the former team member.
  • Previous versions of files.

What isn’t transferred during an account transfer?

  • Groups can’t be transferred via account transfer. Instead, an admin or group member will need to manually add new team members to groups.
  • Dropbox Backup content.
  • Shared folders owned by someone outside your team that contain more than 250,000 items.
  • Access to Paper docs the deleted member didn’t own.
  • Datastores (a type of data that some third-party apps may use to store their data).

How to transfer files from a previously deleted member

You can only transfer a team member’s files and folders to another member after the first member is deleted. Learn how to delete a member from your team.

To transfer files from a deleted team member:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin Console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Members in the left sidebar.
  4. Under Removed, select Deleted from the dropdown.
  5. Click More  to the right of the former member’s name and select Manage files from the menu.
  6. Select the option to Transfer them to another team member.
  7. Enter the recipient’s name or email address and click Submit.
    • Note: The recipient must be a member of your Dropbox team account.

How to troubleshoot 2-factor authentication issues with Dropbox

2-factor authentication adds an extra layer of security to your account by requiring both your password and a code sent to your phone. This article addresses common 2-factor authentication issues with Dropbox and offers steps to resolve them:

  • Lost phone or changed number
  • “Invalid code” message
  • Didn’t receive a 2FA code
  • Received a 2FA code without requesting one
  • Not prompted to enter a 2FA code

What if I lost my phone or changed my phone number?

If you lost your phone or got a new phone number and no longer have access to your old phone number, there are several ways to receive a 2-factor authentication code.

1. Use your recovery email

If you added a recovery email to your account, you can use it to receive security codes or reset your password. Learn how to add a recovery email.

2. Use your Dropbox emergency backup code

You may have set an emergency backup code when you turned on 2-factor authentication. If you did, you were asked to save it for your records. If you still have your backup code, click Having trouble getting a code? in the window that appears when you try to log in, and click Enter the emergency backup code and type in your code.

3. Use your backup phone

You may have added a backup phone number when you turned on 2-factor authentication. If you did, or you think you might have, click Having trouble getting a code? in the window that appears when you try to log in, and click Text my backup phone. Then, find that phone or contact the person that has it, and follow the prompts from there.

4. Use the Dropbox desktop or mobile app

If you have the Dropbox desktop or mobile app, click Having trouble getting a code? in the window that appears when you try to log in, and click Send me a notification. You should receive a notification on any connected devices where you’re logged in to Dropbox. Tap Review, then Yes to log in.

5. Use the Dropbox desktop app in the taskbar/menu bar

If you use the Dropbox desktop app, your computer is a trusted device, so you won’t need to enter a 2-factor authentication code to log in. Click the Dropbox icon in your taskbar (Windows) or menu bar (Mac), and click the globe icon. This will open dropbox.com and you’ll automatically be logged in. From here you can turn off 2-factor authentication or change your 2-factor authentication number.

If you’ve followed these steps and are still seeing an error message about an invalid code, contact Dropbox support.

What if I didn’t receive a 2-factor authentication code from Dropbox?

If you didn’t receive a 2-factor authentication code, or got an error message that the code “couldn’t be sent,” the issue may vary depending on your authentication method:  

SMS authentication If you’re using SMS for 2-factor authentication, make sure that your phone number is correct and that your phone provider isn’t blocking these types of messages.

  • Learn how to check for blocked messages on Android.
  • Learn how to check for blocked messages on iPhone.

Authenticator app If you’re using an authenticator app and are unable to get a code, try the following:

  • Make sure your phone’s time and date are set correctly, as this can impact the code generated by your authenticator app.
  • Check if your authenticator app needs an update and install any available updates. 
  • Verify that you’re using the correct account or email in the authenticator app.

Additional authentication

If you’re asked for an additional authentication with a 6-digit code sent to your email, this is a security measure to verify your identity. It may occur if there are unusual login attempts or if you’re logging in from a new device. Check your email for the code and enter it to continue.

If an email hasn’t arrived in your inbox, check your spam or junk folder. Sometimes email providers may mistakenly flag automated emails. You can also add no-reply@dropbox.com to your email address book or contacts list to help ensure future messages are delivered.

If you’re unable to access the email address associated with your Dropbox account, contact your ESP provider to regain access.

If you still can’t find your 2-factor authentication code, wait 24 hours and then try to log in again.

What if I received a 2-factor authentication code while not trying to log in to Dropbox?

If you received a 2-factor authentication code when you’re not trying to log in, change your Dropbox password as soon as possible. If you’re unable to log in to your account, contact Dropbox support to make sure your account is secure.

What if I’m not prompted to enter a 2-factor authentication code?

If you set up 2-factor authentication with Dropbox but aren’t being prompted to enter a code, it probably means you’re using a trusted device.

To see the prompt again, you can clear the cache and cookies in the web browser on your computer or revoke trusted status from your devices. To revoke trusted status:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials).
    • Depending on your plan, your avatar may appear in the top-right or bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the Security tab.
  5. Scroll to the 2-factor authentication section.
  6. Click Revoke All next to Trusted Devices.

If you still need help troubleshooting 2-factor authentication issues, contact Dropbox support.

Set up a passkey to log in to your account without a password, or 2FA

If you’d prefer not to use 2-factor authentication in the future, you can choose to log in with a passkey. Once set up, logging in with a passkey bypasses any existing 2-factor authentication steps you’ve set up for your account.

Learn how to use passkeys.

How to turn 2-factor authentication on and off

2-factor authentication (also known as multi-factor authentication, MFA, two-step verification, or 2FA) is a recommended security feature that helps protect your Dropbox account. By turning 2-factor authentication on, you add an extra layer of protection that helps keep your personal information and files safe from unauthorized access.

To use 2-factor authentication, you need a mobile device that can run a compatible authenticator app, or can receive text messages.

Already use 2-factor authentication and locked out? Learn how to regain access to your account.

How to turn on 2-factor authentication

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials).
    • Depending on your plan, your avatar may appear in the top-right or bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the Security tab.
  5. Toggle 2-factor authentication to On.
    • If you see Managed by single sign-on under the Security tab, your team admin has enabled single sign-on (SSO). This means you don’t have to use 2-factor authentication with Dropbox and can access your account by logging in to a central identity provider. Contact your admin to learn more.
  6. Re-enter your password and click Submit.
  7. Choose if you want to receive your security code by text message or via an authenticator app, and follow the instructions for your choice below.

How to change my 2-factor authentication phone number

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials).
    • Depending on your plan, your avatar may appear in the top-right or bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the Security tab.
  5. Click Edit next to your phone number in the 2-factor authentication section.
    • You’ll be prompted to enter your password to continue.

How to add a backup method for 2-factor authentication

After turning on 2-factor authentication, we recommend you add a backup phone that can receive text messages as well. If you ever lose your primary phone, or can’t access your authenticator app, you can send a security code to your backup phone number instead.

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials).
    • Depending on your plan, your avatar may appear in the top-right or bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the Security tab.
  5. Under 2-factor authentication, click Add next to Backup method.
  6. Enter your password.
  7. Enter the phone number of your backup device.

How to use an emergency backup code for 2-factor authentication

When you turn on 2-factor authentication, you’ll receive 10 backup codes. Each eight-digit code can be used once to access your Dropbox account in case of emergency. 

How to find your backup codes

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials).
    • Depending on your plan, your avatar may appear in the top-right or bottom-left corner. 
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the Security tab.
  5. Click Show next to Recovery codes.
  6. Enter your password.
  7. Use or save the code that appears.  

How to use a backup code

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click Having trouble getting a code?
  3. Click Enter emergency backup code.
  4. Enter one of your emergency backup codes.
  5. Click Enter.

How to use a security key for 2-factor authentication

You can use a security key for 2-factor authentication, rather than a six-digit security code. A security key is a small USB, Bluetooth, or Near Field Communication (NFC) device that follows one of the open standards:

  • FIDO Universal 2nd Factor (U2F)
  • Web Authentication (WebAuthn), also known as FIDO2

Unlike SMS or mobile app verification, a security key doesn’t require a separate battery or network connection. Most importantly, security keys use authenticated communication to defend against phishing attacks.  

How to add a physical security key

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials).
    • Depending on your plan, your avatar may appear in the top-right or bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the Security tab.
  5. Under 2-factor authentication, click Add next to Security keys. If you don’t see this section, follow the How to turn on 2-factor authentication instructions above before proceeding.
  6. Enter your password.
  7. Insert your security key into a USB port, then click Begin setup.

How to remove a physical security key 

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials).
    • Depending on your plan, your avatar may appear in the top-right or bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the Security tab.
  5. Under 2-factor authentication, click Edit next to Security keys.
  6. Click ☑ (delete) next to the security key you’d like to remove.
  7. Enter your password.  

Where can I use my security key?

Once you have a security key, it can be enabled for both your personal and work Dropbox accounts. It can also be used with other WebAuthn or U2F enabled services, such as Google apps.

Currently, security keys are only supported on select devices and browsers, so you must first set up 2-factor authentication for your Dropbox account and select to receive codes via SMS messages or a mobile app. This step ensures that you have a backup method, in case a device doesn’t support your security key.

Dropbox only supports using a security key when logging in to dropbox.com on Chrome or Firefox web browsers. You can’t use a security key to log in to the Dropbox desktop or mobile apps. Don’t worry, you still have the option to use text or mobile app 2-factor authentication on devices and platforms that don’t support U2F or WebAuthn, or if you don’t have your security key available.

Learn how to use passkeys.

How to use a passkey for 2-factor authentication

You can use also use passkeys for 2-factor authentication. Passkeys provide an additional level of security against phishing and SIM swap attacks. When you log in to Dropbox, you’ll confirm your identity with biometrics, or by scanning a QR code with one of your other devices.

How to add a passkey when logging in

You might see a prompt to create a passkey right after you log in. Follow the on-screen instructions to finish setting up your passkey.

Once complete, you’ll be able to use your passkey instead of your password for faster, more secure log-ins.  

How to add a passkey to your Dropbox account
  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials).
    • Depending on your plan, your avatar may appear in the top-right or bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the Security tab.
  5. Under Passkeys, click Add passkey.
    • If you already have a passkey, click Manage passkeys, and then Add new passkey.
  6. Enter your Dropbox account password and click Next.
  7. Follow the instructions in your browser to create a passkey.
  8. Enter or edit a nickname for your passkey, if you wish.
  9. Click Save.  
How to remove a passkey from your Dropbox account
  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials).
    • Depending on your plan, your avatar may appear in the top-right or bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the Security tab.
  5. Under Passkeys, click Manage passkeys.
  6. Click ☑ (delete) next to the passkey you want to remove.
  7. Enter your Dropbox account password and click Next.
  8. Click Delete.
  9. To fully remove the passkey, delete it from your device’s credential manager as well. Steps may vary depending on your device or browser.

Learn how to use passkeys.

How to turn off 2-factor authentication

You can turn off 2-factor authentication for your Dropbox account at any time. To do so:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials).
    • Depending on your plan, your avatar may appear in the top-right or bottom-left corner. 
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the Security tab.
  5. Toggle 2-factor authentication to Off.  

How to reset a team member’s 2-factor authentication method

If you’re a Dropbox team admin, you can reset a team member’s 2-factor authentication method. You may need to do this if they change their phone number or mobile device.

To reset a team member’s 2-factor authentication method:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Members in the left sidebar.
  4. Click the ☑ (more options) next to the team member’s name.
  5. Select Reset two-factor authentication.
  6. Click Reset.

Your team member will receive an email notification that their 2-factor authentication method has been reset.

How to use a passkey to log in to your account

Passkeys provide a secure way for you to log in to your account without using a password. They provide an additional level of security against phishing and SIM swap attacks, as well as making the log in process quicker and more convenient.

How to set up a passkey

You may see a prompt to create a passkey right after you log in. Follow the on-screen instructions to finish setting up your passkey.

Once complete, you can use your passkey instead of your password for faster, more secure log-ins.

Enabling passkeys as an admin

Team members won’t be able to create new passkeys, or log in with existing passkeys until the admin enables the feature from the admin console.

To turn passkeys on for your team:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Select the Security tab.
  5. Under Authentication, toggle Passkey sign-in to On.

Once enabled, team members can start using passkeys the next time they log in.

Log in with a passkey

Passkeys and 2-factor authentication

Logging in with a passkey bypasses any existing 2-factor authentication steps you’ve set up for your account, including team accounts where the admin has set 2-factor authentication as a requirement.

When you use either biometrics or a physical key that requires a pin to access your account through passkeys, this automatically satisfies the requirement for a second factor. This means that passkeys can replace security codes by text message and authenticator app.

If you already use 2-factor authentication, you don’t have to use your passkey every time you log in. You can still choose to verify with your existing 2-factor authentication method, such as SMS or an authenticator app. This can be helpful if you don’t have access to your passkey.

How to use the admin console search bar

The admin console search bar allows you to quickly find settings, members and groups from your team, and help center articles directly from the admin console.

To use it:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click the search bar at the top of your screen. 
  4. Enter your query.

As you type, suggestions will appear in a dropdown below the search bar. You’ll see the title of the suggestion, with Settings, Help center article, Member, or Group below it, depending on what kind of result the suggestion is. Clicking a Settings, Member, or Group suggestion will bring you to that location in the admin console. Selecting a Help center article suggestion will open the article in a new tab in your browser.

How to use the Dropbox Sign admin console

Dropbox Sign admins can use the admin console to manage their team’s members, settings, and more. To access the admin console:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Click Admin console.

In the left sidebar there are five pages: Users, Team, Reporting, Settings, and Security. Learn more about what you can do from each page in the sections below.

From the Users page, you can:

  • Invite users to your team
  • View pending invitations
  • Remove users from your team
  • Edit a user’s role
  • Reset a user’s password
  • Lock a user’s account
  • View templates a user has created
  • View when a user was last active
  • Move a user to a different team*

From the Team page, you can:

  • View the admin(s), team manager(s), and parent team* of each team
  • Edit team names
  • Create a new team*

From the Reporting page, you can:

  • Run user activity, compliance, and document status* reports
  • View charts of recent activity*

From the Settings page, you can:

  • Edit your company information and branding
  • Configure signature request preferences and customize outgoing emails
  • Configure document and template settings
  • Manage connected apps

From the Security page, you can:

  • Require multi-factor authentication
  • Enable SAML SSO*

*Only Dropbox Sign teams on a Premium plan

How to use the Enterprise console for admins

The Enterprise console allows Enterprise admins manage multiple Enterprise teams all in one place. 

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Enterprise console in the left sidebar.

In the Enterprise console, you’ll find four different tabs to manage different aspects of your team and their activity: Teams, Members, Activity, and Settings. 

Teams tab

View and manage all connected teams:

  • To invite a new team, click Invite a team.
  • To remove a team, click the  ☑ (More options) next to the team name and click Remove.
  • Click a team to a view details, admins, and activity.
  • To manage an admin, click the  ☑ (More options) next to their name. From here, you can:
    • Reset their password
    • Edit permissions
    • Suspend or remove them

Members tab

The Members tab shows a summary of all the members of your connected teams, including admins. You can search and filter them by:

  • Members
  • Teams
  • Role
  • Status

You can also move team members to another Dropbox team account you manage.

To manage a member:

  • Click the ☑ (More options) next to their name to: 
    • Reset their password
    • Edit permissions
    • Remove them from a team

To add an enterprise admin:

  1. Go to the Members tab.
  2. Search for the member you’d like to make an enterprise admin.
  3. Click the ☑ (More options) next to their name.
  4. Click Edit admin permissions.
  5. Select Enterprise admin, then click Next.
  6. Click Make enterprise admin to confirm.

Activity tab

The Activity tab is similar to the team activity log in the regular admin console. It shows a summary of the activity of all admins and team members in one place. You can filter activities by: 

  • Date
  • People
  • Content
  • Activities
  • Team

Settings tab

The Settings tab shows the teams you manage.

To update settings for a specific team:

  1. Go to the Settings tab.
  2. Find the team you want to manage.
  3. Click Manage settings.
    • This open’s the team’s admin console where you can update settings using Enterprise admin permissions.

How to verify your Dropbox email address

You need to verify the email address associated with your Dropbox account so you can always keep access to your files.

If you don’t verify your email address, Dropbox won’t be able to help you if you ever need to regain access to your Dropbox account. It only takes two minutes to verify your email address following the instructions below.

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox helps you effortlessly share files and folders.

How to check if you’ve already verified your email address

If you’ve ever clicked on a link in an email we’ve sent you, you’ve already verified your email address and don’t need to do anything else. If your email address hasn’t been verified yet, we’ll send you a link via email the first time you take an action that requires verification.

How to verify your email address

To verify your email address:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Send a verification email to the email address associated with your account.
  3. Look for the verification email from no-reply@dropbox.com in your inbox and click the link in that email.

A confirmation message will appear in your web browser.

Didn’t get the verification email?

If you don’t see the email in your inbox, try the following:

  1. Check your spam or junk folder. Sometimes email providers may mistakenly flag automated emails.

  2. Add Dropbox to your contacts. Add no-reply@dropbox.com to your email address book or contacts list to help ensure future messages are delivered.

  3. Check with your email provider or IT administrator. It’s possible that your email service is filtering out Dropbox messages before they reach your inbox.

Still not receiving the verification email?

If none of the steps above work, try one of the following:

  • Use a different email address. You can change the email on your Dropbox account to another one you already use, or create a new email address and use it instead. 

    Learn how to change your email address.

 

  • Contact Dropbox support. If you’re still unable to verify your email and can’t change it, contact our support team. We may be able to manually verify your email if we can confirm your identity through a questionnaire or email exchange.

Issues logging in to Dropbox using Sign in with Apple

If you’re trying to create a new Dropbox account using Sign in with Apple and your phone dies or the app crashes for any reason, the next time you attempt to sign up you may see an error message that says your login attempt failed.

Find solutions to other common issues logging in to Dropbox.

Why did this happen?

If you encounter this issue, it means your Apple ID connected to your Dropbox account before the sign up process completed. In order to complete your sign up, you’ll need to disconnect and reconnect your Apple ID.

How to disconnect your Apple ID
  1. Go to appleid.apple.com/account/manage.
  2. Next to Security, click Manage… below Apps & Websites Using Apple ID.
  3. Click Dropbox.
  4. Click Stop Using Apple ID.
  5. Click Done.

Once you’ve stopped using your Apple ID with Dropbox, you should be able to successfully create your Dropbox account using Sign in with Apple.

I’m having trouble signing in to my Dropbox account

If you’re having trouble signing in to your account, this article discusses some of the common causes and solutions to this issue.  

Sections in this article:

  • I forgot my password
  • I received a Dropbox security email
  • I’m on a Dropbox team account user and can’t sign in  

I forgot my password

If you forgot your password, you can reset it.  

Learn more about resetting your password.

My password has expired

Your password will expire periodically for security reasons. You’ll need to change it to access your account, log in on a new device, or connect an API app.

Learn more about changing an expired password.

I received a Dropbox security email

If we detect suspicious sign-in attempts on your account, we’ll email you a one time security code.

Learn what to do if you received an email with a one-time security code.  

If you’re still unable to access your account, contact Dropbox Support.

I’m a Dropbox team account user and can’t sign in

If you’re a member of a Dropbox team account and you’re having trouble signing in, here are some things to check:  

1. Has your admin turned on single sign-on (SSO)?

Single sign-on (SSO) lets you access Dropbox in the same way you access other applications at work—by using your organization’s sign-in page. Contact your admin to find out whether this feature has been turned on.

If so, enter your email address and leave the password field blank on Dropbox’s sign-in pages, and learn more about what you need to do to access Dropbox on the web, computers, and mobile devices. Also make sure that the email address for your Dropbox account matches the one you use for your organization’s sign-in page.

2. Have you forgotten your password?

If so, you can reset it yourself. If your admin has turned on single sign-on (SSO) and you forgot your work password, use the “forgot password” link on your organization’s sign-in page or contact your admin. If you’d like help resetting your password, your admin can follow these steps:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin Console.
  3. Click Members.
  4. Click  next to the team member’s name.
  5. Choose Reset Password.  

3. Has your admin enabled password control? 

Password control allows Dropbox team admins to set password requirements or reset passwords for your team. If your team admin has set a new password requirement, you’ll need to reset your password the next time you sign in.  

4. Has your account been suspended?

If you’re a non-admin Dropbox team member, your admin can suspend your account. If this is the case, you’ll see an error message when you attempt to sign in or create a new account. You’ll also receive an email notifying you about your account’s suspension. If you need access to your account, you’ll need to contact your admin.

Can’t sign in to view your admins? Try contacting your organization’s help desk, IT department, or management team for further help.  

5. Have you been removed from the Dropbox team account?

If you left your organization, your admin may have disabled access to your account. Reach out to your admin to learn about the status of your account and what policies and procedures are in place for your team.

Leave a Dropbox team

If you’re a member of a Dropbox team account, your admin can help you remove your account. If you’re an admin, learn how to remove an account from a Dropbox team.

How to leave a Dropbox team account

Your admin can remove your account from your Dropbox team when you leave your organization. There are several ways your account can be removed from your team. Your account can be:

  • Suspended from the team
  • Deleted from the team
  • Converted to a personal account

You can’t leave an active Dropbox team without the help of an admin. Contact your admin to help choose the best option for your work account.

How to leave a team account if your team is in locked state

If you’re a member of a team in locked state, you can leave the team and convert your member account into a free Dropbox Basic account. Your personal folder will move to this new account but you’ll lose access to most team content. To learn more about what you’ll lose access to after converting to a Basic account, see the Accounts converted to a personal accounttab in the section above.

To leave a team when you’re in locked state:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Navigate to 0.
    • Note: The link above is only accessible if your team is currently in locked state.
  3. Click Leave the [Team name] team.
  4. Check the box next to I understand I’ll need to be invited by the team admin if I want to join the team again.
  5. Click Leave team and log out.
  6. You can log in to your Dropbox Basic account with the same email and password that you used for your member account. You can also change the email address associated with your new Dropbox Basic account.

Link user logins in Dropbox DocSend

Overview

If you have multiple DocSend accounts, you can link them to one another and seamlessly toggle between them from your Linked Logins page.

How to Link Logins

To link a user account: 

  1. Review the company name configured in your Company General Settings page. The selected name is what is visible when switching between different user accounts.
  2. Navigate to the User Settings page under your profile icon and select Switch Company.
  3. Click Link Another Login to connect your other user account.
    • Note: The account you’re currently signed into will say “ACTIVE” in the login details.
  4. Enter the email address of the account you’d like to connect and click Initiate Linking.
  5. Once added, you will receive an email confirmation to complete the connection. The email will include a list of all accounts you’d like to connect - just click Link Logins to complete the process!
    • Note: The link will be accessible for 1 hour. If the link expires, you can repeat the steps above to resend the email confirmation.
  6. Once connected, you can find all linked accounts on the Linked Logins page by selecting Switch Company (from step 2).
    • Note: Switching companies will require you to log into the associated email account.  

Switch between Linked Logins

Switch between your linked logins just like you would switch between companies.  

Gmail and Outlook Extensions

In Gmail, you can switch between profiles by selecting Switch on the top-right of the extension. Check out our article DocSend Extension for Chrome to learn more.

In Outlook, you can switch between profiles by selecting Switch under the Settings icon. See our Download the Outlook Add-in article for more information.

Locking member accounts in Dropbox Sign

Admins and team managers on Dropbox Sign Standard and Sign Premium teams can lock individual members’ accounts, preventing them from logging in. This provides an extra layer of security for sensitive information, if an employee leaves or is suspended.

How to lock a Sign account

To lock a team member’s account:  

  1. Log in to Dropbox Sign with your admin credentials.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Click Admin console.
  4. Click Users in the left sidebar.
  5. Click ⋮ (ellipsis) next to the member you’d like to lock out.
  6. Select Lock Account from the dropdown.
    • To unlock an account you’ve previously locked, select Unlock.

As team admin, you’ll receive a notification by email if a locked out team member attempts to log in. 

 

A locked out team member will see the following message if they try to log in: “Your account has been locked out by the administrator. Please contact your administrator to have your account unlocked.”

Log in to Dropbox with Google Sign-In

If you use Google (for example, Gmail or Google Docs), you can use your Google account to access Dropbox. With Google Sign-In, you can access Dropbox without having to remember a Dropbox password.

You can access Dropbox with Google Sign-In on:

  • dropbox.com
  • The Dropbox desktop app
  • The Dropbox mobile app for iOS and Android

How to sign in to Dropbox using Google Sign-In

Admins: How to turn off Google Sign-In for your team

By default, your team members can use Google Sign-In for their team accounts. Certain types of admins can disable Google Sign-In. To do this:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Single sign-on.
  5. Toggle Google sign-in to Off.

Manage invitations for your Dropbox team account

Certain types of admins can manage invitations and membership settings from the admin console. Learn more about admin permissions.

Learn how to invite people to your team account.

Manage membership settings

To manage who can send invitations and how people can join your team:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Settings in the left sidebar.
  4. Under Members, click Membership.
  5. Under each section, toggle the setting you’d like to change on or off.
  6. Click Save.

Different types of accounts have different settings available:

  • Member invites: If this setting is on, team members can invite people to the team. You can decide whether all members or only approved members are allowed to send invites. You can also choose whether those members can invite anyone or only people with email addresses on your organization’s domain. When a member invites someone, you’ll receive an email notification. This setting only applies to members, not to admins.
  • Coworkers can ask to join your team: If this setting is on, users on your organization’s domain—and collaborators outside your team—can discover your team and request to join. They can do this from several places, including dropbox.com/team. Some teams may see an Automatic approval for team join requests from [your team domain] checkbox below this setting. If checked, users on your organization’s domain can join the team automatically, without admin approval.
  • Team members can recommend inviting others: This setting is on by default. You can see a list of invite suggestions in the Pending members section of the Members page. When an admin approves a suggestion, an invite is sent to the suggested person’s email. 
  • Let me know when invited people join the team: If this setting is on, you’ll receive an email when someone accepts an invitation to join your team. All admins with permission to send invitations will receive this notification as well. If the setting is turned off, no admins—regardless of role—will receive an email when someone joins.
  • Reminders for requests to join the team: If this setting is on, you’ll receive an email reminder for requests to join the team that have been pending for more than two days.

Invite or dismiss requests to join

To manually invite or dismiss requests to join your team:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Members.
  4. Under Requests to join, click Approve and invite or Deny next to the request you’d like to approve or deny.

Manage sub-team folder access in Dropbox DocSend

Overview

Owners and admins can manage access to team folders on the Content page. By controlling access, you can ensure that each sub-team in your organization only sees the content relevant to them.

Folder access levels

There are three levels of folder access that you can apply to a sub-team:

  • No access: Users can’t view the folder or any of its content.
  • View and share only: Users can view the folder, its content, and create links to share it.
  • Edit and share: Users can view, share, and manage content in the folder, including adding, removing, and updating files. They can also manage folder access and move content, including sub-folders. 

Update folder access

To update folder access levels for a specific team folder: 

  1. Click    (more options) next to the folder name.
  2. Select Manage access.
  3. Review and update access levels from the dropdown next to each sub-team.
  4. Click Update folder access to save.

Overview of user roles in Dropbox DocSend

DocSend offers multiple levels of user access depending on your plan type. The DocSend Personal plan consists of one account owner and members. The DocSend Standard, Advanced, Advanced Data Rooms, and Enterprise plans consist of one account owner, members, and admins who hold privileges similar to the account owner. 

Learn more about Dropbox DocSend plans.

User roles

There are three distinct user roles in DocSend, each with different permissions and access.

Member

All plans allow members to upload and use DocSend without having direct access to company-wide settings.

Members can:

  • Upload content
  • Edit and update content
  • Share presentations
  • Create links
  • Export visits from self-owned documents only  
Admin (Standard, Advanced, Advanced Data Rooms, Enterprise)

Admins manage members and content across the account. They have all the member privileges and access to the company settings. The owner and admins can designate as many admins as needed.

Admins can:

  • Adjust the general team name
  • Customize branding settings
  • Manage users
  • Archive contact and accounts
  • See visit data on all documents in a Team folder
  • Export visits from all documents in a Team Folder
  • Configure Salesforce
  • Update NDA settings
  • Transfer user data
Account owner

All plans have a single account owner who has admin privileges, access to the billing page, and can transfer account ownership.

Transferring account ownership

When the current account owner transfers ownership to another individual, the previous account owner is then reassigned as a member and loses access to billing information. 

How to update a user’s role

Admins and account owners can update team member roles at any time.

To update a member’s role:

  1. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the top-right corner.
  2. Click Settings.
  3. Click Company.
  4. Click Users.
  5. Click ☑ (more options) next to the member you want to update.
  6. Choose Make Admin or Make Owner from the dropdown and confirm.
    • Note: To turn an admin back into a member, choose Make Member.

Plan-specific considerations

When you downgrade to the Personal plan, the account owner and admin roles remain, but their visibility is limited to self-owned document and link analytics. Team-wide reporting isn’t available on Personal.

Password appeared in breach on Dropbox Sign

To keep your information safe, Dropbox Sign uses an internal tool to check your sign in credentials against a list of known data breaches. When you create an account or reset your password, we use this tool to make sure your credentials are as secure as possible.

Does this mean my information has been exposed by Dropbox Sign? No. This warning doesn’t mean that any of your accounts have been compromised. However, it does indicate that your information might have been exposed elsewhere.

What do I do now? We require you to choose a different password to sign in to Dropbox Sign. You should also change this password if you use it anywhere else.

Remove a member from a Dropbox Fax team

Team members can’t quit their teams on their own. The team’s administrator will need to make that change from within his or her own account.

To remove a member from a Fax team:

  1. Sign in to sign.dropbox.com with your admin credentials. 
  2. Click the Team tab on the left.
  3. Find the email address of the member to be removed in the list of team members.
  4. Click the small downward arrow to the right of their email address to pull down the menu.
  5. Click Remove.

Restrictions and limitations for team deployments of Dropbox Dash

Dropbox Dash connects your apps, files, and messages into one workspace. Whether you’re an admin managing team accounts or a team member connecting apps and using tools, there are a few limitations to keep in mind. This article makes recommendations around those limits.

Table of contents

  • Deployment requirements
  • Team management
  • Platform and device support
  • Apps and integrations
  • AI features and access
  • Files and uploads
  • Security and governance
  • Content organization and collaboration

Deployment requirements

Eligibility requirements

Dash for Teams is available only if all of the following apply:

  • Dropbox plan: Your account is on Dropbox Basic, Dropbox Standard, Dropbox Business, Dropbox Advanced, or Dropbox Business Plus.
  • Supported regions: Your team is located in the United States, United Kingdom, or Australia.
  • Account language: Your Dropbox account’s primary language is set to English.
  • Encryption key management: Managed encryption keys must be turned off on your Dropbox account.
  • Replay or Sign users: If your Dropbox team account includes Replay or Sign, all users on the team must have licenses. Learn more about Dash for teams.

Unsupported deployments

Dash for Teams isn’t currently available for:

  • Individual users on Dropbox Plus, Professional, or Essentials plans.
  • Customers on managed teams.
  • Accounts that require HIPAA compliance. Learn more about Dash for teams.

Setup limitations

  • Device-wide installs on shared machines aren’t supported.

Team management

Member management

  • Each team member needs a Dash account and license to get started.
  • After a member is removed, the same email address can’t be reused to create a new Dropbox account for seven days.
  • If the removed user’s files are transferred to another team member during removal, the email address can be reused immediately. Learn more about managing team members in Dash.

Platform and device support

Mobile app

  • The Dropbox Dash mobile app is available only in select countries.
  • The app is available in English only.
  • The Dash mobile app must run on supported operating systems. Learn more about Dash system requirements.
  • Ask, Write, and Organize aren’t available on mobile.

Desktop app

  • The Dash desktop app must run on supported operating systems. Learn more about Dash system requirements. 
  • Local file search is supported only on the Dash desktop app.

Browser extension

  • The Dash browser extension requires a supported browser version. Learn more about Dash system requirements. 
  • Turning off the Dash start page during installation may also turn off the entire extension.
    • Note: If the extension turns off after disabling the Dash start page, turn the extension back on in your browser’s extensions menu, and disable only the Dash start page setting.

dash.ai

  • dash.ai can’t search files stored locally on your computer.
  • AI features, including summarization, aren’t supported for local files.

Apps and integrations

Connecting apps

To connect an app to Dash:

  • Certain apps must first be enabled by a Dash admin.
  • You must authorize the app during setup.
  • You must have an active account with the app you want to connect. Learn more about connecting apps to Dash.

Individual app connections

  • Depending on the app, you may not be able to connect your own individual account after an admin connects that app for your team.
  • Some apps support both:
    • An admin-connected version for shared team content.
    • An individual connection for personal or private content. Learn more about connecting apps to Dash.

Multiple account limitations

  • Connecting multiple accounts for the same app isn’t supported.
  • You can’t connect multiple profiles for apps such as Gmail or Google Drive. Learn more about connecting apps to Dash.

Search limitations

  • Dash searches content from connected apps only.
  • Search capabilities vary depending on the integrations you’ve connected.

AI features and access

AI features

  • Ask, Write, and Organize are available on dash.ai and the Dash desktop app.
  • Ask, Write, and Organize aren’t available on the mobile app.
  • AI features, including summarization, aren’t supported for local files.

Chat model selection

  • You can choose from a curated set of AI models before sending a prompt.
  • Not all AI models are available to every user.
  • Available models may change over time. Learn more about choosing a chat model in Dash.

Activity feed

  • The activity feed shows files only from select connected apps.

Files and uploads

Upload limits

The following upload limits apply in Dash:

  • Maximum file size: 25 MB per file
  • Files per upload: Up to 10 files at a time.
  • Images per conversation: Up to 50 images.
  • Text extraction limit: Up to 4.5 MB of text per file.
  • PDF limit: Up to 75 pages.
  • PowerPoint (.ppt, .pptx) limit: Up to 75 slides.

Supported file types in chat

You can attach the following file types in chat:

Documents

  • CSV (.csv).
  • Word (.doc, .docx).
  • Markdown (.md).
  • PDF (.pdf).
  • Text (.txt).
  • Excel (.xlsx, .xls).

Images

  • BMP (.bmp).
  • GIF (.gif).
  • JPEG (.jpg, .jpeg).
  • PNG (.png).
  • TIFF (.tiff).
  • WebP (.webp).

Videos

  • 3GP (.3gp).
  • 3GPP (.3gpp).
  • 3GPP2 (.3gpp2).
  • ASF (.asf).
  • AVI (.avi).
  • DV (.dv).
  • M2T (.m2t).

Verified files

  • Only admins can verify files.
