Security and governance

Dropbox Protect

  • Protect currently supports only Dropbox, Microsoft 365, and Google Drive.
  • Policies run once daily at 08:00 UTC.
  • If you edit or deactivate a policy, queued actions may still run.
  • Admins can view files from supported connected apps, but can’t access local files or browser history.
  • When exporting to CSV, export filtered results only. Exporting all results isn’t recommended. Learn more about managing Protect in Dash.

Content organization and collaboration

Company directory

  • Some profile fields, such as job title, location, and manager, are synced from your company directory and can’t be edited in Dash.
  • Company directory isn’t available during the free trial.

Stacks

Comments

  • Each item in a Stack can have only one comment.
  • Comments can be up to 2,000 characters long.
  • Only the comment author or the Stack owner can delete a comment.

Publishing

  • Only admins can publish company Stacks.

Sharing and availability

  • Creating Stacks directly in Dropbox is currently available only to teams eligible for a preview of Dash in Dropbox.
  • You can currently share Stacks on dropbox.com only with members of your team.

Browser support

  • Adding a group of tabs to a Stack is currently supported only in Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge. Learn more about using Stacks with Dash.

Single sign-on (SSO) in Dropbox DocSend

DocSend offers the option to log in securely through Okta, OneLogin, or Entra ID via SAML 2.0. As an added layer of security, DocSend also supports SCIM for user provisioning with both Okta and OneLogin.

To explore activating SSO for your account, please reach out to sales@docsend.com for information on upgrading to DocSend’s Enterprise plan. Once you’ve followed the steps outlined in their presentation, contact our support team with the necessary information in our email response to you.

OneLogin

For an in-depth, step-by-step instructional guide for including OneLogin as part of your company’s account, please visit our presentation on Connecting OneLogin.

Okta

Okta provides a guide on how to configure SAML 2.0 for DocSend. Once you’ve followed the steps outlined in their article, contact our support team with the necessary information in our email response to you.

Entra ID

To set up Entra ID SSO login:

  1. Contact our support team and request that they enable SAML 2.0 for your account.
  2. The DocSend Support team will provide you with your EntityID and Reply URL(Assertion Consumer Service URL) value. 
  3. In Entra ID, set the value of Identifier (Entity ID) and Reply URL (Assertion Consumer Service URL) that you received from DocSend Support team.

Managed accounts

Please contact your Customer Success Manager directly for more information on enabling SSO for your account. Not sure who your dedicated Customer Success Manager is? Reach out to our support team for more information.

How can I purchase the add-on?

You can reach out to sales@docsend.com for more information or to activate this add-on for your plan.

SMS discontinuation for 2-factor authentication FAQs in certain countries

Why is Dropbox removing the SMS option for 2-factor authentication?

SMS delivery reliability and security vary across regions. To ensure a consistent and trustworthy 2-factor authentication (2FA) experience, Dropbox continuously reviews authentication methods worldwide and supports SMS 2FA only in countries where these needs can be effectively met.

How to replace your 2-factor authentication method

To keep using 2FA, you’ll need a mobile device with a compatible authenticator app. Authenticator apps generate time-sensitive security codes even when you don’t have mobile or data service, which can be helpful when traveling or in areas with poor coverage.

Popular apps that support the Time-based-One-Time Password (TOTP) protocol include:

  • Google Authenticator (Android/iPhone)
  • Duo Mobile (Android/iPhone)
  • Authenticator (Windows Phone 7)

If you’re prompted to switch when logging in (after January 9, 2026)

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. A new window appears with a QR code and a secret key. 
  3. Choose one:
    • QR code: Scan the code with your phone’s camera.
    • Secret key: In your authenticator app, add a new account and enter the secret key.
  4. Click Next.
  5. Enter the 6-digit code generated from your authenticator app and click Next.
  6. Click Continue to Dropbox to finish setup.

From your account settings (available anytime)

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials).
    • Depending on your plan, your avatar may appear in the top-right or bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the Security tab.
  5. Toggle 2-factor authentication to On.
    • If you see Managed by single sign-on under the Security tab, your team admin has enabled single sign-on (SSO). This means you don’t have to use 2-factor authentication with Dropbox and can access your account by logging in to a central identity provider. Contact your admin to learn more.
  6. Re-enter your password and click Submit.
  7. Select Authenticator app and click Submit.
  8. Choose one:
    • QR code: Scan it with your phone’s camera.
    • Secret key: Add a new account in your authenticator app and enter the secret key.
  9. Click Next.
  10. Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app and click Next.
  11. Add a secondary phone number (optional), then click Save or Skip for now.
    • This option is only available for certain countries.
  12. Store your recovery codes safely and check I’ve stored my recovery codes in a safe place.
  13. Click Finish, then Done.

Why is this change only happening in certain countries?

SMS delivery reliability and security differ by region. Dropbox maintains SMS 2FA only in countries where service providers can ensure consistent delivery and security.

Will this affect my or my team’s account security?

No. Switching to an authenticator app increases security. Authenticator apps are more secure than SMS-based codes. However, disabling 2FA entirely will make your account more vulnerable.

What happens if I don’t switch from SMS 2FA?

After the discontinuation date on January 9, 2026, you’ll be prompted to update your 2FA method. The next time you log in on the web and complete SMS verification, you’ll be prompted to switch to an authenticator app or disbale 2FA. 

You won’t be able to dismiss this prompt.

Will I need to use the authenticator app every time I log in?

If you choose Trust this computer when signing in, you’ll only need to provide your two-factor authentication code once on that device.

For admins: How will my team members be notified?

Admins will receive an email notification about this change one week before their impacted team members. While not required, we encourage admins to notify their teams ahead of time so members can expect Dropbox’s emails and in-product prompts with detailed instructions.

What happens if I disable 2-factor authentication?

You can disable 2-factor authentication, but this will significantly reduce your account security. Passwords are often the weakest defense, we strongly recommend keeping 2FA enabled to protect your data. Learn more about 2-factor authentication.

SMS two-factor authentication for Dropbox Sign

Two-factor authentication (2FA) provides an extra layer of security when logging into sign.dropbox.com. 

When a sender enables two-factor authentication, they will be prompted to enter a unique code sent to their mobile phone before logging into Dropbox Sign. 

To set up 2FA: 

  1. Log in to your account.
  2. Hover over your email address in the upper-right corner.
  3. Select My Settings from the dropdown menu. 
  4. Click the Profile tab near the top of the screen.
  5. Scroll to 2-Factor Authentication and enter your mobile phone number.
  6. Click Verify.

 

  1. You’ll receive a text message with a verification code.
  2. When prompted, enter the verification code you received.
  3. Click Submit.

Suggested team members

A suggested member is a Dropbox user who has been recommended to join a Dropbox team account. Team members can suggest members, and Dropbox will automatically suggest members based on the criteria listed below.

View suggested team members

You can view members suggested by Dropbox from either your Home page or your  admin dashboard.

To view members suggested by your team members:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Members.
  4. Click Filter by and select Suggested by Dropbox.

Suggested members will appear under the Members section once filtered.

How does Dropbox determine suggested members for my team?

Dropbox suggests new members for your team who either have a Dropbox account on your organization’s domain or are a member of one of your team’s shared folders.

Team level document syncing and storage with Dropbox Sign

With team cloud sync, your team can organize all their Dropbox Sign documents in one place, like Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, or Box.

How to set admin controls for document syncing and storage

Admins can control the syncing and storage integration options for the entire team in the admin console.

To change team-wide settings:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Click Admin console.
  4. Click Settings in the left sidebar.
  5. Click Documents and templates in the left sidebar.
  6. Click Link my account next to the integration you’d like to use and follow the prompts.

Once the process is complete, all the connected accounts on your team will show in Connected accounts and a folder with the name of your team will be created in the storage integration. All documents will sync, including retroactively.

Transfer user data in Dropbox DocSend

Overview

Being able to transfer content and data is an important step in properly managing your account. With our Transfer User Data feature, DocSend Owners and Admins can transfer all of a suspended or deactivated user’s data to another active user, ensuring that the inactive user’s DocSend links and documents remain accessible. This article will provide a step-by-step guide on how to transfer user data and detail what is retained during this process.

What data gets transferred?

  • Documents 
  • All links 
  • Historical visitor data
  • Contacts
  • Accounts
  • Spaces
  • Subteams

Transfer User Data

To begin the transfer process, access the Company User Settings to view all suspended and deactivated users. Only inactive user data can be transferred to an active user. If the user is still active, you will need to deactivate or suspend them before beginning the data transfer.

  1. Select the “more options” menu next to an inactive user to access the Transfer user data option.
  2. Once selected, search for an active user to transfer the data to by typing their name or email address.
  3. After selecting an active user, type in “TRANSFER”
  4. Click Transfer user data to complete the process.
  5. Once confirmed, the transfer process can take up to 3 minutes to complete.

After the data transfer is complete, the active user will now own all aspects of the inactive user’s:

    • Documents
    • Links
    • Visitor data
    • Contacts
    • Accounts
    • Spaces
    • Subteams (Enterprise only)

Files from the suspended or deactivated user’s personal folder will be available in the new active user’s personal folder named “[Inactive User]’s My Content”.

Team content uploaded previously by the deactivated user will remain in the same team folder.

Transferred links will remain in the same state that they were in prior to the transfer. For example, links that were disabled prior to transferring will continue to remain in a disabled state.

Use Dropbox DocSend on mobile browsers

Overview

DocSend is fully accessible on iOS or Android mobile browsers if you need to create, manage, and share links while on the go! You’ll notice that most of the behavior mirrors the desktop experience and any nuances are available on our respective help center articles. 

Compatible Browsers

While DocSend is supported on all desktop browsers, the mobile experience is currently  optimized for the following:

  • Google Chrome
  • Apple Safari
  • Mozilla Firefox
  • Microsoft Edge

Browser Shortcut

For rapid access and convenience, we recommend creating a shortcut to DocSend on your mobile device. IOS or Android users can set up browser shortcuts for DocSend on their mobile device’s home screen.

  • For Mozilla Firefox: Open Firefox > Menu button > Add Page Shortcut 
  • For Apple Safari: Go to your Safari > Share > Add to Home screen 
  • For Microsoft Edge: Add this to your favorites or as an InPrivate tab.  

Things to consider

  • Currently, DocSend does not have a dedicated mobile app.

User management in Dropbox DocSend

User management is critical for keeping your documents secure and your billing up to date. DocSend owners and admins can visit the Company settings page to add new users, remove existing users, and manage account access.

Before getting started, keep the following in mind: 

  • Adding new users may result in additional charges depending on your plan (see our pricing page for details). 
  • DocSend uses an invitation system. Invited users will receive an email with a link to join your team.  
    • Note: Invite limits may vary for new users and increase over time. If you need higher limits, contact support. On Advanced Data Rooms plans, you can import email addresses using a CSV file. 
  • If you have a managed account, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) for assistance with adding or removing users. 
  • If your company uses SSO, your user management experience may differ from the steps outlined below.

Invite a new user

To invite a new user to your team:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the upper right.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Company.
  5. Click Users.
  6. Click Add users.
  7. Enter the user’s email address and select a user role for them. 
    • Note: If you’re adding multiple users, separate each user’s email address with a comma.
  8. Click Send invite.

To re-invite a user to your team:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the upper right.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Company.
  5. Click Users.
  6. Click Invited.
  7. Click (more options) next to the name of the user you’d like to re-invite.
  8. Click Resend invite.

Deactivate a user

If someone on your team no longer needs access to DocSend, you can easily deactivate the user from the Company settings page. 

When a user’s account is deactivated:

  • The user can no longer log in.
  • The user’s links are disabled.
  • The user’s team documents are still accessible.
  • The user’s historical visitor data is still visible for owners/admins.
  • The user is removed from your DocSend subscription.

To avoid losing access to the user’s links and Spaces, admins or owners should transfer ownership to another user when deactivating the user. Admins and owners will see a list of affected links and Spaces before they confirm the deactivation.

To deactivate a user:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the upper right.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Company.
  5. Click Users.
  6. Click (more options) next to the name of the user you’d like to deactivate.
  7. Click Deactivate. 
    • To transfer ownership of the user’s links or Spaces, click Transfer and continue, then click Deactivate and transfer.
    • To deactivate without transferring ownership, click Skip, then click Continue.
    • If the user doesn’t own any links or Spaces, click Deactivate.

Suspend a user

You can suspend a users to prevent them from logging in while keeping their documents and links active.

When a user’s account is suspended:

  • The user can no longer log in; a new password is set and can’t be reset.
  • All of the user’s documents, links, and Spaces remain active.
  • The user’s team documents are still accessible.
  • The user’s historical visitor data is still accessible.
  • The user is still part of your DocSend subscription.

To suspend a user:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the upper right.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Company.
  5. Click Users.
  6. Click (more options) next to the name of the user you’d like to deactivate.
  7. Click Suspend account. 
  8. Click Yes, suspend to confirm.
  9. Enter a new password and click Change password.

Reactivate a user

You can also reactivate a deactivated or suspended user at any time by following the steps below. If you’ve been deactivated or suspended and need access to DocSend again, please reach out to your company’s owner or admin to help reactivate your DocSend account.

To reactivate a user:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the upper right.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Company.
  5. Click Users.
  6. Click Inactive.
  7. Click (more options) next to the name of the user you’d like to reactivate.
  8. Click Reactivate.
  9. Click Reactivate to confirm.

Using Dropbox Sign without Gmail

While Dropbox Sign is heavily integrated with Google and Gmail, you do not have to use Gmail to use Dropbox Sign.

If you send your clients a signature request via Dropbox Sign, they simply need to have a valid email address and internet connection. That’s it!

Only our Dropbox Sign for Gmail plugin and Google Drive and Docs integrations require a Gmail account, but you don’t need to use those features to use Dropbox Sign. Those are just added integrations for those using Gmail.

View team activity and Stack reports in Dash

If you’re an admin on a Dropbox Dash team account, you can view membership, activity, and Stacks data for your team. You can also create and export reports to share with others.

How to view team membership data

  1. How to view team membership data 
  2. Log in to dash.ai using your admin credentials. 
  3. Select Admin console.
  4. Click Members.
  5. Click on their name to open their profile. You’ll see the following information: 
    • Email: The member’s basic contact information.
    • User type: The person’s role within the organization. User types include:
      • Team admin
      • User management admin
      • Support admin
      • Member
    • Usage: The amount of storage space that member is.
    • Member since: The date the member joined your Dash team. 
    • Group membership: The list of groups the member belongs to.

How to view and export Dash activity reports

Admins can generate and export detailed reports showing when a member performs the following actions in Dash:

  • Connected or removed an app
  • Opened dash.ai for the first time
  • Opened the Dash desktop app for the first time

To generate and export a report on a member’s activity:

  1. Log in to dash.ai using your admin credentials.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the lower left.
  3. Select Admin console.
  4. Under Products, click Dash, then click Settings.
  5. In the Security section, click Open next to Security logging.
  6. Use the filters to select the type of activity events and time period to retrieve the data you’d like to export.
  7. Click Apply.
  8. Click Create report to the right of your filters.
  9. Click Generate in the pop-up window. Download the file to your computer.

How to view and export Stack activity reports

Admins can generate and export detailed reports showing when a member performs the following actions on Stacks:

  • Adds, deletes, or edits a comment in a Stack
  • Creates, clones, renames, archives, or deletes a Stack
  • Checks access permissions to a Stack
  • Opens a Stack
  • Adds, shares, or removes a link to a Stack
  • Changes the audience of a shared link to a Stack

To generate and export a report on a user’s Stack activity:

  1. Log in to dash.ai using your admin credentials.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the lower left.
  3. Select Admin console.
  4. Under Products, click Dash, then click Settings.
  5. In the Security section, click Open next to Security logging.
  6. Click the Activities filter, and enter “Stack” in the search field.
  7. Use the filters to select the type of Stack activities and time period to retrieve the data you’d like to export.
  8. Click Apply.
  9. Click Create report to the right of your filters.
  10. Click Generate in the pop-up window. Download the file to your computer.

View team activity in the admin console

As an admin, you can use the dashboard in the admin console to get a high-level view of your team’s usage, storage and security.

Learn more about the features of the admin dashboard.  

For more detailed insights, the Activity section of the admin console shows specific team activity and lets you generate reports based on that data.  

File types that preview as a link

If your saved website has one of the following extensions, it will preview as a shortcut to the website.

Create and export an activity report

To create and export an activity report:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com using your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Activity in the left sidebar.
  4. Use the filters to select the type of data and the time period you’d like to export.
  5. Click Create report to the right of your filters.
  6. Select the report type you want to generate. 
  7. Click Generate.

The report will be saved as a CSV in a folder named Dropbox Business reports. You’ll receive an email when the report is ready.

What can I see in activity reports?

Each entry in the activity report shows:

  • Date: The exact date that an action took place
  • Member: The member that initiated the action
  • Activity: Details of the event itself
  • Content: The type of file 

Generally, a team member’s actions appear in activity logs in a few hours. At most, actions appear within 24 hours.

Admins have the following events available in their team activity reports:

  • Apps
  • Comments
  • Devices
  • Domains
  • File operations (Dropbox Business Plus, Advanced and Enterprise only)
  • File requests
  • Groups
  • Logins
  • Members
  • Paper
  • Passwords
  • Reports
  • Sharing
  • Signature activity†
  • SSO
  • Team folders
  • Team policies
  • Team profile
  • Two-factor authentication

*These events are only available to customers on Dropbox Business and Business Plus.

†These events are only available to customers on a paid Dropbox Sign plan or Dropbox Standard, Advanced, Business, or Business Plus. 

As a team admin, you’ll see events for files owned by your team and files shared with your team members. If you’re a team admin on a Dropbox Business Plus, Advanced, or Enterprise account, you’ll also see file-level activity including adding, editing, moving, and deleting files.

You can use these events to investigate and troubleshoot problems, such as accidental file deletions, misplaced files or folders, or information security audits.  

Replay in the activity report 

The report now allows admins to review their team’s Replay activity, including:

  • When a team member logs in to Replay for the first time or connects their Dropbox account to Replay
  • When a team member uploads a file to Replay, including the file name and the uploader
  • When a team member deletes a file, including the file name and who deleted it
  • Any changes to team policies for Replay content
  • When links are created or modified for files in Replay, including:
    • What file it links to
    • Which team member did it
    • Whether the link is watermarked
    • Who can access it:
      • Anyone: Anyone with the link
      • Logged in users: Only users who are logged in
      • Team only: Only members of your team
      • Team + Approved: Only members of your team and approved users

Why do I see “Dropbox” in the Name column?

On rare occasions, Dropbox may update listings in your account for you. Some admins may see “Dropbox” listed in the Member column because:  

A team member deleted a nested shared folder

When a team member deletes a nested shared folder, the name of the person who deleted it appears as “Dropbox.” Certain types of admins can see the name of the team member by following these steps:

  1. Click Create report.
  2. Open your report in Excel.
  3. You can see the team member’s email address in the “Context” column.  

You’ve asked Dropbox support for help with a task

If you’ve contacted Dropbox support, any action we take appears on your Activity page as a task labeled “Dropbox.” These actions include inviting the original set of admins for your team. However, the Dropbox support team won’t make any changes to your account without your permission.  

Dropbox has updated your account

The Dropbox system regularly updates your account to keep it current with the latest Dropbox products. These updates appear on your Activity page as tasks labeled “Dropbox.” These actions can include renaming or moving team folders or updating your Dropbox team account with new products. Otherwise, the Dropbox system won’t make any changes to your account without your permission.

What happens when a user joins my Dropbox team account?

After you invite a user to join your Dropbox team account, they will be able to join the team. They can either transfer an existing account to a Dropbox team account or create a new account using their work email address.

If they choose to transfer an existing account, they will be given the option to merge their existing files to the Dropbox team account or create a new Dropbox Basic account for those files.

New members will automatically have access to content in the team space and any folder shared directly with them.

What if the member has a paid subscription? When joining a team, if any member has a paid Dropbox subscription, they will receive a prorated refund for the unused period back to the card they previously used to pay for the service.

What is a Dropbox Sign account conflict?

A Dropbox Sign account conflict happens when a member of a Dropbox team account has existing files associated with a Sign account with the same email address. 

How to resolve a Dropbox Sign account conflict

If you have a Sign account conflict, you’ll see the message “How should we handle your account on Dropbox Sign?”when you click the Signatures page on dropbox.com. 

Before you can resolve the conflict, you’ll need to choose one of these options:

  • Keep your personal Sign account separate from the team: You’re the only one with access and you maintain ownership of the content
  • Combine your Sign account with the team account: It will be shared with the team and the Dropbox team now owns the content

If you choose to keep it separate from the team:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click Signatures in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Update email.
    • You’ll be taken to hellosign.com and asked to log in.
  4. Log in with your Sign credentials.
  5. Click Update email address. 
  6. Enter a different email address that doesn’t have an existing Sign account.
  7. Check your email inbox for a verification email, then click Verify your email in that email.
    • You’ll get a confirmation message to say your email address has been verified, then you’ll be logged out of your Sign account.
      • Note: The Sign account conflict is only resolved after you verify your new email address.

If you choose combine accounts:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click Signatures in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Combine accounts.
    • This will automatically merge your existing Sign files with your Dropbox team account. If applicable, it will automatically refund a prorated amount for your Sign subscription.
    • Depending how many files you have, it may take a few minutes to transfer all the files.

Once completed, you‘ll be routed to hellosign.com. 

How to prevent a Dropbox Sign account conflict

If you have an existing Sign account with the same email address as your Dropbox team account, you can prevent a Sign account conflict by doing one of the following:

  • Ask your team admin to invite you to the Dropbox team account using a different email address than the one associated with your Sign account.
  • Change the email address associated with your Sign account before clicking the Signatures page on dropbox.com.
  • Delete your Sign account before accessing the Signatures page on dropbox.com.

What is locked state for teams?

Your team can enter locked state if:

  • Your Dropbox Standard, Advanced, Business, or Business Plus trial ends.
  • You cancel your team plan.

What happens next depends on whether you had a paid team subscription or a trial, and whether your team had any paid individual accounts:

  • A team canceling a paid subscription, and a trial team without any paid individuals, will go into locked state. If an admin doesn’t take action with the team account within a certain timeframe, the team account may be deleted automatically.
    • Admins will always be notified by email before their team account is deleted automatically.
    • If your team trial concludes without converting to a paid subscription and you’re the only team admin with no team members, we may downgrade you directly to Dropbox Basic after a period of time. You’ll be notified by email after the downgrade completes.
  • If your Dropbox Dash team is in locked state, data from any apps you’ve added to Dash will be automatically deleted after 30 days. You’ll be notified through email and when you open Dropbox Dash before this data is deleted.
    • Note: Any stacks you’ve created aren’t affected.

How to know if your team is in locked state

If your team is in a locked state, you’ll see a notification in your Dropbox account and some features will be unavailable until the team plan is resumed or changed.

You may notice:

  • A banner or notification on dropbox.com explaining that your team is locked.
  • Messages that certain actions are unavailable.
  • Prompts for admins to resume or change the team’s plan.

If your team is locked, the following features are unavailable:

  • Syncing files using the Dropbox desktop app
  • Sharing files or folders
  • Previewing files on dropbox.com
  • Uploading files on dropbox.com
  • Creating folders
  • Adding shared folders to your Dropbox
  • Inviting new team members
  • Creating or editing Paper docs (some teams will have read-only access)

If you try to use one of these features, you’ll see a message explaining that the action isn’t available while your team is locked.

How to get out of locked state

If you’re a team member, you can:

  • Contact your admin: They need to buy or renew your team’s subscription.
  • Leave your team: You’ll lose access to most team content.
    • Note: If your team is in locked state and has both Dropbox and a Dropbox Dash subscriptions, you can’t leave unless an admin disbands the team.

If you’re an admin, you may have the following available:

  • Purchase or renew your team’s subscription.
  • Disband your team.
  • Delete your team.
  • Downgrade to a Basic team.
    • Note: This option is only available to users in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada.

Details for each option are below.

What is the email address on my Dropbox account?

To log in to Dropbox, use the email address you used to sign up to Dropbox. 

If you’re not sure what the email address on your Dropbox account is, you can find it from a device you linked to your account or through a folder you shared, or through your payment information if you purchased a subscription.  

How can I find my email address if I can’t log in to Dropbox?

If you can’t log in to Dropbox, you can use our credit and debit card charge lookup tool to find the email address associated with a charge.

If you’re a member of a shared folder, you can also ask another member of that folder to look up your account’s address by doing the following:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click Shared in the left sidebar.
  3. Click the Folders tab.
  4. Find the shared folder and click the ☑ (more options) next to the shared folder name.
  5. Select Share.
  6. Click Who can access.

In the list of shared folder members, the person will be able to see the email address under to your name.

Was your account inactive?

If your Dropbox account was inactive for more than 12 months, it may have been closed due to inactivity. After it’s closed, the account and all its data are permanently deleted and can’t be recovered.

If that’s the case, you won’t be able to locate your account using an email address, and you’ll need to create a new account instead.

Learn more about inactive accounts.

What to do if you got an email about an inactive Dropbox account

Dropbox may close and delete inactive Dropbox Basic accounts.If there’s no activity on your Dropbox account for an extended period of time, Dropbox will notify you (the account owner) by email.

To keep your account active, log in and we’ll know you want to keep it. If you no longer want your account, you can close it instead.

What does “inactive” mean?

Dropbox determines inactive accounts by looking at log-ins and file activity (adding, editing, or deleting) anywhere on Dropbox during the past 12 months. If you’ve logged in or had any file activity on Dropbox within the previous 12 months, your account is considered active.

How to keep your Dropbox account

Why did I receive an email even though I use Dropbox?

If you recently used your Dropbox account but still received an email about account closure, it’s likely the email refers to a different Dropbox account that you no longer use or may have forgotten about.

Many of our users have multiple Dropbox accounts, and even the addition or removal of a period (“.”) from the email address can indicate a different account.

Before contacting support, check the following:

  • Confirm that the email was sent to the same email address you actively use with Dropbox.
  • Check whether the email was forwarded from another email account.
  • If you have multiple email addresses, log in to each Dropbox account to verify which one the email refers to.

If you’ve confirmed that the email refers to the Dropbox account you actively use and believe you received it in error, you can contact Dropbox support using the instructions at the bottom of this article.

How do I keep my account active?

To keep your account active:

  • Log in to your account on dropbox.com, the Dropbox desktop app on your computer, or the Dropbox mobile app.
  • Use any Dropbox app on your account.
  • View, add, edit, or remove files or folders.
What if I forgot my password?

You can reset your password if you’ve forgotten it.

What if I’ve lost access to my email address?

If you no longer have access to the email address associated with your Dropbox account, you can contact your email service provider to try to regain access. If you’re not sure what the email address on your Dropbox account is, learn how to find your Dropbox account email.

How to close your Dropbox account

If you no longer want your Dropbox Basic account, you can simply leave it inactive. If your account is eligible for deletion due to inactivity, we’ll send you multiple reminder emails before your account is closed. Each reminder includes the scheduled deletion date and explains how to keep your account active.

If we don’t notify you that your account is inactive, your account won’t be deleted due to inactivity.

Can I close my account now?

If you want to close your account, visit the account deletion page. You can also learn how to close a Dropbox Basic, Plus, Family, or team account.

How do I save my files before closing my account?

You can log in to dropbox.com or the Dropbox mobile app and save your files onto your hard drive or mobile device.

What happens when my account closes?

After your account is closed, any remaining files in your account will be subject to deletion, and you won’t be able to log into the account on dropbox.com or any of the devices on which you have installed the Dropbox app.

Learn more about our closed-account policy.

Does Dropbox delete files after inactivity?

If you receive an email that your account is inactive and don’t take steps to keep it active, we’ll send multiple reminder emails before it’s automatically closed, and your files will be deleted within 90 days. Each email includes the scheduled deletion date and explains what to do to keep your account.

If you don’t receive an email about account inactivity, your account won’t be subject to deletion for inactivity.

FAQs about account closures

I tried to log in, but got a message that my account doesn’t exist

The “Account doesn’t exist” message usually means the email address you entered doesn’t match the one associated with your Dropbox account. First, try logging in again and check that you’ve entered the correct email address. If that doesn’t work, and you received an email about an inactive account, it’s possible your account has already been closed. If so, contact us using the instructions below.

Can I recover an account that was closed?

Dropbox doesn’t reopen accounts that were closed because of inactivity. If your account was closed without permission, and you have proof that it wasn’t you (like signs of suspicious activity), we may be able to help. Contact Dropbox support to look into it.

Who do I contact Dropbox about account closures?

If you have questions about an account closure or an inactivity email:

  1. Log out of your Dropbox account.
  2. Navigate to our sign in issues support page.
  3. From the What’s your issue? dropdown, select Disabled account.
  4. Complete the form.
    • Note: Under email, enter the email associated with the account you’re asking about. 
  5. Click Submit.

Which web browsers does Dropbox DocSend support?

Overview

DocSend is a web-based application that’s compatible with most modern desktop and mobile web browsers. For the best experience, please make sure your browser version is up-to-date!

Supported Web Browsers

DocSend offers support for the following web browsers:

  • Google Chrome
  • Safari
  • Mozilla Firefox
  • Microsoft Edge

Why am I being prompted to join a Dropbox team account?

You may be prompted to join a Dropbox team account for several reasons:

  • You created a Dropbox Basic, Plus, or Professional account using your work email address.
  • Your admin sent a Dropbox team account invite to your personal account.
    • In this case, you’ll want to ask your admin to resend the invite to your work email

What are my options if I receive a prompt to join a team?

Dropbox may send you a prompt to request access to join a team, or you may receive a link from an admin in your email to join their team. In both cases, you have options. 

Receiving a prompt from Dropbox to request to join a team 

In this situation, Dropbox has noticed that you frequently collaborate with a Dropbox team and believes you may benefit from being part of that team account. When you open a link to a file or folder you received from a Dropbox admin, a window from Dropbox will give you the option to send a request to join the team account, or to bypass this prompt and proceed with opening the file or folder.

Receiving an invitation from a Dropbox admin to join their team

An admin from a Dropbox team may send you an email invite to join their team. You have the option whether to accept their invitation. 

If you decide to join the Dropbox team: 

  • You’ll get access to additional storage through the team’s total storage pool and enjoy quicker access to shared content that’s already available within the team.
  • Your account will transfer to that team, but you will control what happens to your existing files.
    • You can decide to transfer all of your current files to your new Dropbox team account. 
      • If you choose this option, your admin will have access to those files. 
    • Alternatively, you can decide to keep your files separate, and your admin will not have access to your files. 
      • When you choose this option, you’ll be prompted to create a new Dropbox account for all of the existing files in your account. 
  • You won’t be able to leave the team without the admin’s permission.
  • Your admin can choose to delete your account at any time. 

If you don’t choose to join the team: 

  • You will only be able to collaborate on the specific file or folder that was shared with you.
  • You will continue using your current storage space. 
  • Your Dropbox account will remain independent from the team account. 

Learn more about joining a Dropbox team.  

Will my team’s admin have access to my personal files?

Yes, transferring an existing account to a Dropbox team account will give your admin access to view, open, share, and delete files. 

If you create a secondary, personal Dropbox account, your admin won’t have any access into this account.   

Learn more about what kind of access your team’s admin has to your account.

Why can I not change the email on my Dropbox Sign account?

Looking for instructions on how to change the email address on your account? Click here

If you seem to be unable to change your email address, there are a few possible reasons.

  1. You may have initiated an email address change on your account, but you have not confirmed the change yet. Check the inbox under your new email address for a confirmation link.
  2. You may have a second account under the email address you wish to change your account over to. Log into the free account under the email address your wish to change your account to and delete it by following the instructions in this article.

Still having trouble? Please forward both email addresses to our support team by going here. Indicate which account you want to keep and which email address you’d like the account under for further assistance.

Please note that we are unable to merge accounts at this time.

Why did I get an email about a one-time security code?

To protect your account, Dropbox sends a one-time security code to your email address when you access your account from an unrecognized device or location. This 6-digit code adds an essential layer of protection, ensuring that only you can log in. We’ll also notify you on your linked mobile or desktop device.

If you tried to log in to your Dropbox account and received an email about a one-time security code, use this code to finish logging in.

What should I do if my one-time security code isn’t working?

If your one-time security code isn’t working, the code may be expired. Try to log in to your Dropbox account again to receive a new code. If you still aren’t able to log in to your account, contact Dropbox support.

What if I didn’t try to log in to my account recently?

If you didn’t recently try to log in to your Dropbox account, but you received an email about a one-time security code, someone else may be trying to access your account. Follow the instructions below based on the email you received.

If you received the email above, click I didn’t try to sign in, and follow the prompts to reset your password.

If you received the email above, you don’t need to take any further action.

What to do if you didn’t receive an email with the one-time security code

If you didn’t receive a one-time security code, the email may have been sent to a spam folder or held by a spam filter. 

Add no-reply@dropbox.com to your contacts or trusted senders and click on Resend Code.

If the one-time security code email isn’t in your spam folder, and you still can’t receive the code, contact Dropbox support.

What should I do if I’ve lost access to my email?

If you’ve lost access to the email you used to register with Dropbox, try the following methods before contacting Dropbox support:

Check your Dropbox desktop or mobile app and backup phone number

If you have the Dropbox desktop or mobile app, or a backup phone number, check those for any notifications or codes that may help you regain access to your account.

Use your recovery email

If you previously added and verified a recovery email, you can use it to receive security codes or reset your password. Learn how to add a recovery email.

Use your Dropbox emergency backup code on your Dropbox Desktop or mobile app

If you set an emergency backup code in your security settings, you can use it to access your account. This code is useful if you’ve lost access to your email.

To use your emergency backup code:

  1. Click Having trouble getting a code? on the window that appears when you try to log in.
  2. Click Enter the emergency backup code.
  3. Enter your code.

To prevent a similar issue occurring again, change the email address associated with your Dropbox account to one you have access to.

Learn more about changing the email on your Dropbox account.

What should I do if I can’t access my registered email and I don’t have a verification code?

If you can’t reset your expired password or haven’t received a verification code, you can use the account access recovery questionnaire. To skip the verification code, you need to answer as many questions as possible correctly. This keeps your account safe because only you are likely to know the right answers.

To access the account access recovery questionnaire without a backup code:

  1. Click Having trouble getting a code?
  2. Fill out the self-serve recovery form and click Submit Answers. 

To access the account access recovery questionnaire with an expired password:

  1. Click I can’t recover my account using this page.
  2. Under “Have you lost access to your email?” click Yes.
  3. Under “Do you have a computer or mobile device linked to Dropbox?” click No. 
  4. Fill out the self-serve recovery form and click Submit Answers.

If you still aren’t able to log in to your account, contact Dropbox support.

Can I log into my Dropbox account without a one-time security code?

Yes, you can log in to your Dropbox account without a one-time security code. You will need to either use one of your emergency backup codes or answer the access recovery questionnaire, as explained above. 

These options are available when you select Having trouble getting a code? on the window that appears when you try to log in to Dropbox.

Why does Dropbox Sign keep logging me into the wrong Gmail account?

This is most likely because you’re using a Dropbox Sign for Gmail add-on. Our system automatically creates a new account for every Gmail address you log into using Chrome or Firefox because you installed the Gmail extension on your browser, not on the specific email account.

Where it gets tricky is that you’ll need to use Google Login to log into both accounts. Which means that you’ll only be able to log into the Dropbox Sign account that corresponds to the email you’re logged into Gmail with.  

Since that can be sort of confusing, we recommend resetting your password on one account so that you use your email/password to access one and Google Login to access the other.  

You can also reset both passwords so you’re always sure what account you’re logging into.

You could delete one of the accounts, but you will just create it again when you log into that Gmail account using Chrome. So if you use multiple Gmail accounts on Chrome, taking one of our recommendations above is your best bet.

Why does it say my email address is already in use

If you’re seeing a message that says you already have an account, there can be a few possible explanations. To resolve the issue, find the section below that’s most relevant for you and follow the instructions.

Alternatively, learn what to do if you no longer have access to the email address associated with your Dropbox account.

I’m trying to create a new account

If you’re seeing this message when trying to create a new account, it means you’ve already created a Dropbox account with that email address. In this case, you can simply log in to that account.

In the desktop app, select I already have a Dropbox account. On dropbox.com, choose Login.

If you don’t remember the password, you can reset it. Or, learn how to troubleshoot issues with logging into your Dropbox account.

I’m trying to update the email address for my existing account

If you’re seeing this message when trying to update the email address on your account, it means you have another Dropbox account that’s currently using this email address. To make this address available again:

  1. Log out of your first account.
  2. Log in to the second account (if you don’t remember the password, you can reset it).
  3. Change the second account’s email address to another one that you own.
  4. Go back to the first account and update it with the desired email address.

Alternatively, if you’re sure you don’t need the second account, you can delete it to free up the email address.

I don’t think I created an account with that email address

If you don’t think you created an account with that email address, please first log in to the account to be sure. It’s common for Dropbox users to have multiple accounts, and to have forgotten they created one with a specific email address.

You can reset the password if you need to.

If you log in, but the account information, files, or folders don’t look familiar, it’s possible that someone mistakenly created a Dropbox account with your email address. People can make a typo and enter the wrong address.

If you’re sure this has happened, please contact us.

Why has my Dropbox account been disabled?

Our mission is to design a more enlightened way of working, which requires creating an environment people can trust. To do this, we seek to ensure the protection of individual safety and legal rights.

What behavior is considered unacceptable on Dropbox?

Our Terms of Service and Acceptable Use Policy describe the types of behavior that are unacceptable on Dropbox. We won’t tolerate content or activity that puts our users at risk.

We have a highly-trained team dedicated to enforcing our policies and will take swift action when a user has violated them.  

We’ll disable accounts and terminate service for abusive behavior, or for creating, storing, or sharing illegal or egregious content, particularly when it risks or depicts harm to others.

What type of behavior will result in a disabled Dropbox account?

Some of the common types of abhorrent content or behavior which violate Dropbox policies and can lead to an account being disabled include: 

  • Malware, phishing, or spam.
  • Child sexual exploitation and abuse material, including illegal child sexual abuse material or any content which sexually exploits minors (in accordance with US law, when Dropbox becomes aware of apparent child sexual abuse material on our Services, we’ll make a report to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children).
  • Extreme acts of violence or terrorism activity, including the promotion of such activity.
  • Malicious activity that interferes with or disrupts any user, host, or network.

When an account is disabled, all access to the account and content on Dropbox is terminated.

How to request a review of an account disable

Our team takes care in enforcing our policies. If you think we made a mistake in disabling your account, you can ask us to review your account by filling out this form.

A note about team accounts

Admins can disable team accounts and delete members from their teams.

If you’re on a team and your account was disabled, please first contact your admin.

Why is my DocSend sharing activity restricted?

To help protect customers and prevent abuse, DocSend may limit sharing activity on paid accounts if elevated spam complaint activity is detected. When sharing is restricted, you won’t be able to create or share new links, or invite people to groups, and visitors will lose access to previously shared content. Your account will need to be reviewed to determine whether access can be restored.

What happens when sharing is restricted

If your account reaches the spam complaint threshold, you may see an error message when trying to share content or invite collaborators.

Restricted users may be unable to:

  • Create new links for content or Spaces.
  • Copy or share existing links.
  • Send group invites.
  • Previously shared content will be restricted for visitors.

You may see messages similar to the following:

  • “Link creation failed. Please read more about our acceptable use policy and contact us at support@docsend.com if you have any questions.”
  • “Operation failed. Please read more about our acceptable use policy and contact us at support@docsend.com if you have any questions.”

Why sharing restrictions happen

Sharing restrictions may be applied after repeated spam complaints or reports of abusive activity associated with your account. This helps protect recipients and maintain trust and safety across Dropbox and DocSend services.

How to restore sharing access

If your account has been restricted and you believe this was done in error, contact support for review.

  1. Contact support at support@docsend.com.
  2. Include details about your account and the activity that triggered the restriction.
  3. Wait for the review process to complete.

Restrictions aren’t automatically removed after a waiting period. Accounts must be reviewed manually to determine whether sharing access can be restored. Learn about DocSend’s Terms of Service. 

Account Settings

Access your Dropbox DocSend Support PIN

Overview

Security is top of mind at DocSend, and we want to make sure that extends to all parts of our business. When discussing account-specific information during a phone call with our Support team, you may be asked to provide a unique PIN that’s generated under your account as a means of verifying your access to the account. 

Access your Support PIN

Your unique PIN will refresh every 60 seconds. To locate your PIN, you’ll need to be logged into your DocSend account. 

  1. Click on your avatar icon. 
  2. Click Settings. 
  3. Under the Personal Settings tab, click on the Support section.
  4. From there, provide the 6-digit code to the chat or phone representative.

Accessibility support

Dropbox is committed to providing a user experience available to everyone. That means valuing and including the experience of people with varying functional abilities, using a range of assistive technologies, and in different circumstances.

Our aim is to craft delightful products that help everyone unleash their full potential. We partner with a third-party accessibility testing service to ensure we deliver on this commitment, measuring against a set of standards set by the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG).

VPAT

You can download the VPAT (Voluntary Product Accessibility Template) for any of the core Dropbox products as a PDF.

  • VPAT Dropbox Web
  • VPAT Dropbox Desktop Mac
  • VPAT Dropbox Desktop Windows
  • VPAT Dropbox iOS
  • VPAT Dropbox Android

If you have any questions or concerns around the accessibility of the Dropbox product, please contact us at dropboxforall@dropbox.com.

Age requirements for using Dropbox

To comply with legal regulations, Dropbox users must meet different minimum age requirements.

The age requirements to use Dropbox vary by location.

  • If you’re in the United States: You must be 13 or older.
  • If you’re outside the United States: You must be 16 or older.

Once you reach the required age in your location, you can create a new Dropbox account. Learn how to create and set up a Dropbox account.

What happens if I don’t meet the age requirement?

If you’re under the minimum age required to use Dropbox, your account may be scheduled for deletion. You’ll be notified 48 hours in advance, and you’ll be prompted to download all your content before it’s permanently deleted. During the grace period you’ll be able to download your content from dropbox.com or the Dropbox desktop app.

Learn how to download your files from dropbox.com.

Learn how to save your files to your device on the Dropbox desktop app.

If you can’t download your data before the deletion date, contact Dropbox support at dropbox.com/get_help.

After 48 hours, you’ll be logged out of all Dropbox apps and you won’t be able to log in again. Your account will be deleted in accordance with our retention policy.

Why your access to the Dropbox mobile app may be disabled

Dropbox uses age and parental-approval information provided by the Apple App Store and Google Play Store. This information helps us follow our Terms of Service and comply with laws designed to protect minors.

Your access to the Dropbox mobile app may be disabled for the following reasons:

  • You’re under the minimum age required to use Dropbox: If you’re under 13 years old in the United States, or under the applicable age limit in your region, you’ll lose access to the Dropbox mobile app. You’ll be notified that your account will be deleted and you’ll have a limited amount of time to download your content from dropbox.com or from the Dropbox desktop app before permanent deletion.
  • You’re between 13–17 years old and need parental approval: If you’re between ages 13–17, you may need approval from a parent or guardian to continue using the Dropbox mobile app. If you don’t have parental approval, your access to the Dropbox mobile app will be disabled temporarily. You’ll be notified that parental approval is required, and once it’s granted, your access will be restored.
  • Your parental approval request was denied: If your parent or guardian denies approval, your access to the Dropbox mobile app will be disabled.

What happens if I’m a Family plan manager?

If you’re a Dropbox Family plan manager that doesn’t meet the age requirement:

  1. The plan will be disabled after 48 hours.
  2. Everyone of age on the account will be downgraded to a free Dropbox Basic account.
  3. After 48 hours, you’ll be logged out of all Dropbox apps. You won’t be able to log in again.
  4. Your account will be deleted in accordance with our retention policy.

What if I already paid for a subscription?

If you’ve paid for your subscription through Dropbox:

  • The remainder of your subscription term will be refunded to your original form of payment. 

If you purchased your subscription from the Apple App Store:

  • You’ll need to cancel your Apple subscription to avoid being billed. 
  • You can also request a refund directly from Apple.

What if my access was accidentally disabled

You may have been assigned to the wrong age category, for example if you entered your date of birth incorrectly, or if a parent was signed in on a child’s device:

  1. Contact Dropbox support within 30 days to have your account reactivated. 
  2. Our support team will ask you to provide proof of your date of birth. 
  3. After your information is verified, you’ll be notified through email when your account has been reactivated.

Allow masked data downloads in Dropbox Sign

Teams on Dropbox Sign Premium can mask sensitive data received from senders. Learn how to mask document data.

By default, only admins can download masked document data. However, as a Dropbox Sign admin, you can grant this permission to others in the admin console.

How to allow senders to download masked document data

To allow senders to download masked document data as a CSV:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the top-right corner.
  3. Click Admin console.
  4. Click Settings in the left sidebar.
  5. Click Documents and templates in the left sidebar.
  6. Toggle Allow sender to download document CSV to On or Off.
  7. Click Save settings in the bottom right.

If you don’t wish to allow senders to download masked document data as a CVS, there are other ways senders can view masked data.

Can a Dropbox Fax number have two functions?

No. If you’re thinking about porting a number that currently has a different function, such as forwarding calls, it will lose that function once you port the number to Dropbox Fax. Your number can only be used as an inbound fax number, nothing else.

Can I merge Dropbox accounts?

Currently, there’s no way to automatically combine individual Dropbox accounts. 

The easiest way to combine individual accounts is to move all files and folders from the older account to the main one you want to use. 

Can I merge multiple Dropbox team accounts?

Unfortunately, you cannot merge individual Dropbox team accounts. However, you can easily move files between accounts.

If you’re a Dropbox team admin, you can merge two Dropbox team accounts.

How to transfer all files and folders to another account

Learn how to move files between two accounts.

Can I port my Google Voice number to Dropbox Fax?

Yes, you can port your Google Voice number.  However, once you port the number you will no longer be able to use it as anything else other than an inbound fax number.

Your Google Voice number is automatically locked to prevent it from being ported out without your consent. Before you can port your Google Voice number to another service provider you must first unlock it. There is a fee that comes with unlocking your number.

To unlock your number:

  1. Go to www.google.com/voice/unlock and log into your Google Voice account.
  2. If you only have one Google Voice number, click Unlock my number underneath your Google Voice number. If you have more than one number, then select the number you wish to port from the dropdown menu and then click Unlock my number.
  3. Click Continue to confirm that you wish to unlock your number.
  4. Log into Google Wallet to complete your port out process.

Once you’re finished, your Google Voice number is ready to be ported out.

Change the language and date format of your account

You can change the language and date format of your Dropbox account. By default, Dropbox is in the language of the device used to access your Dropbox account.  

How to change file date format on dropbox.com

You can change how dates are shown on dropbox.com from your account settings. For example, you might prefer day/month/year rather than month/day/year.

To change the date format:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the General tab.
  5. Under Preferences, select the date format from the Date format dropdown menu.

Dates on dropbox.com will appear in the format you chose.

Change the name of a Dropbox team account

If you’re an admin of a Dropbox Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise account, you can change the name of your team. Your new team name will display to all team members.

How to change the name of a Dropbox team account

To change the name of a Dropbox team account: 

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Under Account and Team profile, click your team’s name next to Team name.
  5. Click Change.
  6. Enter your new team name. You can set different names for:
    • Display name: Shown as your team name on dropbox.com and any connected devices your team members have. Limited to 20 characters.
    • Billing name: Appears on billing statements and should be your organization’s full name.
  7. Click Change name.

When you update your team’s Display name, it changes the name of your team on dropbox.com and on any connected devices your team members have. Files and folders won’t resync when the Display name changes.

Configure a Contact Card in Dropbox DocSend

Overview

DocSend gives you the option to display a Contact Card within the Docsend document viewer so that your visitors can reach out and connect! 

Configure your Contact Card

To enable the DocSend Contact Card, go to your Contact Card settings and click Show Contact Card. You can choose to display your picture, tagline, email, phone number, and LinkedIn profile. To disable any of these options and the card itself, simply uncheck the box!

Update Contact Card Information

The contact options are mapped to the information configured in your Personal Account Settings. You can update any of the fields on your contact card from this page.

Viewer Experience

Your visitor can access your Contact Card from the document viewer by clicking the image icon.

Custom branding in Dropbox DocSend

DocSend’s custom branding options enable you to customize your links and document viewer to add a personal touch and professional polish to your shared DocSend content. You can enable customizations within Company Settings if you are an admin or account owner.

Custom branding options

You can update any or all of the following settings at any time to personalize your visitors’ DocSend experience.

Customizations include: 

  • Subdomain: Add a subdomain name to the front of all links, including Live Present links.
  • Site URL: Add your website URL, the logo in the document viewer will take visitors to the specified website.
  • Logo: Add your company logo to the document viewer to replace the default DocSend logo.
  • Brand color: Change the accent color in the document viewer. 

Logo recommendations

You can update the logo at any time from the Company Branding Settings page. Here are some best practices for logo uploads: 

  • Uploaded in PNG file format
  • At least 60px tall and no wider than 320px
  • Have a transparent or dark background color
  • Unlocked image dimensions in image preferences

The Dropbox copyright policy

Important note on copyrighted material

You should only use shared folders, public links, and photo galleries for files that you have the legal right to share with others (for example, documents, photos, software, music, and videos that you personally created). You don’t have the right to share files unless you own the copyright in them or have been given permission by the copyright owner to share them. Purchasing or legally acquiring video, music, ebooks, or software doesn’t give you the right to share that material with third parties over the Internet.

If you have any doubts about whether you have the legal right to share certain files, you shouldn’t share them. By using the shared folder, public folder, or photo galleries features you represent that files placed in those folders don’t violate the Dropbox Terms of Service and that you own all copyrights to them or have been given permission by the copyright owner to share them. Dropbox has adopted a policy of terminating the accounts of users who repeatedly infringe copyright or whose accounts are subject to multiple infringement allegations. If you repeatedly share files that infringe others’ copyrights, your account will be terminated.

For more information on the Dropbox copyright policy and the steps to take to report a claim of copyright infringement, please visit the Dropbox DMCA page or submit a claim here.

Dropbox Fax multiple email delivery

Do you want to share an inbound fax number, and have more than one person receive faxes and notifications simultaneously?

You first need to create a Team, and invite all members to your Dropbox Fax team. Each member will need to accept the invitation to confirm their membership.

How do I add members to my Dropbox Fax team?

Please be sure each member accepts the invitation they receive in their inbox.

Once part of your Dropbox Fax team, you can assign inbound fax number(s) to their email addresses. Everyone who has a fax number assigned to them will get an email notification when a fax is received at that fax number. They can also see all of their transmissions in their Faxes tab.

How can more than one email address receive faxes at the same time?

Dropbox Fax notification settings

How do I manage fax notification emails?

You can control which e-mails you receive from Dropbox Fax by clicking on your email in the top right of the page, then selecting Settings. Select Profile and scroll all the way down until you see Notifications.

Here, select which emails you wish to receive. To make sure you receive confirmation emails when you send out an outbound fax, please make sure the checkbox next to When I send a fax is enabled.

You can also decide whether or not your notifications will include a .pdf copy of your fax, or if you’d prefer not to receive your faxes as an attachment.

Dropbox Paper notification settings

By default, Dropbox Paper will send emails notifying you of weekly activity, comments, @mentions, to-dos, and changes to docs you follow. 

To change these settings:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your profile picture or grey circle in the upper-right corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the Notifications tab.
  5. Under Paper, uncheck the box next to any emails you don’t want to receive.
  6. Your changes will automatically save.

You will still receive an email notification if:

  • Someone shares a doc with you
  • Someone replies to a comment you left on a doc
  • You’re @mentioned
  • You leave a notification unread for 2 hours. To change this, click the bell icon in Dropbox Paper and then Mark all as read.

Dropbox Services Partners

Dropbox maintains a global network of partners to provide valuable professional services to our customers. By using these partnerships, you can make the most of our products to meet your business’s unique needs. From executing simple deployment projects to architecting, implementing, and maintaining complex integrations, our certified partners are ready to help.

Dropbox Sign branding for sub-teams

Within the admin console, each organization admin or manager has the ability to set the branding for the whole company. This includes logo, tagline and company name. 

If Multi-Teams has been set up, each team, or individual users, can be given the ability to edit their own branding. This can be enabled within the admin console by the organization admin or manager. 

To enable team admins and managers to set their own team’s branding, the organization admin or manager will need to navigate to their admin console.

To do so:

  1. Click Settings in the left sidebar. 
  2. Select General to open branding settings. 
  3. Click Company name.
  4. In the far right, use the dropdown menu to select who will own the ability to edit this item. 
    • Selecting Team admin/manager will set this for their individual team.
    • Selecting Each User will allow all individual users on the account regardless of team to edit this field in their business settings. 
  5. (Optional) Repeat step 3 for all following options. 
  6. Click Save settings at the bottom of the page after editing has been complete. 

Once enabled, the team admins and managers will be able to edit branding items within the admin console.

Dropbox Sign reports in the admin console

Admins can view recent activity and generate status or compliance reports for all users and documents on their team or account. 

Reports available to admins

User Activity report (available on Standard and Premium)

This report includes the following information by user:

Document Status report (available on Premium)

This report includes the following information by document:

Compliance report (available on Standard and Premium)

A compliance report consists of three reports that are delivered in separate emails to the admin. The admin can download each one in a separate CSV. The tables below include descriptions of each report with information by user.

Report 1: Account & API Key Details
Report 2: API Call Activity
Report 3: Log In Activity

How to view recent activity

Admins on Premium can view charts of recent activity, by request status and send activity.    To view recent activity: 

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Click Admin console.
  4. Click Reporting in the left sidebar. 

The first chart reflects the status of signature requests for the entire account or team for the current month.

The second chart shows the number of requests sent per day by the entire account or team. 

How to generate a report

You can generate detailed activity and status reports for a custom date range.

To generate a report: 

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Click Admin console.
  4. Click Reporting in the left sidebar. 
  5. Scroll to Run a report.
  6. Enter the date range for your report. 
    • Note: The end date can’t be more than a year later than the start date.

 

  1. Check the box next to the correct report.
  2. Click Request Report.

The report will be processed and a link to a CSV file will be sent to your email address. 

Limitations

Number of entries per report

Reports can take up to 30 minutes to generate, depending on the timeframe selected and number of results included in the report.  

Please note that the maximum number of entries per report is approximately 250,000. If a report generates close to the maximum number of entries, you may receive the error, “There was a problem preparing your report.“  

If this happens, generate the report again with a smaller date range to include fewer entries. If you still can’t download your report, please submit a request to our support team for further investigation.

Retrieving past data
