Email notification settings in Dropbox DocSend

Overview

Get notified about your link activity by setting up email notifications. Simply enable the types of visit notifications you’d like to receive to see visitor engagement in real time. Email notification preferences are configured individually for each user within an account.

Configure Email Notifications

  1. Log in to docsend.com. 
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the upper-right corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Notifications.
  5. Check or uncheck desired notifications.
  6. Click Save changes. 

Types of Email Notifications

As Visits Occur

This email notification triggers immediately once a visitor accesses any of your created links.  This will enable you to reach out to your visitor as the visit occurs. The email notification will consist of the following visit information: 

  • Visitor Identity: Device used, geolocation.
  • Content Viewed: How much of the document the visitor viewed (%)
  • Time Spent: Quick snapshot of the time spent on the document. Please note, the visit may still be ongoing so please review the document details in the Content section for more accurate visit information.

When Disabled Links are Opened

This email notification triggers whenever a visitor accesses a disabled link you created.  This is a great way to gauge interest on disabled content. Visitors attempting to access your disabled link will not be able to see the content and will not have any visitor information captured. The email notification includes the following visit details:

  • Anonymous visitor
  • Document name and link
  • Ability re-enable link (see Reenable it here)

As Invites are Accepted

You’ll receive an email anytime your invite is accepted. This notification can help you:

  • Manage your Billing settings
  • Manage your team members through the User Settings page

As Signatures Occur (Standard, Advanced)

You’ll receive an email notification anytime a visitor signs one of your signable documents. The notification includes the following information:

  • Name of the Signer
  • Email Address of the Signer
  • Document name
  • Option to download a copy of signed document

When a Viewer Attempts to Access with an Unauthorized Email (Advanced)

You’ll receive this email notification whenever an unauthorized visitor tries to access your link with Allowed Viewers enabled. By receiving this notification, you can take action either by disabling the link or granting access to unauthorized visitors you trust. For more information on how to enable this feature, visit our help center article, Allowed Viewers. 

The following information will be included in the email notification: 

  • Document link and name.
  • Option to allow an unauthorized visitor to access the document.

As diligence tracker task updates occur

You’ll receive an email notification whenever a task in the diligence tracker is updated, such as, when it’s assigned, completed, or modified, to stay up to date on task progress without checking the tracker manually.

The notification may include:

  • Task name and description
  • Status updates (e.g., assigned, completed, updated)
  • Associated due date
  • Link to view the task in the diligence tracker

Diligence tracker tasks due soon summaries

A daily or weekly summary of tasks that are approaching their due date to prioritize upcoming work and ensure tasks are completed on time.

The summary may include:

  • List of tasks due soon
  • Due dates
  • Assigned users
  • Links to view and complete tasks

Diligence tracker overdue task summaries

You’ll receive an email summary of tasks that are past their due date to identify and follow up on overdue work.

The summary may include:

  • List of overdue tasks
  • Original due dates
  • Links to review or update tasks

Digest Emails

Daily Digest

This email notification is a daily summary of all visit activity that occurred across your created links. This can help you stay up to date without having to receive multiple email notifications as visits occur. The digest will include:

  • Number of visits: The number of cumulative visits received a day
  • Average % completion: Cumulative average of how much of the document(s) visitor(s) viewed (%)
  • Visit Recap
    • Visitor: Contact accessing the document
    • Content: Name of the document
    • Completion: How much of the document the visitor viewed (%)
    • Duration: Time spent viewing the document

Weekly Team Update Digest

This is a weekly summary of all the visit activity that occurred under the Team Folder. For minimal email notifications, this is an ideal option. The digest will include the following:

  • Busiest day: highlights the day(s) out of the week you received the most visits.
  • Visit Recap: Included only for members users. This is an outline of visits to your own created links. 
    • Date: The day the visitor visited the document
    • Visitor: Contact accessing the document
    • Content: Name of the document
    • Completion: How much of the document the visitor viewed (%)
    • Duration: Time spent viewing the document
  • News from your team
    • Content updates: Existing content that was updated over the past week
    • Most used content: Content with the most links created
    • Most visited content: Content that received the most visits

Enable desktop visit notifications in Dropbox DocSend

Overview

You can stay up-to-date on who is accessing your content by enabling desktop notifications. Once enabled, you will know exactly when your content is being viewed and be able to see how your visitors are interacting with your content in real-time.

Check out the links below for more information about setting up notifications on commonly used browsers. 

  • Chrome: Turn notifications on or off
  • Safari: Customize website notifications in Safari on Mac
  • Mozilla: Web Push notifications in Firefox

How can I set a default language for my Dropbox team account?

If you’re the admin of a Dropbox team account, you can change Dropbox’s default language for your team. Changes to your team’s default language will be reflected throughout Dropbox.

  • Invites to new team members will be in your selected default language.
  • New team members’ accounts will be set up in the default language.
  • The team activity report will be in the team’s default language.

Individual team members, including the admin, can always change their language preferences without affecting the team’s default language settings.  

Change your team’s language settings:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com using your admin credentials.
  2. Click on Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Team Profile under Account.
  5. Click  Change next to Default language.
  6. Select a default language from the pop-up window.

How do I change my Dropbox username or account photo?

Dropbox account photos and usernames can personalize your Dropbox account, and are visible to your friends and coworkers — this feature can help others recognize you around Dropbox. For example, profile pictures are displayed in the Dropbox badge when you collaborate on a file with another person.

You also see your account photo at the top of the page on dropbox.com.

How to change your name on dropbox.com

To change your name on dropbox.com:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the General tab.
  5. Click Edit next to your name.
  6. Type the name you’d like to use.
  7. Click Change name.

What file can I use for my profile picture?

Your profile picture must be at least 256px by 256px. You can use any of these file types:

  • .bmp
  • .gif
  • .jpeg
  • .jpg
  • .png
  • .tif
  • .tiff

How long does Dropbox keep my deleted files and information?

Dropbox saves deleted and previous versions of files for a specific period of time so you can recover them if desired. After that time, the deleted files are marked for permanent deletion in our system and are removed from our storage servers. Once they’ve been deleted, they can no longer be recovered or restored.  

Your default file recovery period depends on your Dropbox plan:

  • Dropbox Basic, Plus, and Family customers have 30 days.
  • Dropbox Professional, Standard, Essentials, and Dropbox team users have 180 days.
  • Dropbox Advanced, Enterprise, Education, and Dropbox team Plus users have 365 days.

However, there are several add-ons that extend your file recovery period. Learn more about extended version history.

Permanently deleting files

When you mark files for permanent deletion, you initiate the process for permanently deleting your files from our servers. This process can take several days.

You can’t recover files once they’ve been marked for permanent deletion. However, if we detect suspicious activity on your account, we may temporarily delay the permanent deletion process to protect you from malicious file deletion.

Learn how to permanently delete files.  

If you’re a member of a Dropbox team account, your team admin may have limited your ability to permanently delete files.

Deleting your Dropbox account

If you delete your Dropbox Basic, Plus, Family, Professional, or Essentials account, we’ll initiate deletion of the files you store on your account.   

See the Retention section of our Privacy Policy for more details.  

If you’re a member of a Dropbox team account, only your admin can disable your account and delete your files.

How long to port a fax number to Dropbox Fax

On average, it takes two weeks to port an existing fax number to Dropbox Fax. The time it takes to complete the port request can vary depending on how quickly all parties, including your current carrier, are able to review and approve your request.

How to access the Dropbox account of someone who has passed away

If someone close to you has passed away, we’re sorry for your loss.   

To access the files of someone who has passed away, first look in the Dropbox folder on the person’s computer if you can. Many Dropbox users have all of the files from their account available in this folder, which syncs to their account online. 

If you aren’t able to access their Dropbox folder on their computer, you’ll need to request access from Dropbox directly. 

Dropbox respects the security and privacy of our customers above all else. For this reason, requesting access to the account of someone who has passed away can take some time. Please also note that we can’t guarantee that we’ll be able to provide access. Thank you in advance for your patience and understanding.  

To request access to the account of someone who has passed away, you’ll need to provide documentation that:

  • The person is in fact deceased
  • You have a legal right to access the person’s files under all applicable laws

To do that, please create a support ticket and include the following information in your message:

  • The full name of the deceased person
  • The email address associated with that person’s Dropbox account
  • Your name, mailing address, email address, and your relationship to the deceased person
  • A photocopy of your government-issued ID
  • A valid court order establishing that it was the deceased person’s intent that you have access to the files in their account after the person passed away, and that Dropbox is compelled by law to provide the deceased person’s files to you

We’ll review the information you provide and let you know whether we can move forward with your request.

We wish you the best during this difficult time.

How to add a second email to your Dropbox account

Your email is the username for your Dropbox account. You can add a secondary email to make it easier to manage content. With a secondary email, any files or folders shared with either your primary or secondary email will go directly to the same Dropbox account.

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox helps you effortlessly share files and folders.

How to add a secondary email

To add a secondary email to your Dropbox account:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. In the General tab, scroll down to Secondary emails.
  5. Click Add secondary email.
  6. Enter the secondary email you’d like to add.
  7. Click Add.
  8. Click Done.
  9. Check the inbox of your secondary email for a verification email.
  10. Open the email and click Verify your email. You’ll be redirected to your Dropbox account, where you’ll see a confirmation message.
  11. Click Done.

You’ll have both a primary and secondary email(s) on your account. Your primary email is the main email connected with your account.

How to change your primary email

On dropbox.com you can make one of your secondary emails your primary email. To do so:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. In the General tab, scroll down to Secondary emails.
  5. Click Edit.
  6. Click Make primary next to the email you’d like to make primary.

How to remove a secondary email

To remove a secondary email from your Dropbox account:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. In the General tab, scroll down to Secondary emails.
  5. Click Edit.
  6. Click Delete next to the email you’d like to remove.
  7. Click Delete again to confirm.
  8. Click Done.

How to disable secondary emails for your team

By default, the secondary emails setting is off for your Dropbox team account. If you previously enabled the secondary emails setting and want to turn it off:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Under Products, click Dropbox.
  4. Click Settings.
  5. Select the Content tab.
  6. Under Receiving content, scroll to Secondary emails.
  7. Toggle the switch to Off.

When you turn off secondary emails, any secondary emails your team members previously added are removed.

If you’re experiencing issues with secondary emails and you still need help, please contact Dropbox Support.

How to add branding with Dropbox Sign

With branding, you can include your company’s logo and other details on signature requests. 

Branding is available on Standard and Premium plans.

Individual users can set up branding in their account settings.

  1. Log in to your account.
  2. Hover over your email address in the upper-right corner.
  3. Select My Settings from the dropdown menu.
  4. Click the Standard Features tab and scroll to Branding.
  5. Click Upload to add a logo.
  6. Enter an Email tagline to display a short message under your logo.
  7. Enter a name in From field to customize who the email is addressed from.
  8. Enter an Email signature to customize the closing of the email message.
  9. Enter a custom URL if you’d like to send signers to a specific web page after they’ve finished signing.

How to set admin controls for branding

Team admins and managers can set branding for their entire team, and choose whether to allow individual users to change their settings.

To change team-wide settings:

  1. Log in to your admin account.
  2. Hover over your email address in the upper-right corner.
  3. Select My Settings from the dropdown menu.
  4. Click the Team tab and scroll to Team settings.
  5. Click Upload to add a logo.
  6. Enter an Email tagline to display a short message under your logo.
  7. Enter a name in From field to customize who the email is addressed from.
  8. Enter an Email signature to customize the closing of the email message.
  9. Enter a custom URL if you’d like to send signers to a specific web page after they’ve finished signing.

You can prevent team members from customizing individual settings. To do so, click the Lock default for team checkbox next to any of the branding settings.

How to add more fax lines to your account in Dropbox Fax

To add more fax lines to your account: 

  1. Log in to your Dropbox Fax account.
  2. Click Team.
  3. Click Add a fax line.
  4. Select your country, state/province, and area code.
  5. Click Register fax number.

You’ll be charged a prorated amount for the additional fax line, based on where you are in your current billing cycle. Confirm the purchase and the additional fax line will be available to use immediately.

One inbound fax line is included in the cost of your Dropbox Fax subscription. Additional fax numbers are available at $4.99 per month, or $55 for the year.

How to add team members to Dropbox Fax

To invite teams members:

  1. Sign in to sign.dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click the Team tab  on the left side of the screen.
  3. Enter in the email addresses of the people you’d like to invite in the field under your team’s name (one at at time). A window will pop up confirming the email address you invited to the team.

The person you invited will receive an email from Dropbox Fax and two links: one to accept and one to reject the invite. Clicking the accept link will automatically add them as the team’s newest member.

To assign a team member to your inbound fax line:

  1. Sign in to sign.dropbox.com with your admin credentials. 
  2. Click the Team tab on the left.
  3. Click the drop down box underneath the fax number you want to add that member to. (It should only have the admin email in the box to start.)
  4. Tick the box next to the email address of all teams members who should receive faxes sent to that number. Once that’s done, all future incoming faxes will be sent to any team member who has that number assigned.

How to change team settings in Dropbox Sign

Admins and team managers on Standard and Premium plans can manage certain settings for their entire team.

  1. Log in to Dropbox Sign.
  2. Hover over your email address in the upper-right corner.
  3. Select Admin Console from the dropdown menu.
  4. Click the Settings tab on the right-side menu.  

On the General page you can:

  • Upload a logo to be shown on emails and on signature requests
  • Change your industry
  • Change your company name
  • Change your company’s tagline

On the Signature requests page you can:

  • Customize the From field to show your business name on emails, instead of Dropbox Sign
  • Add a closing salutation to all emails
  • Change the date format
  • Change the timezone
  • Enable signature reminders
  • Enable Signer Authentication 
  • Enable NOM 151
  • Enable Tamper proofing
  • Add a customer URL Redirect
  • Manage what types of signatures you accept

You can also lock these features so only an admin/ team manager can change them. If they’re unlocked, any member of your team will be able to make changes in their own account settings.

How to change the date and time format in Dropbox Sign

You can change the way the date and time appear in your Dropbox Sign account. To do so:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Profile.
  5. Scroll down to Date & time and update your preferences.
  6. At the bottom of the page, click Save.

How to change the email address on your Dropbox account

The email address linked to your Dropbox account is what you’ll use to log in to Dropbox and receive important Dropbox notifications. If you can no longer access that inbox, you can always log in to Dropbox without access to your email address.

This article explains how to edit the email address on your or a team member’s Dropbox account, update your billing address, and how to use a recovery email. If you don’t know what your Dropbox email address is, learn how to find the email address on your Dropbox account.

How to change your Dropbox email

To change the email address on your Dropbox account:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the upper-right corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Under the General tab, find your email address.
  5. Click Edit next to your email address.
    • If you see Verify email instead of Edit, you’ll need to verify your email address before you can change it.
    • If you see an info icon (i inside a circle) instead of Edit, you’ll need to contact your admin to change your email address.
  6. Enter your new email, confirm email, and Dropbox password.
  7. Click Update email.
    • We’ll send a verification email to your new email address.
  8. Open the email and click Verify your email.

Use a recovery email

You can add a recovery email to help keep your account secure. A recovery email is a backup email address used to help you access and secure your account. For example, you may use it to:

  • Reset your password
  • Receive one-time passcodes (OTPs) when logging in from an unrecognized device

If you lose access to the email address linked to your Dropbox account, a verified recovery email can help you log in again. Your recovery email is separate from the email address linked to your Dropbox account.

Learn how to add a recovery email.

Admins: How to change a team member’s email address

If you’re an admin, you can change the email address on a team member’s Dropbox account. To do so:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Members.
  4. Click the name of the team member.
  5. Next to their current email address, click Change and enter the new email address.

We’ll send an email to their original email address letting them know that an admin on their team changed their Dropbox email address.

How to change the billing email address on your Dropbox account

Changing the email address associated with your Dropbox account won’t change the billing email address. If you pay for a Dropbox subscription and need to change the billing email address, you will need to update your billing information.

How to change your email address on your Dropbox Sign account

Change the email address on your Dropbox Sign account

To change the email address you use to log in to Dropbox Sign:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the upper-right corner..
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Profile.
  5. Click Change email address.
  6. Enter your new email address.
  7. Scroll down to the bottom of the page and click Save.

Confirm your new email address

After you save your changes:

  1. Open the confirmation email sent to your new email address.
  2. Click Activate Address.
  3. When you’re redirected to the Dropbox Sign log in page, log in with your old email address and password to confirm the change.

If your new email address is already in use

If you see an error that states the email address you’d like to use already exists, then you’ll need to:

  1. Log in to the account of the email address you’d like to remove, then delete that account.

 

  1. Log back in to the account that you’d like to keep, then update to the new email address by following the instructions above.
  2. Check the inbox for your updated email address for a confirmation email.
  3. Click Activate address in the confirmation email.
  4. Enter your old email address and password to confirm the change.

How to change your email notification settings

You can opt in or out of email newsletter, tips, and account notifications in your email notification settings. Learn how to turn off and manage notifications.

How to change your email notification settings

To change your email notification settings:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click the avatar at the top of any page.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Notifications.
  5. Check or uncheck the boxes next to the email notifications you’d like to change.

How to unsubscribe from email notifications

You can unsubscribe from email notifications by unchecking the box next to the notification you’d no longer like to receive.

You can also click Unsubscribe at the bottom of an email you receive from Dropbox to unsubscribe from that type of notification.

How to change your preferred language in Dropbox Sign

You can update the default language in your Dropbox Sign account settings, so you can work in your preferred language.

To change your preferred language:

  1. Log in to your account.
  2. Hover over your email address in the upper-right corner.
  3. Select My Settings from the dropdown menu. 
  4. Click Profile near the top of the screen.
  5. Scroll to Language.
  6. Select the correct language from the dropdown.

How to complete the Dropbox Fax porting LOA

If you received the Dropbox Fax Letter of Authorization to fill out in order to port your number, and have questions about what information goes where, please use this guide to help.

Company (or Individual) Name: This is the name (company or individual) that your account is under with your current carrier.

Address: Please enter the service address that is referenced on your bill.

Current Service Providers: This is your current carrier who you pay for your number now.

Current Account Number: This is the account number associated with the fax number.

Type of Traffic: Fax

Telephone Number Begin: Please list your 10-digit fax number here. If you’re porting more than one number, hit enter to fill in the space beneath.

Provide BTN (billing telephone number): This is your contact phone number associated with your account.

Port Date Requested: You can enter today’s date or ASAP. If there is a deadline, please specify in your email to support.

Print your name, add your signature, and click “I agree” and the LOA will automatically be sent to support and a copy will be sent to your email.

Learn more about how the porting process works.

How to request live chat support

How to contact Dropbox support

Support hours and response times

  • Email support:

    • If you’re on Dropbox Plus, Family*, Professional, or Essentials, live chat is available during your local business hours (9:00am–5:00pm, Monday–Friday).
  • Social media support:
    • Support on Facebook, Instagram, and X, is available from Monday to Friday, 3:00am–7:00pm CST. You’ll receive a response within one hour during these hours. Learn more about social media support.

*Family manager only

†Admins only

‡To access email and live chat support, users will first use the Dropbox AI assistant. This experience is currently available only to Dropbox Plus and Professional customers, with additional plans to follow.

If you need to contact support outside of these times, you can use the help center and community forums 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

How to keep signed documents separate in Dropbox Sign

Customers on a Standard or Premium plan can opt to download a ZIP file of separate PDF documents, rather than one multi-page document. 

To change whether signed documents are merged: 

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Select Settings from the dropdown menu. 
  4. Click the Standard Features tab and scroll to the Preferences section.
  5. Click the Enable checkbox next to Do not merge signed documents.
  6. Click Save to save your changes.

When you download completed documents, they will download as a ZIP file with separate PDFs.

How to manage Dropbox accessibility settings on Mac

Accessibility is an Apple setting that allows applications on your Mac to interact with other applications. For example, it allows the Dropbox badge to work in non-Dropbox applications. 

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox makes managing file permissions easy.

Why does Dropbox want to turn on accessibility?

Accessibility is used for some Dropbox features like:

  • The Dropbox badge
  • Seeing who’s viewed your files 
  • Better prioritization for file syncing

How to turn on accessibility

To turn on accessibility from the dialog box:

  1. Click Turn on Accessibility.
  2. Go the Privacy tab, if you’re not there already. 
  3. Click the lock icon to unlock your system preferences.
    • You’ll be asked to enter your computer username and password (not your Dropbox username and password).
  4. Check the box beside the Dropbox icon to enable accessibility.
  5. Click the lock icon again to re-lock system preferences.

How to turn off Dropbox accessibility prompts

If you don’t want to keep being asked about accessibility, check the box next to Don’t show this to me again, then click Not Now.

How to edit accessibility settings

If you want to edit accessibility settings after you’ve already installed Dropbox, follow the instructions for your operating system in this article.

After you edit your settings, you may also be prompted to:

  • Enable accessibility for the Dropbox badge, if you haven’t already
  • Restart the Dropbox desktop application

How to manage Dropbox account settings

This article explains how to manage account-wide settings on dropbox.com. Account settings don’t include device-specific preferences for the Dropbox desktop app.

Learn how to manage desktop app preferences.

Your Dropbox account settings are managed online and apply to every browser and device you use with Dropbox. Your options may vary depending on your plan, but include:

  • Profile and preferences
  • Plans and billing
  • Passwords, devices, and security
  • Notifications, connected apps, and plan-specific features

How to access your account settings

To access your Dropbox account settings:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
    • Note: To access different types of settings, click the tabs along the top of the page. Learn more about the different tabs and settings below.

If you’re on Dropbox Basic, Plus, or Professional, select Manage account to view subscription and billing information.

General

Basics Add or update your profile picture, name, and email address. If you’re on Dropbox Essentials, Standard, Business, Advanced, Business Plus, or Enterprise, you may also have options to add a secondary email and link your work and personal accounts.

Info about where you work If you’re on Dropbox Standard, Essentials, Business, Advanced, Business Plus, or Enterprise, you can add your job title and the name and size of your organization.

Preferences Set your language, date, and time preferences, and choose whether to get access to our newest features with Dropbox early access. You can also clear manually added contacts, enable the default access to folder uploads, enable the Dropbox system extension, and use online-only files and folders.

Delete account Learn how to delete your Dropbox account. Deleting your Dropbox account deletes all of your data from dropbox.com and unlinks your devices from Dropbox. Deleting your Dropbox account can’t be undone.

Plan

If you’re on Dropbox Basic, Plus, Family, or Professional, select Manage account under your avatar to view subscription and billing information.

If you’re on Dropbox Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise, you’ll use this tab to see your current plan and available upgrade options. You can also check your available storage space.

Billing

If you’re on a Dropbox Plus, Professional, or Essentials plan, or are the manager of a Family plan, you can manage your payment method and billing frequency, as well as view invoices and receipts. Certain types of admins can access billing information from their admin console.

Family

If you’re a member of a Dropbox Family plan, you can view a list of all the members on your plan. Family plan managers can also invite and remove plan members.

Security

Security checkup Use the security checkup tool to review your email address, connected apps and devices, and password. If you’ve two-factor authentication enabled (see below), you can also check the authenticator apps, phone numbers, or security keys associated with your account.

Password Change your password regularly to keep your account secure. If you forget your password, you can also reset it from the forgot password page or by clicking Forgot your password? when you log in to dropbox.com.

Recovery codes View the recovery codes that can be used to access your account in case you lose access to your email or two-factor authentication device.

Two-factor authentication Set up and manage two-factor authentication to add an extra layer of security to your account. Two-factor authentication requires you to enter a security key or code, in addition to your password, when you log in to your Dropbox account. After you’ve followed the steps to enable two-factor authentication, you’ll have options to change your authentication methods, add a physical security key, and revoke trusted status from linked devices.

Web browsers See which browsers are currently logged in to your Dropbox account from where, and when they were last active. You can log out of recent sessions by clicking “X”next to the time of activity.

Devices See what devices are linked to your Dropbox account, their location, and when they were last active. Click “X” next to a device to unlink it from your account if you’re no longer using it. When you unlink a device, you’ll be logged out of your Dropbox account on that device, and files and folders on the device won’t sync with changes made on dropbox.com or other linked devices.

Paper mobile devices Unlink all devices that are logged in to the Dropbox Paper app. Paper docs and folders are stored online, so unlinking devices won’t affect how they’re updated. You’ll need to log back in to the Paper app when you’re ready to use it.

Mobile contacts If you’ve allowed the Dropbox mobile app for iOS or Android to access your contacts, you can remove them from the suggested contacts in your account. 

Notifications

Choose what email notifications you’d like to receive from Dropbox. You can opt in or out of notifications about file and account activity, as well as news and updates from Dropbox.

Apps

Manage the third-party apps that you’ve connected to your Dropbox account, as well as apps you’ve allowed to access and edit content stored in your Dropbox account. If you’re a member of a Dropbox team, your admin may manage some apps for your entire team.

Default editing apps Choose how you’d like to open certain types of files from your Dropbox account, like Microsoft Office files and Paper docs.

Branding

If you’re a Dropbox Professional or Essentials customer, or a member of a Dropbox team, you can use branded sharing to display your logo and brand name when sharing files and folders with clients.

Privacy

Manage your cookie preferences and Do Not Sell or Share settings, submit a data access request, or a data deletion request.

Refer a friend

If you’re on Dropbox Basic, Plus, Family, or Professional, you can earn up to 32 GB for referrals. You get 1 GB for every friend who installs the Dropbox desktop app, and your friend will get 500 MB. Learn more about how to earn free space.

Sharing

You can set the defaults for how you share your files and folders. Learn how to manage your default sharing settings.

How to manage Dropbox mobile app settings

This article discusses how to manage account-wide settings on the Dropbox mobile app. 

Learn more about downloading the Dropbox app to your mobile device.

General

From the Dropbox mobile app, you can:

  • Add or update your profile picture.
  • View your available storage space.
  • Manage offline files.
  • Create, save, and sync unique passwords.
  • Connect a computer.
  • Manage camera uploads.
  • Recover deleted files.

To access these features from your Account page:

  1. Launch the Dropbox app.
  2. Tap Account at the bottom of your screen.

How to manage your mobile Dropbox app settings

Offline files

You can make your Dropbox files and folders available offline on your mobile device. This is similar to downloading your files and folders, except it also keeps them in Dropbox, so they’re saved offline on your device as well as online on dropbox.com. 

Learn how to make a file or folder available offline from the Dropbox mobile app.

Use cellular data

When this is toggled on, Dropbox will download offline files using the data plan associated with your mobile device. If the toggle is not on, offline files will only download when you’re connected to Wi-Fi.

Passcode

You can set up a four-digit passcode to secure access to your account on your mobile device. If you’ve the passcode lock activated, you’ll need to enter it each time you launch or return to the Dropbox app. You can change your passcode or turn it off at anytime from your Settings screen.

Learn more about configuring Dropbox mobile app passcodes.

Files

The Dropbox mobile app lets you to create and upload files directly to your Dropbox account from your phone or tablet. Uploaded files sync everywhere you access your files in Dropbox.

Learn how to upload files to Dropbox on a mobile device.

Learn how to delete files in your Dropbox account from your mobile device.

Support

You can view our Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, submit a support request, rate the Dropbox mobile app, and more from this tab.

Clear history

Tapping Clear search history will clear the search data from your Dropbox mobile app. 

Clear cache

Tapping Clear cache will clear the files stored locally on your mobile device. This may improve speed and functionality when using the Dropbox mobile app.

Managing your files on the Dropbox iOS app on File Provider

Dropbox iOS on File Provider is our latest update that utilizes Apple’s updated File Provider API to more deeply integrate with mobile devices running iOS. 

The Dropbox iOS app will be automatically updated onto this latest version when you update your iOS. If you would like to go back to using the classic integration (still on File Provider), you can do so following the steps below. 

Actions

Tapping Convert all to classic integration will revert the app back to the classic File Provider integration on iOS.

To do this:

  1. Launch the Dropbox app.
  2. Tap Account on the bottom of your screen.
  3. Tap ✗ (settings) to open the Settings menu.
  4. Tap Native Files.app integration under Files.
  5. Tap Convert all to classic integration.
  6. Tap Convert.

Clear cache

Tapping Clear cache will clear the files from Files.app on your mobile device. This may improve speed and functionality when using the Dropbox iOS app. 

Sharing

To share files or folders in your Dropbox account on your mobile device:

  1. Launch the Dropbox app.
  2. Tap Files at the bottom of your screen.
  3. Tap “⋮” (vertical ellipsis on Android) or “…” (ellipsis on iPhone or iPad) next to the file or folder you want to share.
  4. Tap Share.

Learn more about how to save or share files with other apps.

How to manage email notifications in Dropbox Sign

You can control the emails Dropbox Sign sends you. To do this:

On sign.dropbox.com

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Profile.
  5. Scroll down to Notifications. Check the boxes next to the notifications you’d like to receive.
  6. Click Save at the bottom of the page.

Android

  1. Open your device’s Settings.
  2. Tap Notifications.
  3. Tap App Settings.
  4. Tap the toggle next to Dropbox Sign to turn notifications on or off.

iOS

  1. Open your device’s Settings.
  2. Tap Notifications.
  3. Tap Dropbox Sign.
  4. Tap the toggle next to Allow Notifications to turn notifications on or off.

How to manage template link notifications in Dropbox Sign

When someone shares a template link with you, you’ll receive an email containing a copy of the signed document each time someone signs using that template link. If you no longer want to receive these emails, you can turn off this feature.

Turn off notifications for your template links

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Select Templates in the left sidebar.
  3. Click My Templates in the dropdown.
  4. Click the title of the template link you want to update.
  5. Click “v” (arrow icon) next to Ways to sign in the right sidebar.
  6. Uncheck Receive signed copies.

Turn off notifications for team template links (admins)

Admins can also turn off notifications for team template links they didn’t create.

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Settings in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Profile.
  4. Scroll to Notifications.
  5. Uncheck When someone signs my team’s document through a template link.
  6. Click Save.

Turn on notifications for specific template links (admins)

If you’ve turned off notifications but still want updates for certain template links:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Select Templates in the left sidebar.
  3. Click My Templates in the dropdown.
  4. Click ☑ (vertical ellipsis) next to the template link.
  5. Click View info.
  6. Click Ways to sign in the right sidebar.
  7. Check Receive signed copies.
  8. Click Save.

How to manage your Dropbox desktop app preferences

The Dropbox desktop app is available for Windows, macOS, and Linux operating systems. The preferences menu allows you to customize the Dropbox app to your liking.

Depending on your operating system (Windows, macOS, or Linux), you may see some or all of the options below in the preferences menu. On Linux, you can change some of these settings using commands.

If the Dropbox icon isn’t showing in your taskbar or menu bar, relaunch the app or download 0 (or re-download) the Dropbox desktop app and log in to your Dropbox account when prompted. The Dropbox icon may have “disappeared” because the desktop app was inactive on your computer.

The General tab

Start Dropbox on system startup

This setting opens the Dropbox desktop app automatically whenever you start your computer. Your Dropbox desktop app must be open to sync changes between the Dropbox files on your computer and everywhere else you access your files in Dropbox.

Language

To specify a different language from the default operating system settings, select it from this menu.

Dropbox badge

Choose if Dropbox badge appears each time you open a Microsoft Office file, to see it only when others are viewing a file, or to never see the badge.

About Dropbox

This is the current version of your Dropbox installation. Reference this number in support cases or to see if you have the latest version of Dropbox.

The Account tab

In the account tab, you can log in and out of your Dropbox accounts, view which plan you’re on, and view your storage space. If you have two linked accounts, you can log in and out of them in this tab. If you log into both your linked accounts, you can easily switch between them in the desktop app.

The Backups tab

This PC/This Mac

You can set up a backup or manage your backups.

External drive backups

Choose if you want to see notifications about setting up backups when you plug in new external drives.

Photos

Choose if you want to enable camera uploads to automatically upload photos and videos from your phone, camera, SD card, or other devices whenever you connect to your computer. 

Devices

Devices configured for importing photos will show up here.

Screenshots

Whenever you take a screenshot, Dropbox will automatically save it to your Dropbox and copy a link to your clipboard so you can share it instantly.

The Bandwidth or Network tab

Bandwidth

This setting lets you manage how much bandwidth your internet uses to run the Dropbox desktop app.

Proxies

This setting lets you connect the Dropbox desktop app to a proxy server, if there’s one available.

Enable LAN Sync

This setting lets you enable LAN sync in your Dropbox desktop app preferences. If your computer is connected to a LAN, enabling this setting in the Dropbox desktop app will override your bandwidth settings and may speed up syncing for files stored on your LAN.

The Notifications tab

Notify me about

You can set your notification preferences to choose what notifications to receive.

Snooze notifications

You can temporarily snooze notifications for a specific period of time.

The Sync tab

Storage of new files

Using the online-only feature on the Dropbox desktop app helps you save hard drive space on your computer. Using the available offline option takes up hard drive space but doesn’t require wifi to open files. Learn more about online-only files and folders.

Select folders to sync

Selective sync is a feature in the Dropbox desktop app that allows you remove specific Dropbox folders from your hard drive so you can save space on your computer. Learn more about the selective sync feature.

Dropbox folder location

On Windows and Linux computers, this setting lets you move the Dropbox folder to a different location on your computer.

On Mac computers with the updated Dropbox for macOS experience, you can no longer move the Dropbox folder. Learn more about the expected changes with the Dropbox for macOS update.

How to manage your Dropbox Replay settings

You can change your Dropbox Replay settings to manage your Replay email notifications and file activity.

How to change your Dropbox Replay email notification settings

How to change keyboard shortcuts

How to merge Dropbox Sign accounts

For security reasons, we’re unable to merge two different Dropbox Sign accounts under two different e-mail addresses, even if they both belong to you.

Similarly, we can’t assign the same email address to two different accounts.

However, you can delete the account you don’t want, then change the e-mail address on the account you want to keep on the “Settings” page. To do so:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Profile.
  5. Click ChangeEmailAddress.
  6. Add the new email address for the account.
  7. Scroll down to the bottom of the page and click Save.

Keep in mind that you can’t have two accounts with the same email address, so you may need to delete an existing account before using the address for your second account.

How to opt in to Dropbox early releases

Dropbox offers customers the ability to opt in to early releases to get feedback on new products or features before general availability.

To opt in to early releases:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Under Preferences in the General tab, toggle on Early releases.

To opt out of early releases:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Under Preferences in the General tab, toggle off Early releases.

How to opt out of the beta experience for Dropbox for macOS

To opt out of the beta experience for Dropbox for macOS and revert your Dropbox account to its previous configuration:

  1. Click ☑ (Dropbox) in the menu bar.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Preferences.
  4. Under the General tab, click Leave beta experience.
  5. Click Leave beta.

Your Dropbox folder will be accessible under Favorites in the Finder window. If you’re on a paid Dropbox plan, your files will start out as online-only. You can make files available offline by right clicking the file and selecting Make available offline. Any files that were not synced prior to leaving the beta experience will be stored in your ~/Library/CloudStorage folder for future access.

How to access files that were not synced

To access your ~/Library/CloudStorage folder:

  1. Open Finder.
  2. From the menu bar (at the top of the screen), click Go.
  3. Hold the option key and click Library.
  4. Open the CloudStorage folder.

Any files not synced prior to leaving the beta experience will be automatically stored in an archive folder (EX: Dropbox (4-25-22 3:00 PM) Archive).

How to opt out of the beta experience for macOS as an External Drive Backup or Computer Backup user

If you are using Dropbox Backup or External Drive Backup, you must opt out of all early releases to leave the beta experience for Dropbox for macOS.

To opt out of early releases:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Under Preferences in the General tab, toggle off Early releases.
  5. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  6. Click Sign out.
  7. Close the Dropbox desktop app.
    • Click ☑ (Dropbox) in the menu bar.
    • Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
    • Click Quit.
  8. Open the Applications folder in Finder.
  9. Click the Dropbox icon and drag to the trashcan in your dock.
  10. Download and install the latest version of Dropbox.

Once Dropbox has been installed, you can log back into your account. At this point, the local files from your previous Dropbox sessions will be archived and stored in your ~/Library/CloudStorage folder for future access.

How to port a fax number to Dropbox Fax

If you want to port your fax number over to Dropbox Fax, you need to check if it’s eligible.

To do so:

If your number is eligible, you’ll receive an email telling you what to do next. Follow the prompts to proceed with porting your fax number to Dropbox Fax.

How to remove the number at the bottom of a signed document in Dropbox Sign

By default, a document ID number appears on the bottom of your signed documents. Customers on Standard and Premium plans can choose to hide the document ID.

How to hide the document ID

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Select Settings from the dropdown menu. 
  4. Click the Team tab and scroll to Team settings.
  5. Click the checkbox next to Hide document ID.
  6. Click Save to save your changes.

How to set admin controls to hide the document ID

Team admins and managers can hide document IDs for their entire team. Additionally, org admins can choose whether to allow individual users to change their settings.

To change team-wide settings:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Click Admin console.
  4. Click Settings in the left sidebar.

How to save a signature in Dropbox Sign

If you don’t want to type your signature or use a mouse to draw it, you can upload a photo of your signature.

 

To upload your signature:

  1. Log in to your Dropbox Sign account.
  2. Hover over your email address in the upper-right corner.
  3. Select Edit signature.
  4. Click the camera icon on the left-hand side.
  5. Click Add photo.
  6. Locate the image file on your computer and click Open.
  7. Adjust the image as needed.
  8. Click Select to save your signature.

How to separate the audit trail in Dropbox Sign

The audit trail is an important part of how Dropbox Sign identifies that your signer is who they say they are, and it’s part of what makes Dropbox Sign legal. For this reason, it can’t be turned off altogether.

However, if you’re on a Dropbox Sign team plan, you can configure your account so that the audit trail is not attached to the signed document, and is returned to you as a separate file instead. 

To separate the audit trail:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Select Settings from the dropdown menu.
  4. Click the Standard Features tab and scroll to the Preferences section.
  5. Click the Enable checkbox next to Do not merge signed documents.
  6. Click Save to save your changes.

When a document is returned to you and you download it from the documents page, the document itself and the audit trail will download as two separate PDFs.

How to separate the audit trail with the API

If you’re using the Dropbox Sign API, you can download the document with the Get Files endpoint. You can specify the parameter file_type=zip and the documents are returned as a collection in a ZIP file.

How to set a custom URL for documents in Dropbox Sign

A custom URL lets you redirect your signers to a web page of your choice after they’ve signed a document or template.

To set a custom URL:

  1. Log in to your Dropbox Sign account.
  2. Hover over your email address in the upper-right corner.
  3. Select My Settings from the dropdown menu. 
  4. For admins, click the Team tab. For individuals, click the Standard Features tab. 
  5. Scroll to Take signers to this page after they signed?
  6. Click the checkbox next to Enable.
  7. Enter the URL.
  8. Click Save to save your changes.

Manage timestamps and signature frames

With Dropbox Sign, you can control how signatures appear in your documents by adding advanced signature details and a signature frame.

Advanced signature details add information like the signer’s name, date, and timestamp directly to each signature. The signature frame adds a visible border around each signature to show that the document was digitally signed.

These features help you meet internal standards or compliance requirements and make signatures easier to review.

How to enable advanced signature details

To enable advanced signature details in Dropbox Sign:

  1. Log in to your Dropbox Sign account.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Profile.
  5. Check the Advanced signature details checkbox.
  6. Click Save.

When advanced signature details are enabled:

  • The signer’s name, date, and time are automatically added to each signature block.
  • The timestamp appears below the signature, to the right of the signer’s name.
  • The format is: MM/DD/YYYY hh:mm am/pm TZ (time zone), for example: 03/22/2025 09:13 am PST.

How to enable the signature frame

To enable the signature frame in Dropbox Sign:

  1. Log in to your Dropbox Sign account.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Profile.
  5. Check the Signature frame checkbox.
  6. Click Save.

When the signature frame is enabled:

  • A box appears around each signature in the document.
  • The frame includes the standardized text “Digitally signed by:”.
  • The signature frame is visible immediately after signing and in the final document.

Managing fax numbers and assigning them to team members in Dropbox Fax

To manage and assign out numbers to team members:

  1. Sign in to sign.dropbox.com with your admin credentials. 
  2. Click the Team tab on the left.
  3. When this page loads, you’ll see a column on the right side of the page where you can add or remove fax lines, and assign these out to team members. You can also choose to port your number through this page.  

Searching and managing fax lines

If you have more than five fax lines, you’ll see a search box appear at the top of this column that will allow you to manage numbers easily. To find a specific fax line, simply type in digits within the line you are looking for.

Our search bar will also auto-suggest numbers that include the digits you are typing in the search box. You can also search using a team member’s email address, and this will bring up all the fax numbers assigned to the specific team member.

Once you find the fax line you need to manage, simply click on the drop down menu to display all team members. Select check the box next to the member you want to assign the number to. Uncheck the box if you need to remove the line from them. You can also use the Ctrl+Find function on your browser to get to the team member you need.   

Deleting a number

To remove or completely delete a number, simply click on the “X” next to the fax line.

Looking to add a fax number? Learn how to add more fax lines to your account.

Report abuse on Dropbox

If you find content on Dropbox that violates our Acceptable Use Policy, you can report it using the Report an issue form or by following the steps below.

  2. Select the Help dropbown menu in the top-left corner of the screen.

Usage and compliance reports in Dropbox Sign

Admins and managers on Standard and Premium plans can use reports to get insights on their team’s activity. 

To access reports:

  2. Click Team in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Download a report.

Compliance report

View your Dropbox support ticket history

You can view all of your tickets with Dropbox support in a single place. To view the full list of your support tickets:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Go to dropbox.com/support.
  3. Under Your support tickets, click Your requests in the top right corner.

There are different support ticket statuses: 

  • New: Tickets that are input into the system and not yet assigned to agents. 
  • Open: The request has been assigned to an agent who is working to resolve it. You can reply to the support agent, see when a reply was received, and check when a ticket will close.
  • On-hold: The support team is waiting for a third party before proceeding to work on the ticket.
  • Pending: The agent working on the ticket is waiting for a response from you, the requestor.
  • Solved: Your issue is resolved and there are no further follow-up questions. Tickets will be closed after either a resolution has been reached or there hasn’t been any correspondence from either side for 96 hours. Closed tickets can’t be re-opened, but you can create a follow up ticket if your issue is not resolved.

Reply to a support ticket

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Go to dropbox.com/support.
  3. Scroll to the section titled Your support tickets, and click Your requests in the top right corner.
  4. Click the ticket you’d like to reply to.
  5. Under Add a reply, type your response in the text box.
  6. If desired, click Add or upload files here to add an attachment to your reply.
  7. Click Reply.

What does it mean for a Dropbox product to be in “alpha” or “beta?”

At Dropbox, we are constantly creating and exploring new products. Some of these products are still in development but show a lot of promise, so we want to give you a chance to try them out. We use several different names to refer to these products, including “early access,” “alpha,” “beta,” “preview,” or words or phrases with similar meanings.

These products usually haven’t been subjected to the same reliability, availability, and security testing as other Dropbox products. Also, the features they contain are still changing. If one of these products doesn’t delight users to the extent that we expect it to, we may even stop offering it altogether. Because of this, we ask that you use care when deciding when and if you use one of these products.  

Finally, these products are subject to some additional terms of service. If you have a Dropbox team account, the following terms apply to your use of these products:

  • Beta Services. Use In Customer’s Discretion. Despite anything to the contrary in the Agreement: (a) Customer may choose to use Beta Services in its sole discretion; (b) Beta Services may not be supported and may be changed at any time without notice; (c) Beta Services may not be as reliable or available as the Services; (d) Beta Services have not been subjected to the same Security Measures and auditing to which the Services have been subjected; and (e) DROPBOX WILL HAVE NO LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH BETA SERVICES – USE AT YOUR OWN RISK.

 

  • Feedback. Dropbox offers Beta Services in order to get user feedback. In exchange for using Beta Services, Customer Agrees that Dropbox may contact Customer and its End Users to obtain feedback regarding Beta Services. Customer agrees to: (i) and hereby does, assign to Dropbox all right, title, and interest in any feedback; and (ii) provide Dropbox any reasonable assistance necessary to document and maintain Dropbox’s rights in the feedback. This feedback may include oral or written comments, suggestions, error reports, and analysis. 

 

  • Confidential. Beta Services are confidential until officially launched by Dropbox. Customer will take reasonable measures to keep information regarding the Beta Services confidential, including at least those measures Customer takes to protect its own confidential information of a similar nature. Customer will not disclose information regarding Beta Services to any third parties, and will keep new features and functionality confidential until officially launched by Dropbox. Customer may disclose information regarding Beta Services to the extent required by law or regulation if Customer gives Dropbox reasonable advance written notice, to the extent permitted, so Dropbox can seek to prevent or limit the disclosure.

If you are using an individual Dropbox account, the following additional terms apply to your use of these products:

  • Beta Services. We sometimes release products and features that we’re still testing and evaluating (“Beta Services”). Beta Services are labeled  “alpha,” “beta,” “preview,” “early access,” or “evaluation” (or with words or phrases with similar meanings) and may not be as reliable as Dropbox’s other services. Beta Services are made available so that we can collect user feedback, and by using our Beta Services, you agree that we may contact you to collect such feedback.

 

  • Beta Services are confidential until official launch. If you use any Beta Services, you agree not to disclose any information about those Services to anyone else without our permission.

What is a custom URL in Dropbox Sign

With a custom URL, you can redirect your signers to a web page of your choice after they’ve signed a document or template.

Team admins can choose whether to lock this setting, or allow team members to customize their own settings.

If admins lock the setting, the URL they set will be the redirect URL for all documents sent from anyone on their team.

If admins leave the setting unlocked, each team member can set the redirect URL on any documents they send.

Learn how to set a custom URL.

What is Dropbox Premium Support?

The Dropbox Premium Support Add-On provides enhanced support options and allows admins to create, track, and reply to support tickets directly from the admin console.

Premium Support Add-On features

Dropbox team accounts can choose between two versions of the Premium Support Add-On:

  • Premium Support: Essentials
  • Premium Support: Enhanced

Refer to the table below for a breakdown of the features available in each add on.

*English support is available 24/7. Japanese support is only available from 9:00 am–5:00 pm Japan Standard Time, Mon–Fri.

Support options for champions

Dropbox Champions are expert users who provide valuable feedback, share their experiences, and creatively use our solutions. We reward their efforts with the following additional support benefits. Learn more about Dropbox Champions.

Refer to the table below for a breakdown of features available for each add on.

How to buy or remove the Premium Support Add-On

There are two ways to purchase the Premium Support Add-On:

  • Select teams with more than 10 licenses can use the Billing page.
  • For non-credit card payments, contact your sales executive or the Dropbox sales team.

To buy or remove the add-on from the admin console:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Billing.
    • Note: Only certain types of admins can access the Billing page.
  4. Under Products, scroll to Add-ons, and click Add or Remove next to Premium Support.
  5. Click Confirm.

How to access the Premium Support page

To access premium support in the admin console:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com using your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Premium Support.  

By default, the My Tickets tab displays. Here, you can view your recent tickets and issue trends, review previous tickets, check statuses, and submit new tickets. Click the Team’s Tickets tab to access the tickets created by your team members.

How to create a support ticket

Only admins can create tickets through the Premium Support page. Team members don’t have access to that page, but can email Dropbox Support for 24/7 assistance. They’ll receive the same fast response times included in the Premium Support plan.

To create a new support ticket:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com using your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Premium Support.
    • Note: The support hours and response times for the Premium Support Add-On are different for Dropbox and Dropbox Dash.
  4. Click Contact Support.
    • Note: If you’re subscribed to both Dropbox and Dropbox Dash, be prepared to specify which product your question concerns.
  5. Choose the type of support you’d like to receive:
    • Submit a request: Follow the prompts to complete the form and click Submit. You’ll receive a reply by email.
    • Chat: You’ll be connected to a live chat session with a customer support representative.
    • Request callback:  This is recommended for urgent issues. You’ll be redirected to request a callback in the admin console:
      • Enter a phone number that can be dialed directly.
      • Confirm support language.
      • Click Request a call. You should receive a call when the next customer support representative is available. This is recommended for any urgent issues.

How to view or reply to active support tickets

To view or reply to an active support ticket you created:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com using your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Premium Support.
  4. Click the My Tickets tab.
  5. Open the ticket you want to view. 
  6. Type a reply and click Send.

How to view or reply to another team member’s support ticket

Only team admins can view and reply to active support tickets submitted by other team members.

To view or reply to a support ticket:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com using your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Premium Support. 
  4. Click the Team’s Tickets tab.
  5. Select the ticket you want to view from the recent list.
  6. Type a reply and click Send.

Your reply is listed as a Collaborator comment and the original submitter is notified.

How to access tailored support resources

You can view a curated selection of articles from our help center, as well as videos and courses from Dropbox Learn, based on your previous support tickets.

To access these resources:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com using your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Premium Support.
  4. Click the Recommendations tab.

These resources are updated with every support ticket you submit. If you haven’t submitted any tickets yet, you’ll see our most popular help center articles and Dropbox Learn resources.

How to access the Insights page

The Insights page displays trends and patterns in your open support tickets, including total open support tickets, top issues, and top products by issue.

  • Top issues shows the most common problems you encounter, helping you identify recurring themes.
  • Top products by issue shows the number of tickets submitted for each Dropbox product you use.

To view insights: 

  1. Log in to dropbox.com using your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Premium Support.
  4. Click Insights.

What is Dropbox Sign premium branding?

With premium branding (formerly “white labeling”), you can customize the logo, color scheme, and legal text of the signer page to match your company’s branding. Learn how to personalize your signer page using premium branding.

Premium branding is available to Dropbox Sign API users on a Premium plan. If you’d like to test premium branding, you can do so on a Free API plan in “test_mode”.

What signature types are available in Dropbox Sign?

Dropbox Sign supports three types of signatures. You can choose which types you’ll accept on your signature requests:

  • Signature drawn with a touchpad or mouse
  • Typed signature
  • Uploaded image of signature

When a recipient signs your document, they only see the signature options you selected on your Settings page.

How to choose signature types

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over your email address in the upper-right corner.
  3. Select My Settings from the dropdown menu.
  4. Click the Team tab and scroll to Preferences.
  5. Under Accepted signature types, click the boxes for the types you prefer. You can choose any or all types of signatures.
  6. Click Save.

Where can I find my Dropbox Fax number?

Once you’re logged into Dropbox Fax, you will see your fax number on the left side of your page.

If you don’t see a fax number there, it means you’re on a free plan. If you’re looking to have an inbound fax line, you’ll want to upgrade to a paid plan by visiting our pricing page. Please keep in mind that buying and maintaining an inbound fax line for you is a monthly cost to us, so inbound fax lines are only available with paid subscriptions.

Why am I not receiving email notifications from Dropbox Sign?

If you’re not receiving email notifications from Dropbox Sign, here are some possible reasons and solutions.

Possibility 1:

First, check to see if your email notifications are turned on.

To do this, go to Settings, and then Notifications. 

Make sure that all checkboxes are ticked for the notifications you want to receive, and click Save Preferences.

Possibility 2:

Second, if you’re not receiving the notification that the signature request has been completed, you might want to check what email address you sent it with.  

If you have more than one account with Dropbox Sign, you may have sent your signature request from your second account, which means the notification email would be sent to the email address on your other account.

You can go to your Documents page to make sure you sent the signature request from the account in question.

Possibility 3:

Finally, all e-mails will come from noreply@mail.hellosign.com. It’s possible your e-mail is bouncing e-mails from this address or sending them to spam.

Try adding noreply@mail.hellosign.com to your e-mail contacts so our e-mails won’t be directed to spam or bounced out.

If none of these suggestions applies or resolves your issue, please contact our support team here.

Why Dropbox Fax assigns a number when porting

When you sign up for a paid plan it automatically comes with a temporary number for you to use. If you want to port your number, please fill out our Porting Request. Once we get the information we need from you, we’ll begin transferring your number(s).

The porting process can take up to two weeks, but there’s no interruption to your service during that time. After your numbers have transferred, you can keep the temporary number or get rid of it, the choice is yours!

Why smartphone signatures fail in Dropbox Sign

The most common reason this happens is because your email client auto-corrected the “To” field in your email to our support email address.

Please try again and be sure that you entered sign@hellosign.com (not support@hellosign.com) in the “To” field and that you’ve properly typed the unique subject code shown to you on the “Edit signature” screen in your Dropbox Sign account.

If your mobile signature still doesn’t appear, please click the Contact button at the bottom of the Dropbox Sign page, or the Help button if you’re logged in to your Dropbox Sign account, and send us a message about what happened step by step.

If an error occurred, please include the error code if one is listed. Don’t forget to select A Technical Issue under Reason for Ticket, and enter the email address you use to log in to your Dropbox Sign account, and our Support Team will investigate.

Accounts Billing

Can I get a refund on a Dropbox or Dropbox Dash subscription?

In most cases, payments for Dropbox and Dropbox Dash subscriptions and team member licenses aren’t refundable.

If you have an issue with your account, or think there has been an error in billing, please check your support options for more help. However, if you purchased your Dropbox subscription through your device’s storefront, please reach out to the storefront for any refund requests for account issues or billing errors.

Learn how to request a refund from Apple.

Learn how to request a refund from Google.

How to request a direct debit refund

If you paid for your Dropbox subscription with a direct debit payment, please contact your bank for a refund, as only your bank can process a chargeback request.  

What happens when I submit a chargeback request?

Any chargeback requested from your bank will change your Dropbox subscription to a Dropbox Basic (free) plan.

If you have a Dropbox team subscription, a chargeback request will cause your team to be placed in a locked state, which allows the team to continue access to the team files, but removes most team syncing and sharing features. The team admin will need to choose to disband the team or re-subscribe.

Live in the EU, UK, or Turkey?

If you live in the EU, UK, or Turkey, you’re eligible for a refund if you cancel your Dropbox Plus, Family, Professional, or Essentials subscription within 14 days of purchase. To request a refund, contact support for assistance.
