How to verify your Dropbox email address

You need to verify the email address associated with your Dropbox account so you can always keep access to your files.

If you don’t verify your email address, Dropbox won’t be able to help you if you ever need to regain access to your Dropbox account. It only takes two minutes to verify your email address following the instructions below.

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox helps you effortlessly share files and folders.

How to check if you’ve already verified your email address

If you’ve ever clicked on a link in an email we’ve sent you, you’ve already verified your email address and don’t need to do anything else. If your email address hasn’t been verified yet, we’ll send you a link via email the first time you take an action that requires verification.

How to verify your email address

To verify your email address:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Send a verification email to the email address associated with your account.
  3. Look for the verification email from no-reply@dropbox.com in your inbox and click the link in that email.

A confirmation message will appear in your web browser.

Didn’t get the verification email?

If you don’t see the email in your inbox, try the following:

  1. Check your spam or junk folder. Sometimes email providers may mistakenly flag automated emails.

  2. Add Dropbox to your contacts. Add no-reply@dropbox.com to your email address book or contacts list to help ensure future messages are delivered.

  3. Check with your email provider or IT administrator. It’s possible that your email service is filtering out Dropbox messages before they reach your inbox.

Still not receiving the verification email?

If none of the steps above work, try one of the following:

  • Use a different email address. You can change the email on your Dropbox account to another one you already use, or create a new email address and use it instead. 

    Learn how to change your email address.

 

  • Contact Dropbox support. If you’re still unable to verify your email and can’t change it, contact our support team. We may be able to manually verify your email if we can confirm your identity through a questionnaire or email exchange.

What is Dropbox Advanced?

Dropbox Advanced gives teams 15 TB of total storage space, shared among the entire team (5 TB per actively-used license with a 3 license minimum), along with advanced admin, audit, security, and integration capabilities.

Learn more about each Dropbox plan and its features.

What features are available to teams on Dropbox Advanced?

The Advanced plan helps teams stay organized, focused, and work together more effectively. It has all of the features available to teams on Dropbox Standard, in addition to:

  • Storage per license:Starting at 15 TB of total storage space, shared across the team (5 TB per actively-used license with a 3 license minimum).*
    • Notes: 
      • An actively-used license is when a unique person regularly logs in and uses Dropbox.
      • Inactive licenses aren’t removed automatically. Certain types of admins can add or remove licenses from the admin console.
  • Large file delivery:Send files with Dropbox Transfer, with a transfer size limit of 100 GB.
  • Team controls: Manage team invitations, approve which devices team members use for work files, and access team member work accounts with sign in as a user.
  • App integrations: Use single sign-on (SSO) integrations and API calls for data migrations.
  • Admin management:Delegate team administration with access to tiered admins.
  • Security alerts and ransomware detection: Get notified of suspected threats and take action to protect your data immediately.
  • Real-time support: Contact support by phone, chat, or email.
  • Advanced key management:Encrypt your data with unique team keys and a multi-layered key encryption approach.
  • End-to-end encryption:Help prevent third parties from accessing your transferred data.

*Some legacy Dropbox Advanced plan customers can still request additional storage space, depending on their purchase date. Requests are approved as appropriate while allowing Dropbox to manage storage responsibly.

Billing

Billing page overview in Dropbox DocSend

Overview

Account Owners have sole access to the Billing page for reviewing and updating any billing settings. As the Owner, the Billing page is where you can review your transaction history, access past invoices, and make general updates to your subscription.

Billing Page Layout

On the Billing page, you’ll see two main sections: Plan Information and Payment History. 

Plan Information

The Plan Information section is a high-level overview of your subscription, which outlines the price, number of active seats, and renewal date among other fields listed below: 

  • Accountcredit: If applicable, the amount of credit currently applied to your account
  • Seats: The number of active users (including suspended users) and price per user on your account. 
  • Billing cycle: The billing term you’re subscribed to (E.g., monthly, annual)
  • Next bill date: The date of your next renewal charge. Your bill date is the day you subscribed to DocSend; any proration (if applicable) will be based on this date.
  • Card on file: The last 4 digits and expiration date of your default payment method
  • Billing Contact Email: Additional email address configured to receive Invoices. 
  • Invoice billing info: The option to add or update billing information (E.g., address, tax ID, etc.) on future invoices. 

Payment History

In this section, you can review historical transactions on your account. 

  • Description: Contains the transaction date, plan type and any applicable add-ons. 
    • Transaction Date: Date the transaction took place.
    • Status: The result of the transaction
      • Paid: The transaction was successful.
      • Failed: The transaction was not successful.
      • Credited: The transaction resulted in account credit.
  • Quantity: The number of user seats with the exception of the Advanced plan where Qty 1 = 3 user seats and any additional user seat after the 3rd is labeled as an add-on: Additional user - Advanced Annual/Monthly.  
  • Unit Price: The cost of 1 user seat with the exception of the Advanced plan (listed under quantity). 
  • Amount: The Unit Price x Quantity. 
    • Total: Total amount paid on the transaction date; totals may differ from the amount column if any credits or discounts were applied. A positive total is the amount paid, a negative total is a credit to your DocSend account.

Dropbox DocSend referral program overview

Overview

Our referral program is a great way for you to show your appreciation for DocSend to others in your network while receiving a $15 credit for each new user you invite. This article will show you the many ways you can invite someone and how they can set up their own user account.

Refer in-app

  1. Select Earn Credit on your settings tab to access the invite page.
  2. You can invite new referrals through Gmail, Email, Social media, or through your referral link. Selecting the Gmail or email option will allow you to share your invite through DocSend. 

Once your referral accepts and creates a new user account, they must follow the requirements under Referral Requirements to complete the process.

Referral Requirements

Once you submit your referrals, your referrals must follow specific instructions and must meet the conditions listed below in order to receive the referral credit. Once these conditions have been met, both parties’ will receive the $15 credit automatically. 

  • Referrals must sign up using your custom referral link in order to receive credit. The referral link can be accessed on your invite page.
  • Your referrals must:
    •  (1) Upload their first document 
    •  (2) Create a DocSend link
    •  (3) Receive a visit

Referral Status

You can click on check out the status of your referrals button on the referral page to see the status of your referrals and what step they are on out of the 3 listed below:  

  1. Signed up
  2. Confirmed their account
  3. Activated their account

You can also send reminder emails by clicking the Remind button to the referred user to help them finish setting up to receive the credit.

Things to Consider

  • If a referral is duplicated in a way that exploits the DocSend referral program, the referral credit will automatically be deducted from the account.
    • Continued attempts to exploit the DocSend referral program may lead to account deactivation.
  • Non-USD users will receive a 1 month equivalent of DocSend personal. Please reach out to our support team for assistance.
  • Referrals must sign up using the referral link to receive credit. If you believe there is an error, please contact our support team.

Dropbox Fax overage charges explained

What is the overage charge for paid subscribers?

If you’ve used up your monthly allotment of fax pages and you’re subscribed under a paid plan, you’ll be charged 5 cents for each additional page you send or receive. These overage pages are charged on a monthly basis (when they occur).

If you see a note in your account stating you’ve exceeded your pages and you would like to upgrade to a larger plan instead of paying for overage pages, you can do so by going to our Pricing page.

Fix a declined or failed Dropbox DocSend payment

Overview

When a payment fails, our system will automatically retry the charge three more times. If all attempts fail, your subscription will be canceled and switched to our limited trial. For more information, see What is the Limited Trial?

Failed Payments

Reach out to our support team to learn more about a failed payment on your account.

You can also visit Stripe’s Decline Code article for more information on common decline codes that result in a payment failure.

Resolve a Failed Payment

Failed payments are typically resolved by contacting your bank for more insight or updating your card information.

Once you’ve updated your card or resolved the issue with your bank, reach out to our support team so we can retry the payment manually. Otherwise, the payment will retry automatically on a scheduled date.

How to access and manage Dropbox DocSend invoices

Overview

If you’re an Account Owner, you can review past transactions and access all past invoices associated with your account on the Billing page.

Important: Invoices are not automated at this time.

Add a Billing Address to your Invoice

  1. Go to the Billing page.
  2. Click Add Billing info under Invoice billing info. 
  3. Input your company’s billing address along with your company’s tax ID if necessary.
  4. Click Add.

Add a Billing Contact

Adding a billing contact will send invoices to the owner email address and the billing contact email address. Only the account owner can modify the billing contact. 

  1. Go to the Billing page.
  2. Click Add billing contact
  3. Fill in the text box with an email address
  4. Click Add

Modify the Billing Contact

To remove the billing contact or update the contact to a different email address, click into the Billing contact email textbox and remove the current email address and click refresh. From there, click on Add billing contact or leave without a billing contact in place. 

Obtain a Copy of your Invoice

You can receive your invoice by going to your billing page and clicking email invoice. Please note, invoices are not automatically sent when processed. 

  1. Go to the Billing page.
  2. Scroll down to the Payment History section and locate the desired transaction.
  3. Under the transaction status, click Email Invoice.
  4. You’ll receive an email with a copy of your invoice.

Things to Consider

  • If you’d like to change the email address that your invoices are sent to, you can go to your personal settings and update your account email address. 
  • Check your spam folder if you’re having trouble locating your invoice.
  • The Billing Contact will not have access to the billing page. 
  • The Billing Contact is only available for paid subscriptions.

How to add a VAT ID or GST ID number to your Dropbox account

Depending on your location, you may need to pay value-added tax (VAT) or goods and services tax (GST) on your monthly or yearly Dropbox Professional, Essentials, Standard, Business, Advanced, or Business Plus subscription. If your business is registered for VAT or GST, you can add your VAT or GST ID number to your Dropbox account at any time.

If you’re a VAT-exempt or GST-exempt business that mistakenly paid VAT or GST, you should be able to reclaim payments from your tax authorities.

If needed, you can download a copy of Dropbox’s W-9 form and use our US Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN). Dropbox International Unlimited Company’s VAT ID number is IE 9852817J.

How do I know what my VAT rate is?

Learn about VAT rates for each country.

Dropbox Professional and Essentials

To add a VAT ID or GST ID to your account:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Manage account.
  4. Click Billing in the left sidebar.
  5. Under Invoice details, click Update.
  6. Under VAT number, enter your VAT ID or GST ID.
  7. Click Save changes.  

Dropbox Standard, Business, Advanced, and Business Plus

To add a VAT ID or GST ID:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click the Billing tab.
  4. Select the Payment history tab.
  5. Click Edit next to the most recent invoice to update your billing address.
  6. Check the box next to I am registered for VAT/GST in my country and I am acquiring Dropbox’s services for business purposes.
  7. Under VAT number,enter your VAT ID or GST ID.
  8. Click Save changes.

How to add your Tax ID in Dropbox DocSend

Overview

Depending on your location, you may need to pay taxes such as VAT on your monthly or annual DocSend subscription. If need be, you can add your VAT or Tax ID (EIN) number to your DocSend account at any time.  

How to add VAT/TAX ID

As the account Owner, you can add your VAT/Tax ID as follows:

  1. Go to your Billing page
  2. Click Add Tax ID
  3. Paste your Tax ID into the Tax ID text box. 

To update, click Update tax id or Delete tax id. 

If you experience any problems adding your Tax ID, please contact our support team.  

Things to consider

  • Learn about VAT rates for each country here. 
  • Your Tax ID will populate on your DocSend invoice under the Bill to section.

How to calculate tax on Dropbox subscriptions

You may have to pay tax on your Dropbox subscription, depending on the billing zip code or country associated with your account.  

If you’re within a jurisdiction where you’re required to pay taxes, you’ll see the tax as a line item on your billing invoices and receipts.

How to calculate tax before you buy

You don’t need to type in payment details to view your estimated tax.

To view your estimated tax:

  1. For Plus, Family, Professional, and Essentials accounts, visit this page. For Standard, Business, Advanced, and Business Plus accounts, visit this page.
  2. Select the plan you want.
  3. Scroll to the bottom, select your country, and enter your zip code.
  4. The price will automatically adjust, and you’ll find a tax estimate under Order summary.

Does Dropbox offer tax exemptions?

Some non profit and educational institutions can receive tax exemptions on Dropbox team subscriptions. If you’re an admin for a Dropbox team account, contact support to see what your options are.  

If your business is registered for VAT or GST, you can add your VAT ID or GST ID number to your Dropbox account at any time.  

Tax on Dropbox by location

Tax rates change frequently. Visit this page to see how much tax you’ll be charged.

How to change credit card in Dropbox Fax

If you’re logged in to your Dropbox Fax account right now, you can visit this page to update the card on file.

You can change your credit card information by logging in and finding and hovering over your email address in the upper-right corner. Click Settings from the drop down menu that appears. Click the Billing tab at the top and then on the green Update button to change your credit card information.

How to change credit card information for your Dropbox Sign account

You can change your credit card information in your account settings.   

To change your credit card information:  

  1. Log in to your account.
  2. Hover over your email address in the upper-right corner.
  3. Click My Settings from the dropdown menu. 
  4. Click the Billing tab near the top of the screen.
  5. Click Update next to Billing information.

How to change the currency on your Dropbox subscription

Your currency is based on the billing address that you first used to purchase a Dropbox subscription.

Dropbox-supported currency types:

  • Australian Dollar (AUD)
  • British Pound (GBP)
  • Canadian Dollar (CAD)
  • Euro (EUR)
  • Japanese Yen (JPY)
  • United States Dollar (USD)

If your billing address has changed, you can take one of the following actions:

  • If your new billing address uses a different currency, you must cancel your current Dropbox subscription and resubscribe with your new address to change your currency.
    • Note: If you downgrade your Dropbox Advanced subscription and later upgrade it again, you’ll lose any unpaid legacy storage add-ons and access to features that are no longer offered. You can review your storage add-ons in the Billing tab of your admin console, where any legacy storage add-ons will display an expiration date.
  • If your new billing address uses the same currency, you can update your billing information in your account settings.

How to change your billing cycle in Dropbox Sign

You can change your billing frequency from monthly to annually, and vice versa, in your account settings.

To change your billing cycle:  

  1. Log in to your account.
  2. Hover over your email address in the upper-right corner.
  3. Select My Settings from the dropdown menu. 
  4. Click the Billing tab near the top of the screen.
  5. Scroll to Billing cycle and click Switch to annual or Switch to monthly.

How to change plans

You can also switch to a different subscription in your account settings.

To change your plan:

  1. Log in to your account.
  2. Hover over your email address in the upper-right corner.
  3. Select My Settings from the dropdown menu. 
  4. Click the Billing tab near the top of the screen.
  5. Scroll to Plan and check Change plan.

You’ll be prompted to choose a different plan from our pricing page.

After choosing a new plan, the change will be confirmed and the card on file will either be charged or refunded the difference of the subscription change.

How to change your organization name on a Dropbox invoice

Legally, Dropbox must display the same billing information on your invoice that you entered at the time of your purchase.

To change your name on a Dropbox invoice:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. In the General tab, click Edit on the right of your name.
  5. Enter your organization name, split over the First name and Last name fields. You must type something in both fields. 
  6. Re-enter your billing information, even if you want to use the same method of payment. 

From now on, your new account name will appear on invoices and when you share files.

To access an invoice, visit your billing page.

How to edit information on a Dropbox invoice

You can update the billing name and billing address on previously issued invoices by following the instructions for your plan below.

Dropbox Plus

If you’re on Dropbox Plus, you cannot edit the information on your invoices. You can, however, update the name that appears on future invoices. The name on the invoice must be the same name that’s associated with your account. Learn how to change your account name.

You can also change the address that appears on future invoices by updating your payment method. Learn how to update your Dropbox billing information.

Dropbox Professional and Essentials

To edit the billing information on past or future invoices for your Dropbox Professional or Essentials account:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Manage account.
  4. Click Billing in the left sidebar.
  5. Edit your invoices:
    • To edit past invoices, click Edit next to the invoice you’d like to change.
    • To edit future invoices, click Update or Add invoice details next to Invoice details.
  6. Click Save changes.

From now on, your new account details will appear on future invoices. To access an invoice, visit your billing page.

Dropbox Standard, Business, Advanced, and Business Plus

Certain types of admins can edit or customize the billing information for past or future invoices. To do so:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar. 
  3. Click Billing.
  4. Click the Payment history tab.
  5. Edit your invoices:
    • To edit past invoices, click Edit next to the invoice you’d like to change.
    • To edit future invoices, click Edit invoice details on the right.

Change your postal or ZIP code or add a VAT ID

To change your postal or ZIP code, edit the payment method for your account or team. You can re-enter the same payment details and simply change the postal or ZIP code before saving. Learn how to update your billing information.

To add a VAT ID, update your invoice details. Changes to your VAT ID apply to future invoices only. Learn how to add a VAT ID.

How to pay for Dropbox with SEPA Direct Debit

Users in certain countries can pay for Dropbox Plus or Professional subscriptions with Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) Direct Debit. 

You can pay with SEPA Direct Debit if the country associated with your billing information is one of the following:

  • Austria
  • Belgium
  • Cyprus
  • France
  • Germany
  • Greece
  • Ireland
  • Italy
  • Luxembourg
  • The Netherlands
  • Portugal
  • Spain

Direct Debit payments take up to five business days to authorize, but you can use your new subscription right away.

How to pay for Dropbox with SEPA Direct Debit

To pay with SEPA Direct Debit:

  1. Visit this page for Plus and Professional users or visit this page for team users.
  2. Select your desired plan type.
  3. Under Enter payment details, select the Direct Debit tab.
  4. Enter your information and click Complete purchase.

How to pay per fax in Dropbox Fax

Once you’ve used all your free pages, our system will prompt you to pay per fax. We understand that not everyone needs a paid subscription, so we let you pay as you go.

It costs $0.99 for a fax of 10 pages or less. Each page after the tenth page costs $0.20. For example, a 10 page fax would cost 99 cents, and an 11 page fax would cost $1.19.

You’ll get a notice to enter your credit card information, and once that’s squared away, you’re free to fax as you please.

How to update tax ID in Dropbox Sign

If you pay taxes on your Dropbox Sign subscription, you can add your tax ID to your Dropbox Sign account at any time. Learn more about the taxes in your location.

To add or edit your tax ID:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Click My Settings.
  4. Click Billing.

To update your Dropbox or Dropbox Dash billing information, including your payment method, billing cycle, or billing name and address, follow the instructions for your account type below.   

Learn how to find out what plan you have.

Dropbox Plus, Professional, Essentials, or Family

Change or update a payment method

To add or remove a payment method, or to change a billing name or address for a Dropbox Plus, Professional, Essentials, or Family account:

  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.

If you’re unable to change your payment method, or there’s no option to do this, check which Dropbox plan you have. The process may be different to the steps described above if you’re not on a Plus, Professional, or Essentials plan.

Change a billing name or address

To change a billing name or address for a Dropbox Plus, Professional, Essentials, or Family account:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.

Switch between monthly and yearly billing cycle

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner. 
  3. Click Manage account.
  4. Select Subscriptions in the left sidebar.

Dropbox Standard, Business, Advanced, Business Plus, and Dropbox Dash

To update billing information for a Dropbox Standard, Business, Advanced, and Business Plus account:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Billing in the left sidebar.
  4. Make your changes:
    • To add or remove a payment method, scroll to Payment method under Products, then click Update.
    • To switch between monthly and yearly billing, scroll to Billing period under Products, then click Switch to monthly or Switch to yearly.
      • Note: The yearly payment cycle begins as soon as you switch from monthly billing.

  5. Click Save changes.

Any change to your billing date will take effect at the end of your current billing cycle.

What if no one is listed as an administrator for my Dropbox Standard, Business, Advanced, or Business Plus account?

If the original admin for your Dropbox plan has left the business or is no longer involved, their email address may have been deleted. However, they will still be listed as the team admin for your Dropbox plan.

Try recreating this email account so you can access that inbox. Once you have access, reset the Dropbox password for that account, log in, and set up an existing member of your business as the new team admin. We recommend setting up two admins in case of this scenario in the future.

Dropbox Enterprise and Education

To update billing information for a Dropbox Enterprise or Education account, contact your account executive or Dropbox Support.

Or, if you’re logged into your Dropbox Sign account right now, you can click here.

Non-profit discounts for Dropbox DocSend

Overview

DocSend is happy to offer non-profit and charitable organizations a 30% discount to use toward any of the subscription plans. Keep reading to learn more!

Requirements

  • The organization is documented in the IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search.
  • The organization holds valid charitable status with the IRS in the US.
  • The organization holds a valid 501(c)(3) registration.

Application

DocSend account Owners can submit a request for a non-profit discount by the following:

  1. Create a free account through our sign-up page. 
  2. Contact our support team with the email associated with your DocSend account and include:
  • Subject line: Non-profit Discount Request
  • Your organization’s legal, registered name (see IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search). 
  • A brief description of your organization and the request. 

Submission Review

Our team will review your submission within 2-3 business days. Once approved, we will update your billing information within 5 business days of your submission approval date. If your team is not approved, you’re welcome to apply in the future if the status of your organization changes. 

Things to consider

  • We can only extend one discount per qualifying organization. 
  • We do not offer refunds for subscription fees paid prior to being approved for the DocSend Nonprofit discount.

Pay to receive one time faxes Dropbox Fax

Unfortunately, we don’t have the ability to let you receive one-time faxes. It’s something we’ve considered, but is not technically and logistically feasible for us. If you’d like to receive faxes, you’ll want to sign up for a paid subscription. Each of our plans comes with a personal inbound fax line (with the area code of your choice), a monthly fax page allotment, and a thirty day free trial.

You can check out all of the details of our subscriptions on our Pricing Page.

Once you’ve subscribed to a plan, our system will email you with your new fax number and you can start receiving faxes immediately.

Supported currencies in Dropbox DocSend

Overview

DocSend supports three currency types: British Pound £ (GBP), Euro € (EUR), and United States Dollar $ (USD). The currency will automatically be selected based on your browser’s primary language setting.

United States Dollar ($)

USD is the default currency when your primary language is set to English (United States) and all other languages outside of those associated with GBP and EUR currencies. 

Great British Pound (£) & Euro (€)

GBP and EUR currencies reflect at checkout when: 

  • Your primary browser language is set to English (UK).
  • Your primary language is from a European country that uses the Euro.

Users that have their primary language set to the above languages will be given the option to change their currency using the currency switcher located at the top right corner of the upgrade page. 

Things to Consider

  • If you received a coupon code with a fixed dollar amount but are interested in subscribing with a different currency, please reach out to our support team for further assistance. 
  • Payments are refunded at the same rate they were charged.

Tax on Dropbox Sign and Dropbox Fax subscriptions

You may have to pay tax on your Dropbox Sign and Dropbox Fax subscription based on the billing address associated with your account. If your subscription is subject to tax, you’ll see the tax as a line item on your invoices and receipts.

Dropbox Sign and Dropbox Fax taxes by country or region

The amount of tax you’re charged varies by tax type/rates and location.

In some places, you can add your VAT number to your Dropbox Sign account to get tax exemptions.

View Dropbox Sign billing and subscriptions

To find out what kind of subscription you have, log in to your Dropbox Fax account and click on your email address in the upper right corner of your home page. A dropdown menu will appear, then click on Settings. 

From here, click Billing. Click Subscription in the second section down. It will list which subscription you are on, how much you are paying for it, and whether your plan is billed monthly or annually.

If you’re on a free subscription without monthly or annual payments, your account settings won’t display the Subscription or Billing Information fields.

What is this Dropbox charge on my credit card?

This article answers some of the frequently asked questions about credit card charges from Dropbox.

Why am I being charged for Dropbox?

Dropbox Basic is our only free plan. You may have taken a 30-day free trial for Dropbox that has now ended, causing the account to automatically renew into a paid subscription.

Learn how to find out which plan you have, or check your Dropbox account directly.

How can I look up a Dropbox charge on my credit card statement?

If you don’t recognize a Dropbox charge on your credit card, you can look up the email address and payment date associated with it. 

All Dropbox purchases made with a credit card will appear on your statement as DROPBOX*(transaction ID).

How to look up a credit card charge from Dropbox
  1. Find the transaction ID for the Dropbox charge on your credit card statement. You can do this by searching your statement for “Dropbox”.
  2. Click to visit our credit card charge lookup tool.
    • Note: If you paid with PayPal or another form of payment, you won’t be able to use this tool but can contact Dropbox support for assistance.
  3. Enter the transaction ID. 
    • If you’re not signed into Dropbox, you may have to enter the last four digits of your credit card number and the expiration date.
  4. Click Submit. You’ll see the account email associated with the charge, as well as the transaction details. 
Tool not working?

Log in to dropbox.com and contact Dropbox support from the same web browser. Make sure you have the transaction ID from your credit card statement.

My old credit card expired. Why did my new credit card get charged?

If you were paying for a Dropbox subscription with a credit card that expired (or declined the payment for some other reason), your bank may have automatically transferred your subscription payments to your new credit card. Therefore, even if the credit card you were using for Dropbox is no longer active, you can still be charged.

If you’d prefer to use a different payment method, you can update your billing information for your Dropbox account.

If you’d like to cancel your Dropbox subscription instead, follow the steps in this article.

Can I get a refund on a Dropbox subscription charge?

In most cases, payments for Dropbox subscriptions and team member licenses aren’t refundable. Learn how to get a refund on a Dropbox subscription.

Why is my Dropbox subscription not showing in the iOS mobile app?

If you used an Apple device to purchase a Dropbox subscription or start a free trial and you still see Dropbox Basic in the account tab, your subscription hasn’t started. To activate your Dropbox subscription or free trial, follow the instructions below to force start it.

  1. Open the Dropbox mobile app.
  2. Tap Account.
    • If you’re a Dropbox team user and you have both a work and personal account, you’ll see either Personal or the name of your team instead of Account.
  3. Tap the account icon (person) in the bottom right and then the gear icon in the top left.
  4. Tap Restore Purchases.

Why was my credit card declined?

If you were purchasing Dropbox for the first time, the most common reason why your card may have been declined is because of a typo in the card number or billing address.

  • Try entering in your card number and billing address again, and double check to make sure the details are right. 

If your payment failed to automatically renew, the credit card associated with your account may have expired.

  • In that case, update your payment method or add a new one.

If you continue to receive a credit card processing error, we recommend contacting your bank or credit card provider. 

What happens when there’s an error processing a Dropbox team payment?

If your payment for a Dropbox team account gets declined, we recommend you update your billing information as soon as possible.

If a payment continues to fail, eventually we won’t be able to renew your team subscription. Your files will be safe, but your team will be temporarily locked until you update your payment method or disband the team.

Still having trouble?

If you’re still having trouble processing a payment, log in with your admin credentials and click this link to contact support.

Create Upload

Add in-document videos in Dropbox DocSend

Add videos to your documents or PowerPoint presentations to create a more engaging viewing experience. 

In DocSend, you can include videos by:

  • Linking to videos using platforms like YouTube or Vimeo
  • Embedding videos directly in PowerPoint files

When a visitor interacts with a video, you can track engagement through In-Document Link Clicks. View the visitor experience. 

Add videos as hyperlinks

You can add videos to your document by linking to a video URL using platforms like YouTube or Vimeo. These videos will play within the DocSend document viewer when supported.

You can also embed a video file directly into your PowerPoint presentation.

Visual example of how hyperlinking a screenshot of a video functions as a preview of the video:

To add hyperlinked videos as screenshots: 

  1. Take a screenshot of your video. 
  2. Add the screenshot as an image to your document. 
  3. Add the video URL as a hyperlink to the image.
  4. Save and upload the document.

Add embedded videos (PowerPoint)

If you upload a PowerPoint file with embedded video content, supported video formats will play directly within the slide.

Supported formats:

  • .m4v
  • .mov
  • .mp4
  • .webm

Limitations for embedded videos

  • Embedded videos are not supported when watermarks are enabled.
  • PowerPoint files uploaded before March 18, 2025 do not support in-slide video playback.

Track video engagement

Monitor video engagement data and statistics tracked in the page as In-document link clicks.

You can view:

  • The page within the document that was viewed.
  • The video URL that was accessed.
  • Details of visitors who viewed the video.

To do so:

  1. Go to the Recent activity page.
  2. Open a visit record.
  3. Click Visit details.

Additional considerations

  • Videos from platforms such as Wistia, JW Player, Brightcove, and Vidyard will open in a new browser tab instead of playing in the document viewer.
  • Video files like mp4s, can also be uploaded and shared directly using the DocSend video player.

Connect cloud storage providers in Dropbox DocSend

Overview

You can upload documents or folder structures up to 2 GB using any of the providers listed below. With Google, you also have the ability to upload from shared, Team drives, and personal drives. 

  • Box
  • Dropbox
  • Google Drive
  • OneDrive
  • Egnyte
  • Sharepoint

Connect Dropbox

To upload your Dropbox content, follow these steps:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Content library in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Upload.
  4. Click Cloud storage.
  5. Select Dropbox from the service options provided.
  6. Enter your Dropbox login credentials.          
  7. Click Allow DocSend to access your Dropbox account so you can start uploading files.

Connect Box

To upload your Box content, follow these steps:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Content library in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Upload.
  4. Click Cloud storage.
  5. Select Box from the service options provided.
  6. Enter your Box login credentials.                      
  7. Click Allow DocSend to access your Box account so you can start uploading files.

Connect Google Drive

To upload your Google Drive content, follow these steps:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Content library in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Upload.
  4. Click Cloud storage.
  5. Select Google Drive from the service options provided.
  6. Enter your Google login credentials.
  7. Click Allow DocSend to access your Google account so you can start uploading files.

Connect OneDrive

Since OneDrive and OneDrive for Business are powered by Microsoft, the steps to connect these services are the same.

To upload content from your OneDrive account, follow these steps:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Content library in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Upload.
  4. Click Cloud storage.
  5. Select OneDrive/OneDrive for Business from the service options provided.     
  6. Enter your Microsoft login credentials associated with OneDrive/OneDrive for Business or SharePoint Online.
  7. Click Next.
  8. Click Accept when it asks whether you want this app to access your info.

Connect Egnyte

To upload your Egnyte content, follow these steps:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Content library in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Upload.
  4. Click Cloud storage.
  5. Select Egnyte from the service options provided.
  6. Enter your Egnyte domain.
  7. Allow DocSend to access your Egnyte account so you can start uploading files.

Connect SharePoint online

To upload your SharePoint content, follow these steps:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Content library in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Upload.
  4. Click Cloud storage.
  5. Select SharePoint Online from the service options provided.
  6. Enter your Microsoft login credentials.
  7. Click Allow DocSend to access your Microsoft/SharePoint account so you can start uploading files.

Manage external cloud storage providers

You can have all your preferred providers connected and switch from one provider to another whenever you need to upload your documents.

Disconnect external cloud storage provider

To disconnect an external cloud storage provider:

  1. Navigate to your Settings page.
  2. Go to the Connected Apps page.
  3. Click Disconnect under the application you wish to disconnect.

Copy or duplicate Dropbox files

You can make an exact copy (a duplicate) of a Dropbox file or folder on dropbox.com, the Dropbox mobile app, and the Dropbox desktop app.

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox makes syncing files easy.

On dropbox.com

To make a copy of a file or folder on dropbox.com:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the file or folder you’d like to copy.
  3. Click the “…” (ellipsis).
  4. Click Copy.
  5. Click the folder where you’d like to save your copy.
  6. Click Copy to confirm.

In the Dropbox desktop app

To make a copy of a file or folder in the Dropbox desktop app:

  1. Open the Dropbox desktop app.
  2. Open your Dropbox folder in File Explorer (Windows) or Finder (Mac).
  3. Right-click the file or folder you’d like to copy.
  4. Click Copy. The file or folder is copied to your computer’s clipboard.
  5. Click the folder where you’d like to save your copy.
  6. Right-click in the folder.
  7. Click Paste (Windows) or Paste item (Mac).

On the Dropbox mobile app

To make a copy of a file or folder in the Dropbox mobile app:

  1. Open the Dropbox mobile app.
  2. Tap Files.
  3. Tap the “⁝” (vertical ellipsis on Android) or “…” (ellipsis on iPhone/iPad) next to the file or folder you’d like to copy.
  4. Tap Duplicate (Android) or Copy (iPhone/iPad).
  5. Tap the folder where you’d like to save your copy.
  6. Tap Paste (Android) or Save copy (iPhone/iPad) to confirm.

Create a form with Dropbox Forms templates

You can use pre-made templates in Dropbox Forms to expedite the process of creating and sending forms. Templates offered by default are:

  • Sample Job Application Workflow
  • Form W-8BEN
  • Offer Letter
  • Form I9
  • Background Check Authorization
  • Job Application - Applicant Info
  • Registration Form
  • IRS W-4 Form

How to use a template to create a form

To create a form from a template:

  1. Log in to Dropbox Forms.
  2. Click Create form on the top left.
  3. Choose a template.
      • To use a Dropbox Forms template, click Templates.
      • To use a template from your team, click Team Templates.
      • To create a new template, click Build your own.
  4. Review the form, and confirm that this is the template you’d like to use.
      • To view how your form will appear to recipients, click the Form tab.
      • To view how the template will appear when a recipient returns it, click the PDF tab.
      • If the form you’re using has conditional logic, learn about the flow the signer will follow by clicking the Form routing tab. Learn more about conditional logic.
  5. Click Use template.
  6. Add components to your form. Learn more about navigating the Dropbox Forms editor.
  7. When you’re finished populating your form, click Review and Publish.
  8. To send your form, click Publish & Send.
  9. Click the dropdown under Select a form to send, and choose the correct form.
  10. To choose whether to send the file as an attachment or a link, click the dropdown next to Email completed documents to participants via.
      • Note: To get a notification when the form is complete, check the box next to Notify the sender or team members when complete.
  11. Add the names and addresses of the recipient(s).
      • Note: You can also send your form to multiple recipients by clicking Bulk Send.
  12. To create a link that anyone can click to open and fill out the form, toggle Enable shareable link to on. Then, click Copy to share your link.
  13. Click Send.

The recipient will receive a copy of the fillable form in their email. You can view the progress of all your sent forms by clicking Sent on your Dropbox Forms home page.

Does Dropbox DocSend support documents marked as final?

Overview

Documents that have been marked as final must be unmarked as final or exported as a PDF file to upload into DocSend. Attempting to upload the file marked as final will trigger the error message below:

“This document could not be converted because it has been marked as final. To resolve this issue, unmark the document as final or export to pdf prior to upload”

Unmark a Document as Final

  1. Open the presentation.
  2. Click Edit Anyway.
  3. Resave the file unmarked as final.
  4. Reupload the unmarked document into DocSend.

Dropbox Form components overview

Form components are the fields that participants fill out when they receive your form. All forms are made up of different customizable components — each with its own set of helpful features. Below is an overview of each component and its customization options.

Though each component has its own set of customizations, most of them share these options:

  • Label: You can customize the component label on the form.
  • Required: You can require the component to be filled out by the participant.
  • Pre-fill: Form-to-form mapping is a way to copy repetitive data from one form to the next.
  • Placeholder: You can customize the example text to guide a participant.
  • Help text: You can customize the specific helpful information you think the participant may need, like a clarification or explanation.

Below is an overview of each component and its customization options.

Text Input

Text Inputs are one of the most versatile components. Use this for any single-line text entry. You can edit the label of this component on your form for different situations, such as:

  • Name
  • Country of citizenship
  • Foreign Tax Identifying Number
  • Print name of signer

Multiple Choice

Use the Multiple Choice component to offer a pre-defined set of options to choose from. To change how this component is displayed, select Button, Dropdown, or List next to Presentation.

To allow multiple responses, click the toggle next to Allow Multiple Responses.

Checkbox

Use the Checkbox component to add a checkbox for participants to select. This is often used for asking participants to acknowledge something, agree to, or to indicate a choice or option.

Signature

The Signature component can be used for signature collection. Select SingleTap, Draw, or Type next to Signing Options to choose how you’d like participants to be able to sign.

Multi-line Text Input

The Multi-line Text Input component can be used for questions that need a slightly longer response such as, “Why do you want to work here?” or, “Why did you leave your last job?”

Features of the multi-line text input component:

  • Starts off with a minimum of 50 character limit, but you can set it lower, if you’d like.
  • Has an output field preview that displays lines to indicate how many lines of text it will likely generate.
  • Font size is adjustable for uploaded PDFs.
  • The maximum character limit is 500 or depending on depicted component size on the pdf.

Address

The Address component offers a simple way to collect US street addresses. It includes a built-in state selector and validation for zip codes.

Date

The Date component provides a simple way to collect valid dates on your form. Participants will be able to use a date picker on a calendar to fill this field out.

Phone Number

The Phone Number component is formatted to collect 10-digit (US) phone numbers.

Email Address

The Email Address component is similar to the Text Input component, but it includes preselected validation for email addresses.

ID Number

The ID Number component allows you to collect Social Security Number (SSN), Employee ID Number (EIN), or Social Insurance Number (SIN) on your form.

File Attachment

The File Attachment component allows participants to upload files when completing the form.

Files must be 20 MB or smaller and one of the following types:

  • doc
  • docx
  • pdf
  • ppt
  • pptx
  • jpg
  • jpeg
  • png
  • xlsx
  • txt
  • gif

Conditional Rule

The Conditional Rule component allows you to selectively display other components based on participant inputs. This allows you to add follow-up questions only if they are relevant based on the participants’ answers.  

Agreement Text

The Agreement Text component is only used to display text in a form and doesn’t collect participant information. It supports a full rich-text editor with basic formatting, styling, and links.

Calculation

The Calculation component allows you to combine two numeric values to produce a result within your form, using one of four basic mathematic operators (+, -, ×, ÷). Calculated results can be rounded to two 0-6 decimal places.

For example, if you create an order form and need to know how many cupcakes are needed, you can use the calculation component to automatically total the cost on the form.

If you type “quantity” into the first Value box, the number the participant enters will be used to calculate a result. This could be the number of cupcakes the participant would like to order.

When you type a number into the Value box, the total is displayed on the completed copy sent to the participant. This could be the cost per cupcake, and the participant would be sent the full cost for their order of cupcakes.  

Instruction Text

The Instruction Text component allows you to customize instructions for the participant to follow. It will only be displayed on the form the participant fills out. Instruction Text doesn’t appear on the saved document.

Number Input

The Number Input component allows you to add a field where the participants can enter a numeric value. You can customize a minimum and maximum allowed range and the number of decimal places up to 6.

Dropbox Replay FAQs

This article answers frequently asked questions about Dropbox Replay. Get quick answers to common questions about Dropbox Replay, including common error messages and how to solve issues.

What are my Dropbox Replay storage limits?

Dropbox Replay is available for all Dropbox plans, but Replay has these additional file limits:

  • Dropbox Basic: 4 files
  • Dropbox Plus: 4 files 
  • Dropbox Family: 4 files
  • Dropbox Professional: 4 files 
  • Dropbox Essentials: 10 files
  • Dropbox Standard, Advanced, and Enterprise: 4 files 
  • Dropbox Business and Business Plus: 10 files

With the paid Dropbox Replay Add-On, there is no file creation or upload limit. The storage limit of your Replay files depends on your Dropbox plan storage. 

Files added to Replay directly from your local drive, Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, third-party editing software, or any source other than your Dropbox will count against your Dropbox Replay storage limit and your Dropbox plan storage limit. Files added to Replay from your Dropbox account don’t count towards your Dropbox plan storage limit.

Learn how much storage space your plan includes.

Can I buy the Replay Add-On directly in Replay?

Yes, you can now buy the Replay Add-On without leaving Replay.

Learn more about buying the Replay Add-On.

What happens if I delete the original file from my Dropbox account?

Deleting, moving, or renaming the original video, image, audio, or PDF file in your Dropbox account won’t affect your Dropbox Replay project. The only way a video, image, audio, or PDF file (and its comments) can be deleted from Replay is by directly removing it from your Replay dashboard.

Who can access files in Dropbox Replay that I imported from Dropbox?

You can manage access to your video, image, audio, or PDF files in Dropbox Replay using the sharing settings. When creating shared links for files, you can make them public, private, or share them with specific people. You can also turn shared links off.

Learn more about sharing Replay files and projects.

If your file is in a team project folder, everyone on your team has access. An admin on your team can take ownership of files or projects shared in the team folder of current and former team members.

Learn more about Dropbox Replay admin control features.

What happens to Dropbox Replay files if a team member leaves?

When a team member leaves, admins have the ability to take ownership of shared files or projects by that team member. 

Once an admin has taken ownership of a project, they’ll be able to take all of the actions that an owner can take, including: 

  • Edit, delete, or add a password
  • Toggle downloads on or off 
  • Resolve comments 
  • Pin or label comments 

Learn more about Dropbox Replay admin control features.

Are there any system requirements for Dropbox Replay?

Dropbox Replay runs through the internet browser on your desktop. To ensure the best experience, we recommend using Google Chrome.

Learn more about system requirements for Dropbox Replay.

I forgot to post my drawings, can I get them back?

If you haven’t exited or closed the file you drew in, your drawings on videos will be saved as drafts and marked as empty circles on the video timeline that you can click to view. You can either Post drawing as comment by clicking the paper airplane icon or Delete drawing by clicking the trash can icon.

Can I add comments on a file that are only visible to my team?

If a project is created by someone with a Replay Add-On, you can leave editor-only comments that won’t be visible to clients or other reviewers. These editor-only comments can only be posted and seen by someone who’s been added to that particular project with edit access or as a project owner.

Learn more about adding comments in Replay.

Why can’t I set a password for my Dropbox Replay file?

Password protection is a paid feature included in the Dropbox Replay Add-On. If you were a beta user and you turn off password protection for a file, you won’t be able to turn it back on unless you buy the Replay Add-On.

You’ll still be able to edit any existing passwords you’d already set on your files when you used the beta version of Replay or when you had the Replay Add-On.

I used to have unlimited files and now I have a limit. How do I find the right files to delete to get under my quota?

Only files uploaded after April 25, 2023, count against the file limit, so you can sort your files by creation date and choose which files you’d like to delete or archive.

I don’t pay for Dropbox but I want to use Dropbox Replay. What do I do?

Dropbox Replay is available to all customers with a Dropbox account, but the Dropbox Replay Add-On is only available to customers on Dropbox Plus, Essentials, Professional, Standard, Business, Advanced, Business Plus, and Enterprise.

Can I see comments from previous versions of a file?

You can choose to view comments on the current version, all previous versions, or both current and previous versions.

Learn more about viewing comments on Replay files.

Can I get lossless audio playback on files?

Customers who’ve bought the Dropbox Replay Add-On can get lossless HD audio playback for their audio files. Replay supports lossless audio resolutions up to 24-bit/96 kHz.

To turn on lossless audio:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Open the audio file you’d like to turn on lossless audio for.
  3. Click the Audio quality dropdown.
  4. Select Lossless in the dropdown menu.

Do I need to buy the Replay Add-On for my whole team?

No. Admins on teams who pay by credit card can buy the add-on for specific team members. However, teams that don’t pay by credit card will need to buy a minimum of 10 add-ons for their team.

Can I transfer a Replay Add-On from one team member to another team member?

Admins can move an add-on from one active team member to another active team member in the Members page. First, you’ll need to remove the add-on from the member that it’s currently assigned to. You can then assign it to another team member.

Learn more about managing Replay Add-Ons for team members.

Can I add more Replay Add-Ons if I need them?

Admins on teams that pay by credit card can buy a new Replay Add-On at any time. You’ll be charged at a prorated amount for the rest of your current billing period. Teams with a dedicated Account Manager will need to contact them directly to request more add-ons.

Can a user be assigned a Replay Add-On if they aren’t a team member?

No, a Replay Add-On can only be assigned to team members.

What happens to your Replay files after you cancel the Replay Add-On?

You’ll retain access to all Replay files. You can edit or remove any passwords you’ve set for your files, but you can’t add any new password protection after cancellation.

Why can’t I access extended version history, data governance, or advanced security with my Reply Add-On

Extended version history, data governance, and advanced security are only available as full-team add-ons, as they apply to the entire team. You can’t access these features with a partial add-on.

File upload limitations in Dropbox DocSend

This article explains the different methods to upload content in DocSend and details the upload limits for each product feature across plans. For a full overview of available features, visit our pricing page.

Upload limits

Individual files

  • Page upload limit: Total number of pages each document can have per upload.
  • Upload size limit: Total allowed size of each individual file upload.
  • Audio upload size limit: Total allowed size for each individual audio upload.
  • Video upload size limit: Total allowed size for each individual video upload.

For Spaces (available on Standard, Advanced, Advanced Data Rooms, and Enterprise plans) 

  • Total files in a Space: Number of files allowed for each Space.
  • Files per Space folder (Advanced plans only): Number of files allowed for each Space folder. 

Learn more about upload limits per file type.

User account

  • Total Document Limit: Number of documents you can have in a user account.
  • Total Included Storage: File storage size you can have in your user account.

How can I export to an SD card from my Android phone?

If you’d like to export files from Dropbox to an SD card on your Android phone, you’ll first need to check that you have the correct version of the Dropbox app. If you’re running Android 4.4 or later, you’ll need version 12 (or later) of the Dropbox app.

The latest version of the Dropbox app is available on the Google Play store.

Once you’ve verified you have the correct version of the Dropbox app, you’re ready to export to an SD card. To do so:

  1. Tap the Quick Action button to the right of the file name you wish to export.
  2. Tap More.
  3. Tap Export.
  4. Tap Save to device.
  5. Select your external SD card.

If you don’t see your external SD card listed:

  1. After tapping Save to device, tap the Menu button.
  2. Tap Settings.
  3. Select Display advanced devices.
  4. You should see your external SD card appear as an export location.

What happens when I export a file to a different app on my device?

When you choose to export a file to another application, the file is opened with the application selected. That application then handles the file. For example, if you’ve exported a file to the Gallery app on your device, that app will display the file but not actually store the file.

To store a file in another location please choose “save to SD card.”

How to add a Dropbox Sign signature on smartphones

The smartphone option is supported by all models and operating systems.  You need to be able to take a photo with your phone and then email that photo from your phone.

1. Take a picture of your signature on your smartphone.  

If you do not know how to add or change a signature, please follow the instructions in the “How do I edit my signature?” FAQ article.

2. Once you have the “Create Signature” window open with four signature options, choose smartphone.

3. You will see a window with instructions and a unique subject code. From your phone, email the photo to sign@hellosign.com with the unique code in the subject line.  Make sure it is typed correctly, and send.

4. On your HelloSign screen, click “Continue.” 

5. On the editor screen, you can adjust your signature image contrast and rotate. You’ll also want to be sure to crop your signature image to ensure correct sizing.

All images uploaded will be in black and white. 

How to add merge fields to a template in Dropbox Sign

If there’s information you need a sender to fill out each time they use a template, you can assign them a merge field in the template. For example, if you create a template for a car lease agreement, the sender may want to add the make and model of the car to the document before sending it to the signer.

To add merge fields to a template:

  1. Follow the instructions to create a new template or edit an existing template until you get to the document editor.
  2. Click and drag a Textbox from the left sidebar to your document.
  3. Click the dropdown menu below Assigned to in the right sidebar.
  4. Click Sender.
  5. Give the field a name in the box below Merge field. This is the prompt the sender will see when they use the template to send a signature request.

How to copy files from Google Drive

You can copy files from Google Drive to your Dropbox account. This feature is only available on dropbox.com.

How to import files from Google Drive to Dropbox

To copy files from your Google account to dropbox.com:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click Upload under the search bar at the top.
  3. Click Import from Google Drive. A pop-up window will display files and folders in your Google account.
    • If prompted, allow Dropbox access to your Google account.
  4. Click on the file that you’d like to upload to Dropbox.

Notes:

  • You can use the dropdown in the search bar to filter different types of files.
  • You can select multiples files by clicking and dragging your cursor, or by clicking while holding down ctrl (Windows) or alt (Mac) on your keyboard.
  • You can only import files from Google, not folders.
  1. Click Select.
  2. Check any of the appropriate checkboxes to manage how Google Drive files are organized in your Dropbox account. You can choose to:
    • Keep folder structure: When the checkbox next to this option is checked, the uploaded files will be organized in the same folder structure they’re organized as in Google Drive. This means that if you select a file that is organized into a folder and parent folder, the file, folder, and parent folder will show in your Dropbox account. However, only the files you select will be uploaded in your Dropbox account, not all the files that exist within these folders in your Google Drive.
    • Overwrite files with same name: When the box next to this option is checked, files you upload from Google Drive will replace existing Dropbox files with the same name.
    • Delete files from source: When the box next to this option is checked, the files or folders that you upload from Google Drive will be deleted in Google Drive after they’re uploaded to Dropbox.
  3. Click Upload.

You’ll receive an email that confirms the upload.  

Can I copy files from more than one Google account?

Yes, you can upload files from any Google account you have access to. However, you won’t be able to connect more than one Google account at any given time.

To add files from a different Google account:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click Upload under the search bar at the top.
  3. Click Import from Google Drive.
    • If a pop-up window appears, click the Switch Google account button in the top-right corner. Then, follow the prompts to connect a different Google account to Dropbox.
  4. Choose the Google account you’d like to log into, or click Use another account.

Learn more about how to manage third-party apps on Dropbox.
