Links are named via the account they’re associated with, and the same account name can be connected to multiple links across multiple spaces. The visitor analytics for all links associated with a particular account show up under the Accounts page.

Dropbox DocSend Spaces (data rooms) templates

Overview

Templates provide an easy way to get started using Spaces. Templates can be used to create documents, share files, assist clients and employees, and much more. Learn more about the DocSend Advanced Data Rooms plan.

Requirements

  • Any plan that has access to Spaces (data rooms).
    • Spaces are available to all plans except Personal.

What’s a Space (data room)?

Spaces are what we call our virtual data rooms (VDR). Data rooms provide a way to group, organize, and share high volumes of content with others using a single link. Data rooms provide a high level of customization to allow teams to tailor each data room to their unique needs. Data analytics provide additional support by allowing owners and collaborators to keep track of contributions and visitor activity.

How to use a template in Spaces (data rooms)

To use a template in Spaces (data rooms):

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Spaces (data rooms) in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Use template under the template you’d like to use.

You can select from these templates:

  • Client Portal - This is used for proposals, contracts, and other professional documents.
  • Virtual Data Room - This is used to store and share sensitive files and collaborating on requests.
  • Onboarding Space - This is used for onboarding clients and employees while keeping their information secure.
  • Board Meeting - This is used to share agendas and meeting notes and to archive documents.

Dropbox Paper FAQs

Dropbox Paper is an online document workspace, where you can organize and display text, media, and files all in one place. Paper lets you easily collaborate with others and access your Paper docs from anywhere.  

Are my Paper docs stored in my Dropbox folders?

If you’re on the old release of Dropbox Paper, your Paper docs are stored in Paper folders in your account on paper.dropbox.com.

If you’re on the new release of Dropbox Paper, your Paper docs are stored in your account on dropbox.com, with your other files and folders.

To find out if you’re using the old or new release of Dropbox Paper:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click  New next to the search bar.
  3. Hover over Document.
    • If you see Dropbox Paper doc in the list of document types, then you’re using the new release of Dropbox Paper.
    • If you don’t see Dropbox Paper doc in the list of document types, then you’re using the old release.  

Do you need a Dropbox account for Paper?

Yes, you need a Dropbox account to create and open Paper docs.

If you share a Paper doc with someone who doesn’t have a Dropbox account, they’ll receive an email with a link prompting them to create a Dropbox account. Once they create an account, they can access your Paper doc.  

Is Dropbox Paper free?

Yes, Dropbox Paper is free.  

Do Paper docs count towards my Dropbox storage quota?

Paper docs will take up very little space in your Dropbox account—less than 100 bytes, which is less than one-30th of a standard document file.  

Is there a limit on the amount of Paper docs I can create?

No, there is no limit on Paper docs you can create with a Dropbox account.  

Do I need to be signed in to Dropbox to access Paper?

Yes, you must be signed in to Dropbox to access Paper.   

What security and privacy features does Paper have?

Paper has the same level of security as Dropbox, with a few exceptions for Dropbox teams.

How do I open and close the sidebar (Paper folder view)?

The folder view is a sidebar on the left side of your Paper doc that lets you jump to other docs inside the same folder as the doc you have open. To open and close the folder view, click the open folder view icon (half-grey square) in the upper-left corner of a Paper doc.

Duplicate a Space (data room) in Dropbox DocSend

Overview

Duplicating Spaces (data rooms) allows you to quickly replicate an existing Space. You can leverage this feature to create Space templates, saving time for both you and your team.

How to duplicate a Space (data room)

You can easily duplicate a Space (data room) from the Spaces page or within the Space itself. This will copy all content, sections, Space folders, header and layout options into a new Space. 

  1. From the Spaces page, expand the “more options” menu next to the desired Space and select Duplicate Space.
  2. From here, you can rename the Space or keep it the same, then click Duplicate to confirm.
  3. Or, if you’re already in the Space, click the Duplicate Space icon located on the Space header settings.

Personal content

While you can duplicate a Space (data room), the content that you or the Space owner don’t have access to will not carry over into the new Space. A warning message will appear, indicating that some content may not be copied because you don’t have permission to access it.

Personal content is indicated by a lock symbol. Similarly, Space Collaborators are not copied over to the new Space and will need to be added again. See our article Collaborate in a Space (data room) for more information.

Processing delay

Duplicating a Space (data room) may take a couple of minutes to appear on your Spaces page. This depends on the size of the Space - the larger the Space, the longer it may take to duplicate.

FAQs about modified dates for files and folders

The modified date of a file or folder represents the last time that file or folder was updated. If you’re having trouble with the modified dates of your files or folders, check out these frequently-asked questions:  

How do I organise files by their modification date?

You can organize files by their modification date. To do so:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click Modified at the top of the list of files. It will become bold.
    • If you don’t see Modified, hover over the Name heading. Then, click the down arrow and click Modified.
  3. Click the arrow directly to the right of Modified to switch between viewing files by oldest and most recent modification date.  

Which changes affect the modified date of a file?

A file’s modified date will update on all devices and dropbox.com if you edit the file in your Dropbox account or another user edits the file in a shared folder.

In some cases, like the ones listed below, a file’s modified date will change only on the device it’s edited on and won’t be synced to other devices.

  • If you download a file from dropbox.com to a device, the file’s modified date on that device will change to the time it was downloaded but won’t sync with other devices.
  • If you manually change a file’s modified date on the Dropbox desktop app without editing the file’s content, the file’s modified date on that device will change to the time you set but won’t sync with other devices.

Will Dropbox preserve the modified date of a file or folder if I upload or download it to my account?

To preserve the modified date of a file, upload or download the file using the Dropbox desktop app. 

Why is the modified date of my folder different across devices?

The following actions could result in conflicting modified dates:

  • You download the folder from dropbox.com to a device. The folder’s modified date on that device will change to the time it was downloaded (or edited) but won’t sync with other devices.
  • You add a file or folder from the desktop app. The folder’s modified date will only update on the Dropbox desktop app, but it won’t change on dropbox.com.
  • You change the online-only/available offline status of the folder on a device. The folder’s modified date on that device will change to the time of the update, but won’t sync with other devices.
  • You manually change the folder’s modified date on the Dropbox desktop app without making edits to the folder. The folder’s modified date on that computer will change to the time you set but won’t sync with other devices.

File and folder icons, symbols, and colors

This is a glossary of icons, symbols, and colors that appear on your files and folders in your Dropbox account.

If you’re looking for a different icon that isn’t listed here, check this article on sync icons.

How do I create a Dropbox folder shortcut on my Android device?

On Android devices, Dropbox folder shortcuts allow you to quickly access folders that are nested deep inside your Dropbox.

To create a folder shortcut:

  1. Long press a blank, available space on your home screen.
  2. Tap the Widgets icon.
  3. Scroll to Dropbox Folder.
  4. Long press the Dropbox icon and drag it to your home screen.
  5. When prompted, select a folder from your Dropbox and tap Create shortcut.

How do I transfer a former team member’s files to another member?

If you’re the team admin or user management admin of a Dropbox team account, you can use account transfer when you delete a team member’s account from a Dropbox team account or later on if it makes more sense (for example, after you’ve onboarded a new person who will need the files). Keep in mind that you can use account transfer just once for each member.

Delete a member’s account and transfer

  1. Log in with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Members.
  4. Click More  next to the member you want to remove and select Delete from the menu.
  5. In the pop-up window, leave the selection at Transfer now to immediately transfer the deleted user’s Dropbox files to another team member.
  6. Enter the recipient’s name or email address (the recipient must be a member of your team account).
  7. After choosing whether or not to use the remote wipe option, click Continue.

Transfer from an already deleted member

  1. Log in with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Members.
  4. Click Removed and choose Deleted from the dropdown.
  5. Click the gear icon to the right of the former member’s name and select Manage files from the menu.
  6. Select the option to Transfer to another team member.
  7. Enter the recipient’s name or email address and click Submit (the recipient must be a member of your Dropbox team).

How to arrange files in Dropbox Sign

Users are able to rearrange the order of the files they’ve uploaded for a single signature request. To reorder these files simply click on the name of the file and drag and drop it to the desired spot in the order.

How to create tags for Dropbox files

You can add tags to files and folders to help you organize and quickly find everything in your Dropbox account. Tags are available to all Dropbox users and can be added to individual files, folders, or in bulk. Anyone who can view or edit a file or folder can see its tags, but only people with edit access can add or remove tags.  

How to add a tag

To add a tag to a file or folder:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the file or folder where you’d like to add a tag.
  3. Click   (more options) next to the file or folder, or click the file to preview it.
  4. Click File info.
    • If you’re previewing the file in Full screen, click File instead. Then, click Info.
  5. You’ll see # Add a tag in the right-side panel.
  6. Type your tag and press Enter (Windows) or Return (Mac).

How to remove a tag

To remove a tag from a file:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the file where you’d like to remove a tag.
  3. Click  (more options) next to the file or folder.
  4. Click File info.
    • Tags for that file will appear under the file preview in the right sidebar.
  5. Click the X to the right of the tag you’d like to remove.  

How to search for a tag

There are multiple ways to search for a tag: 

  • Enter the tag in the format of #tag_name in the search bar at the top of the screen. 
  • As you start typing in the search bar, you’ll see a list of suggested tags. Select the tag you’re looking for.
  • Click the tag in the left-side panel when previewing a file to view all the files associated with that tag.
  • Click the search bar and select the tag you wish to search under Tags.  

How to use tags with an automated folder

Using automation, you can apply tags to files within a specific folder by default.

To create a folder with automated tags:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click  New next to the search bar.
  3. Hover over Folder. 
  4. Select Automated folder.
  5. Click Choose a tag to organize and find files.
  6. Add at least one tag.
  7. Click Save.

To add automated tags to an existing folder:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click the folder where you’d like to add automated tags.
  3. Click  (settings) next to the folder name. 
  4. Hover over Organize.
  5. Click Add automation.
  6. Click Choose a tag to organize and find files.
    • To add this automation to all files currently within this subfolder, click Apply to current files.
    • To add this automation to all subfolders of this folder, click Include files in all subfolders.
  7. Add at least one tag.
  8. Click Save.

Learn more about automated folders.

How to delete Dropbox Backup

Before deleting a backup, check the following:

  • You must have the Dropbox desktop app installed to delete your backup. If you’ve already uninstalled the desktop app, reinstall the desktop app to delete your backup.
  • If you no longer have access to the device, you can delete your backup by unlinking the device from your Dropbox account.

Delete your computer backup or external hard drive backup

To delete your computer or external hard drive backup: 

  1. Click 🗀 (Dropbox) in your taskbar 0 (Windows) or menu bar 1 (Mac).
  2. Click your avatar (photo or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Preferences.
  4. Click Backups.
  5. Click Manage backups.
  6. Click Delete backup.
  7. Click Confirm if it’s a computer backup, or Delete drive if it’s an external hard drive backup.

How to export visitor data from Dropbox DocSend

You can export a CSV spreadsheet of all visits to content housed in your Space for Team folders or for individual files.

How to export visitor data

To export visitor data for a Space:

  1. Navigate to the Space you want to export data for.
  2. Click ☑ (more options).
  3. Click Export visits.

How to export visitor data for a file:

  1. Click the file title within a Space or Content library.
  2. Click ☑ (more options) in the upper-left corner.
  3. Click Export visits.

Visit CSV data

The CSV spreadsheet will highlight information about the visit and visitor:

The following data will be included when exporting visit data from a Space:

  • Contact name: Populates when Signable document is completed (includes access gating agreements)
  • Contact email: Populates when Require Email to View is enabled.
  • Name
  • Space link
  • Space link owner
  • Content name
  • Content link
  • Content version
  • Content visit date (date + time in UTC)
  • Duration
  • Downloaded at: When downloaded from the DocSend document viewer
  • Printed at: When printed from the DocSend document viewer.
  • Percent completion
  • Location
  • Device (mobile, desktop, tablet)
  • Atypical visit

The following data will be included when exporting visit data from a file:

  • Created at
  • Name
    • When any Signable Document is completed (including access gating agreements)
  • Email
  • Link Name
  • Link Owner
  • Total Visit Duration
  • % (Visit) Completion
  • Content version
  • Account
  • Downloaded at

How to find and manage duplicate files

On dropbox.com, you can find and manage duplicate files in your Dropbox account. If you have copies of the same files stored in multiple locations, with our Find duplicates feature you can identify and locate those files, helping you free up space, stay organized, and improve your overall file management experience.

How to find and manage duplicate files on dropbox.com

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. You can find duplicate files in the following ways:
    • If you have an individual account, click ☑ (settings) next to All files or next to a specific folder.
    • If you have a team account, click ☑ (settings) next to a folder you have edit access to. 
      • Note: Admins and members of team accounts can only find duplicates in the folders they have edit access to.
  3. Click Organize.
  4. Click Find duplicates.
  5. A list of all your duplicate files will appear.
    • To delete a file, click ☑ (delete) next to the duplicate file you’d like to delete.
    • To delete multiple files at once, select your desired files and click Delete in the top-right corner.
    • To see a preview of a file, click ☑ (more options) next to the duplicate file you’d like to preview, then click ☑ Preview.

Learn more about deleting Dropbox files and folders.

Learn how to restore or recover deleted files or folders in Dropbox.

How to get started with the team space

After the Dropbox for teams update, everyone in a Dropbox team account shares a team space. If you’re an admin, learn how to manage the team space for your team.

What’s the team space?

Everyone on your Dropbox team account can access the team space. It contains both personal folders and team folders, all organized in a shared structure that’s the same for every team member. This makes it easy to keep content organized in one place that the whole team can access and collaborate on.

What’s the top level?

The top level is where you can find the first set of folders that contain all subfolders.

On dropbox.com, you can view top-level folders in the Allfiles section of your account. For team members, this includes team folders and a personal folder.

Admins control who can edit team folders at the top level. Team members with edit access can convert a shared folder from their personal space into a team folder. 

Learn how to create a team folder at the top level.

What’s the difference between team folders and personal folders?

You have two different kinds of folders.

Team folders

  • Everyone can create team folders by default, but admins can manage that permission.
  • Team folders can be shared with the entire team, certain groups, or individuals. 
  • Within a team folder, each file or subfolder can be shared with a different set of people. 
  • Admins can choose to allow others to view or edit the files in a team folder, or block access altogether. 
  • Team members with edit permissions can create subfolders within team folders.

Personal folders

  • Your personal folder is your space and is private to you. However, you can choose to share files in your personal folder with other members of your team if you’d like.

Example of personal and team folders

Your name is Janey Smith, and you’re in the design department of an organization named Hanford Inc. You’ve just joined your team’s Dropbox account.

In your Dropbox account, you see several folders: 

  • “Janey Smith” — This is your personal folder. Only you can access content in this folder, unless you choose to share it.
  • ”Design” — This is a team folder that you have access to, which contains files and folders for design projects. You can access and view all the files in this folder. 
  • “Marketing” — This subfolder within the “Design” folder has a blue folder with a diagonal line in a circle on it. If you try to open it, you see an error message: No access to the folder “Marketing”. You can’t access to this subfolder.

Who can access team folders?

Not all team members have access to all content by default. Admins can grant team members different permissions to team folders or remove access for team members to team folders:

  • Can edit: You can view, edit, and manage access to the contents of this folder.
  • Can view: You can view the contents of this folder.
  • No access: You can’t view the contents of this folder.

By default, anyone with edit permissions to a folder has edit permissions to all subfolders inside that folder as well, unless a subfolder is restricted. 

You can also share a folder by selecting edit or view permissions, clicking Copy Link, then pasting and sharing where desired.

Members of your team that receive an edit link can add the folder to their Dropbox account and collaborate on content. If an edit link is sent to someone who isn’t a member of your team, they’ll need to request and be granted permission before they can add the folder to their Dropbox account and collaborate on content.

Learn how to manage the team space for your team.

Sharing files and folders with your team

If the file or folder lives in a personal folder

If you’re the owner of a file or a folder, you can share it from your personal folder with groups or individuals in your team. If you share a file or folder that lives in your personal folder, only the file or folder you select is shared. Nothing else in your personal folder is shared unless you choose to share it.

You can:

  • Share the file or folder by email. 
    • Note: Whoever you shared the folder with will receive a folder invite. This invite shows where the folder will be added: either into their personal folder or a team folder.
  • Send a link to view or edit the file or folder.
  • Move the file or folder from your personal folder into a team folder. This means the file or folder will be accessible to everyone who can access the folder you’re moving it to.

If the file or folder is in a team folder 

You can: 

  • Share the file or folder by email.  
  • Send a link to view or edit the file or folder.
  • Share the team folder by email or via a link.

How to copy or move a team folder

Learn how to copy or move a folder.

How to hide content suggestions on dropbox.com

The content suggestions section on the Dropbox homepage suggests files or folders you may want to access, based on your recent usage. 

How to hide content suggestions

To temporarily hide your content suggestions when you log in: 

  1. Log in to dropbox.com
  2. Scroll down to the Suggested for you section.
  3. Click Hide (eye icon) to the right of Suggested for you. 
    • To show the content suggestions section again, click Show (closed eye icon) to the right of Suggested for you. 

How to turn off content suggestions

You can also choose to permanently hide content suggestions on your account from your settings page. To do so: 

  1. Log in to dropbox.com
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom left corner. 
  3. Click Settings. 
  4. Toggle off Content suggestions in the General tab. 

How to lock or unlock a Dropbox file

File locking is a feature that prevents a file from being edited. This allows teams and collaborators to coordinate who is editing a file and avoid conflicted copies.

What happens when you lock a file?

If a file is locked, those who have access to the file will still be able to view, comment on, and share a link to the file. A person with an edit-link to a locked file won’t be able to edit the file. If they try, they’ll see a prompt to reach out to the person who locked the file. Only the person who locked the file or a team admin can unlock files.

How to edit a locked file

If you need to edit a locked file, you can request that the file be unlocked by clicking Ask to Unlock in the window that appears when you attempt to open the file. Or, you can make a copy of the locked file—however, any changes made to the copy won’t be reflected in the original file when it’s unlocked.

Admins: Unlock a team member’s file

Team admins can unlock a team member’s file. To do so:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click the dropdown to the left of Dropbox, under Products.
  4. Click Content.
  5. Click Locked files.
  6. Click ☑ (more options) on the right of the file you’d like to unlock.
    • To unlock multiple files at once, check the checkbox next to each file you’d like to unlock.
  7. Click Unlock Files. 
  8. Select whether you’d like to notify the user who originally locked the file.
    • By default, the user who originally locked the file will receive an email notification that their file has been unlocked.
    • If you don’t want to notify the original user who locked the file, uncheck the checkbox next to Let [user who locked file] know you’ve unlocked editing.
  9. Click Unlock editing.

Admins: Disable file locking

Team admins can turn off file locking for their team.

To disable file locking:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click the dropdown to the left of Dropbox, under Products.
  4. Click Settings.
  5. Click the Content tab.
  6. Under Content tools, toggle File locking to Off.
  7. Click Save.

How to manage Dropbox Backup

You can manage your backups, by viewing the contents, progress, and history, skipping files, modifying which folders are backed up, and more.

To manage your backups:

  1. Click the Dropbox icon in your notification center 0 (Windows) or menu bar 1 (Mac).

  2. Click the Backups tab.

  3. Select the backup you’d like to manage. 

     

From the Dropbox Backup window, you can:

  • Click View backed up files to open a browser window and see all files and folders in that backup.
  • Click View status to see the live progress of that backup.
  • Click View history to see the version history for that backup.
  • Click Skip files to open a File Explorer or Finder window and select a file to exclude from syncing (computer only).
    • This feature isn’t available on the updated Dropbox Backup.
  • Click Rewind backup to restore a previous version of your backup.            
    • Dropbox Rewind isn’t available to users on Dropbox Basic. 
    • This feature isn’t available on the updated Dropbox Backup.
  • Click Choose folders to change the folders you’d like to back up (computer only). 
  • Click Delete backup to turn off your computer or external hard drive backup.
  • Click View deleted files to open a browser window and recover recently deleted files.

To manage your backups with the updated Dropbox Backup:

  1. Click the Dropbox icon in your notification center (Windows) or menu bar (Mac).
  2. Click the Backups tab.
  3. Select the backup you’d like to manage on the left.
    • Click View backed up files to open a browser window and see all files and folders in that backup.
    • Click View status to see the live progress of that backup.
      • Note: You can also see the status of your backup under the backup name at the top of the window. You’ll see [x]% backed up, Done, Paused, Backups paused, Error, Partially done, Unplugged, or Stopped. Hover over the status to see more information.
    • Click Choose folders to change the folders you’d like to back up (computer only).
    • Click Rename to change the name of your backups.
    • Click View deleted files to restore previous versions of selected folders within Backup.
      • Rewind isn’t available on the updated Dropbox Backup.
    • Click Delete backup to turn off your computer or external hard drive backup.
    • Click View deleted files to see files deleted within the past 30 days.

Learn how to update Dropbox Backup.

How to manage Dropbox Backup for your team

Dropbox Backup makes it easy to automatically back up important files and folders from your computers and external hard drives. This helps to keep your content safe and quickly recover it if things go wrong.

Certain types of admins can manage Dropbox Backup for their team, including turning features on or off and viewing their team’s backup activity.

How to turn Dropbox Backup on or off for your team

To turn Dropbox Backup on or off for your team:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Under Products, click the dropdown to the left of Dropbox.
  4. Click Settings.
  5. Click the Content tab.
  6. Under Backup, toggle the following features to On or Off:
    • Camera uploads
    • Computer backup
    • External drive backup
  7. Click Save.

How to manage Dropbox DocSend content folders

In Content library, you can leverage folders to organize your content. You can create folders to separate content by team, prospect or customer, or even document type.

You can also store all files used in DocSend Spaces in the Content library section. And with the ability to add subfolders to your folder structure, the possibilities are endless!

There are two main folder types for all content: Personal folders and team folders.

  • Personal Folders are perfect for storing any private or sensitive documents. This section is private to each user and won’t be visible or accessible to other users on the account.
    • When content stored in a personal folder is added to a Space, team members will see only the file name with a lock icon, indicating restricted access.
  • Team folders can be used to store and arrange public content that your team has access to. When files located in team folders are added to a Space, they’ll be visible to everyone in the team who has access to that Space. Team folders can be found under the Team Folders section of the Content library page.

Create a folder

You can easily create a new folder or subfolder on Content library:

To create a new folder:

  1. Click Content library in the left side bar.
  2. Click Team folders or Personal folders.
  3. Click Create folder.
  4. Name your folder.
  5. Click Add folder.
  6. Click Confirm.

You can now upload content into the new folder or drag and drop existing content into the folder.

The Content library shows the combined count of recent visits to each file in your folder, reflecting both company and external visitor activity.

Learn about how to create a folder in a Space. 

Manage folders

On the Content page, you can perform additional actions to manage your content folders. When you hover over a folder and click “…” (more options), you can:

  • Share as Space: Create a Space link containing all documents in the folder. Learn more about how to create a Space from Content folders.
  • Create folder: Create a new folder or subfolder.
  • Rename: Rename a folder.
  • Request files: Use the form to request files from an account.
  • Delete: Delete a folder. When you do so, a confirmation message will appear before the folder is deleted.
  • Linked Spaces: Shows the Spaces linked to files. 

Filters

  • Team: Shows only team content.
  • Personal: Shows only Personal content. 
  • Shared folders: Shows content shared with others.

Move multiple files into a folder

  1. Check the boxes next to the files you want to move.
  2. Click and drag the files into the desired folder. 
    • Note: You can click Move back in the bottom status window to undo this action.

Move single a file into a folder

  1. Select the file you want to move.
  2. Click and drag that file into the desired folder. 
    • Note: You can click Move back in the bottom status window to undo this action.

Move files and folders into a specific folder

  1. Select the files and folders you want to move.
  2. Click and drag the content into the desired folder. 

Delete multiple files and folders

  1. Check the boxes next to the files you want to delete.
  2. Click Delete. 
    • A confirmation box will appear to confirm this action.
  3. Click Delete again to confirm.
    • Note: This will remove access for all invited users and deactivate any active links to these files and folders.

Moving content into folders with varying privacy settings

  • Moving content from team folder to team folder typically has no effect on the content or its visibility.
  • Moving content from apersonal folder to a team folder immediately shares the content with your team and allows other users to see it.
  • Moving content from a team folder to a personal folder immediately removes any teammates’ links and prevents other users from accessing the content. A confirmation message will appear before the content is moved.

Best practices

  • To facilitate collaboration, use team folders for documents that require review from multiple team members.
  • For documents that are confidential or in draft form, use personal folders to maintain control over who can access them.
  • Check the content in both your personal and team folders regularly to ensure that the right files are accessible to the users that really need access to them.
  • You can drag and drop files from a team folder to a personal folder, and vice-versa. Learn more about content folders.
    • Note: Privacy and access settings will change if you move files from a team folder to a personal folder and vice-versa.

How to manage Stacks for teams

Stacks help your team organize related content in one place. As an admin, you can create and publish Stacks for your team, making it easier to find and work on shared projects. You can also manage access and visibility to ensure the right people have access to the right content.

Learn how to use Stacks with Dropbox Dash.

How to publish a Stack to your entire team

As an admin, you can pin Stacks to your team members’ start pages, allowing you to share resources to your whole team quickly and easily.

To do so:

  1. Log in to dash.ai with you admin credentials.
    • You can also open the Dash desktop app by pressing control-shift-e (Windows) or command-shift-e (macOS).
  2. Click Account in the left sidebar.
  3. Select Published content.
  4. Enter the name of the Stack you’d like to publish in the search bar.
  5. Click (add) next to the Stack you’d like to publish.
  6. Click Publish.

The Stack will be visible to everyone on your team.

You can quickly generate insights, ask questions, and create summaries of the information in your Stacks.

To ask a question about one of your stacks:

  1. Log in to dash.ai.
    • You can also open the Dash desktop app by pressing control-shift-e (Windows) or command-shift-e (macOS).
  2. Click Stacks in the left sidebar.
  3. Select the Stack you’d like to ask a question about.
  4. Click Ask Dash in the top right corner.
  5. Enter your question in the text box and click  (send).
    • You can also use this text box to summarize each file in your Stack, including Stacks of more than 20 items.

Once your answer appears, you can ask follow-up questions by entering your query in the text box and clicking (send).

How to manage folders shared with your team

You can choose if team members can add editable folders from outside of your Dropbox team.

To permit outside folders in team Stacks:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Under Products, click the dropdown to the left of Dropbox.
  4. Click Settings.
  5. Under Content, scroll to the Receiving content section.
  6. Toggle Outside folders to On.

How to manage team folders

Team folders help admins manage team files and folders. You can share team folders with your entire Dropbox team, or with specific groups.

This article explains how to manage team folders, access to folders, and your team space.

Learn more about managing file and folder permissions.

How to create a team folder

To create a team folder as a team member:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click ☑ New folder.
  3. In the pop-up window, select a location enter a name under Folder name.
  4. Choose to share the new team folder with Everyone with access to [Team folder name] or Only specific people.
  5. Click Create.
  6. If you chose to share the folder with only specific people, a pop-up window will appear. Enter the names of the groups or individuals you’d like to share the team folder with, then click the dropdown to select whether to give people edit or view-only access.
    • You can also invite groups to the team folder by entering a group name. Learn how to set up groups.
  7. Click Share.
    • Note: The team folder is only shared with people after you enter their name(s) or email(s) and click Share. If you cancel out of this screen without adding anyone, the team folder won’t be shared with anyone else but you can still access and manage it in your Dropbox account.  

How to rename a team folder

Admins can always rename team folders. Depending on your team’s top-level content management setting, team members may also be able to rename team folders they have edit access to.

To rename a team folder or subfolder:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the folder you’d like to rename and click ☑ (more options).
  3. Click Rename.
  4. Enter the new name and press the enter key.

How to copy or move a team folder

Depending on your team’s top-level content management setting:

  • Team members can move subfolders to the top level of the team space.
  • Team members can move top-level team folders out of the team space or nest them inside other folders.
  • If these actions are restricted, only admins can perform them.

To copy or move a file or folder from a team folder into your member folder:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Go to the file or folder you want to copy.
  3. Hover over the folder and click  (more options).
  4. Click Copy or Move.
  5. Select your member folder and click Copy or Move.

How to delete a team folder

To delete a team folder:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Go to the team folder you want to delete.
  3. Hover over the folder and click ☑ (more options).
  4. Click Delete.
  5. Click Delete for everyone to confirm.

When a team folder is deleted, it’s removed from the team space.

How to add or remove people from team folders

Admins can manage who can add or remove people from a team folder in the admin console. Some team members may also be able to change this setting.

To manage access to a team folder:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Under Products, click the dropdown to the left of Dropbox.
  4. Click Content.
  5. Navigate to the folder you want to manage.
  6. Click ☑ (more options).
  7. Select Manage access.
    • Note: You’ll see a list of names and groups of everyone who can access the folder.
  8. Click the dropdown next to the name of the person or group to change their access:
    • Select Can edit or Can view from the dropdown to change their permissions.
    • Click Remove, then click Remove again to remove their permissions entirely.
    • To add people, type their name and click Share.

 

To manage access for individuals within a team folder:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Members.
  4. Click Manage access next to a member’s name.
  5. Check or uncheck team folders to modify access for individual members.
  6. For checked folders, select Can edit or Can view from the dropdown.
  7. Click Apply.

How to move a shared folder into a team folder

Team members and admins can move a shared folder into the team space as long as the following requirements are met:

  1. The folder is owned by someone on the same team as the user who’s moving it into the team space.
  2. The user has edit access to the folder they’re trying to move. To check:
    1. Hover over the folder, click ☑ (more options).
    2. Click Manage permissions.
      • See if the user has Can edit to the right of their name or group.
  3. The Manage access setting is set to Folder members. To check this:
    1. Click ☑ (more options).
    2. Hover over ☑ (share).
    3. Select ☑ (share with Dropbox).
    4. Click ☑ (settings).
    5. Click Folder settings.
    6. The dropdown next to Manage who can add people will show you who has access to this folder.
      • Team members who can edit, or Only the owner will be shown.

How to manage the team space

Certain types of admins can control the top-level folders in the team space. Top level folders are the ones that host any sub-folders, and the team space contains member folders and team folders.

Learn more about your team space.  

How to manage who can create top-level team folders

To manage who can create team folders at the top level of the team space:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Under Products, click the dropdown to the left of Dropbox.
  4. Click Settings.
  5. Click the Content tab.
  6. Under Content Tools, click the dropdown next to Top-level folder management.
  7. Select All members or Admins only.
    • Note: If set to All members, all team members will be able to create, rename, move, or delete top-level team folders.

Team members with edit access to the top level of a team space can convert shared folders to team folders. They can also convert team folders to normal folders.  

How to manage access to a team folder

To manage who can view or edit a team folder:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Under Products, click the dropdown to the left Dropbox.
  4. Click Content.
  5. Click ☑ (more options) next to the team folder name.
  6. Click Manage access.
  7. Click the dropdown next to a group or user name to change their permissions.
    • Click Can edit to give them edit access.
    • Click Can view to give them view-only access.
    • Click Remove to remove access completely.  

To manage permissions for a team folder:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Under Products, click the dropdown to the left of Dropbox.
  4. Click Content.
  5. Click ☑ (more options) next to the team folder.
  6. Click Manage access.
  7. Click ☑ (settings).
  8. Click the dropdown next to Manage who can add people and select permissions for the folder:
    • Team members who can edit: Team members with edit access can add or remove people from the folder.
    • Only Team Admins: Team members with edit access can’t add or remove people from the folder.
  9. Click Save.

To manage permissions for individual team members within a team folder:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Members.
  4. Click Manage access next to the individual.
  5. Check or uncheck team folders to modify access for individual members.
  6. For checked team folders, select Can edit or Can view from the dropdown. 
  7. Click Apply.  

How to create a top-level folder

If you’re an admin, learn how to create a team folder from the admin console.

How to manage access to top-level folders

To manage access to a folder that’s at the top level of the team space:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Under Products, click the dropdown to the left of Dropbox.
  4. Click Content.
  5. Hover over the folder you’d like to manage access to and click ☑ (more options) next to the folder.
  6. Select Manage access.
    • Note: You’ll see a list of names and groups of everyone who can access this team folder.
  7. Click the dropdown next to the name of the person or group to modify their access.
    • Select Can edit or Can view from the dropdown to change their permissions.
    • Click Remove, then click Remove again to remove their permissions entirely.
    • To add people, type their name and click Share.  

How to access a team member’s folder

Team admins on Advanced, Business Plus, and Enterprise can access team member’s personal folders using log in as member.

[Learn more about personal folders.

](#how-to-get-started-with-the-team-space)

To access a team member’s folder from the Content page:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Members.
  4. Click More next to the user.
  5. Click Log in as member.
  6. Click Sign in to confirm.
  7. When you’re done, click Logged in as [X] in the top right and select Switch back.

 Learn more about logging in as a member.

How to manage your team in Dropbox Dash

If you’re an admin on a Dropbox Dash team, you can invite or remove team members, as well as assign licenses to them in the admin console.

To access the admin console:

  1. Log in to dash.ai with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Account in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Admin console.

How to manage and assign licenses to new members

You can also assign licenses to team members for different products in the admin console.

To assign or remove licenses:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Members.
  4. Find the team member you’d like to assign or remove licenses for.
  5. Click ① (add) or ② (edit) under Products.
  6. Click ① Assign or ③ Remove next to the product you’d like to assign or remove a license for.
  7. Click Confirm.

How to invite team members

To invite new members:

  1. Log in to dash.ai with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Members.
  4. Click Invite members.
  5. Enter the email addresses for the members you’d like to invite.
  6. Click Invite.

If your team account also includes Dropbox file storage and you send an invite to someone outside of your company domain who already has a Dropbox account, they can join your Dash team using a different email address than the one you sent the invite to. You’ll receive an email letting you know which email they’ve used to sign up for the team.

How to remove team members

When you delete a team member’s account, several things happen:

  • The team member receives an email notifying them that an admin deleted their account and that they no longer have access.
  • An admin will need to transfer the team member’s content, including Stacks, to another member.

To remove a team member:

  1. Log in to dash.ai with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Members.
  4. Locate the member whose account you want to remove. You can use the search bar or scroll through the list of members.
  5. Click ☑ (more options) next to the member’s name and select Delete Member.
  6. Click ☑ (more options) next to the member’s name, then select Delete Member.
    • A confirmation window with options for transferring the member’s Stacks and content will appear.
  7. Choose when to transfer the team member’s Stacks and content:
    • Click Transfer Now to transfer their content immediately, then enter another team member’s email address who should inherit the content.
    • Click Transfer Later to choose later. Learn more details about how to transfer files from a deleted team member. 

How to move files between a team and personal account

If you have a Dropbox team account and a personal account, you can log in to both accounts on the same computer and drag and drop files from one account to the other.   

To do so:

  1. Connect your accounts.
  2. Open your Dropbox desktop app preferences.
  3. Click the Account tab.
  4. If you’re already logged in to your work account, click the Personal tab. Or, if you’re already logged in to your personal account, click the tab with your organization’s name.
  5. Click the Link button.
  6. Enter the password for your second account.
  7. In Explorer (Windows) or Finder (Mac), you’ll now see two Dropbox folders. You can open one folder, select the files you want to move, and drag and drop them into your other folder.    

If you have multiple Dropbox Professional, Family, Plus, or Basic accounts, learn how to move files between accounts.

How to move files between two Dropbox accounts

The easiest way to move files between accounts is through a shared folder.  

Dropbox team accounts: Learn how to move files between your two accounts.  

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox helps you effortlessly share files and folders.

From your first account

  1. Log in to the account that has the files you’d like to move.
  2. Create a shared folder and invite your second account.
  3. Manually move files by dragging and dropping them into your newly created shared folder.
  4. Log out of this account.

From your second account

  1. Log in to dropbox.com using the email address for your second account.
  2. Click Shared in the left sidebar. 
  3. Hover over the folder you just shared and click Join folder.
  4. The folder will open and you can now move the files from that folder to other places in your Dropbox account.

Once the files are moved out of the shared folder, they’re no longer accessible from the first account.

How to organize Dropbox files and folders

Staying organized from the start means less time tracking down and managing files like documents, photos, and videos. Here’s how to get started:

Create a folder hierarchy

  • Give every file a designated home. 
  • Group folders and subfolders into categories that make sense to you.
  • Add or create fewer folders at the top level, then add more as you go deeper.

Any changes you make in your file or folder structure appear across your connected devices and the Dropbox website. 

Learn more about syncing your files and folders across your devices and on dropbox.com.

Establish a naming convention

  • Alphabetical order
  • Chronological order (YYYY-MM-DD)
  • Numerical order
  • By group (i.e., client, location, file type)
  • Something that will help you remember

Learn more about using naming conventions to organize your Dropbox account.

Add tags to files and folders

Locate file and folders quickly by adding tags. You can tag files by:

  • The topics they relate to
  • The projects they’re part of
  • The team(s) who owns them

To search your files and folders by tag, use the search bar at the top of your screen. You can also remove tags from a selected file or folder by clicking the X to the right of the tag.

Learn more about using tags to organize your Dropbox account.

How to pin files and folders

If you want to organize your Dropbox files and folders into sections for easy retrieval, you can now do so with Quick access.

What is Quick access?

Quick access allows you to organize files and folders into sections to quickly access them from the left sidebar on dropbox.com. These sections are private to you. Files and folders that you star will automatically be placed in a section named Starred.

Other people can’t see how you organize sections in the Quick access tab. Rearranging files and folders in the Quick access tab doesn’t affect other people.

Learn more about Quick access.

How to rename a file or folder

You can rename files or folders in your Dropbox account in three different ways:

  • On dropbox.com
  • From the Dropbox mobile app
  • From the Dropbox desktop application

You can also rename shared folders.

Renaming on dropbox.com

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click All files in the left sidebar. 
    • You can also click Folders in the left navigation bar to locate your file.
  3. Select the name of the folder you want to rename.
  4. Hover over the name of the file or folder and click   (more options).
    • If you’re in grid view, click   (more options).
  5. Click Rename.

Renaming on the Dropbox desktop app

On your computer, rename the file or folder as you normally would. For example, click the file, wait a moment, and then click the filename again to edit it.

The new name appears on all devices linked to your Dropbox account and on dropbox.com.

How to rename documents in Dropbox Sign

When you rename a document, the change will only reflect in your Dropbox Sign account. Anyone else who has access to the document will still see the original name.

To rename a document:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Click Documents in the left sidebar.
  3. Hover over the  (vertical ellipsis) next to the documents you’d like to rename.
  4. Click Rename.
  5. Type what you’d like to name the document.
  6. Click OK.

How to restore files and folders with Dropbox Backup

You can easily restore your backed up files and folders to a new computer if things go wrong. 

To restore your entire computer backup to a new computer:

  1. Download the Dropbox desktop app on your new computer.
    • If you have an existing backup, you’ll be prompted to restore from your backup.
    • If you have more than one existing backup, select your preferred backup from the dropdown.
  2. Click Confirm.
  3. Click OK.

You can use your computer as normal while your restoration completes in the background. Once it’s complete, click OK on the notification that appears.

To only restore a part of your computer backup or any part of your external hard drive backup to a new computer:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click ☑ (dense grid organization) in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Backup from the menu that appears.
    • Dropbox Backup will open in a new tab.
  4. Click Mac or PC.
  5. Check the boxes next to the folders you’d like to download.
  6. Click Download.

You can also restore recently deleted folders within Dropbox Backup on your computer or external hard drive. To do this:

  1. Click the Dropbox icon in your taskbar (Windows) or menu bar (Mac).
  2. Click the Sync and Backups tab.
  3. Select the backup you’d like to restore.
  4. Click View backed up files.
  5. Click Show deleted files.
  6. Check the box to the left of the deleted folder (will display the trash icon) you’d like to restore.
  7. Click Restore.
  8. Click Restore all files.

Learn more about Dropbox Backup.

How to set up Dropbox Backup

Dropbox Backup allows you to automatically back up files and folders from your computer and external drives to Dropbox, ensuring they’re safely stored in the cloud and easily accessible from anywhere.

Before setting up a backup, make sure to:

  • Check your available storage and that you’re within your plan’s limits. Learn how to check which plan you’re on.
  • Close all open files and applications on your computer.
  • Install the Dropbox desktop app, if you haven’t already.
  • Resume syncing if you’ve paused it. Learn how to resume syncing.
  • Connect to the internet.
  • While the updated Dropbox Backup can back up files and folders that are also backed up with other providers, like iCloud, Google Drive, and OneDrive, we recommend you disable those backups before using Dropbox Backup to prevent conflicts between backups.

To set up a backup:

  1. Click ☑ (Dropbox) in your taskbar 0 (Windows), or menu bar (Mac).
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Preferences.
  4. Click the Backups tab.
  5. Click Manage backups.

 

  1. Under Add a backup, select the computer or external hard drive you’d like to back up.
  2. Click Let’s get started (computer) or Back up [drive name] (external hard drive).
  3. Check the boxes next to the folders you’d like to back up.
  4. Click Set up or Back up.
  5. If you’re on a Mac, click OK when prompted to give Dropbox permission to access your folders.

You can use your computer normally while the back up is in progress. 

 

If any files or folders fail to back up, they’ll appear in your sync error queue. To view those files:

  1. Click ☑ (Dropbox) in your taskbar (Windows) or menu bar (Mac).
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click View sync issues.

Learn more about troubleshooting sync issues.

How to share Stacks with Dropbox Dash

You can share your Stacks both inside and outside your organization. You can do so by adding people directly through their email, or by copying a link to the Stack and pasting it where you’d like to share the Stack.

How to set sharing permissions for Dropbox files and folders in Stacks

Anyone with the Stack link can access the content it contains. However, if the content is stored in Dropbox, access still depends on the file’s sharing settings. Only content with link-based access enabled can be opened.

How to turn off Stack-based access

To prevent Stack links from granting access to Dropbox content, you can enable link restrictions on the content’s parent folder.

When link restrictions are enabled:

  • Stack links will only work for those who already have access to the files or folders in Dropbox
  • All link-based sharing is turned off for that content, including traditional shared links outside of Dash

Learn how to manage sharing permissions for Dropbox content.

This setting affects everyone with access to the parent folder, including people who may have added the content to a Stack. Use this option when you need tighter control over who can view or open your files, regardless of how they’re shared.

Learn how to manage Stack permissions.

How to sort Dropbox files and folders

You can sort and filter files and folders on dropbox.com by Name, Modified, Who can access, Type, Extension, Size, and Tags. To do so:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click Home in the left navigation bar.
  3. Click All files in the left sidebar. All your files and folders will display on the main page.
  4. You can sort and filter your files using the following options:
    • To view files you’ve accessed recently, click Recents on the main page.
    • To view your starred files and folders, click Starred on the main page.
    • Hover over a column header and click the arrow to sort by ascending or descending order. You’ll see options to add, remove, or reorder columns. You can also rearrange columns by clicking and holding the title column name, then dragging and dropping it to a new location. 
    • To resize columns, hover over the column header and click the vertical lines that appear. Then, drag and resize the columns horizontally. 
    • To change views, click the list icon (four horizontal lines) in the upper-right corner of your file list. You can choose from Grid, Large grid, List, or Large list views.

How to star a Dropbox Sign template

You can star templates and template links for easy access. When you star a template or template link, it’s starred only for you, not for anyone else who you’ve shared the template or template link with.

To star or unstar a template or template link:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Select Templates in the left sidebar.
  3. Click My Templates on the dropdown menu.
  4. Click the star icon next to the template or template link you’d like to sta or unstar.

To view your starred templates and template links:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Select Templates in the left sidebar.
  3. Click My Templates on the dropdown menu.
  4. Click Starred above the templates list.

How to star files and folders

You can star files and folders for easy access on dropbox.com and the Dropbox mobile app. 

When you star a file or folder, it’s starred only for you. It’s not starred for anyone else who shares the file or folder.

How to store shortcuts to webpages in your Dropbox folder

You can store a shortcut to a webpage in a Dropbox folder, just like you would store a file. Shortcuts are stored with the file extension .web and are represented by a globe icon. Shortcuts open in your default web browser.

Create a shortcut in Dropbox

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Navigate to the folder you’d like to store your shortcut in.
  3. Click Create.
  4. Hover over More and click Shortcut.
  5. Enter the URL and Name for your shortcut.
  6. Click Create.

Rename, move, copy, or delete a shortcut

You can rename, move, copy, or delete a shortcut exactly the same way you would a regular file. However, you can’t edit the URL itself.

Can I share a shortcut?

You can’t share a .web shortcut you’ve stored in Dropbox. Instead, you would send the URL itself.

You can, however, share the folder the shortcut is stored in. The shortcut will open for anyone you share the folder with.

Save a webpage as a PDF to Dropbox

If you want to save a webpage as a PDF to Dropbox instead of a shortcut, follow the steps below.

  1. Open Safari on your iOS device.
  2. Navigate to the webpage you wish to save.
  3. Tap ☑ (share arrow).
  4. Tap Options.
  5. Select PDF, then tap Done.
  6. Tap the Dropbox mobile app icon.
  7. Choose a folder to save the PDF to.
  8. Tap Upload.

A PDF of the webpage will be saved to the Dropbox folder you selected.

How to tell if you’re on the team space experience for Dropbox team accounts

Not all Dropbox team accounts have access to the same experience. While most Dropbox team accounts are on the team space experience, a small percentage are not. The team space experience comes with its own ways to navigate, organize, and collaborate on content. 

Knowing whether you’re on the team space experience makes it easier to find relevant help center articles, organize your files, and communicate with your team. To find out if you’re on the team space experience, log in to dropbox.com:

  • If you see a folder icon with one person on it, then you have the team space experience. Learn more about the team space experience.
  • If you don’t see this folder, then your team uses team folders and is not on the team space experience. Learn more about team folders.

How to transfer ownership of a Paper doc

If you’re a member of a Dropbox team account, you can easily transfer ownership of a Paper doc to another member of the same team. Team admins can also transfer ownership of any doc that they currently have access to.

To transfer doc ownership:

  1. Open a Paper doc.
  2. Click Invite.
  3. Click the dropdown beside the name of the person you’d like to transfer ownership to.
    • If you don’t see their name, share the doc using their email address first.
  4. Select Make owner.

How to unfollow a Paper doc

Unfollowing (or unsubscribing) from a doc will turn off email notifications about doc updates. You’ll still see the doc in your file list and have access to it. By default, you follow all docs you own or edit.  

To unfollow or unsubscribe from a Paper doc:

  1. Open the Paper doc you’d like to unfollow. 
  2. Click the … (ellipsis) icon.
  3. Uncheck Following. 

To change your Paper notification preferences:

  1. Click the bell (Notifications) icon in the upper right corner of a Paper doc.
  2. Click the gear icon next to Mark all as read.
  3. In the Paper section at the bottom, uncheck any notifications you want to unsubcribe from. 

How to unsubscribe from notifications on a comment thread

To unsubscribe from notifications on a specific comment thread:

  1. Open the email notification about that comment thread. 
  2. Scroll to the bottom and click unsubscribe from this thread.

How to update Dropbox Backup

Dropbox is continuing to update Dropbox Backup. The updated experience provides more control and flexibility when managing backups.

With the updated Dropbox Backup, you can:

  • Back up more folders. Select any folder within your computer’s home folder to back up, including subfolders. You’re no longer limited to folders like “Documents”, “Desktop”, and “Downloads”.
  • Schedule your backups. Get flexibility to schedule when your device backups occur.
  • View progress of your backups. Check the percentage of your backup progress to get more insight into your backup completion.
  • Quickly get back up and running. Get more options to kick off your backup restoration—from either the web or your computer.
  • Name your backups. Customize the name of your device backup so you can distinguish between multiple backups.
  • View backups for multiple devices in one place. If you have multiple devices backed up through Dropbox Backup, you can go to 0 to keep track of them.

If you haven’t been prompted to update and would like to be on the updated Dropbox Backup, you can do so by disabling Dropbox Backup, restarting the Dropbox app, and then re-enabling Dropbox Backup.

To restart the Dropbox desktop app:

  1. Click the Dropbox icon in your taskbar (Windows) or menu bar (Mac), and then click your profile picture or initials.
  2. Click Quit Dropbox.
  3. Open your applications menu, re-launch Dropbox, and then log in again (if necessary).

To delete Dropbox Backup:

  1. Click the Dropbox icon in your taskbar (Windows) or menu bar (Mac).
  2. Click your initials or avatar.
  3. Click Preferences.
  4. Click Backups.
  5. Click Manage backups.
    • If you see Set Up instead of Delete, it means Dropbox Backup is already off.
  6. Click Delete.

To re-enable Dropbox Backup:

  1. Click the Dropbox icon in your menu bar (Mac).
  2. Click your initials or avatar.
  3. Click Preferences.
  4. Click the Backups tab.
  5. Click Manage backup.
  6. Under Add a backup, select the computer you’d like to back up.
  7. Click Let’s get started.
  8. Check the boxes next to the folders you’d like to back up.
  9. Click Set up or Back up.
  10. Click OK when prompted to give Dropbox permission to access your folders.

How to use activity, notifications, and recent lists

The information in the desktop tray is unique to your account and shows the most recent activities that have occurred to the files and folders that you manage.  

This information is unique to your account and helps you access your most important files and folders. Information is accessible through the Dropbox desktop app, Dropbox mobile app, and dropbox.com.

Your activity and history

The Your activity feed shows the list of files and folders you recently opened or edited within your Dropbox history. If you’re a member of a Dropbox team account, you’ll also see the Team activity tab that shows your team’s shared activity.

To view your activity:

  1. Click the Dropbox icon in your notification center (Windows) or menu bar (Mac).
  2. Click the Your activity or Sharing activity tab.
    • If you’re a member of a Dropbox team account, you can switch between Your activity and Team activity to see your activity or your team’s shared-file activity.

Recents

On the mobile app and dropbox.com, your Recents feed is similar to your Activity feed but only focuses on your activity.  

To view your recent activity:

  • On dropbox.com, click All files in the left sidebar. Then,click the Recents tab under All files on the main page.
  • On the mobile app, tap the Home tab at the bottom, then tap Recent (Android) or Recents (iOS) near the top.

How to use AI organize on Dropbox DocSend

AI organize is a built-in, intelligent assistant that can draft a folder tree, and classify files to help keep your Space structured, searchable, and ready for sharing. 

Learn how to manage and customize your Space (data room).

Features of AI organize

Folder tree generator

The folder tree generator creates a recommended folder structure based on the type of data room you’re building.  After generating the folder tree, you can preview it before making any changes. If needed, you can make inline edits like renaming folders within the current version.

Sorting and classification

Sorting and classification uses AI to review your file names and metadata, then suggests where each file should go. It automatically groups related documents such as financials, legal materials, and HR files. Before any changes are made, you can review and confirm the suggested organization. For each file, you’ll see where it was moved from so you can track updates easily. Unknown or unrecognized files are handled separately so nothing gets lost.

All applied changes are recorded in an audit log, which you can reference for auditing or troubleshooting.

How to use AI organize

Use AI Organize prompt to create a folder structure in an empty Space

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Spaces. 
  3. Click Create Space. 
  4. Enter a prompt within the box under What are you building describing the data room you want to create.
    • Note: Make sure your description is detailed, and list needed features.
  5. Click   (send) to send the prompt. 
  6. To make changes, edit the folder structure directly or use conversational prompting.
  7. Click Add to Space to finalize.
How to use AI Organize to create a folder structure in an existing Space.
  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click the Space you want to organize.
  3. Click Organize.
  4. Select Organize with AI.
  5. Select Let AI edit and create folders.

6. To make changes, edit the folder structure directly or use conversational prompting.

  • Note: Click Discard changes and have it re-generate suggestions for the file structure for more options. 

7. Click Apply to retain changes.

How to use AI Organize to organize existing folders.

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click the Space you want to organize.
  3. Click Organize.
  4. Select Organizewith AI.
  5. Select Use existing folders.

AI Organize will sort your files into the folders that already exist in your space. 

Editing a suggested folder structure

After AI Organize generates a folder structure, you can review and customize it before applying any changes.

You can adjust the structure in several ways:

  • Edit folders directly by renaming, adding, removing, or reorganizing folders and subfolders.
  • Add new folders to expand the structure.
  • Collapse or expand folders to review different levels of the structure.
  • Use conversational prompting to ask for specific changes. 
  • Regenerate suggestions by clicking Discard changes and generating a new structure.

You can also provide additional context to improve results, such as: 

  • Describing what the Space is for.
  • Referencing how similar Spaces are organized.
  • Using templates or importing a folder structure from a CSV file.

All changes can be reviewed before applying them to your Space.

Conversational prompting 

To use conversational prompting to ask AI Organize to edit a folder structure: 

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Spaces. 
  3. Click Create Space. 
  4. Enter a prompt in the box under What are you building describing the data room you want to create.
  5. When the folders are generated, enter your prompts in the box under Need any changes describing any edits you want to make.
  6. Undo or save any changes you made: 
    • Click Undo to revert to the previous version.
    • Click Apply to save changes.

What AI organize doesn’t do

AI organize helps you create structure and order in your data room, but it never makes changes without your approval. 

To keep your content secure and your workflow predictable, there are a few things it won’t do:

  • It doesn’t apply changes automatically, you’ll always be able to review and confirm any changes.
  • It doesn’t delete or remove files from your account.
  • It won’t appear if AI features are turned off in your settings.

How to use Dropbox faster with keyboard shortcuts

Keyboard shortcuts help you use Dropbox faster. Keyboard shortcuts are available on dropbox.com.

On dropbox.com, click Files and press the ? key (question mark) to access the full keyboard shortcut menu. You can do the following actions using keyboard shortcuts.

  • Move between files or folders: ↑ or ↓ (up and down arrow keys)
  • Open a file or folder: Enter (enter or return key)
  • Search files and folders: / (forward slash key)

Select multiple files

Using keyboard shortcuts, you can select multiple files on dropbox.com.

To select multiple consecutive files or folders:

  1. Select the first item.
  2. Press and hold Shift.
  3. Click the last item.

To select multiple nonconsecutive files or folders:

  1. Press and hold Ctrl (control on Windows) or ⌘ (command on Mac).
  2. Select all files or folders you want.

How to use dynamic filters

Dynamic filters help you find content faster by showing filters that are unique to your files.

Features

  • Navigate through your content more precisely: Find what you’re looking for by using multiple filters to narrow your search in seconds.
  • Sort multiple content types in just a few clicks: Organize data thematically and easily locate content, regardless of file type.

How do dynamic filters work?

Powered by Dropbox-built AI, dynamic filters use the context of your folders and files to automatically generate personalized content filters.

Some examples are:

  • Content themes
  • File extensions 
  • Collaborators involved

Dynamic filters are generated using an internal machine learning model. This means that your data is not sent outside of Dropbox in order for dynamic filters to work. 

How to use dynamic filters

You’ll see an automatically generated set of custom filters above your file list on dropbox.com. Click on one or more at a time to activate the filters.

To hide the dynamic filters feature:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click the “⁝” (vertical ellipsis) next to the filters.
  3. Click Hide dynamic filters or Show dynamic filters.

How to use multi-file organize to sort Dropbox files

Multi-file organize helps you arrange your Dropbox content. The feature organizes your files using options such as date, keyword, or file activity. 

How to use multi-file organize

To use multi-file organize for your files on dropbox.com:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Open the folder you’d like to organize.
  3. Click the gear icon next to the folder name. 
  4. Click Organize.
  5. Select Multi-file organize from the dropdown.
  6. Select the filter option you’d like to apply. 
    • Learn more about filter options below.
  7. Click Preview.
    • This will open a preview that shows how the folder will look after organizing.
    • From the Preview screen, you can deselect any files you don’t want included in the grouping.
    • To apply multi-file organize to files that are moved into the folder in the future, check the box next to Apply rule every time a file is added to this folder.
  8. Click Apply.

How to use Quick access on Dropbox

With Quick access, you can organize your Dropbox files and folders into sections for easy access and retrieval.

What is Quick access?

Quick access allows you to organize files and folders into sections to quickly access them from the left sidebar on dropbox.com. These sections are private to you. Files and folders that you star will automatically be placed in a section named Starred.

Other people can’t see when you star a file, or how you organize sections in the Quick access tab. Rearranging files and folders in the Quick access tab doesn’t affect other people.

How to use Quick access

To create a new section
  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click ☑ (add) next to Quick access in the left sidebar. 
  3. Enter a name for the new section then click Create.
To add files or folders to a section
  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Scroll down to Quick access in the left sidebar. 
  3. Hover over the section you want to add files or folders to, then click + (add).
  4. Click Add items. 
  5. Choose the item or items you want to add, then click Choose. 
To move a file from one section to another section
  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Scroll down to Quick access in the left sidebar. 
  3. Hover over the file you want to move, then click ⁝ (more options). 
  4. Click Move to section. 
  5. Click the dropdown next to select a section, then choose a section. 
  6. Click Move. 
To remove a section
  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Scroll down to Quick access in the left sidebar. 
  3. Hover over the file you want to move, then click ⁝ (more options). 
  4. Click Remove from section.

How to use Stacks with Dropbox Dash

Stacks allow you to organize and collaborate on all types of content, including files, apps, and browser links, in one place and share them instantly both inside and outside of your team.

Not using Dropbox Dash yet? Organize, share, and collaborate with Stacks.  

How to create a Stack

You can create Stacks on dash.ai, by using the desktop app, or through the browser extension.

How to manage suggested Stacks

Dash will create Stacks based on your activity in Dash. You can keep these Stacks made by Dash or remove them from your Dash home feed.

To keep a Stack made by Dash:

  1. Log in to dash.ai.
  2. Click Preview on the Stack you want to keep.
  3. Click Keep.
    • Note: You can remove a suggested Stack from the preview screen by selecting Remove from the “Is this Stack helpful?” prompt.

To remove a Stack made by Dash:

  1. Log in to dash.ai.
  2. Navigate to the Stack you want to remove.
  3. Click Remove.

Stacks made by Dash have the same functionality as any other Stack created by you. 

How to add a group of tabs to a Stack

You can add a group of tabs directly to a Stack using the Dropbox Dash browser extension.

To do so:

  1. Open each page you’d like to add to the Stack as a separate tab.
  2. Hold Shift and click the first and last tab in the range of tabs you’d like to add to your Stack.
    • You can also hold control (Windows) or command (macOS) and click each tab you’d like to add individually.
  3. Enter a name for your Stack.
  4. Click Create.

A tab will open with your new Stack.

How to manage Stack permissions

Stack permissions allow you to control who can view or edit a stack. As the owner of a Stack, you can change these permissions at any time.

  1. Log in to dash.ai.
    • You can also open the desktop app by pressing control-shift-e (Windows) or command-shift-e (macOS).
  2. Click Stacks in the left sidebar.
  3. Select the Stack you’d like to edit.
  4. Click Share.
  5. Click Can view or Can edit next to the person whose permissions you’d like to edit.
  6. Select Can edit, Can view, or Remove as needed.

How to comment on Stacks

If you can edit a Stack, you can leave a comment on any item that’s part of that Stack, to add context or direct other team members to specific items. 

To comment on a Stack:

  1. Log in to dash.ai.
    • You can also open the Dash desktop app by pressing control-shift-e (Windows) or command-shift-e (macOS).
  2. Click Stacks in the left sidebar.
  3. Select the Stack you’d like to add a comment to.
  4. Click  ①(comment), or right-click the item and then select ①Comments, next to the item’s name.
  5. Enter your comment, then click Post.

Click ① to delete or ① to edit next to the comment you’d like to change.

If you’re not an admin, you can set link restrictions for individual folders that you own.  

To do this:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the name of the folder and click Share.
  3. In the popup, click ☑(settings).
  4. Select the Folder settings tab.
  5. Toggle Link restrictions to On.

How to manage Stack notifications

You’ll be notified by email when:

  • The name of the Stack is changed
  • Items are added or deleted from the Stack
  • The Stack is archived or unarchived
  • A comment is posted on an item that you added to the Stack
  • A response is posted to one of your comments
  • The Stack description is changed

To turn notifications for stack activity on or off:

  1. Log in to dash.ai.
  2. Click ☑ Stacks in the left sidebar.
  3. Select the Stack you’d like to toggle notifications for.
  4. Click ☑ (settings) next to the name of the Stack.
  5. Click Turn on notifications or Turn off notifications as required.

If you’ve installed the Dropbox Dash browser extension, you’ll also receive a push notification in your browser whenever someone shares a Stack with you. Clicking this notification will open the Stack that’s been shared in a new tab.

To turn this notification on or off:

  1. Log in to dash.ai.
  2. Click Account in the left sidebar.
  3. Select Settings from the dropdown.
  4. Scroll to Extension under the General tab.
  5. Click the toggle next to Notify me when someone shares a Stack with me to turn notifications on or off.

How to use the diligence tracker feature
