Learn how to use the diligence tracker in Dropbox DocSend to request, collect, and track documents from visitors during due diligence or other structured workflows. You can assign tasks, set due dates, and monitor progress without relying on spreadsheets or email threads.  

How to create tasks in your Space (data room)

Use the diligence tracker to request specific files, forms, or information from visitors and organize the uploads directly within your data room. Each task includes an assignee, optional due date, and a destination folder where uploaded documents will appear. You can also view an audit log of all task updates or changes that occur within your space.

To create a task manually:

  1. Log in to docsend.com. 
  2. Click Spaces (data rooms) in the left-side bar.
  3. Navigate to the Space (data room) you’d like to create a task for.
  4. Click Diligence tracker in the left-side bar.
  5. Click Create task.
  6. Type a task name in the title box. 
  7. Type the email(s) for the individual you want to assign tasks.
  8. Set a due date.
  9. Type a task description.
  10. Choose the folder location within your Space where files should be uploaded. 
  11. Add any necessary attachments for the assignee from within your Space. 
  12. Click Save.

To notify assignees who haven’t yet been invited to your Space of their assigned tasks:

  1. Click Grant access from the Diligence tracker home.
  2. Click Invite now.
  3. Click Done.

Assigned tasks are emailed to recipients, and the assigner receives notifications as each task is completed.

To create multiple tasks using a CSV file:

  1. Log in to docsend.com. 
  2. Click Spaces (data rooms) in the left-side bar.
  3. Navigate to the Space (data room) you’d like to create a task for.
  4. Click Diligence tracker in the left-side bar.
  5. Click Import tasks. 
  6. Click Download the CSV template.
    • Note: The CSV template must be used to ensure the task fields upload correctly.
  7. Fill out the CSV template.
  8. Click Import tasks.
  9. Click Choose file. 
  10. Upload the completed CSV template. 
  11. Click Save.  

How to manage tasks (admin)

The diligence tracker provides admins with a centralized view of all tasks, including assignees, due dates, and completion status, with built-in tools for managing them.

From the diligence tracker page, admins and account owners can:

  • Review pending, completed, declined, or overdue tasks.
  • Open a task to view uploaded files or comments.
  • Update the task’s assignee, due date, or status.
  • Update the Space file location where assignees upload documents.
  • Reopen a task if the submission is incorrect, and add a note explaining what needs to be fixed.
  • Apply bulk actions to update multiple tasks at once.
  • Filter tasks by Assignee, Status, or Due date. 

To manage a task:

  1. Select the desired task.
  2. Click  (more options).
  3. Select Edit, Delete, Mark Complete.

To manage individual tasks:

  1. Click  (more options) next to the task you want to edit.
  2. Manually change the Task name, Assignee, Due date, Description, Space file location, or Attachments. 
  3. Click Save.

To manually change the status of a task:

  1. Check the box next to the task you want to update. 
  2. Click (edit). 
  3. Update the status.
  4. Click Save.

To manage multiple tasks at once:

  1. Check the box next to Task name to manage all available tasks, or check the individual boxes next to the tasks you want to manage in bulk.
  2. Click (edit). 
  3. Update desired fields. 
  4. Click Save.

All tasks will be updated in bulk and reflect your changes. 

To reopen a task that’s been declined:

  1. Select the desired task.
  2. Click  (more options).
  3. Click Request changes.
  4. Provide feedback for requested changes. 
  5. Click Send request. 

An email will be sent notifying the recipient of the requested changes and will reopen the task.  

How to complete tasks as a visitor

When admins assign you tasks, you’ll receive an email notification with a link to sign in to the diligence tracker. Once signed in, you’ll see a focused list of tasks assigned to you, where you can upload documents, provide information, or complete other requested actions.

To access your assigned tasks:

  1. Click the invite email in your inbox.
  2. Click View content.
  3. Type your email address.
  4. Click Confirm.
  5. Go back to your inbox. 
  6. Click the email verifying your identity.
  7. Click Verify email address.

You’ll be taken to the diligence tracker home page. 

To complete a task:

  1. Select the individual task to view assigned details.
  2. Upload the requested file(s) within the task.
  3. Click Submit for review.

Decline a task

If a visitor believes a task doesn’t apply to them:

  1. Select the individual task to view assigned details.
  2. Select Decline task.
  3. Provide feedback for declining.
  4. Click Decline to confirm.

If a submission is rejected

If an admin reopens a task, the visitor will see a note explaining why. They can upload a new file and resubmit.

Task email reminders

You will receive reminder emails both when tasks are due, and in weekly summary emails when tasks are overdue.

Manage email reminders

You can manage email reminders for your tasks:

  1. Log in to docsend.com. 
  2. Click (Settings).
  3. Check or uncheck desired notifications.

Notification settings

Admins can change the email notification settings for the diligence tracker. Learn more about how to change Email notification settings.

How to use the Dropbox DocSend Q&A feature

Overview

The Q&A feature allows visitors to submit questions about content directly within a shared DocSend space. Admins and collaborators can manage these questions by accessing the Q&A tab within the Space. When a visitor submits a question, the Space owner and assigned collaborators receive an email notification with a direct link to the question, allowing for quick responses. This feature helps centralize communication and keeps all inquiries related to the shared content organized in one place.

How to access Q&A

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Navigate to the desired Space.
  3. Click Q&A in the left side bar to view and respond to questions.

The requestor will receive an email with your response.

How to respond to a question

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Q&A in the left side bar.
  3. Click Expand and reply next to the question you want to respond to.
  4. Type your response in the text box.
  5. Click Publish.

When publishing a response to a question it will automatically email the individual who asked the question and will be visible to all visitors. 

How to edit a question

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Q&A in the left side bar.
  3. Click (more options) next to the question you want to edit.
  4. Edit the question, the answer, or both.
  5. Click Save.

An email notification will be sent to the user who posted the question detailing the changes that were made.

How to disable publishing questions and answers to all visitors

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Q&A in the left side bar.
  3. Toggle off next to Publish.

The questions and answers no longer be public to visitors. 

How to change the status of a question

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Q&A in the left side bar.
  3. Under Status, click the dropdown menu.
    1. Select Replied to indicate the question has been responded to.
    2. Select Decline to indicate the question will not be addressed. 

How to delete a question

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Q&A in the left side bar.
  3. Click ☑ (more options) next to the question you desire to delete.
  4. Select Delete question from the dropdown menu.

How to deactivate Q&A

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Q&A in the left side bar.
  3. Click Allow visitor questions at the top of the page.
  4. Select Visitor questions disabled from the dropdown menu.

How to submit a question as a visitor

  1. Log in to docsend.com or create a View only account.
  2. Click Q&A in the left side bar.
  3. Click Add question in the upper-right corner.
  4. Type your question in the text box.
  5. Click Publish.

A published question will be visible to all visitors.

How to verify files in search results

Verified files, marked with a blue checkmark, appear at the top of search results when a member enters the exact phrase designated by an admin. This checkmark signifies that an admin has reviewed and confirmed the file as the most relevant and up-to-date resource. By verifying files, your team can quickly access accurate information, reducing the time typically spent sifting through search results.

For example, if multiple versions of a policy, procedure, or strategy document exist, the verified checkmark helps team members quickly identify the official version, preventing confusion and ensuring consistency across teams. It‘s also useful when duplicate copies of files are stored in different locations, allowing employees to find and rely on the correct, organization-approved version.

How to mark a file as verified

Admins can mark files as verified directly from the search results page. This pins the file to the top of the search results when team members search for relevant keywords or phrases.

To mark a file as verified:

  1. Open Dash.
  2. Search for the file by entering a keyword or phrase in the search bar.
  3. Locate the file in search results, hover over it, and click ② (manage verification).
    • To improve visibility, enter relevant search phrase in the Search terms field and click and click (add). For example, enter “company holidays” to ensure the most recent holiday schedule appears at the top of the search results when a member searches for that phrase. 
    • Repeat this step for each additional phrase.
  4. Click Done.

How to view file activity in Dropbox

File activity is a list of all activity on a file, folder, or project. It includes any time a file is:

  • Added
  • Edited
  • Moved
  • Renamed
  • Reverted back to a previous version with version history or Dropbox Rewind

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox helps you effortlessly share files and folders.

View file activity

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click a file to open its preview.
    • Make sure you have your previews set to Full screen.
  3. Click File in the top-left corner.
  4. Click Activity.
    • The Activity tab will open on the left, where you can see who performed an action and when the action happened. 

You can also see sharing actions, including when:

  • The file was shared
  • Member roles changed
  • The file was unshared

If you’ve enabled viewer info, you can also see who viewed a file and whether they’re currently viewing that file.

How to view metadata for a file in Dropbox

Metadata is information you can see about a file. It includes information like the date your file was created and the size of the file.

To see metadata about a folder:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the folder and click “⁝” (vertical ellipsis).
  3. Click Folder info.  

To see metadata about a file:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click the name of the file you’d like to see information about. 
    • If you’ve opened the preview in Full screen, click File.
  3. Click File info.
    • If you’ve opened the preview in Full screen, click Info.

In the details pane, you’ll see different types of information depending on the type of file you’re previewing. All files display the following metadata:

  • The location of the file (Saved in)
  • The size of the file in bytes (Size)
  • When the file was last modified (Modified) 
  • The type of file (Type)Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox helps you effortlessly share files and folders.

File-specific metadata

Some types of files display specific metadata in addition to the basic metadata listed above. For more information, refer to the lists of metadata by file type below.

Image files
  • Aperture
  • Artist
  • Camera make
  • Camera model
  • Caption
  • Category
  • Color profile
  • Copyright
  • Creator
  • Credits
  • Date created
  • Description
  • Dimensions
  • Dots per inch (DPI)
  • Dots per centimeter (DPCM)
  • Flash
  • Focal length
  • Headline
  • ISO
  • Keywords
  • Lens model
  • LicensorURL
  • Metering
  • Orientation
  • Rights usage terms
  • Shutter speed
  • Title
  • White balance
Microsoft Office files
  • Title
  • Copyright Notice
  • Revision Number
  • Pages
  • Paragraphs
  • Words
  • Characters

Manage content in a Dropbox DocSend Space (data room)

Add content to your Space (data room) to prepare it for sharing by uploading files, adding content from your library, or connecting apps to import content. 

You can update, remove, and restore content in your Space at any time, even after sharing, and notify visitors when updates are made. Learn more about Space notifications.

Undo upload content

If you uploaded the wrong content and want to undo that action, click X (remove) beside the content you wish to remove, or click Cancel.

You can also create a file request to allow visitors to upload files directly into your Space. Uploaded files are immediately visible to collaborators. Learn more about file requests. 

Content accessibility in a Space

You can manage content accessibility in a Space at any time, even after sharing the Space.

To manage Space accessibility

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Spaces.
  3. Toggle Active to Yes or No next to the Space you’d like to manage accessibility for.

To manage content accessibility

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Spaces.
  3. Click your Space. 
  4. Toggle Visible to Yes or No next to the content you’d like to manage accessibility for.

You can update existing content in a Space from Content library. When you update content, all associated links will automatically update to reflect the latest version. Learn more about updating content.

How archiving works

  • Archived content doesn’t count toward your asset limit.
  • You can restore content at any time, and it will become searchable again.
  • Removing content from a Space doesn’t affect historical visit data. If you select Delete from the Content library, content is moved to the ‘Deleted content’ folder, not Trash. It will be permanently deleted after 30 days. Learn more about deleting content.
  • Visitors aren’t notified of changes unless automatic notifications are enabled.

Move content in a Space

To move one or more items in a Space: 

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Spaces.
  3. Click your Space. 
  4. Check the checkbox beside the item or items you want to move.
  5. Click Move.
  6. Click Change to choose a destination folder.
  7. Click Move.

Organize content with Space folders

Organize content in your Space using folders, folder structures, sections, templates, or AI Organize. Learn more about AI Organize for customers on the Advanced Data Rooms plan.

Space folders and folder structures

Space folders help you group content into subfolders by stage, topic, or workflow.

You can create a folder structure in several ways:

  • Create folders manually.
  • Import from another Space.
  • Use a template.
  • Upload a CSV file.
  • Use AI Organize to generate a structure.

Each Space can hold: 

  • 2,000 assets (Advanced, Enterprise)
  • 4,000 assets (Advanced Data Rooms)

Each folder can contain up to 200 assets, and subfolders count toward your Space’s total asset limit. Folders can’t be shared individually however, the Space link can be shared. Learn more about file upload limitations.

Create a folder in a Space manually

To create a single folder:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Spaces.
  3. Click an existing Space or create a new Space.
  4. Click Create folder.
    •  To hide the folder from visitors, click Change beside Folder will be visible to Space visitors and use the toggle to choose Hidden from Space visitors.
  5. Name your folder and click Create.

You can now click the new folder and add content.

To import a folder structure from another Space:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Spaces.
  3. Click Create Space.
  4. Click Another Space next to Or import a folder structure from, under the prompt box. 
  5. Type the name of the Space in the search box.
  6. Click your Space. 
  7. Click Add to Space to finalize adding the folder structure to your newly created Space.

To import a folder structure from a template:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Spaces.
  3. Click Create Space.
  4. Click Template next to Or import a folder structure from, under the prompt box. 
  5. Type the name of the template in the search box or click Show more to see all available templates. 
  6. Choose the template.
  7. Click Add to Space to finalize adding the folder structure to your newly created Space.

To import multiple folders from CSV:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Spaces.
  3. Click an existing Space or create a new Space.
  4. Click Create folder.
  5. Click Import from CSV.
    • Note: When you import a .csv, the format should show the indexing information in column A and the folder names in column B.

Filtering content (visitor)

To filter content:

  1. Click Recently added on the right-hand side. 
  2. Under Home click the drop-down menu to filter files by days last recently added. 
    • Note: This feature won’t be shown if the Admin has turned it off. 

Managing content filter (admin)

To manage the content filter:

  1. Click the Space you want to manage. 
  2. Click ☑(more options) next to Preview, on the right-hand side. 
  3. Click Turn off recently added filter under Visitor experience. 
Important considerations
  • Folders are not searchable within a Space.
  • Grouping folders into sections can improve navigation.
  • Duplicating a Space copies its folders and content.
  • Moving content between folders does not apply to sections.
  • If you downgrade from a plan that supports Space folders, those Spaces will be disabled. To restore access to the folders move them into Archive. 

How to download folders, files, or an index from a Space

You can download an entire Space, download a folder, or download specific files from a Space. Advanced Data Room customers can also download the index of a Space. Learn more about downloading a Space or downloading items from a Space. 

Move Dropbox files and folders

You can move files and folders in Dropbox to organize the contents of your account.  

To move a file or folder on dropbox.com:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the file or folder you’d like to move, and click the “…” (ellipsis). 
  3. Click Move.
  4. Click the folder you’d like to move it to. Or, click Createnew folder.
    • To browse all folders, click Personal.
  5. Click Move.  

To move a file or folder on the Dropbox mobile app:

  1. Open the Dropbox mobile app.
  2. Tap the “…” (ellipsis) next to the file or folder you’d like to move.
  3. Tap Move.
    • You might have to scroll down to see this on iOS.
  4. Tap the folder you’d like to move it to.
  5. Tap Move.  

To move a file or folder in the Dropbox folder on your computer, drag the file or folder you’d like to move to a new location.  

Learn more about moving shared files and folders.

Naming Dropbox files and folders

To ensure the best experience with Dropbox across all platforms and operating systems, we recommend following these guidelines when naming files and folders in your Dropbox account. This includes Windows, Mac, Android, iPhone, iPad, and Linux. Each operating system has its own file and folder name limitations, but the recommendations below cover all of them.  

Learn how to rename a file or folder in Dropbox.  

Even if you don’t get an error message when you name a file on your operating system, if you don’t follow the guidelines below, it could cause a problem when you try to open or sync the file on another operating system.

File and folder name recommendations

☑ Keep file and folder paths under 260 characters

A file path includes the full location of a file or folder. File paths must be fewer than 260 characters.

Example:

C:\Users\Panda\My Documents\Dropbox\Creative Nonfiction\My Autobiography\Favorite Things\Favorite Foods\Bamboo\Family Recipes\Fresh Leaves.doc

This path is 142 characters.

☑ Don’t use restricted characters in file or folder names

Always disallowed

  • / (forward slash)
  • \ (backslash)  

Not recommended These characters may cause syncing or display issues, especially on Windows:

  • < (less than)
  • > (greater than)
  • : (colon)
  • ” (double quote)
  • | (vertical bar or pipe)
  • ? (question mark)
  • * (asterisk)
  • . (period) — see the notes below for exceptions
☑ Don’t add a space at the end of a file or folder name

For example, don’t name a file or folder Panda .png.

Emoji and Unicode Support

Dropbox also supports a wide range of characters in filenames—including emojis . This lets you use expressive, modern filenames across devices, and see them display consistently.

Dropbox supports an extended set of characters, including:

  • Emojis
  • CJK (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) scripts
  • RTL (right-to-left) scripts

Examples:

  • Project launch 🚀.doc
  • 📚 Budget review.xls
  • Team pics 🐱.zip
  • 𝛑 formula.txt
  • 𩸽.pdf

These names appear the same on dropbox.com, in the Dropbox desktop and mobile apps, and across supported devices.

Rename or move a shared folder

You can rename or move a shared folder like any other folder on your hard drive. If you rename or move a shared folder, the folder remains shared.  

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox makes file and folder organization easy.

How to rename a shared folder

If you’re the owner of a shared folder, and you want to rename it, the change will only be reflected in your Dropbox account, but not in the Dropbox accounts of the shared folder members. Only new members that join the shared folder after the rename will see the new name.

If you’re not the owner, but you have editing permissions of a shared folder, and you want to rename it, the change will only be reflected in your Dropbox account, but not in the Dropbox accounts of the shared folder members. Learn more about Dropbox file and folder sharing permissions.

Learn how to rename files and folders.

If you want to rename a shared folder for all members, you must unshare the folder, rename it, and then reshare the folder.

How to move a shared folder

If you’re the owner of a shared folder in your work Dropbox and you want to move it to your personal Dropbox, first take a look at the folder’s settings:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the name of the folder and click Share.
  3. Click   (settings) in the bottom right.
  4. Check the setting Folder membership.
    • If it shows “Anyone”, you can move the shared folder to your personal Dropbox without a problem. 
    • If it shows “Only team members”, moving the folder to your personal Dropbox will break your membership in the folder, and you’ll have only a non-shared copy of it in your personal Dropbox.

If there are no sharing restrictions, moving a shared folder from one Dropbox to another will be recorded as an event in your admin’s sharing activity log.

Copying a shared folder

Copying a shared folder from one Dropbox to another will have no effect on your membership in the folder.

For example, if you copy a shared folder from your work Dropbox to your personal Dropbox, your work account will still be a member of the shared folder, and a non-shared copy of the folder will be in your personal Dropbox.

Select multiple files on dropbox.com

You can select multiple files at the same time on dropbox.com. This allows you to quickly take actions like:

  • Moving the files into a folder
  • Copying the files
  • Deleting the files

To select multiple files on dropbox.com:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the first file you want to select.
  3. Click the checkmark that appears. Repeat this for all the files you want to select.
  4. Choose the action you’d like to take from the options above the file list.

Space (data room) notifications in Dropbox DocSend

Overview

Spaces are what we call our virtual data rooms (VDR). Data rooms provide a way to group, organize, and share high volumes of content with others using a single link. The Space (data room) notifications feature allows you to instantly notify your visitors about any changes you make with a customizable email notification. This means you’ll be able to send an update to specific visitors whenever you make changes to your Space.

Requirements

To send Space (data room) notifications, your Space must:

  • Have visits associated with at least one link.
  • Enable the Require email to view setting on said Space link. Learn more about link settings.

Learn more about the DocSend Advanced Data Rooms plan.

Send Space (data room) notifications manually

Space owners and collaborators can set up and send notifications.

To send Space (data room) notifications:

  1. Click the vertical ellipsis icon next to Preview.
  2. Click Send update email under Manage.
  3. Add an optional message (up to 500 characters).
  4. When you’re satisfied with your message and list of recipients, click Send. 
    • Note: If you’re on the Advanced Data Rooms plan, you’ll be able to view when email notifications were sent out in the audit log. The audit log won’t track who receives or opens the email.

Set up automated Space (data room) notifications

Customers on DocSend Advanced and Advanced Data Rooms can set up automated space notifications to send to visitors whenever new content is added to the Space.

To set up automated notifications:

  1. Click Spaces in the left sidebar.
  2. Select the Space you want to automate notifications for.
  3. Click the vertical ellipsis next to Preview.
  4. Click Set up notifications under Manage. 
  5. Toggle Automatic notifications from Off to On. 
  6. Customize your Preferences. You can set up notifications for:
    • New content and versions: Updates visitors about new content or document versions in the Space.
    • New content only: Only updates visitors when new content is added to the Space.
    • New versions only: Only updates visitors when there are new versions of a document.
  7. Toggle New visitor preferences to Opt in if you want new visitors to be automatically opted in to notifications for that Space.
  8. Select your recipients.
  9. Click Save. 

Now that your automated notifications are set up, your visitors will receive email updates whenever new content is added or version changes are made. Only people with access to the content that’s being changed will be notified. New or updated content will have a badge next to it that says New.

You can view which links visitors are using to access the Space under Recipients.

Stop Space (data room) notifications

If a visitor wants to stop receiving email notifications about a specific Space, they can unsubscribe from receiving notifications about that Space. Each Space has its own subscription rules, so unsubscribing from one Space won’t unsubscribe you from all Spaces.

When a visitor unsubscribes from a Space, the next time the sender opens the Space Notifications modal, they won’t be able to select that visitor as a recipient.

To unsubscribe from a Space (data room):

  1. Open the email notification from the Space you want to stop receiving email notifications from.
  2. Click Click here and the unsubscription notification page will open. 

If you accidentally unsubscribed, you can re-subscribe on the unsubscription page by clicking the Re-subscribe button at the bottom. If for any reason, you close the tab, you can re-access the page by clicking on the “click here” text in the notification email again.

Visitor experience

Once your notification is sent, your chosen recipients will receive an email from DocSend notifying them that the Space (data room) has been updated, along with your message, and a link to your newly updated Space.               

Replies

When a visitor replies to the notification, their message will be sent to the Space notification sender’s email inbox (outside of DocSend). Please note, only the DocSend user who sent the notification will receive this reply. 

Things to consider

  • Space (data room) notifications aren’t tracked within DocSend at this time.
  • Space notifications are currently only available through paid subscriptions.
  • Links within custom messages aren’t clickable by recipients.
  • Space owners and collaborators visiting the Space in preview mode will be excluded from the list of potential recipients when logged into DocSend. Visits outside of preview mode will be included in the list of potential recipients.

Visitor experience in Dropbox DocSend Spaces

When visiting a Space, there are few things you can do to navigate through the shared content.

Creating a view-only account

To create a view-only account:

  1. Visit a Space someone has shared with you.
  2. Click Get Started in the banner.
  3. Fill out the form.
  4. Click Agree and signup.
  5. Verify your email.
  6. Customize your experience.

You will have access to a Shared with me space that consolidates all links sent to you in one location.

Visitor information prompt

When accessing shared content or a data space, you may first be required to provide your email address or sign an NDA.  Learn more about DocSend link settings. 

Page navigator

You can navigate to a different page on the document, quickly switch between documents, and go back to the home page without ever leaving the document viewer in page navigator.

Search bar

You can look for specific content in your files using the search bar.

Download files in a Space

When downloading is enabled, you can download specific folders, ZIP files, or a ZIP of the entire Space. Use the download icon in the top-right corner to download all available content, or click the icon next to an individual item to download it individually. 

For larger downloads, you can select Email download link in the pop-up window to have the files sent directly to your inbox. To ensure the best experience, download content on the same device where you originally viewed the Space. The ZIP file will preserve the folder and section structure, but updates or new additions to the Space may require you to download the assets again. URL links cannot be downloaded, and the download icon only appears if the Space owner has enabled downloading for that item. If a folder includes files that aren’t downloadable, those files will be excluded from the download.

What are Spaces (data rooms) in Dropbox DocSend?

Overview

Spaces are what we call our virtual data rooms (VDR). Data rooms provide a way to group, organize, and share high volumes of content with others using a single link. Data rooms provide a high level of customization to allow teams to tailor each data room to their unique needs. Data analytics provide additional support by allowing owners and collaborators to keep track of contributions and visitor activity. 

Learn more about the DocSend Advanced Data Rooms plan.

What can I do with a Space (data room)?

  • View multiple types of content in a one place.
  • Collaborate and manage with your team members.
  • Customize each Space so that it’s unique to each of your projects.
  • Track visits and content engagement.

 

  • Create groups to customize and streamline workflows.
  • View data rooms via group invite or links.
  • Visitors can filter by Recently added content.

What content can I search in Dropbox Dash?

Dropbox Dash supports different types of content depending on the apps you’ve connected to your account.

Check out the table below to see what data is searchable from each app:

What’s a conflicted copy?

A conflicted copy is a file that Dropbox creates when multiple people edit the same file at the same time. The editor’s username, “conflicted copy”, and the save date will be added to the filename.  

There are three ways a conflicted copy can happen:

  • Two users change the same file at the same time.
  • Someone edits a file offline while someone else edits the same file.
  • A file is left open on another user’s computer, which Dropbox saves as a new edit—this is especially common when using applications with an auto-save feature.

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox makes syncing files easy.

What do I do now?

The best way to resolve a conflicted copy is to compare both versions and merge them manually.  

Conflicted copies can happen with all types of files. If you’re using Microsoft Word, you can check out their help article on how to compare and merge two documents.

How do I prevent a conflicted copy from happening again?

The best way to avoid a conflicted copy is to collaborate on files in real-time with a program like Dropbox Paper or Microsoft Office Online. (Dropbox Paper is free with your main subscription).

If you’re collaborating with a colleague using the Dropbox badge, you can click ✗ (download) when prompted by the badge to download the latest version of the file, which includes any changes that have been saved by your colleague.

Learn more about the Dropbox badge.

If you’re unable to collaborate in real-time, the next best way to avoid a conflicted copy is to move your file out of its Dropbox folder while you’re working so that nobody else can access it. Once you’re done editing, you can move the file back into its original location.  

Alternatively, here are a few other tips you can try:

  • Create a new folder for all in-progress files titled “In Use” so your collaborators know not to make changes.
  • For Dropbox teams: When the Dropbox badge notifies you that another person is editing a file, coordinate with that person to take turns editing.

A conflicted copy is a file that Dropbox creates when multiple people edit the same file at the same time. The editor’s username, “conflicted copy”, and the save date will be added to the filename.  

There are three ways a conflicted copy can happen:

  • Two users change the same file at the same time.
  • Someone edits a file offline while someone else edits the same file.
  • A file is left open on another user’s computer, which Dropbox saves as a new edit—this is especially common when using applications with an auto-save feature.

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox makes syncing files easy.

What do I do now?

The best way to resolve a conflicted copy is to compare both versions and merge them manually.  

Conflicted copies can happen with all types of files. If you’re using Microsoft Word, you can check out their help article on how to compare and merge two documents.

How do I prevent a conflicted copy from happening again?

The best way to avoid a conflicted copy is to collaborate on files in real-time with a program like Dropbox Paper or Microsoft Office Online. (Dropbox Paper is free with your main subscription).

If you’re collaborating with a colleague using the Dropbox badge, you can click ✗ (download) when prompted by the badge to download the latest version of the file, which includes any changes that have been saved by your colleague.

Learn more about the Dropbox badge.

If you’re unable to collaborate in real-time, the next best way to avoid a conflicted copy is to move your file out of its Dropbox folder while you’re working so that nobody else can access it. Once you’re done editing, you can move the file back into its original location.  

Alternatively, here are a few other tips you can try:

  • Create a new folder for all in-progress files titled “In Use” so your collaborators know not to make changes.
  • For Dropbox teams: When the Dropbox badge notifies you that another person is editing a file, coordinate with that person to take turns editing.

What’s a Dropbox file case conflict?

A case conflict happens when you name a file or folder with the same name as a file or folder in the same location, but with different upper-case and lower-case letters. For example, two files named “records” and “Records”.

Although you can store these two files in the same place on dropbox.com, you can’t store them in the same place in the Dropbox folder on Windows, Mac, and other file systems. Instead, one will be appended with the words (Case Conflict).

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox makes syncing files easy.

What do I do now?

If one of your files is appended with the words (Case Conflict), you can resolve it with either of the following options:

  • Simply leave both files or folders alone, and let one continue to have the name appended with (Case Conflict)
  • Rename one of the files or folders

How can I prevent a case conflict from happening again?

If you’d like to avoid case conflicts in the future, don’t create a file or folder with the same name as a file or folder in the same location, even if it has different upper-case and lower-case letters.

What’s a Unicode encoding conflict?

A Unicode encoding conflict happens when two files or two folders with the same name are saved in the same location on your Dropbox account. To resolve this, Dropbox will append one with the words (Unicode Encoding Conflict).

This type of conflict occurs with filenames containing characters that are encoded with Unicode. If the two filenames look the same but are encoded differently, Dropbox will interpret them to have the same filename.

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox makes syncing files easy.

What do I do now?

If one of your files is appended with the words (Unicode Encoding Conflict), you can resolve it with either of the following options: 

  • Simply leave both files or folders alone, and let one continue to have the name appended with (Unicode Encoding Conflict)
  • Rename one of the files or folders

How can I prevent a Unicode encoding conflict from happening again?

If you’d like to avoid Unicode encoding conflicts in the future, don’t create a file or folder with the same name as a file or folder in the same location.

What’s a whitespace conflict?

A whitespace conflict happens when you name a file or folder with the same name as a file or folder in the same location, but with a space after the filename. For example, two folders named “Records” and “Records “, or two files named “pages.png” and “pages .png”.

The new file or folder you created will automatically be appended with the words (Whitespace Conflict).

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox makes syncing files easy.

What do I do now?

If one of your files is appended with the words (Whitespace Conflict), you can resolve it with either of the following options:

  • Simply leave both files or folders alone, and let one continue to have the name appended with (Whitespace Conflict)
  • Rename one of the files or folders

How can I prevent a whitespace conflict from happening again?

If you’d like to avoid whitespace conflicts in the future, don’t create a file or folder with the same name as a file or folder in the same location, even if one has a space after the filename.

Why am I getting conflicted copies while using the Dropbox badge?

If you and another person are editing a file at the same time and both of you have unsaved changes, you’ll see a red Dropbox badge with an exclamation mark. At this point you can create a conflicted copy of only your edits to the file if you:

  • Click the floppy disk icon
  • Type Ctrl + S or Cmd + S (dependent on your keyboard)

To avoid a conflicted copy we recommend that when you see another person editing—when you see the red Dropbox badge with the lock icon—you coordinate with that person to take turns editing.

If you and another person both have unsaved changes when the red Dropbox badge with the exclamation mark appears, we recommend that you Save As to save a separate version of the file.

Why can’t I add members to a team folder?

If a team folder has too many members, you may see a message telling you that you can’t add any more. This is to ensure your folders sync properly, and prevent issues like folder update errors.  

What can I do if I can’t add members to a team folder?

We’re constantly working to make it so you can add even more members to your Dropbox folders. In the meantime, if you reach the limit, here are a few things you can do:

Remove some members. Take a look at the members who are in the folder already, and consider removing some to make room for the members you’re trying to add.

Reorganize your team folders. If you have a team folder that reaches the member limits, you won’t be able to add people to the team folder, or to any of the shared folders it contains. To solve this problem, you can divide your team members into more team folders that represent smaller teams.

For example, imagine you have a team folder called “Marketing”. Within Marketing, you have two shared folders: “Sales” and “Advertising”. If you make “Sales” and “Advertising” team folders instead of shared folders, that’ll give you more space to add more members.

Plans

Can I get a refund on a Dropbox or Dropbox Dash subscription?

In most cases, payments for Dropbox and Dropbox Dash subscriptions and team member licenses aren’t refundable.

If you have an issue with your account, or think there has been an error in billing, please check your support options for more help. However, if you purchased your Dropbox subscription through your device’s storefront, please reach out to the storefront for any refund requests for account issues or billing errors.

Learn how to request a refund from Apple.

Learn how to request a refund from Google.

How to request a direct debit refund

If you paid for your Dropbox subscription with a direct debit payment, please contact your bank for a refund, as only your bank can process a chargeback request.  

What happens when I submit a chargeback request?

Any chargeback requested from your bank will change your Dropbox subscription to a Dropbox Basic (free) plan.

If you have a Dropbox team subscription, a chargeback request will cause your team to be placed in a locked state, which allows the team to continue access to the team files, but removes most team syncing and sharing features. The team admin will need to choose to disband the team or re-subscribe.

Live in the EU, UK, or Turkey?

If you live in the EU, UK, or Turkey, you’re eligible for a refund if you cancel your Dropbox Plus, Family, Professional, or Essentials subscription within 14 days of purchase. To request a refund, contact support for assistance.

Can I receive faxes for free in Dropbox Fax?

Because buying and maintaining an inbound fax line costs us money, it’s something we have to charge for. Though we let our free users send faxes, you’ll need to subscribe to one of our paid plans if you want to receive faxes.

You can check out all of the details here at our Pricing Page.  

All of our plans come with an inbound fax line (with the area code of your choice), a monthly page allotment, and a 30-day free trial.

We currently provide inbound numbers for the U.S., U.K., and Canada.  

Once you subscribe, all of your faxes will be available in your Faxes** tab (on the left side of the Dropbox Fax window), and forwarded to your email inbox as a PDF unless you disable this option in your settings.**

Can I use Dropbox Sign for free?

Dropbox Sign has a limited Free plan that lets you send 3 free signature requests per month. Your 3 free signature requests renew every 30 days from the day you sign up.

Check out the Dropbox Sign Plans & Pricing to see everything our Free plan includes and to compare it with our paid plans. From the Plans & Pricing page, you can click Sign Up in the top right to sign up for any of our plans, or Contact Us to learn more.

What does a free signature request include?

A signature request refers to the entire transaction of preparing and sending one or more documents to be electronically signed by one or more signers, then receiving the signed document(s). As long as you send the document(s) to the signer(s) in a single bundle, it counts as only one signature request.

Is the audit trail free too?

Yes. When your signature request is completed, you’ll receive a PDF of the signed document(s) plus an audit trail. Self-signed documents—documents signed using the Just Me option—don’t include an audit trail since you’re the only signer.

What do the paid plans include?

If you need more than our Free plan provides, compare the Dropbox Sign Plans & Pricing to choose the best plan for you.

Downgrading your Dropbox Sign account

If you downgrade your Dropbox Sign plan, you’ll still have access to the documents you’ve saved in your account. However, your access to other features like templates, teams, and branding may change.

How changing plans affects your Dropbox Sign account

Changes to other features and limits will depend on the new plan you select.

Teams

  • Teams are available only on Standard and Premium plans.
  • Team features including branding, in-person signing, team transaction overview, and two-factor authentication aren’t available on free or Essentials plans.
  • If you downgrade to a free or Essentials plan, team members will be converted to individual free accounts. They can choose to upgrade to their own paid plan on the pricing page.

Documents

  • On a free plan, you can sign or request signatures on 3 documents per month.
  • On an Essentials, Standard, or Premium plan for the web, you can sign or request signatures on an unlimited number of documents.
  • On an API plan, document limits start at 50 or 100 signature requests.

Templates

  • Templates aren’t available on free plans.
  • 5 templates are available on the Essentials plan.
  • 15 templates are available on the Standard plan.
  • An unlimited number of templates are available on the Premium plan.
  • Previously created templates will remain if you downgrade to a free plan, but they’ll be locked.
  • You can upgrade from a free plan to another plan at any time to unlock and restore the use of your templates.  

Free features

If you downgrade to a free plan, you’ll still have access to audit trails, integrations, and status notifications, as well as all the documents you previously signed or collected signatures on.

The Dropbox Data Governance add-on

The Dropbox Data Governance add-on helps admins on Dropbox team accounts secure and control team data so they’re prepared for any compliance or audit needs.

Data Governance add-on features

Legal holds

With legal holds, admins can place a legal hold on members of their team and view and export all the content that’s been created or modified by those members.

Learn more about legal holds.

Data Retention

Admins can create data retention and disposition policies to help them meet compliance and regulatory requirements.

Learn more about data retention.  

Extended version history

The Dropbox Data Governance add-on increases file version history to 10 years, so teams have more time to recover files.

Learn more about extended version history.

How to get the Data Governance add-on

To purchase the Data Governance add-on, contact your Dropbox sales executive or fill out the Dropbox Sales contact form.

If you don’t have a dedicated sales executive, your team can purchase or remove the Data Governance add-on in the admin console.  

To do this:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Billing.
    • Note: Only certain types of admins can access the Billing page.
  4. Under Products, scroll to Add-ons, and click Add or Remove next to Data Governance.
  5. Click Confirm.

When you purchase the add-on, you’ll be charged at a prorated amount for your current billing period. At the start of your next billing period, you’ll be charged for the full amount of the add-on, in addition to your subscription cost.

When you remove the add-on, your selection will go into effect on your next renewal.

Dropbox DocSend Limited Trial overview

While DocSend does offer a wide range of paid subscriptions, the Limited Trial is great for getting familiar with the basics of using DocSend for free. This plan is similar to our Personal plan with just a few limitations. 

Limited Trial features

On the Limited Trial, you can:

  • Create up to 10 links.
  • Upload and store up to 5 documents at a time.
  • Receive visits on document links.
  • Add users (member role only).

Downgrade to the Limited Trial

If you’re a new user, your Advanced Data Rooms Trial will automatically be downgraded to the Limited Trial if you decide not to upgrade to a paid subscription.

If you currently have a paid subscription, canceling your subscription reverts your account to the Limited Trial. 

When you cancel, any links using premium features will be disabled and inaccessible to visitors. This includes:

  • Spaces (data rooms)
  • Signable documents
  • Any links using advanced security features:
    • Allowed viewers
    • Email authentication
    • NDA
    • Watermarking
    • Campaign or mail merge

Link accessibility

Your content won’t be deleted if you downgrade to the Limited Trial. If any content or links are deactivated, they’ll be reactivated as soon as you upgrade to a plan that supports the premium features.

Re-enable links

You can remove advanced security features from your document links to re-enable them for your visitors. To do this, follow this guide to update link settings or refer to the steps below:

  1. Find the disabled link and click the Settings icon.
  2. Deselect any advanced features.
  3. Click Update Link.

Your link should now be accessible.

Limited Trial limitations

  • A DocSend signup page will be appended to the end of each document in the document viewer. Upgrade to a paid plan to remove the appended page. 
  • When you’ve reached the content limit, you’ll see a popup and a red banner prompting you to upgrade to a paid plan. Click Choose a plan to upgrade to a paid subscription and continue using DocSend. After you upgrade, the popup and red banner will be removed. For more information on paid DocSend subscriptions, check out the Pricing page.
  • You’ll have limited access to content analytics (including recent visits), the Contacts page, the Accounts page.
  • Limitations include:
    • View two visits per document.
    • Contacts page will show one contact. 
    • Accounts page will show one account.

Dropbox DocSend Sub-teams add-on overview

The DocSend Sub-teams add-on allows you to create and manage sub-teams in your organization. Sub-teams are great for keeping sensitive content extra secure, and ensuring that only authorized users can access it.

What’s included in the DocSend Sub-teams add-on?

The DocSend Sub-teams add-on includes the sub-teams feature. Sub-teams allow owners and team admins to decide which team members get access to specific types of content. Learn more about sub-teams in our help center.

How can I purchase the add-on?

You can reach out to sales@docsend.com for more information or to activate this add-on for your plan.

When creating a DocSend account, you will be automatically subscribed to a 14-day trial of our Advanced Data Rooms plan to experience all the features DocSend has to offer.  

Trial limitations

Upload limit

You can upload up to 500 documents. To upload more, you can sign up for a paid subscription through the Upgrade or Billing page. Learn more about how to sign up for a DocSend trial.

Additional users

eSignature

Agreements to gate access

Space (data room) Group invitations

On the Advanced Data Rooms trial, you can invite visitors to a Space using groups. Access to group invitations during a trial may be limited. To unlock full functionality you can purchase a DocSend Advanced Data Rooms subscription.

Sharing external URL links

On any DocSend trial, the sharing external URL links feature is not available. To use this feature, you must wait for your trial to end and sign up for DocSend Standard, Advanced, Advanced Data Rooms, or Enterprise.

Trial expiration

You’ll receive an expiration notice 3 days before your trial end date on the DocSend web application and through email.

Once your trial ends if no card is on file, our system will automatically switch your account to the free limited trial plan and disable all links with premium features enabled. Learn more about downgrading.

Dropbox Family plan FAQs

Dropbox Family is a plan with 2 TB of shared storage space that can be used by up to 6 members. This article answers frequently asked questions about Dropbox Family.

How can I get Dropbox Family?

If you already have an individual Dropbox account, you can switch to Dropbox Family in your account settings.

To switch to a Family plan:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Manage account.
  4. Click Upgrade Plan. If Dropbox Family appears as an option, you can upgrade from here.
  5. Click Family plan.
  6. Click Continue.

If you don’t have a Dropbox account, you can purchase the Family plan directly. 

Who can I invite to my Dropbox Family plan?

You can invite up to 6 members in total to your Dropbox Family plan. All Family plan members must be 13 years or older in the United States and 16 or older anywhere else. If they don’t already have a Dropbox account, invited members can create one when they join a Family plan.

What are the different roles in a Family plan?

Dropbox Family accounts have a Family manager and Family members. They can also have admins, if the Family manager chooses.

  • Family manager: The person who purchases Dropbox Family is the Family manager. They can update billing, manage Family admins and members, disband the Family, and check storage space.
  • Family admins: Admins are able to add or remove members from the Family.
  • Family members: Each Family member has their own private Dropbox account, but storage space is shared with all other Family members.

Learn more about managing a Dropbox Family plan.

Can I join a Dropbox Family plan if I already have a Plus or Professional account?

Yes. If you have a Dropbox Plus or Professional account and are invited to join Dropbox Family, there’s no need to change your plan. Your individual account will be refunded for the prorated cost of your original plan and your plan will be changed to Dropbox Family. If you’d rather keep your original plan, ask the person who invited you to send a new invite to a different email address. You can then set up a new account that will be associated with a Family plan.

Are there any limitations on who can join a Family plan?

Yes. You won’t be able to join a Family plan if you’ve purchased extended version history. You also can’t join a Family plan with an email associated with a Dropbox team account, or if you’re in a restricted country or region.

How do I merge my existing Dropbox account with a Family plan?

There’s no need to make any changes to your account, or move any files or folders, when you purchase or join a Dropbox Family plan. Your plan will change to Dropbox Family, but your account profile, settings, and files will remain the same. However, only the Family manager can view or change billing info for the plan, so if you previously had Dropbox Plus or Professional, you may no longer have access to billing information.

Can the other members of my Family plan see the files I save to Dropbox?

Each member of your Dropbox Family plan has their own private account. Only the files you choose to share can be viewed or edited by others.

How can I get support from Dropbox?

Family plan members can get help from the Dropbox help center, Quick Start Guides, community, and by email. Family managers can also request chat support.

What happens to my files if I use remote wipe?

If you use remote wipe to remove files from a lost or stolen device, the contents of the Dropbox folder on that device are removed. Your files won’t be deleted from your Dropbox account—they’re safely stored in the cloud, so you can re-sync them to any device when you’re ready.

How does sharing files and folders with other Family plan members count toward my storage space?

Every file or folder in a Family member’s account only counts once toward the total storage space quota. Sharing files and folders with other members of the same Family plan does not count toward the storage quota again. If you share with someone outside your Family plan, or if someone outside the plan shares with you, those files will count toward both your account quota and theirs. You can check your account settings to see how much of the storage quota has been used.

Can I buy more storage space?

Individual Family members can free up space by deleting unused files and folders, or they can opt out of Dropbox Family and choose an individual plan that meets their needs.

Can I earn free space on Dropbox Family?

Yes. You can earn free storage space on Dropbox Basic, Plus, Family, and Professional accounts, and the space will be shared with your other Family members. If you leave a Family plan, your free space will still be available on your individual account.

Can I leave a Family plan?

Family members can opt out of a Family plan at any time. If you leave the plan, your individual account will be downgraded to a free Basic plan. You’ll keep all your files and folders but will lose access to the features and storage space of Dropbox Family.

The Dropbox Security add-on

The Dropbox Security add-on provides teams with an extra layer of security by detecting suspected ransomware, classifying personal information, and alerting admins of suspicious activity.

Dropbox Security add-on features

Ransomware detection

Ransomware detection helps prevent malicious ransomware attacks from spreading by detecting suspicious activity early. Admins can manage ransomware detection alerts in the admin console.

Learn about ransomware detection.  

Data classification

Data classification helps teams stay compliant with corporate and government regulations by allowing admins to automatically track and report on personal information stored in team folders, team member folders, and shared folders, such as: credit card, passport, bank account, and social security numbers.

Learn about data classification.  

Security alerts

With security alerts, admins will receive email notifications whenever suspicious behavior, risky activity, and potential data leaks are detected.

Learn about security alerts.

How to get the Security add-on

The Security add-on is available to purchase for Dropbox Standard and Business teams. 

To purchase the Security add-on:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Billing in the left sidebar.
    • Note: Only certain types of admins can access the Billing page.
  4. Under Products, scroll to Add-ons, and click Add next to Security add-on.
  5. Click Confirm.

You’ll be charged for the add-on as soon as you purchase, at a prorated amount. On your next billing period, your subscription cost will include the full price of the add-on.

Dropbox Sign account hold policy

We aren’t able to put accounts on hold or pause your membership. Once a subscription is canceled or downgraded, we return the fax number back to our fax provider and it can be assigned to another user.

However, as long as you don’t delete your account, all of your documents remain on your account for your convenience.

Dropbox Sign and eID

Dropbox Sign supports eID (electronic identification) through the web (sign.dropbox.com) and Sign API. We connect with trusted Qualified Trusted Service Providers (QTSP) to provide both Advanced and Qualified Electronic Signatures, compliant with the eIDAS regulation.

eID helps identify the signer of a document sent via Dropbox Sign. Additionally, eID strengthens legal validity and compliance and helps meet or exceed regional legal and regulatory requirements for validity and enforceability.

Features

  • Identity verification: eID enables the verification of a signer’s identity by relying on digital certificates issued by recognized Qualified Trust Service Providers.
  • Strong legal validity and compliance: Helps meet or exceed regional legal and regulatory requirements for validity and enforceability.
  • Risk reduction: Provides strong protection against tampering or forgery, thus maintaining the integrity of electronically signed documents.
  • Global accessibility: Enables businesses from different parts of the world to engage in secure, cross-border transactions.

Supported eID and digital signatures

Dropbox Sign currently supports the following eID and types of digital signatures. For more information, contact your account manager or Dropbox Sign Support.

How can I enable eID in my signature request workflow?

If you’re on the Dropbox Sign API Premium plan and have purchased the eID add-on, you can enable eID from the admin console.   

To enable eID:

  1. Log in to Dropbox Sign with your admin credentials.
  2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Click Admin console.
  4. Click Settings.
  5. Click Signature requests.
  6. Toggle the Enable eID to On.

For team admins, learn more about managing the use of eID requests for your team below.

How do I create an eID request?

You can create an eID request when preparing a document for signing on sign.dropbox.com or through the Dropbox Sign API.

Dropbox Sign API

To create an eID signature request via the Dropbox Sign API:

  1. Create and send a new a Signature Request with the Dropbox Sign API.
  2. Send “is_eid” with a value of “true”.

For additional information, reference the Dropbox Sign API documentation for sending signature requests.

Learn more about the eID signature flow below.

eID and Dropbox Sign for web

To create an eID signature request via sign.dropbox.com:

  1. Log in to Dropbox Sign.
  2. Click Sign documents in the left sidebar.
  3. Choose either Upload or Add template.
  4. Click Next.
  5. Enter the name(s) and email address(es) of who needs to sign.
  6. Toggle the Enable eID to On.
    • Note: If the option isn’t available, check with your admin to be sure the  eID add-on is purchased and enabled.
  7. Click Enable.
  8. Click Next.
  9. Drag the Signature component onto the document where you’d like to add a signature.
  10. Click Next.
  11. Review your request and add any optional information for the recipient.
  12. Click Send for signature.

How can I sign a document with eID?

When receiving a document via Dropbox Sign requiring signing with eID, you’ll need to verify your identity to finish signing the document.

To verify your identity and finish signing a Dropbox Sign document:  

  1. Open the document sent to your email for signature.
  2. When you’re ready to add your signature, click Review & sign.
  3. Click Get Started in the new document window.
  4. Select Click to sign and add your signature.
    • Note: If other actions are required (for example, initials or completing a checkbox), you’ll be prompted with the appropriate action in another box.
  5. Click Continue.
  6. Click Continue in the review pop-up.
  7. Select your country and method of eID.
  8. You will be redirected to the eID provider’s website to continue through the identity verification workflow.

Once you’ve completed all the necessary steps for identity verification, you’ll be redirected to your document on Dropbox Sign.  

Managing your team’s eID quota

To view and manage your eID quota:

  1. Log in to Dropbox Sign.
  2. Click your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Billing.
  5. Navigate to Add-Ons to view and manage your eID quota.

To temporarily turn off the eID option so your team members can’t use it (such as when you’re approaching your quota):

  1. Log in to Dropbox Sign.
  2. Click your initials in the top-right corner.
  3. Click Admin console.
  4. Click Settings.
  5. Click Signature requests.
  6. Navigate to Signature request options.
  7. Toggle eID to Off.

Dropbox Sign API pricing plans

We have several Dropbox Sign API pricing plans based on the number of signature requests you’d be sending per month. You also have the option of paying month to month, or paying up front for the year at a discounted rate.

Please visit the Dropbox Sign API pricing page for more information.

Dropbox Sign API plans based on signing, requesting and template workflows

Each workflow with the Dropbox Sign API will need a particular API plan to go into production. Each API plan tier also comes with its own set of features, which you can explore in detail on our Dropbox Sign API pricing page.

Below is an overview table outlining the various signing, requesting, and template workflows, along with the minimum Dropbox Sign API plan tier required:

Dropbox Sign document pricing options

We don’t yet offer a pay-per-doc option because we offer the free version of Dropbox Sign for low volume users.

The free version of Dropbox Sign includes 3 document transactions (self-signed documents or signature requests) per month.

Our apologies if our current pricing doesn’t fit your needs right now.

Dropbox Sign free document limits

We give all of our free Dropbox Sign users three free documents to sign/send every month. Those documents renew every 30 days from the day you originally sign up. They do not refresh based on the calendar month.

For instance, if you signed up for Dropbox Sign on January 17th, your pages will renew every 17th of the month (give or take a day for the longer months).

If you used your documents on January 17th, 20th, and 21st, your pages will not renew on February 1st. You will still be out of docs until they renew on February 17th.

Check to see which day of the month you signed up for Dropbox Sign, and that’s when your three free docs will renew each month.

Free Fax pages with Dropbox Fax

Is it 5 free fax pages per month or 5 free fax pages once?

We offer all of our new users 5 free fax pages to send so they can test out our product, along with an opportunity to earn up to 20 more under the Get Free Pages tab. The free fax pages do not renew each month.

Once you’ve used up your free pages, we invite you to take part in our Pay As You Go plan. Per fax transmission, it’s $0.99 cents for the first 10 pages plus $.20 for each additional page. There’s no subscription required to pay as you go.

How to buy and manage the Dropbox Replay Add-On

This article describes how individuals and teams can buy and manage the Dropbox Replay Add-On. The Replay Add-On offers premium features for Dropbox Replay, including password protection for shared links, autogenerated video transcription and captions, large file transfers, and archiving to Dropbox. 

Learn more about the Replay Add-On.

Buy or remove Replay Add-On for individuals

To buy or remove the Dropbox Replay Add-On for your personal account:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom left corner.
  3. Click Manage account.
  4. In the Add-ons section, click Add or Remove next to Replay Add-On.
    • Note: If you don’t see any add-ons, click View all add-ons to expand your choices.
  5. Click Confirm.

You can also use the Buy Replay notifications or banners in Replay to buy a Replay Add-On.

When you buy the add-on, you’ll be charged at a prorated amount for the rest of your current billing period. At the start of your next billing period, you’ll be charged for the full amount of the add-on in addition to your subscription cost.

Buy or remove Replay Add-On for teams that pay by credit card

If your team’s payment method is credit card, you can buy or remove add-ons in the admin console.

How to assign a Replay Add-On to a team member

To buy a new add-on for a team member:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Members in the left sidebar.
  4. Click No add-ons under Add-ons, next to the person you want to assign an add-on to.
  5. Click Add beside Replay in the pop-up that appears.
  6. Click Buy now.
    • Once assigned, No add-ons will change to Replay under Add-ons.
How to remove a Replay Add-On from a team member

To remove an add-on:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Members in the left sidebar.
  4. Click Replay under Add-ons, next to the person you want to remove the add-on from.
  5. Click Remove beside Replay in the pop-up that appears.
  6. Click Confirm.
    • Once removed, Replay will change to No add-ons under Add-ons.
How to buy or remove Replay Add-Ons for multiple team members 

To add or remove add-ons for multiple team members:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Members in the left sidebar.
  4. Check the box beside Name, which will select all team members. Uncheck the box beside any members that you don’t want to include.
    • Click Add add-ons to add multiple team members, then click Confirm. 
    • Click Remove add-ons to remove multiple team members, then click Confirm.
How to request a Replay Add-On from your team admin 

If you’re a member of a team and want to be assigned a Replay Add-On, you can request one from your team admin.

  1. Go to dropbox.com/replay.
  2. Scroll down and click Buy the Replay Add-On.
    • You’ll be asked to log in to your Dropbox account to send the request. 
  3. Click Request add-on.  

You’ll see a notification that says the request was sent. You’ll get an email if it’s approved. 

How to cancel Replay Add-Ons

Replay Add-Ons will automatically be canceled if they remain unassigned at the end of a billing period. This avoids any unnecessary billing of teams.

For example, if a team member with an add-on leaves the team but their add-on isn’t assigned to another team member, this add-on will be cancelled when you renew.

Buy or remove Replay Add-On for teams with an Account Manager

If your team has a dedicated account manager, you’ll need to contact Dropbox directly to buy Replay Add-Ons for your team. Your team must buy a minimum of 10 add-ons, but you don’t need to buy them for the entire team.

Once you’ve bought the add-ons, team admins can assign or remove them in the admin console.

How to assign or remove an add-on

To assign or remove an add-on for an individual team member: 

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Members in the left sidebar.
  4. Find the person whose add-ons you want to update, then assign or remove the add-on under Add-ons.
    • Click No add-ons if you’d like to assign.
    • Click Replay add-on if you’d like to remove.
  5. Click Add or Remove next to Replay Add-On in the pop-up that appears.
  6. Click Confirm.
How to assign or remove multiple add-ons 

To assign or remove add-ons for multiple team members at once:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Members in the left sidebar.
  4. Check the box beside the people who need add-ons assigned or removed.
    • Hover over someone’s name to make the checkboxes appear.
  5. Click Add add-ons or Remove add-ons, depending on what you’d like to do.
  6. Click Add or Remove beside Replay Add-On in the pop-up that appears.
  7. Click Confirm.

How to cancel a Dropbox individual account free trial

If you signed up for a free trial of an individual Dropbox plan like Dropbox Plus, Professional, or Essentials, you can cancel the trial before it ends so you won’t be charged.

If you don’t cancel your free trial before it ends, you’ll be charged for the subscription with the billing information you provided when you signed up, if any.

How to cancel a Dropbox trial

If you signed up for a free trial on a computer, you can cancel the trial on dropbox.com. To do so:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Manage account.
  4. At the bottom, click Cancel trial.
  5. Select a reason for canceling.
  6. Click Continue.
  7. Click Confirm cancel.

You’ll receive an email confirmation that your free trial has been canceled. If you signed up with a credit card, your plan will be changed to Dropbox Basic at the end of your trial period. If you signed up with PayPal, your trial will end and your plan will be changed to Dropbox Basic immediately.

How to cancel trial add-ons

If you included trial add-ons when you signed up for a free trial on a computer, you can cancel them on dropbox.com. To do so:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner. 
  3. Click Manage account.
  4. In the Trial Add-ons section, click Remove next to the trial add-on you’d like to remove.
  5. Click Confirm and remove.

You’ll receive an email confirmation that your trial add-on has been canceled.

Terms of the free trial

When you signed up for your free Dropbox trial, you received an email from no-reply@dropbox.com with the terms of the trial subscription, including the length of the trial. If you don’t see it in your inbox, check your spam folder. You can also find the terms of the trial on the billing page of your account settings.

If you cancel your free trial before it ends, you won’t be charged for the plan.

When you cancel a free trial:

  • Your account will be changed to a free Dropbox Basic plan. If you signed up with a credit card, your account will be changed at the end of the trial period. If you signed up with PayPal, your account will be changed immediately.
  • Dropbox Basic includes 2 GB of storage space. If you exceed this storage quota, you may not be able to sync, upload, share, move, or preview files and folders. If your account remains over the limit, Dropbox may delete files you own to bring your account below the storage limit. If you exceed that limit, your account will stop syncing to your devices.
  • You’ll be able to recover deleted files and restore earlier versions of files for 30 days.

Learn what happens when you exceed your storage limit.

Check that your cancellation has been processed

When you cancel your Dropbox free trial, you’ll receive a confirmation email from no-reply@dropbox.com. If you don’t see it in your inbox, check your spam folder. You can also check the plan page of your account settings to confirm your plan has been changed to Basic.

If you were charged for a Dropbox subscription

If your free trial ended and you have been charged for a subscription, you can change to a free Dropbox Basic account by canceling your current subscription. Your account will be changed at the end of your billing cycle.

If you tried to cancel your trial before it ended but were charged for a subscription, check your support options for more help.

Solve issues with cancelling a free trial

What to know first

  • Deleting or uninstalling the Dropbox app from your phone or computer doesn’t end your free trial or delete your account, it only removes the app.
  • Canceling the free trial doesn’t remove the Dropbox app from your phone or computer, it only changes your account to a free Basic plan.

☑Find your current Dropbox plan If you’re not sure what type of account you have right now, log in to dropbox.com and go to 0.

Refunds

In most cases, Dropbox doesn’t issue refunds. To avoid being charged in the future, cancel your current subscription and change to a free Basic account. If you think there’s been an error in billing, please check your support options for more help.

What if I can’t cancel online?

If you’re not able to cancel online, or if you prefer to cancel another way, you can cancel your subscription by physical mail.

To cancel your subscription by mail:

  • You can use this template, fill it out, and send it to the address below.
  • If you don’t want to use our template, you can send us a letter to request cancellation. Include the following information:
    • Your first and last name
    • The email address associated with your account. If you don’t know it, include the best email address to reach you
    • The payment method you use with Dropbox (credit card, PayPal, etc.)
    • For credit/debit card charges, either a transaction ID or the following information:
      • Card type (Visa, Mastercard, etc.)
      • First 6 digits of card
      • Last 4 digits of card
      • Full name on the credit card
      • Date of last charge from Dropbox
      • Amount charged
      • Billing postal code
    • For PayPal charges, the PayPal transaction ID
    • For iDeal or SEPA Direct Debit charges:
      • Last four digits of your International Bank Account Number (IBAN)
      • Mandate reference number
      • Date of charge
      • Amount charged
      • Billing country

Where to send mail

If you live in the United States, Canada, or Mexico, send your cancellation letter to:

Dropbox, Inc. P.O. Box 77767 San Francisco, CA 94107

If you live anywhere else, send your cancellation letter to:

Dropbox International Unlimited Company PO Box 13480 Dublin 2 Ireland

How to delete your account

Cancel your Dropbox subscription or trial on Android

Cancel your Dropbox subscription or trial on an iPhone or iPad
