Once you create a template, you can use it to send signature requests.

To send a signature request using a template:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Select Templates in the left sidebar.
  3. Click My Templates on the dropdown menu.
  4. Click Use template next to the template you’d like to use.
  5. Upload any additional documents, or just click Next.
  6. Add names and email addresses to each signer role.
    • Note: If you’re on a Premium plan, you have access to variable signing which allows you to leave any signer roles you don’t need blank.
  7. Click Next.
  8. Under Message to signers, add a document title and message.
  9. Click Send for signature.

How to share a template or template link with team members on Dropbox Sign

If you’re on a Dropbox Sign Standard or Premium plan, you can share the templates and template links you create with your team members. Anyone you share a template or template link with will be able to use that template or template link but not edit it. Your admin will automatically have edit access to the templates and template links you create.

By default, anyone you share a template link with will receive an email containing a copy of the signed document any time someone signs using that template link.

To share a template or template link:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Select Templates in the left sidebar.

To remove someone’s access to a template or template link:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Select Templates in the left sidebar.

  4. Click “⁝” (vertical ellipsis) next to the template or template link you’d like to remove someone’s access to.

How to share files and folders with Dropbox Family

Dropbox Family is a great and simple way to get everyone in your family organized. If you’re having trouble with sharing files within your Dropbox Family, this article will explain how Dropbox Family storage works and how to share files and folders with Dropbox Family.

How does shared storage on Dropbox Family work?

On a Dropbox Family plan, every file or folder in a Family member’s account only counts once toward the total storage space quota.

Sharing files and folders with other members of the same Family plan doesn’t count toward the storage quota again. 

If you share with someone outside of your Family plan, or if someone outside the plan shares with you, those files will count toward both your account quota and theirs.

All members of a Family plan can see how much storage space has been used, and how usage is divided between members.

How to check your storage space
  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Plan. “Space available: and”Space used” are shown. 
    • To see each Family member’s usage, click the arrow next to Everyone else’s files.

How do shared files and folders on Dropbox Family work?

When you share a file, Family members will have access to the file in their own Dropbox account. Documents, photos, and other files stored in Dropbox are updated automatically, so everyone with access to a file sees the same version. 

You can share folders in the same way as files. Anyone you share the folder with will have access to the files inside. 

What is the Family Room folder?

All Family members have access to a common folder called “Family Room” that can’t be deleted, moved, or renamed. Each member can find the Family Room folder in their own Dropbox account—it looks like a folder with two or three people on it. It’s a place where your family can organize and access all types of files, from receipts and tax documents to photos and school work.

How do Family Room folders work? 

When you upload or create files and folders inside the Family Room folder, all Family plan members will automatically have edit access to those files and folders. Any Family member can remove files from the Family Room folder at any time. When content is removed, other members won’t see it in their Dropbox accounts any longer. 

How to make a Family Room folder

The Family Room folder is automatically generated and you can’t create additional Family Room folders.

Who manages a Family Room folder?

The Family plan manager is the owner of the Family Room folder. If the Family manager cancels or changes the plan, each member will keep a copy of the folder in their own account.

Who can access a Family Room folder?

Any time the manager invites new members to the plan, the new members will automatically have access to the Family Room folder when they join. 

If the Family manager removes a member from the plan, the manager can choose whether or not the member keeps a copy of the Family Room folder. If a member leaves the plan, they’ll no longer have access to the Family Room folder, or have a copy in their own account.

What are the sharing permissions on a Dropbox Family plan?

Family members can choose to share files and folders with edit access or view-only access. Members can share with a single family member, or all of the members on their plan.

What can family members do with edit access files?

With edit access, family members can make changes to files and folders that are shared with them. These changes will be saved on the shared version, so everyone who has access to it will see the changes.

What can family members do with view-only access files?

With view-only access, family members can view and add comments to shared files and folders, but they can’t make any changes. 

How to share files on Dropbox Family

On a Dropbox Family plan, you can share files with other family members just like you share any other file in Dropbox, such as sharing through email or sharing through a link.

Having trouble with your Dropbox Family account?

If you’re experiencing problems with your Dropbox Family account, learn how to troubleshoot issues with joining a Family plan. Alternatively, you can contact Dropbox support.

How to share files and projects in Dropbox Replay

Once you add files or create projects in Dropbox Replay, you can share them with collaborators. You can also manage sharing permissions, viewer and comment access, download ability, and password protection. Admins have access to all Replay team files and projects.

Learn more about Dropbox Replay admin control features.

How to share files in Dropbox Replay

To share a video, image, audio, or PDF file in Dropbox Replay:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the thumbnail or in the row of the file you’d like to share.
  3. Click “…” (ellipsis) in the upper right.
  4. Click Share from the menu that appears.
    • Note: You can change all your file permissions from your Links tab if you have the Dropbox Replay Add-On.
  5. Select recipient access: 
    • View and comment: Collaborators can view the file and comments, and can add comments of their own.
    • View only: Collaborators can view the file, but can’t see or add comments.
      • Note: Click Manage settings to require a password, hide past comments, require a Dropbox login, enable downloads, or enable link access.
  6. Click Send or Copy link.
  7. Paste the link where you’d like to share it.

How to share or add people to projects in Dropbox Replay

To share or add people to a project in Dropbox Replay:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the file thumbnail or row of the project you would like to add people to.
  3. Click “…” (ellipsis) in the upper right.
  4. Click Add people.
  5. Enter the emails of the people you’d like to add.
    • Notes: 
      • Adding users to a project gives them control over the whole project and everything in it. 
      • You can only add a user to your project via email.
      • You can enter groups or teams you already made in your Dropbox account. Learn more about managing Dropbox Replay for your team.
  6. Add a message, if you’d like.
  7. Choose Can edit or Can comment,depending on the permissions you’d like to grant.
  8. Click Add.

How to enable or disable link access to your shared file

To enable link access to your shared file:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Open the file you’d like to enable link access to.
  3. Click Share in the top-right corner.
  4. Click Manage settings. 
  5. Check or uncheck the box beside Enable link access.

How to hide previous versions of a shared file or project

To only allow people to see the current version:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Open the file you’d like to enable link access to.
  3. Click Share in the top-right corner.
  4. Click Manage settings. 
  5. Check the box beside Hide past versions.

How to delete a user from your project

To delete a user from your project:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Click their avatar (profile picture or initials) at the bottom of the project thumbnail. 
  3. Click the dropdown menu next to their name.
  4. Click Remove.

How to password-protect your shared links

If you have the Replay Add-On, you can password-protect your shared links:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the thumbnail or row of the file or project you’d like to share.
  3. Click “…” (ellipsis) in the upper right corner.
  4. Click Share from the menu that appears.
  5. Click Manage settings.
  6. Check the box beside Require password.
  7. Enter the password in the box that appears and click Save.  

To edit an existing password, repeat steps 1 to 5 then click Edit password (under Require Password) to update the password.

How to add a watermark to your shared link

If you have the Replay Add-On, you can apply a default or customized watermark to your Dropbox Replay videos.

A default watermark link can be sent to your groups or teams, or you can add email addresses and send a new customized link for each email address. If your Replay file has a default watermark, you’ll see Watermark in the top-right corner of the thumbnail image.

Replay files with customized watermarks have the same setting options as a default watermark, but also include email tracking and record the IP address, date, and time of each view.

To add a watermark:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Open the Replay file you’d like to add a watermark to.
  3. Click Share in the upper right.
  4. Select the Watermark tab.
  5. If you haven’t created a watermark yet, click + New Link.
  6. Under the Customize tab, you can adjust these settings:
    • Display text 
    • Custom text
    • Position
    • Theme
    • Opacity
    • Size
  7. Click the Settings tab and adjust the settings, if needed. 
  8. Click Save.
  9. Click the Copy link.  

You can then paste the link with the watermark into an email, message, or anywhere people can access it.

How to add a due date to your shared link

If you have the Replay Add-On, you can add a due date for collaborators to encourage them to deliver timely feedback on your shared media file. You can only set one due date per file.

To add a due date:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Open the file you’d like to add a due date to.
  3. Click Share in the upper right corner. 
  4. Click Add due date and select a due date and time.
  5. Click Save.  

This due date will be visible to collaborators when they view the file in Replay.

How to manage your shared links from your Links page

If you have the Replay Add-On, you can manage your shared links for files and projects from your Links page in Dropbox Replay. You can also see file type, the date the file was created, who has access to your link, and the type of access they have.

To manage access to your files and projects:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Click Links.
    • To change access to a link, toggle Link access on or off. 
    • To share a specific version of a view only link, hover over the link address, click Copyto Clipboard and select which version you wish to send.
  3. Click Close.

How to share files or folders in Dropbox

Dropbox makes it easy to share files and folders with anyone, even if they don’t have a Dropbox account. Whether you’re collaborating with colleagues or sharing personal files, follow these steps to quickly share your content securely.

There are several ways to share the files and folders in your Dropbox account. Before you share, decide if:

  • You want people to have editor access
  • You want people to have viewer access only
  • You need to collect files from someone

Then, decide if you’d like to create a link to your file, folder, or request, or send an invitation via email from your Dropbox account.

If you’re a Dropbox Professional, Essentials, Standard, Business, Advanced, Business Plus, or Enterprise customer, you can also:

  • Customize sharing invitations and links with your professional branding
  • Control link sharing permissions for your team

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox helps you effortlessly share files and folders.

How do I invite people to edit my files or folders?

If you want the people you share with to be able to edit your files, you can share a folder with them. Changes to the contents inside a shared folder are synced with members of that folder almost instantly. It’s a great solution to working together on large projects, sharing important family photos or documents, and any other collaborative effort.

If you’re a member of a Dropbox team account, you can still choose who you want to share the link with even if the team admin changes default link sharing settings.

Learn how to share a folder.  

Share a link to edit files or folders

You can also create shared links to give edit access to your files or folders. 

Learn how to share a link to a file or folder.

How do I invite people to view my files or folders?

Depending on your account type, you can invite someone to view your files or folders by sharing a link or setting permissions. If you need someone to be able to see your files, but not edit them, you can send them a view-only link to that file, or you can give them view-only permissions.  

Share a view-only link to a file or folder

When you share a view-only link with someone, they can view and download the file or folder on dropbox.com. You can send a link by email, Facebook, X (formerly Twitter), instant message, social networks, wherever you want. You can share these links with anyone, even if they don’t have a Dropbox account.

The link opens as a preview on dropbox.com, and recipients can comment on the file.

Learn how to share a link to a file or folder.

How to collect files from people

You can collect files from people by creating a file request. Give the request a name and send the link to anyone you want to collect files from. People submitting files don’t need a Dropbox account.

Learn how to create a file request.

How to share in Dropbox

When you share a file or folder in Dropbox, the person you share it with will receive an email with a link to access it. To view or edit the shared content, the person must have a Dropbox account and be logged in. If they don’t have an account or prefer not to log in, you can share a view-only link instead.

Learn how to manage your default sharing settings.

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox helps you easily share folders.

How to share a link to a Dropbox file or folder

When you share a link, you can grant recipients either edit or view-only access. You can also customize and manage their permissions in your default sharing settings for greater control. 

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox helps you easily share folders.

How to share a Dropbox link

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the file or folder you’d like to share and click Share.
    • Note: You can preview files without opening them. Switch to grid layout, then move your cursor across the item to flip through pages, scrub through a video, or browse folder contents.
  3. Click Copy link.
  4. Click Manage.
    • Select Link for editing for a link with edit access.
    • Select Link for viewing for a link with view-only access.
  5. Click Copy link.

The link is now copied to your clipboard. You can paste it into an email, message, or wherever people can access it.

How to create a view-only QR code to a Dropbox file or folder

You can generate a view-only QR code to any file or folder in your Dropbox account and share it with others. To do so, follow these steps:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the file or folder you’d like to share and click Share.
  3. Click ☑ (more options).
  4. Click Create QR code.
  5. A QR code will be generated automatically for you.
  6. Click Save to download the QR code as a .png file.

Share the image with others so they can scan it to access a view-only version of your Dropbox file or folder.

How to manage links with edit or view-only access

You can make changes to a file or folder link after sharing it.

Learn how to manage Dropbox sharing permissions.

There are some exceptions to this, including if:

  • You remove someone’s access, and they still have a file or folder link, they could regain access. To prevent this, remove the link to the file or folder.
  • Someone you’ve shared a folder link with has joined that folder, the link permissions you set will no longer apply.
  • If you share a link with someone who has direct access, they could edit the shared link settings.

Can I protect my link with a passcode?

You can add passwords to shared links if you’re a Professional, Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise customer.

Customize links and settings

Dropbox Professional, Standard, Advanced, Business, Business Plus, and Enterprise customers can change link settings and customize shared links with professional branding.

Choose how shared links open

When you receive a shared link, you can choose to open that file or folder on dropbox.com or on the Dropbox desktop app.

To open shared links on the Dropbox desktop app by default:

  1. Click a shared link.
  2. If that file or folder is already synced to your device, you’ll be prompted to choose to open it on dropbox.com or on the Dropbox desktop app.
  3. Check Always open synced files in the desktop app.

To manage how shared links open:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click the Sharing tab.
  5. Toggle Open share links on desktop on or off.

Things to be aware of when sharing links to Dropbox files and folders

  • Customers on Dropbox Professional, Essentials, Standard, Advanced, Business, Business Plus, and Enterprise can set additional shared link permissions like passwords and expiration dates.
  • Team admins may change default link sharing settings, but team members can still choose who they want to share the link with.
  • Link settings, including passwords and other restrictions, apply only to people who access a file or folder through the shared link. Anyone added directly, or who already has access, keeps their existing permissions and isn’t affected by link settings.

Will my Dropbox link automatically grant edit access to my folder?

If you’re on a Dropbox Basic, Professional, or Plus account, you can give other Dropbox users edit access to your Dropbox files or folders via a link.

If you share with someone without a Dropbox account, they’ll only be able to preview the file or folder.

If you give another Dropbox user access to a file or folder, they can share that content with others. If you’re an admin on a Dropbox team, you can control the link settings for the rest of your team.

If you’re a member of a Dropbox team account, you can still adjust settings for certain items even if the team admin changes default link sharing settings.

How to sign a Dropbox Sign document

To sign a document you received through Dropbox Sign:

  1. The signing experience starts with an email from Dropbox Sign informing you of a signature request. Click Review & Sign in the blue box.
  2. A new window will open with the document you need to sign. Click Get Started.
  3. A box with Click to sign will indicate where your signature is required. If other actions are required (i.e. initials or checkbox), you will be prompted with the appropriate action and another box.
  4. You’ll be prompted, once you’ve completed all of your action items, to click Continue in a blue box at the top right.
  5. On the next screen, click I agree to confirm that you agree to the terms and to sign the document. If you agree to the terms, your portion of the document will be complete and you will be directed to a final page.

You do not need a Dropbox Sign account in order to access the document or complete a signature request. A PDF copy will be emailed to you, unless the sender has requested for this option to be removed.

Once you sign the document, we email the executed version to you (and the sender) and give you the option of creating a password to access the document on Dropbox Sign if you choose. Creating a password is completely optional!

We do not market or advertise to your clients in any way unless they choose to create a password and sign up for a Dropbox Sign account. If you are being asked to sign in, you have most likely signed a document via Dropbox Sign in the past, created a password, and don’t recollect doing so. You may choose to bypass it, but if you enter a password or have entered one previously, you will be asked to sign in the next time they use Dropbox Sign. All of your previously signed documents will be under this log in.

How to update link settings in Dropbox DocSend

You can make real-time changes to your shared links, from completely removing viewing access to adjusting security settings, all without interrupting your visitor’s viewing experience. This article guides you through the steps for updating document and space links to ensure you maximize the available link settings and maintain control over your shared content.

How to update a document link

  1. Click Content library in the left sidebar.
  2. Click the name of the document you want to update.
  3. Click ☑ (more options) next to the link you want to change.
  4. Select Edit linksettings.
  5. Configure your link settings.
  6. Click Update Link to save your changes.

How to update a space link

  1. Click Spaces in the left sidebar. 
  2. Click on the name of the space you want to update.
  3. Click Share in the upper-right corner.
  4.  Hover over the link you want to update.
  5. Click the edit icon next to the link you want to update.
  6. Make your updates.
  7. Click Save (if required).

How to use signer reassignment in Dropbox Sign

There are occasionally times when the requester will send a document for signature and the recipient isn’t the correct individual within their organization. In cases like this, Dropbox Sign offers a feature which allows the recipient to reassign the document to another individual. 

Enabling signer reassignment

After the requester has entered in the recipient’s name, there will be two checkboxes under the list of names. Check the box next to Enable signer reassignment to enable signer reassignment.

The Signer experience

When the recipient receives the email from Dropbox Sign letting them know they have a document to complete, there will be a note letting them know they can reassign the document at this point, if they already know this document should go to another individual. 

The signer can also open the document and use the three dot menu in the upper left corner to find the Reassign option. 

Once the signer has chosen to reassign the document a popup will appear asking for the name and email of the new signer and the reason for reassignment. 

After the document has been successfully reassigned all parties will receive an email with the reassignment update.

  • Requester: receives an email will provide a notification the document has been reassigned, by whom and who the new list of signers are. 
  • Original Signer: receives an email confirming the successful reassignment
  • New Signer: receives an email informing them they have a document to sign, that the document was reassigned to them, who reassigned it and why.

How to view sent and received transfers

You can view and manage transfers that you’ve sent or received from dropbox.com. This article walks you through previewing, editing, downloading, and deleting your transfers.

How to view and manage sent transfers

To view and manage transfers that you’ve sent:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click ☑ (dense grid organization) in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Transfer from the menu that appears.
  4. In the Sent tab, manage your transfers:
    • To change the name of a transfer, click a transfer, click ☑ (edit) to edit, type a new name, and click Save.
    • To view transfer activity, see the number of Views and Downloads next to each transfer.
      • To manage download notifications, click a transfer, toggle Download notifications to On or Off, then click Save.
    • To password protect a transfer when sending a copy, click on a transfer, type in a password, and click Done. The recipient will be prompted to enter the password when they go to open the transfer.
      • Note: This feature is only available to customers on Dropbox Professional, Essentials, Standard, Advanced, Business Plus, and Enterprise.
    • To change the expiration date of a transfer, click the date next to the transfer, then select a date using the date picker. 
      • Note: This feature is only available to customers on Dropbox Professional, Standard, Advanced, Education, and Enterprise, who can set the expiration date up to a year later.
    • To delete a transfer, click  (more options) next to a transfer, then click Delete.
      • Note: Deleted transfers can’t be recovered.

How to view and manage received transfers

To view and manage transfers that you’ve received:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click ☑ (dense grid organization) in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Transfer from the menu that appears.
  4. In the Received tab, manage your transfers:
    • To download files from a transfer, click  (more options) next to a transfer, then click Download.
    • To preview the transfer files, click the transfer to open it, then click the preview icon (eye).
    • To share the transfer files you’ve received, click the transfer to open it, then click  (link) to copy the transfer link to share.
    • To save the transfer files to your Dropbox account, click the transfer to open it, then click Save to Dropbox in the new page.
    • To delete a transfer, click  (more options) next to a transfer, and click Remove.

How to view expired transfers

To view your expired transfers:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click ☑ (dense grid organization) in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Transfer from the menu that appears.
  4. Click Expired. 

To reactivate an expired transfer, click on it, then click Reactivate transfer.

I received an “Unexpected error occurred” message in Dropbox Sign

Troubleshooting steps:

  1. First, try refreshing the page and signing the document again. We generally get that error when there is a temporary glitch in the system. Refreshing the page usually solves the issue.
  2. If you’re still having trouble, please contact our support team here and be sure to include:
  • the time of the error
  • the error code (if the error message provides one)
  • the name of the document you were working with
  • what you were trying to do: were you self signing, preparing a doc for someone else to sign, or signing a signature request?
  • the email address you were logged in with

And we’ll investigate further for you.

3. In the meantime while we’re investigating, try using another browser. Often, glitches are browser-specific, so you may be hitting a problem in Internet Explorer that you wouldn’t run into with Chrome, for instance.

Are you looking to retrieve an old document you signed? Please click here.

Important changes to the Dropbox Public folder

Dropbox Basic (free) users

As of March 15, 2017, the Public folder in your Dropbox account has been converted into a standard folder. By default this folder is private to your account and it acts just like any other folder that you’ve created. This transition will occur automatically.

Here’s what you need to know:

  • All files in your Public folder will remain safe, but public links to those files will stop working.
  • If someone visits a link to a file in your Public folder, they’ll see an error page.
  • To see a list of your public links, visit the Public folder. Any file in this folder will have had a public link associated with it.
  • Dropbox can’t convert existing public links into Dropbox shared links.
  • If you’d like to re-share any of the files in your Public folder, please use a shared folder or shared link.
Using the public folder to render HTML content

As of October 3, 2016, Dropbox Basic (free) users can no longer use public links to render HTML content in a web browser. 

If you’re a Basic user and you created a website that displays HTML content from your Dropbox account, it won’t work in the browser anymore. The HTML content itself remains safe in Dropbox, and you can share it using any of our other sharing methods.

Effective September 1, 2017, Dropbox Plus and team account users can no longer render HTML content. The Public folder and its sharing functionality have been disabled.

Accounts created after October 4, 2012

Dropbox accounts created after October 4, 2012, wouldn’t have had a Public folder. If you’d like to quickly share files you can use a shared link. Shared links work even if the person you’re sharing with doesn’t have a Dropbox account.

I’m having trouble with a shared folder

There are a few situations when shared folders might not work as expected. Check each of the situations outlined in this article to fix issues with shared folders.

If you don’t find an answer here, visit these articles:

  • Dropbox shared folders FAQs
  • Fix syncing problems in Dropbox
  • Solve issues with joining shared folders
  • Resolve error messages that happen when sharing  

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox helps you effortlessly share folders.

Why can’t I see the most recent versions of files in a shared folder?

There may be a few reasons that you can’t see the most recent versions of files in a shared folder. Visit this article on file syncing issues or check each of the situations below.

Scenario 1: If you delete a shared folder or remove it from your account, you can’t access the folder anymore. To check if you deleted a shared folder on dropbox.com:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click Shared in the left sidebar.
  3. Click the Folders tab at the top of the page.
    • When you hover over folders you’ve removed or shared folders you’ve yet to join, a Join folder button will appear. 
  4. Click Join folder to restore a folder to your account.

If you have the desktop app installed, the shared folder is automatically synced again. If the older version is in the same location, Dropbox syncs the new version and adds “(1)” to the end of the name. This ensures that every folder has a unique name.

You can change or update a file or folder’s default name. Learn how to rename a file or folder.

Scenario 2: If you can’t see files that you expect to see in a shared folder, and you didn’t delete them, you may have unintentionally deleted the folder.

Check that the folder is still shared:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click Shared in the left sidebar.
  3. Locate the shared folder.
    • If you see You haven’t joined this folder below the folder name, you don’t have access to the shared folder. To get access, hover over the folder and click Join folder. 
    • If the shared folder is active, check if your files are in the shared folder on dropbox.com. If they’re missing, learn how to recover or restore your files.

Why can’t I see the shared folder options window?

If the shared folder options window doesn’t pop up when you click Share…, you may be experiencing an issue caused by a third-party browser extension or add-on (such as a pop-up or ad blocker).  

To fix this problem, temporarily disable any browser extensions or add-ons that are running. Once you change your shared folder settings and no longer need the shared folder options window, you can restore these browser extensions.  

If you’d like to continue using the extension, you may be able to create an exception for Dropbox, or whitelist 0. However, not all extensions support this functionality.

Why can’t I share a folder inside another shared folder?

If you can’t share a folder inside another folder, your sharing permissions in that folder may be limited by the owner of the parent folder. Try contacting the owner of the parent folder to share a folder inside their shared folder.  

If you still can’t share a subfolder, you may have reached the limit on how many shared subfolders can be created in a single folder. Learn more about shared folder limits.

I’m a Dropbox Family customer

Dropbox Family customers can’t directly share subfolders that are inside parent shared folders. Learn how to share files or folders inside a parent shared folder via a link.

What happens if I move a shared folder into a team folder?

If you move a shared folder into a team folder, you transfer ownership of that folder to the team. You no longer own the folder, and you can’t remove the folder from the team folder.  

If you’d like, you can make a copy of the folder and move it to the preferred location in your account.

What happens if the owner of a shared folder leaves?

The owner is likely the person who originally invited you to the shared folder. If you don’t see an owner for a shared folder, the owner may have already left it. If this happens you can contact the original owner and ask them to first add the folder back to their Dropbox, and then transfer ownership to you.

If you can’t contact the owner, you can:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Drag the files from the old folder to this new folder.
  3. Re-invite members of the old shared folder to this new shared folder.

If you’re the owner of a shared folder and leave it without transferring ownership, the shared folder will be without an owner. The owner is the only member who can remove members from the folder.  

If you don’t need this folder anymore, but another member does, you can make them the owner. First, you’ll need to add the shared folder back to your Dropbox account.

Learn how to transfer ownership of the folder to another member.  

How can I get edit permissions to a shared folder I can only view?

A shared folder owner or editor can change permissions. If you need to have a different role within a shared folder, contact the owner or any current editor and ask them to update your permissions. Learn more about roles in a shared folder.  

How do I know if my folder has been shared?

To check that a folder is actively shared between you and the other people you’d like to have access to it:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click Shared in the left sidebar.
    • For folders someone else owns: If you don’t see the shared folder listed, then you’re not currently a member. Contact the owner to share it with you.
    • For folders you own: If the person you want to share a folder with doesn’t see it listed, then they’re not currently a member. They should check the Shared page to see if they can click Join folder on the folder. If they don’t see the folder there, they should contact you.

How can I see members of a shared folder?

You can see the members of a shared folder by following the instructions below:  

On dropbox.com

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the folder you’d like to view the members of and click “⋮” (Vertical ellipsis).
  3. Select Manage Permissions.
  4. Click the People tab.  

On the Dropbox desktop app

  1. Open the Dropbox folder in File Explorer (Windows) or Finder (Mac).
  2. Right-click the folder you’d like to view the members of and select Share… next to the Dropbox icon.
  3. Click Who can access.  

On the Dropbox mobile app

  1. Open the Dropbox mobile app.
  2. Tap the “⁝” (vertical ellipsis on Android) or “…” (iOS) next to the correct folder.
  3. Tap Manage access.
  4. Tap the area below [x] members.

What if files are missing from a shared folder that I don’t own?

If files appear to be missing from a shared folder, first check that the folder is active and that other members are using it. Learn how to view file activity in Dropbox.

To check if files are missing:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com. 
  2. Click Shared in the left sidebar.
  3. Click on the shared folder to see if the files appear. If they don’t, then the shared folder owner (or a member with edit access) may need to re-share them.

What can I do if a shared folder has the same name as another folder?

If you join a shared folder that has the same name as a folder already in your Dropbox account, a (1) is appended to the new shared folder name.  

Rename the original folder causing the naming conflict (the one without a (1)). You can then remove the (1) from the shared folder name.

Link settings in Dropbox DocSend Spaces

With Spaces, you can share multiple files or a data room with a single link. Once you’ve created a Space, share it by inviting people to a group or by creating a Space link. Learn more about creating a Space.  

How to create a Space link

To create a Space link from the Spaces page:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Spaces in the left sidebar.
  3. Click the Share button next to the Space you want to share.
  4. Click Create link.
  5. Enter a company or client name under Add a company or client name.
  6. Configure the link settings if required.
  7. Click Create link.
  8. Click either View as visitor to view your new link, or Copy to share the link with others.  

How to delete, deactivate, or preview a link

To delete a link:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Permissions in the left side bar.
  3. Select the link you want to delete.
  4. Click  (more options) next to Copy link in the upper-right corner of the Action Bar.
  5. Select Delete link.

This is an action that can’t be reversed.  

To deactivate a link:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Permissions in the left side bar.
  3. Select the link you want to deactivate.
  4. Click  (more options) next to Copy link in the upper-right corner of the Action Bar.
  5. Click Deactivate link.

To preview a link:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Permissions in the left side bar.
  3. Select the link you want to preview.
  4. Click  (more options) next to Copy link in the upper-right corner of the Action Bar.
  5. Click View as visitor.

This allows you to preview how the link appears to visitors with current settings applied.

Space link settings

Create link

When you click Create link in Spaces, the link is automatically created for you. You can then copy the link to share with others or customize your link from the dropdown menu.

Link settings in the Dropbox DocSend Content library

Content library is designed for sharing individual documents you want to distribute quickly and easily. When you share multiple files from the Content library, DocSend automatically creates a Space to organize and manage those files collectively. Learn more about sharing multiple files in Spaces.

How to create a link for a document

  1. Click Content library.
  2. Select the document you want to create a link for.
  3. Click  (more options).
  4. Click Create link.
  5. Configure your link settings.
  6. Click Create link.
  7. Click Copy link to share the link.  

How to access and copy links

To access the links you’ve created for a document, you’ll first need to open it. Once open, you’ll find a list of all the links you’ve created in the All links section.

  1. Click Content library.
  2. Select a document from your library.
  3. Navigate to the All links section.
  4. Hover over the link you want to copy and click Copy to clipboard.  

How to create a link for multiple documents

You can save time by creating a link for multiple documents directly from your content library.

  1. Click Content library.
  2. Click Share.
  3. Select the content you want to create a link for.
    • Note: If you’re subscribed to a Personal plan and want to share multiple pieces of content, you’ll need to upgrade your plan.
  4. Click Continue.
  5. Click Create link.

Content library link settings

You can configure general link settings for your document uploads and create a custom DocSend link using your company or brand name, a folder name, or another name you prefer.

Add a company or client name

In the add a company or client name section, you can create a name to associate the link and visits to the company, client, or target audience you’re sharing content with.

Manage file access

In the Manage file access section, choose from the following options to control who can access your content.

Add extra security settings

In the Add extra security settings section, choose from the following options to further protect your content.

Customize link

In the Customize link section, you can personalize the URL to make it easier for visitors to recognize.

Manage external sharing in your team

Sharing files and folders outside your team

These settings allow you to choose individual Dropbox products to allow or limit sharing outside the team.

Who can be added to files and folders

This setting controls whether team members can invite people outside the team to view or edit files and folders by email or entire email domains.

If Who can be added to files and folders is set to Members + approved people, you can add individual users by email or entire email domains. To add people or valid email domains to the approved list:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Under Products, click the dropdown to the left of Dropbox.
  4. Click Settings.
  5. Under External sharing, scroll to Who can be added to files and folders.
  6. Change Members only to Members + approved people
  7. Click Manage to the right of the Approved list.
  8. Enter the email of the user or the entire email domain that you want to add to the approved list.
  9. Press enter on your keyboard.
  10. Click Done.
  11. Click Save on the banner at the bottom of your screen.

Share links to files and folders

This setting controls whether team members can share links with people outside the team.

  • On: Team members can share links with people outside the team. Team members can override the Default shared link privacy setting described below.
  • Off: Team members can’t share links with people outside the team or create new links. In addition, existing links created by team members will no longer work for people outside the team.

 

Share files using Transfer

This setting applies to files sent using Dropbox Transfer. To manage this setting:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Under Products, click the dropdown to the left of Dropbox.
  4. Click Settings.
  5. Under External sharing, scroll to Sharing files using Transfer.
  6. Toggle Share files using Transfer to On.
Share Replay content outside your team

This setting applies to links sent using Dropbox Replay. To manage this setting:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Under Products, click the dropdown to the left of Dropbox.
  4. Click Settings.
  5. Under External sharing, scroll to the Sharing Replay content outside your team section.
  6. Next to Who can be added to Replay projects or Who can members share links to Replay files and projects with, click the dropdown menu and select either:
    • Anyone
    • Members + approved people
    • Members only 

Shared file link settings

These settings apply to files shared by links. They don’t apply to Signatures activity, Dropbox Replay, or Dropbox Transfer links.

Default access for shared links

This setting controls the default privacy of shared links created by team members.

  • Anyone: Anyone can access shared links by default, regardless of whether or not they’re part of the team.
  • Only people added: Team members must invite someone to access the link they create.
  • Members only: Only team members can access shared links by default.

Default permissions for shared links

This setting controls the default permissions for shared links created by team members.

  • None: Team members can specify their own default permissions for shared links.
  • Can view: Anyone with access to the file via link can only view it.
  • Can edit: Anyone with access to the file via link can edit it.

Set an expiration for new links shared outside your team

This setting allows you to set a specific expiration date for shared links created by team members. After the selected date, Dropbox will automatically disable the shared link. Anyone attempting to access the link after the expiry date will be given an error message.

Require password for new links shared outside your team

This setting allows your team members to set an access password when creating a shared link.

  • On: People with the link will need a password to view it. The team member who creates the link needs to share the password with the recipient.
  • Off: The recipient doesn’t need a password to access shared links.

Blanket link restrictions

If you’re an admin on a Dropbox team, you can manage link access to your team’s shared folders and subfolders. Enabling link restrictions prevents Dropbox users who haven’t been added to a shared folder from accessing that folder via link. This overrides individual folder sharing settings.

  • On: All shared folders will have link restrictions enabled.
  • Off: Link restrictions won’t be enabled by default, but team members can still enable them on specific shared folders.

If you’re not an admin, you can set link restrictions for individual folders that you own.  

To do this:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the name of the folder and click Share.
  3. In the popup, click ☑(settings).
  4. Select the Folder settings tab.
  5. Toggle Link restrictions to On.  

Folders shared with the team

Adding outside folders

Choose if team members can add editable folders from outside of your Dropbox team: 

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Under Products, click the dropdown to the left of Dropbox.
  4. Click Settings.
  5. Under Content, scroll to the Receiving content section.
  6. Toggle Outside folders to On.

Manage external sharing in your team

Sharing files and folders outside your team

These settings allow you to choose individual Dropbox products to allow or limit sharing outside the team.

Who can be added to files and folders

This setting controls whether team members can invite people outside the team to view or edit files and folders by email or entire email domains.

If Who can be added to files and folders is set to Members + approved people, you can add individual users by email or entire email domains. To add people or valid email domains to the approved list:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Under Products, click the dropdown to the left of Dropbox.
  4. Click Settings.
  5. Under External sharing, scroll to Who can be added to files and folders.
  6. Change Members only to Members + approved people
  7. Click Manage to the right of the Approved list.
  8. Enter the email of the user or the entire email domain that you want to add to the approved list.
  9. Press enter on your keyboard.
  10. Click Done.
  11. Click Save on the banner at the bottom of your screen.

Share links to files and folders

This setting controls whether team members can share links with people outside the team.

  • On: Team members can share links with people outside the team. Team members can override the Default shared link privacy setting described below.
  • Off: Team members can’t share links with people outside the team or create new links. In addition, existing links created by team members will no longer work for people outside the team.

Password-protected documents in Dropbox DocSend

DocSend currently does not support files that are password protected. If a password-protected file is uploaded, you’ll see the following error message:

This document appears to be password-protected. We do not currently support password-protected documents.

While you’ll need to remove the password configured on your document to successfully upload it to DocSend, you can still add protection to your shared content by enabling Passcode protection on your link settings. 

If you’re on the Advanced plan, you can enable enhanced-security features like Allowed Viewers, Email Authentication, Watermarking, Agreements for access gating. Visit our Security section for more details.

Requesting attachments from signers in Dropbox Sign

When sending a request in Dropbox Sign, you can ask signers to attach additional files when they complete their request.

How to request attachments

When you request attachments, the signer will be prompted to add the requested flies at the end of the signing experience.

To request attachments:

  1. Choose to send a one-off signature request or create a standard template and upload your file(s), then select Next.
  2. Add the signer or role.
  3. Click  next to the signer or role. 
  4.  Enter the name of the file being requested, such as “Photo ID” or “Verification of employment.”
  5. Add a description or additional information for the signer (optional).
  6. Click the checkbox next to Required, if you’d like to require the signer to include the attachment.
  7. Click Add if more files need to be requested.
  8. Click Done to finish and return to the document.

Resolving a busy line tone with Dropbox Fax

Starting the day your number is activated with our service, people sending you a fax will have to dial the 1 before your number, or else the fax will not go through and your number will be giving a busy tone.

This is because our provider is an international company. If the sender is faxing locally, adding the 1 should not affect rates, since the area code remains the same.

See document performance in Dropbox DocSend

The Performance tab provides a summary of all the document’s visit activity to keep you up-to-date on how the document is being utilized. You can access the performance tab directly from the document.

Latest Version Highlights

This report will summarize your document’s most recent version and its performance by detailing the following: 

  • Core Metrics is an overview of how the latest version is performing with the average percentage of the document viewed and the total visits gathered.
  • Top Pages shows the most actively visited page(s) and provides the average time spent on a page, the page number in the document, and total visits to the page.  

Comparative Stats & Versions

The Comparative Stats report provides a comparative view of your document versions. Each version will be color-coded, and you can select the toggle located on the right of the report to switch between the different versions. With the interactive graph, you can compare:

  • Time Per Page is the average time spent on each page. You can hover any point on the graph to see the time spent per page.
  • Dropoff Report shows the percentage of visits that reach each page in your document, hovering over each point will list the percentage and amount of visits that reached the page.

Visit Map

The Visit Map is a summary of all the locations listed in the Recent Activity tab of the document. You can interact with the map to zoom in on each location your document is being accessed.

Things to consider

  • The Performance tab is not available for URL content since these visits are ungated; see Share External URL Links to learn more. 
  • Visitors using a VPN connection may show the location of the VPN server instead of the visitor’s actual location.

Set up viewer email validation in Dropbox DocSend

When Require email to view is enabled, you can use viewer email validation to confirm that a visitor’s email address comes from a valid, deliverable source. This helps you accurately identify who’s accessing your shared content. 

Temporary or disposable email addresses, such as those from Mailinator or Guerilla Mail, are automatically marked invalid. Visitors will need to use a valid email address to access your content. 

Configure email validation

As the account owner or admin, you can enable or disable the viewer email validation at the company level. When disabled, visitors can enter invalid  or disposable email addresses and still access shared content, making it harder to track who viewed your content. 

To configure viewer email validation:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Go to Company settings.
  3. Click the Privacy & Security tab.
  4. Disable or enable next to Attempt to confirm that visitors’ email addresses can receive messages.

User experience: Invalid email address

When a visitor enters an invalid email address, you’ll receive an email alert. 

Disable unauthorized email notification

To disable these alerts:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Go to Notification settings.
  3. Toggle disableor enable next to When a viewer attempts access with an unauthorized email.
  4. Select Save Changes.

Visitor viewer experience: Invalid email address

If visitors enter an invalid email address, they’ll be prompted to enter a valid one before accessing your content.

If a valid address is mistakenly flagged as invalid, the visitor can verify it by following these steps:

  1. Click Click here to verify this email address in the prompt.
  2. Open the verification email in their inbox and select Verify your email address.

Once verified, the email remains valid for 30 days, so the visitor won’t need to repeat the process during that time.

Share external URL links with Dropbox DocSend

You can upload an external URL link to DocSend to share and track visits to an external web page. Though visit data is limited for external URL links, DocSend offers basic visitor information that can give you valuable insight.

Upload an external URL link to DocSend

Uploading an external URL link is similar to uploading a document to DocSend.

To upload an external URL link:

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Content library in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Upload.
  4. Select Add URL from the dropdown menu.
  5. Name your URL link and add the hyperlink.
  6. Click Create URL.

Share an external URL link

Once you uploaded the external URL link, you can create a DocSend link to share the URL. Since external URL links are ungated, publicly accessible sites, only a handful of link settings are available for such links.

The link settings available for external URL links are:

  • Account
  • Expiration

Visit data for external URL links

To review visit data on an external URL link, you can check out the Recent Activity tab. DocSend provides basic visit information on external URL links, including:

  • Visitor’s device and operating system (OS)
  • Visitor’s geolocation
  • Time of visit  

Things to consider

  • Content previews on URL links only appear if there’s an image set for the site.
  • External URL links are disabled during the free trial. For security reasons, this feature is only available on a paid plan.

Shared with me feature in Dropbox DocSend

The Shared with me feature allows you to view and manage all of your visited content in one place. Every data room you have visited or document you have opened is listed in the Shared with me tab so you don’t have to keep track of each link separately. These features will enable you to collaborate more effectively and access shared content with ease.  

How to access Shared with me

To access Share with me:

  1. Log in to docsend.com or create a new account.
  2. Click Shared with me in the left sidebar.

Links to your recently viewed data spaces and documents will be listed.  

How to access Shared with me as a visitor

  1. Click on the link in your email to view shared DocSend content.
  2. Follow prompts to register and create a free user account.
  3. Verify your email.
  4. Log in to docsend.com.

You will have a view-only account that consolidates all links sent to you within Shared with me.

Expired links within Shared with me

“Expired” is displayed next to expired links in Shared with me. You can see the expiration date by hovering over the link. If a link has an upcoming expiration date, that date will be listed next to the link.

Things to consider

  • Shared with me will only show links you visited using your email address to view. Any spaces you own will be still be stored under Spaces.
  • If a data space or document has been inactivated or deleted, it will not be shown in the list.

Troubleshooting shared links

If your shared link isn’t working or if it’s showing a 404 error, check the following possible reasons why:

Did you delete the file or folder?

Your shared link won’t work if the file or folder was deleted. If you restore the deleted file or folder, the shared link will work again.

Did you delete the link?

If you do not see the link in your list, you may have deleted it. You can create a new link to the file or folder you want to share.

Has the link expired?

If you’re on Dropbox Professional, Essentials, Standard, Advanced, Business, Business Plus, or Enterprise and you set an expiration for your shared link, it may have expired. When a link expires, it stops working, but you can re-enable it by editing the expiration date. Learn how to set an expiration date to your shared links.

Is the file in a shared folder?

If you’re on a Dropbox team account and the file you’re trying to share is within a shared folder, the folder owner may have changed the settings so that links can only be shared with other team members. The team admin can also turn off the ability to share links with people outside the team.

Were you removed or deleted from a Dropbox team account?

When you’re removed or deleted from a Dropbox team account, you lose access to all team files and Paper docs. Shared links you create may also be deleted, depending on the permission settings:

  • Any shared links you create with view-only access are deleted, unless they’re web-based files, like Paper or Google docs.
  • Any shared links you create with edit access remain active.

Was your link banned?

Dropbox bans shared links when they’re responsible for unusually large amounts of traffic, or when they violate the Acceptable Use Policy (for example, by hosting spam or malware). Learn more about banned links.

Did you rewind your Dropbox account?

If you recently rewound your Dropbox account, your shared link might not work as expected.

We recommend you:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com. 
  2. Click Shared in the left sidebar.
    • Click More in the left sidebar if you don’t see Shared.
  3. Click   (more options) next to the folder you’re having issues with.
  4. Select Share. 
  5. Click either Link for editing or Link for viewing, depending on which link you’d like to remove.
  6. Click Delete link.
  7. Click Delete again.
  8. Create a new shared link to the file.

Does the shared link open in your browser?

If you click a shared link and it won’t open, you may be encountering a browser issue. To correct this, log out of Dropbox and click the shared link again.

Is the link still not working?

If you’re still having an issue with a shared link, we recommend you contact the person who created the shared link, or contact support if you’re the one who created the link.  Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox makes managing file permissions easy.

Using the Activity tab in Dropbox DocSend

The Activity tab gives you an overview of how your visitors are interacting with your shared content. Located on the document page, this tab highlights the page-by-page analytics, and details of the visitor, such as their name, location and device, and much more.  

Recent Visits

The Recent Visits section is a list of all the visits for the document, across all links. 

In this section you can:

  • Click the visitor’s name or email address to open the Contact page. 
    • Note: To identify your visitor, Require email to view must be enabled. Without this enabled, the visit will only capture the visitor’s operating system and geolocation. See Link Settings Explained to learn more. 
  • Hover over the “device” icon to see the viewing device.
  • Hover over the “operating system” icon to see the operating system.
  • Click the location to open an interactive map view.
  • Click the account name to open the related Account page.
  • See the total duration of the visit.
  • Hover over the Total Time Spent Per Page chart to see a preview of the page, page number, and time spent on the page. 
  • Hover over the circle icon to see the percentage of the document viewed.

All Links

The All Links section lists all links created for the document. 

In this section, you can:

  • See the account associated with each link.
  • Copy a link to your clipboard.
  • Toggle a link’s accessibility on or off.
  • Update the link settings for a specific link.
  • Click the dropdown to the right of a link to view additional visit details for that link.  

Things to consider

  • Clicked hyperlinks will be listed under the Total Time Spent Per Page chart as In-document link clicks. 
  • Other visit attributes are also shown on this page; this includes downloads, signatures, an NDA badge (if the visitor signed an NDA), and a verification badge (if the visitor verified their email address).
    • Exception: Download-only content will show partial tracking data; take a look at Download-only Content for more information.
  • Only the Owner and Admins can view other team members’ links and visitor activity.
  • While the location information provided is generally correct there may be situations where a document visitor’s listed location will be different than what is expected. This may occur if a visitor is using a VPN then their IP address will be listed as coming from the location of their company’s VPN server.
  • Visitor activity can be exported on the document level if you’re on Standard and higher-tiered plans.

Using the Contacts tab in Dropbox DocSend

The Contacts tab will show the individual visitors, and all their most recent activities while viewing your content. You’ll be able to filter through contacts across your team or personal contacts.

Contacts in-app

When Require email to view is enabled, your visitor is prompted to input their email. Once provided, our systems will generate a contact profile with public information linked to the email address provided. Learn more about link settings.

Contact page layout

The Contacts tab shows all content visits and document signatures on an individual visitor level. As you begin to receive visits, a contact profile will be generated for each visitor on the Contacts tab page.

Delete contacts

  • Phone numbers

To delete a contact:

Edit contacts
