Editing Dropbox Sign templates after sending

If you need to edit a template or template link, but have already sent out requests using the pre-edited version, there are a few things to consider.

Editing a Template If you edit a template and have already used it to send out requests, you will need to cancel the issued requests and re-send them using your new edited version.

Editing a Template Link If you edit a template link, this will update in real time and the link will stay the same. You won’t need to re-issue the link. However, any signatures that were collected with the older version will need to be redone.

Excel support in Dropbox DocSend

Overview

Spreadsheets can be previewed in the DocSend document viewer without link recipients having to download them first. This is a convenient way to share spreadsheets without having to worry about them accidentally downloading or sharing the sensitive data that may be contained in the spreadsheet.

Visitor experience

When a link recipient opens a spreadsheet preview in DocSend, they can view it in a web browser without downloading it. The spreadsheet will be displayed similarly to how it would be in Microsoft Excel. Visitors can interact with the spreadsheet by scrolling, zooming, and selecting cells. However, they can’t edit the spreadsheet.

Things to consider

  • Supported spreadsheet formats include:
    • Excel (.xls, .xlsx, .xlsm)
    • Google Sheets (.gsheet)
    • Open Document Spreadsheets (.ods)
    • Comma-separated values (.csv)
  • Spreadsheets larger than 40 MB cannot be displayed in the DocSend document viewer. They will be download-only.
  • The maximum upload limit for spreadsheets is 2 GB.
  • The spreadsheet viewer supports features available up to Microsoft Excel 2016. Features introduced after 2016 may not appear in the viewer or may cause errors when loaded.
  • Watermarking is not available for spreadsheets.

Export Dropbox Paper docs

You can convert any of your existing docs to a .docx (Microsoft Word), .md (Markdown), or .pdf (PDF) file.

Export a Paper doc

  1. Click ✗ (more options) in the Paper doc you’re viewing.
  2. Click Export.
  3. Choose the file format for your download.
  4. Click Download.

Export all of the docs you’ve created

You can export all of the docs that you’ve created at once by following these steps:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click ☑ (dense grid organization) in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Paper from the menu that appears.
  4. Click your avatar (profile picture or initials) in the bottom-left corner.
  5. Click Download docs you created.
  6. Choose the format for your download: Microsoft Word (.docx) or Markdown (.md).
  7. Click Export.  

Admins on Dropbox team accounts

If you’re an admin on a Dropbox team account, you can export all of your team Paper docs if you disable Paper for your team. 

Learn how to export all docs.

Find and replace words in a Paper doc

You can find every time a specific word or phrase was written in a Paper doc by using the keyboard shortcut. You can then replace that word or phrase with a different word or phrase once, or throughout the entire doc.

To find a specific word or phrase in your Paper doc:

  1. Type control-F (Windows) or command-F (Mac).
  2. Type the word or phrase into the search bar.

To replace that word with a different word once, or throughout the entire doc: 

  1. Click the “…” (ellipsis) to the right of the search bar.
  2. Type the new word or phrase under Replace with.
  3. Click Replace or Replace all.

How text flows in Dropbox Sign text boxes

Any text box, including those spanning multiple lines, will start the flow of text in the upper left-hand corner as seen below:

 

 

The default font is Helvetica Neue at 11 point size font for text boxes. The text box font size will automatically shrink down to 8 point size font before we stop accepting input.

How to add a signature to a PDF

You can self-sign PDFs while editing them on dropbox.com or the Dropbox mobile app. Using this feature will link your Dropbox Sign and primary Dropbox accounts if both are under the same email address. If you don’t already have a Dropbox Sign account, self-signing a PDF will create a Basic account under the email affiliated with your Dropbox account.

How to add a signature in a PDF on dropbox.com

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click the name of the PDF file you’d like to sign.
  3. Click Edit above the file preview. This will open the editing mode.
  4. Click Sign above the file preview. 
  5. Add your signature. 
    • To draw a signature, click Draw from within the Sign toolbar. Add your signature using your mouse or mousepad. 
    • To type your signature, click Type, then type your name. To change the signature font, click Change font in the lower left of the signature window.
    • To upload your signature, click Upload. Click Upload Photo to make a selection from your desktop or Dropbox files. 
      • Note: Signature photos must be smaller than 40MB and must be one of these file types: .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .bmp, or .gif.
  6. Click Insert to add your selected signature option to the PDF. 
  7. Click Done.
    • Your edited PDF will be saved as a new file within your Dropbox account. Anyone with access to the original file won’t see the changes.

How to add a signature to a PDF on the Dropbox mobile app

iOS and Android

  1. Open the Dropbox mobile app.
  2. Navigate to the PDF you’d like to self-sign.
  3. Tap the PDF to open a preview.
  4. Tap Edit/Sign in the lower left.
  5. Choose Only you.
  6. Tap Add signature.
    • If you don’t have a saved signature, draw your signature under Sign your name.
    • If you have a saved signature, tap the desired signature under Select signature.
    • To add a saved signature, tap + (plus sign) next to Edit signature, draw your new signature, then tap Done.
    • To edit your saved signatures, tap Edit next to Select signature.
  7. Move and resize your signature to the desired area.
  8. Tap Save.

How to add a watermark to files in your Dropbox account

Watermarking is a way to safeguard your images or PDFs from being downloaded and used without your permission.

How to add a watermark

You must be the file owner to add a watermark. To add a watermark to an image or PDF file in your Dropbox account:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click the name of the file to open its preview.
  3. Click Watermark. Or, click the Edit button in the top left and select Watermark in the dropdown.
    • If you’re previewing the file in quick view, click “…” (ellipsis). Then, click Watermark.
  4. Customize your watermark if desired.
  5. Click Save.
    • Select Make a copy or Replace original. 
      • Make a copy will create a watermarked copy of the file with (Watermarked) appended to the filename.
      • Replace original will modify the original file.

How to customize a watermark

You can edit the positioning, rotation, transparency, and size of a watermark. To do so:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click the name of the file to open its preview.
  3. Click Watermark in the menu bar or click the Edit button and select Watermark in the dropdown.
    • If you’re previewing the file in quick view, click “…” (ellipsis). Then, click Watermark.
  4. Click Text or Image to choose the style of watermark.
  5. Edit one or more of the watermark settings below.
    • Select an option from the Position dropdown menu to change the position of the watermark on the file.
    • Select an option from the Color dropdown menu to choose a Dark or Light shade for the watermark on the file.
    • Click the Rotation icons (arrow in a circle) to change the rotation of the watermark in 15 degree increments.
    • Edit the Opacity and Size sliders to change the transparency and size of the watermark on the file.

How to remove a watermark

If you chose Replace original when you added your watermark, you can remove the watermark from your file. To do so:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click the name of the file to open its preview.
  3. Click the File tab.
    • Make sure you have your previews set to Full screen.
  4. Click Version history.
  5. Select the version without the watermark to preview it, then click the X in the upper left to close the preview.
  6. Hover over the version without the watermark and click Restore.
  7. Click the Restore button in the notification that appears.

How to add a watermark to all files in a folder

To add a watermark to all the documents in a folder:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click the folder where you’d like to add a watermark.
  3. Click “…” (ellipsis).
  4. Click Add automation.
  5. Select Watermark files.
  6. Check the box to Include files in all subfolders.
  7. Click Text or Image to choose the style of watermark.
  8. Adjust the watermark settings as needed. You can see a preview of your files with watermarks in the panel on the right.
    • Select an option from the Position dropdown to change the position of the watermark on the file.
    • Select an option from the Color dropdown to choose a Dark or Light shade for the watermark on the file.
    • Click the Rotation icons (arrow in a circle) to change the rotation of the watermark in 15 degree increments.
    • Drag the Opacity and Size sliders to change the transparency and size of the watermark on the file.
  9. Click Save.

Watermarking for Dropbox teams

Team admins can allow members to create custom watermarks:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Scroll down to Additional settings and click Watermarking.
  5. Toggle Watermarking to “On.”

How to add an expiration date and time to your Dropbox Sign signature request

If you’re on a paid Dropbox Sign plan, you can add an expiration date and time to your initial and pending signature requests. You can also edit all aspects of your pending requests. Learn how to edit your pending requests.

To add an expiration date and time:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Click Documents in the left sidebar.
  3. Click “…” (ellipsis) on the document you’d like to edit the expiration date and time for.
  4. Click Add expiration date.
  5. Select Expiration date from the dropdown menu.
  6. In the Edit expiration date window that appears:
    • Note: Your selected date must be more than 24 hours from the current date and time and within 90 days. 
  • To add a date, click the calendar icon and use the date picker to select a date for the request to expire.
  • To add a time, click the clock icon and select a time from the dropdown menu for the expiration time. 
  1. Click Save.

The signer will receive an email letting them know their signature is requested by the expiration date and time you entered. 

Notes for expiration date feature:

  • Signers will receive an email letting them know their signature is requested by the expiration date you enter. 
  • When a signer opens your request, the expiration date and time will be displayed in a banner at the top of your document in their localized time zone.
  • Once the request is sent, you can see the expiration date in the View info panel on the Documents page.
  • The sender must include an expiration date with a specified timezone. If the signer doesn’t have an account with a set timezone, the default timezone will be PDT.
    • Example: If the sender sets the expiration date to January 1 at 5:00 PM ET, the expiration date will be displayed to the signer as January 1 at 2:00 PM PDT if they aren’t signed in to an account with a set timezone.
  • Signature request reminder emails will be sent to signers 3 and 7 days before the signature request expires.

How to add conditional logic in Dropbox Sign

Conditional logic is available to Dropbox Sign users on a Premium plan.

Conditional logic allows you to create rules, or conditions, that change which fields appear on a document based on input from a signer. For example, you could use conditional logic to set up your document so that if a signer checks a checkbox, a dropdown field will appear. You can add conditional logic to signature requests and templates.

Before you create a conditional logic rule, you’ll need to choose a trigger field and selected fields. The trigger field, when completed by the signer, will trigger the selected fields to appear or remain hidden. In the example above, the checkbox is the trigger field and the dropdown is the selected field.

To create a conditional logic rule:

  1. Follow the instructions to send a signature request on hellosign.com until you get to the document editor.
  2. Click and drag the fields you’d like to add from the left sidebar to your document.
    • Note: The trigger field and selected fields have to be assigned to the same signer. You can’t set up a trigger field that, when completed by one signer, triggers fields for another signer.
  3. Click the field you’d like to use as a trigger field.
  4. Click Create Rule under Conditional Logic in the right sidebar.
  5. Click the dropdown below If the following is true… and select a condition for your trigger field.
  6. Click and drag the fields you’d like to use as selected fields from the document to the area below then Show/Hide the following field(s).
  7. Click the dropdown next to then and select whether you want to show or hide the selected fields based on the condition you set for the trigger field.
  8. Click Done, and continue sending your signature request as usual.

How to add content to a Paper doc with quick-add commands

You can quickly add or create content in a Paper doc using the forward slash key and a command. Here’s how:

  1. Type “/” (forward slash) on your keyboard. 
  2. Type a command from the list below.
  3. Press the Enter key. 

For example, if you want to insert a to-do item into your doc, you can type “/todo” and press Enter. Learn more about to-dos in Paper.

Here’s a full list of the commands and associated actions available with Dropbox Paper.

How to add video transcripts and captions in Dropbox Replay

You can add transcripts to video and audio files in Dropbox Replay, and create closed captions for videos. Once generated, you can edit the transcript, select a section to skip to that timestamp, and copy or share the transcripts.

How to add transcripts in Dropbox Replay

To add a video or audio transcript:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Open the video or audio file you’d like to transcribe.
  3. Click the Transcript tab at the top of the Comments sidebar.
    • Note: If the right sidebar isn’t open, click the show icon (arrow pointing left with a vertical line) in the upper right of the screen.

Your transcript may take a few minutes to generate, depending on the length of the video or audio file. When ready, you’ll see it in the Transcript tab in the right sidebar.  

How to edit transcripts in Dropbox Replay

To use the edit tool to modify a video or audio transcript:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Open the video or audio file with the transcript you’d like to edit.
  3. Hover over the section you’d like to edit.
  4. Click  (pencil icon), then edit the text in the box.
  5. Click the checkmark to save.

How to copy your entire transcripts in Dropbox Replay

To copy your entire video or audio transcript:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Open the video or audio file with a transcript.
  3. In the Transcript sidebar, click “…” (ellipsis), then Copy entire transcript. 

How to download your transcripts in Dropbox Replay

To download your video or audio transcript:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Open the video or audio file you added a transcript to.
  3. In the Transcript sidebar, click “…” (ellipsis) in the upper right. 
  4. Download transcript as: 
  • srt file
  • vvt file
  • Plain text

 

  • Learn where to find your Downloads folder on Mac.
  • Learn where to find your Downloads folder on Windows.

How to turn closed captions on or off in Dropbox Replay

To turn closed captions on or off:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Open the video file you’d like to view.
  3. Click CC in the controls at the bottom of the video window
    • Select Video transcript to turn on closed captions.
    • Select None to turn off closed captions.

How to adjust signature size in Dropbox Sign

If you’re adding your signature to a self-signed document, you can adjust the size of the signatures you’re placing. After you’ve positioned the signature on the page, click and drag the bottom right-hand corner of the bounding box. This will let you adjust the size.

How to align fields in Dropbox Sign

To align fields on a document:

  1. Follow the steps to send a signature request until you drag and drop your fields onto the document.
  2. After you place your fields on the document, click and drag the selection box around the fields you’d like to align.
  3. Click one of the alignment buttons in the right sidebar above [x] Fields selected.
  4. Continue the signature request process.

How to Auto-Fill fields in Dropbox Sign

Available on all plans

Auto-filled fields makes the signing experience easier and faster for your signers.

This feature pulls information from your signers, provided from either their own Dropbox Sign profile or from the name and email address entered in by the requester, and populates the information into the corresponding fields. Auto-fill fields are only able to be assigned to signers.

The fields available for Auto fill are: 

  • Date Signed
  • Name
  • Email
  • Company
  • Title

Sending a request to a Dropbox Sign User

When sending to a Dropbox Sign user who has their profile information filled out, you’ll simply place the auto-fill fields down in the desired location on your document by selecting them from the Auto-fill Fields section in the left sidebar menu in the editor.

Once the signer opens the request, they’ll see those fields already populated with the information they filled out within their Dropbox Sign profile. If they need to make a change to the information, for example, their title at their company has changed but they haven’t updated their profile, then the signer will be able to edit the field just like a normal textbox.

Sending a request to a non-Dropbox Sign user

When sending a request to a non-Dropbox Sign user or a Dropbox Sign user who does not have their profile filled out, the auto-fill fields will only be able to pull the name and email address fields. This information is pulled from the name and email, which were entered by the requester in the Who needs to Sign step. The date field will also auto populate with the current date the signer completes the request. 

To use these fields, place them on your document in the desired location while in the editor. Once the signer opens the document, their name and email will be auto filled if those fields are on the request. The company and title fields will not populate with information and the signers will fill them out as normal textboxes. If one or both of these fields are placed on the document more than once, then the duplicate fields will populate as the signer fills out the first field of its kind.

How to choose a chat model in Dropbox Dash

You can now choose from a curated list of AI models in each Chat experience, selecting the model that best fits your needs before submitting a prompt. 

Learn more about model data flows in Dropbox Dash Chat.

How to choose a chat model

The model used to power Chat is set automatically and can vary by task, unless you choose to set a particular model for chats. 

To choose a model:

  1. Log in to dash.ai.
  2. Click Chats on the lefthand side bar to start a new or open an existing chat.
  3. Click Model.
  4. Select a model from the dropdown menu.

How to comment on Dropbox files

Anyone who has access to a Dropbox file can leave a comment and view other comments, unless commenting is turned off.

Learn how to turn commenting off for a file.

New to Dropbox? See how you can easily add annotations to your collaborative work.

How to comment on a file

To comment on a file:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click All files in the left sidebar.
    • You can also click Folders in the left navigation bar to locate your file.
  3. Click the name of the file you want to comment on.
  4. Click ☑ (comments)in the top right.
  5. Add a comment to an area in the file, or a precise point in the file.
    • To comment on an area in the file, click and drag a box around the area of the file you’d like to comment on. Then, click again to create the box. 
      • Note: You can’t change the size or placement of a box after it’s been made.
    • To comment on an exact point in the file, click anywhere on the file to add a comment to that precise location. 
    • To comment on a piece of text, highlight the text to select it, and click  (comments). 
  6. Type your comment in the box that appears.
    • To mention someone in your comment, type @ and then their name or click **@**.
    • Add an emoji to your comment by clicking the happy face icon.
    • Press enter on your keyboard to create a new line.
  7. Click the up arrow next to your comment.

How to comment on a specific part of a file:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click All files in the left sidebar.
    • You can also click Folders in the left navigation bar to locate your file.
  3. Click the name of the file you want to comment on.
  4. Click (comments) in the top right.
  5. Click and drag a box around the area of the file you’d like to comment on.
  6. Click the comment box in the right sidebar.
  7. Type your comment.
  8. Click Post.

Learn how to comment on a specific time in a video or audio file.

How to comment on a specific time in a video or audio file

You can leave a comment on a specific time in a video or audio file on dropbox.com. All video and audio file types that can preview in Dropbox allow for comments on specific times.

To comment on a timestamp:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click All files in the left sidebar.
    • You can also click Folders in the left navigation bar to locate your file.
  3. Click the name of the video or audio file you want to comment on.
    • Make sure you have your previews set to Full screen.
  4. Click ☑ (comments) in the top right. 
  5. Click in the text field in the bottom right, then type your comment:
    • To mention someone in your comment, type @ and then their name or click **@**. 
    • Add an emoji to your comment by clicking the happy face icon.
  6. Check the box next to the timestamp to add your comment at that timestamp.
    • To mention someone in your comment, type @ and then their name or click **@**.
    • Add an emoji to your comment by clicking the happy face icon.
    • Press enter on your keyboard to create a new line.
  7. Click the up arrow next to your comment.

How to comment on a file in Quick view

To comment on a file in Quick view:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click All files in the left sidebar.
    • You can also click Folders in the left navigation bar to locate your file.
  3. Click the name of the video or audio file you want to comment on.
  4. Click Quick view.
  5. Click  (comments) in the upper right.

How to edit or delete a comment

To edit or delete a comment:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click All files in the left sidebar.
    • You can also click Folders in the left navigation bar to locate your file.
  3. Click the name of the file you’ve left a comment on.
  4. Click  (comments) in the top right. 
  5. Click  (more options) next to the comment you’d like to edit or delete.
  6. Click Edit or Delete.  

How to react to a comment

To react to someone else’s comment on a file:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click All files in the left sidebar.
    • You can also click Folders in the left navigation bar to locate your file.
  3. Click the name of the file that contains the comment you wish to react to.
  4. Click  (comments) in the top right. 
  5. Hover your cursor over the comment you wish to react to.
  6. Click the happy face icon that appears.
  7. Click the emoji you’d like to react with.
    • You can find emojis by navigating through the themes at the top of the pop-up window.  

How to create a comment link

You can share a comment with other users by creating a comment link.  

To create a comment link:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click All files in the left sidebar.
    • You can also click Folders in the left navigation bar to locate your file.
  3. Click the name of the file that contains the comment you want to create a copy link for.
  4. Click  (comments) in the top right.
  5. Click the comment you’d like to create the copy link for.
  6. Click  (more options).
  7. Select Copy link.

How to view resolved comments

To view all resolved comments on a file:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click All files in the left sidebar.
    • You can also click Folders in the left navigation to locate your file.
  3. Click the name of the file you want to comment on.
  4. Click ☑ (comments)in the top right. 
  5. Click  (more options) in the right sidebar.
  6. Click View resolved comments.

How to download comments

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click All files in the left sidebar.
    • You can also click Folders in the left navigation to locate your file.
  3. Click the name of the file you want to download comments from.
  4. Click ☑ (comments) in the top right.
  5. Click ☑ (more options) in the right sidebar.
  6. Click Download comments.
    • A .txt file will be created automatically.
  7. Save the file to your preferred location.

How to compare video versions in Dropbox Replay

If you’ve purchased the Dropbox Replay Add-On, you can review and compare two versions of the same video file in a side-by-side view in Dropbox Replay.

To compare video versions:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Click the video file with the versions you’d like to compare.
  3. Click the version number (example: V1) in the upper left.
  4. Click Compare versions.

The video comparison window will open.

How to review and compare comments on video versions

To review and compare comments on different versions of a video file: 

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. In the Comments panel on the right, select the Resolved, Unresolved, or All tab.
  3. Click the dropdown beside Current version/Previous versions. 
  4. Click Select all to see comments on both current and previous versions.  

Learn more about viewing comments on Replay files.

How to convert Dropbox files

You can convert the files in your Dropbox account to PDFs or images (.jpg, .png). You can also convert video files to .mov or .mp4.

To convert a file on dropbox.com:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Hover over the file you’d like to convert and click “…” (ellipsis).
  3. Hover over Save as… and click the desired file format.

Your converted file will appear in the same folder as the original. If you do not see your converted file, refresh your browser.

File types for PDF, .jpg/.png conversion

If your file has one of the following extensions, it can be converted to a PDF or .jpg/.png. The file size limit is 200 MB.

File types for .mov, .mp4 conversion

If your file has one of the following extensions, it can be converted to .mov or .mp4. The file size limit is 100 MB.

File types for unzip

If your file has one of the following extensions, it can be unzipped using the Extract All button.

How to create a code block in a Dropbox Paper doc

To insert a block of code:

  1. Click into a new line in your Paper doc. 
  2. From the menu that appears, click the {} symbol.
  3. You can also type \0` (the key to left of the 1 key). 

To select a different programming language:

  1. Highlight a word or block of text within your code. 
  2. Click Autofrom the menu that appears.
  3. Select your desired language from the dropdown menu. 

To capture inline code, you can type `(the key to left of the 1 key) before and after text.

How to type LaTeX symbols

To trigger LaTeX editing mode, type $$ in your doc. You can then type full LaTeX symbols in Dropbox Paper. When you’re finished typing, you can render the code by pressing Enter or Return on your keyboard.

How to create and format a table in Dropbox Paper

The easiest way to add a table to your Paper doc is to:

  1. Type “/table” into your doc (this is the quick-add commands feature).
  2. Add the desired number of rows and columns.
    • For example, if you want to create a table with 3 rows and 4 columns, you can type “/table 3x4”
  3. Press the Enter key.

Alternatively, you can create a table manually:

  1. Click into an empty line in your doc.
  2. Click the grid icon (Add table) in the grey icon menu that appears.

How to format your table in Paper

Add rows or columns
  1. Click anywhere in your table. Selectors will appear outside of your table.
  2. If you want to add a single column, click the + icon on the top of your table.
  3. If you want to add a single row, click the + icon to the left of your table.
  4. If you want to add multiple columns or rows, click and drag the + icon.
Delete rows or columns
  1. Click anywhere in the row or column you want to remove. Selectors will appear outside of your table.
  2. To delete a column, click the selector above it and click the trash can icon. 
  3. To delete a row, click the selector to the left of it and click the trash can icon.
  4. To delete mulitple rows or columns, hold Shift while you click mulitple selectors and click the trash can icon. 
Reorder rows or columns
  1. Click a cell in the row or column you want to reorder. Selectors will appear outside of your table.
  2. Click the selector of the row or column you want to move and drag it to the desired position. 
Add images
  1. Click anywhere in the cell you want to add an image to.
  2. Click the Add images icon in the menu that appears. 
Add a background color to a row or column
  1. Click anywhere in the row or column you want to change the color of. Selectors will appear outside of your table.
  2. To change the background color of a row, click the selector to the left of it and click the palette icon.
  3. To change the background color of a column, click the selector above it and click the palette icon. 
  4. To change the background color of multiple rows or columns, hold Shift while you click multiple selectors and click the palette icon.

How to sort a table in Paper

You can sort the columns in your table chronologically, alphabetically, or numerically. To do so:

  1. Convert the top row of your table into a header by clicking the selector to the left of the row and toggling the header button (Turn top header on/off).
  2. Click anywhere in the header cell of the column you want to sort. An arrow will appear inside the cell.
  3. Click the arrow to sort.

How to create transcripts and enable closed captions for video and audio files

You can use our AI-powered transcription feature to create transcripts for video and audio files in Dropbox. Once created, you can do the following:

  • Edit the transcript
  • Find and replace text within the transcript
  • Select a section to skip to a timestamp
  • Copy the transcript
  • Enable or disable closed captions for videos

How to create a transcript for video or audio files

To create a transcript for a video or audio files:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Open the video or audio file you’d like to transcribe.
  3. Click Transcript in the toolbar.

Your transcript may take a few minutes to generate, depending on the length of the video or audio file. When ready, you’ll see it in the Transcript tab in the right sidebar.

How to edit a transcript

To use the edit tool to modify a video or audio transcript:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Open the video or audio file with the transcript you’d like to edit.
  3. Click Transcript in the toolbar.
  4. Hover over the section you’d like to edit.
  5. Click  (pencil icon), then edit the text in the box.
  6. Click the checkmark to save.

How to find and replace transcript text

To find and replace text within your transcript:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Open the video or audio file with the transcript you’d like to edit.
  3. Click Transcript in the toolbar.
  4. Click the (search icon) in the Transcript tab in the right sidebar.
  5. Click the (slider icon) in the search field, then enable the Replace toggle.
  6. Type the keywords you’d like to find.
  7. Type the new text you’d like to replace it with.
  8. Click Replace to replace one of the instance or click Replace all to replace all the instances throughout the entire transcript.

How to copy transcript text

To copy a section of a transcript:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Open the video or audio file with the transcript you’d like to copy.
  3. Click Transcript in the toolbar.
  4. Scroll to the section you’d like to copy, select the text you want to copy.
  5. Click the Copy text icon in the top right. 

To copy your entire transcript:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Open the video or audio file with the transcript you’d like to copy.
  3. Click Transcript in the toolbar.
  4. In the Transcript sidebar, click “…” (ellipsis), then Copy transcript. 

How to turn closed captions for a video on or off

To turn closed captions on or off:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Open the video file you’d like to view.
  3. Click CC in the controls at the bottom of the video window to turn closed captions on. 
    • Click again to turn closed captions off.

How to download from Dropbox DocSend

Dropbox DocSend users can download content from their content library, download entire Spaces  (data rooms) in DocSend, or download content from a Space.

Learn more about DocSend Spaces.

Download a document

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Content library. 
  3. Open the document you’d like to download.
  4. Click ☑(more options).
  5. Click Download. 

The requested document will be downloaded to your “Downloads” folder.

 

How to download an entire Space

To download an entire Space: 

  1. Log in to docsend.com.
  2. Click Spaces.
  3. Click your Space. 
  4. Click ☑ (more options).
  5. Click Download space.

Your folders will download as a ZIP file, and a message at the bottom of your screen will let you know when the download is finished.

How to download or print files as visitors in Dropbox DocSend

Overview

Have you received a document you’d like to save? In some cases, shared content can be downloaded or printed from the DocSend document viewer. Follow the steps below to download or print shared content from the document viewer.

Download a Document

If the document owner has enabled downloading on a shared document, you can click the download icon in the top right-hand corner of the document viewer to download it.

Print a Document

You can also print a shared document if the document owner has enabled downloading. If you prefer to print a document directly, you can click the print icon in the top right-hand corner to print it from the document viewer.

Downloading and Printing are Disabled

In certain cases, a document owner may restrict visitors from downloading or printing their shared content. This is true if you don’t see the download/print icons in the document viewer.

If you need to download or print the shared content, we recommend reaching out to the document owner to update the link settings.

How to download signed documents in Dropbox Sign

Once a signature request has been completed, you can download the signed documents on sign.dropbox.com.

Download signed documents on sign.dropbox.com

To download signed documents on sign.dropbox.com:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Click Documents in the left sidebar.
  3. Hover over “⁝” (vertical ellipsis) next to the signature request you’d like to download documents from.
  4. Click Download, Download PDF, Download as CSV, or Download Signed.
    • If you choose Download or Download PDF, documents from that signature request will download to your computer’s Downloads folder (unless your computer’s default settings have been changed).
    • If you choose Download as CSV, you’ll receive an email with a ZIP file containing a CSV file of response data from that signature request.
    • If you choose Download Signed, you’ll receive an email with a ZIP file containing all signed documents from that signature request.

How to edit a template or template link in Dropbox Sign

You can edit a template or template link at any time. Before you make edits, there are a few things to consider:

  • If you edit a template, you’ll need to cancel any pending signature requests that were sent using that template, and send new signature requests using the updated version.
  • If you edit a template link, the URL will remain the same and you won’t need to resend the link.

To edit a template or template link:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Select Templates in the left sidebar.
  3. Click My Templates on the dropdown menu
  4. Click “⁝” (vertical ellipsis) next to the template or template link you’d like to edit.
  5. Click Edit and follow the prompts to make your edits.
  6. Click Save template to save your edits.

How to edit and resend a signature request in Dropbox Sign

You can edit and resend a document for signature at any time; however, once you resend the signature request, anyone who has already signed will need to sign again.

To edit and resend a signature request:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Click Documents in the left sidebar.
  3. Hover over “⁝” (vertical ellipsis) next to the document you’d like to edit and resend.
  4. Click Duplicate, and follow the signature request process as you normally would.
    • Note: You may not have the option to edit the Document title and Message fields if an admin on your team has enabled HIPAA compliance.

How to edit PDFs in Dropbox

You can make edits to PDFs when previewing a file on dropbox.com or on the Dropbox mobile app.  

Try it out by previewing a PDF in your account and clicking Edit.  

All Dropbox users can edit PDFs by modifying pages or adding text. However, customers on Dropbox Professional, Standard, Advanced, Essentials, Business, Business Plus, or Enterprise can also edit text that already exists in the PDF.

Not yet using a PDF editor? See how Dropbox helps you effortlessly edit PDFs.

You can share feedback about PDF editing with the Dropbox team, including what you think of the feature and what you’d like to see in the future. To share feedback:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click ☑ New next to the search bar.
  3. Click Edit, then select PDF.
  4. Select the PDF you want to share feedback on, and click Open. This will open the PDF in editing mode.
  5. Click Feedback on PDF editing in the bottom right of the page.
  6. Type your feedback.
  7. Check the box next to I’d like to participate in Dropbox user research, if you’re interested.
  8. Click Send.

You‘ll see a message thanking you for your feedback at the bottom of the page.

How to edit pending Dropbox Sign signature requests

With Dropbox Sign, you can update any part of a pending signature request after it’s sent without canceling your initial request. Paid Dropbox Sign customers can also add or modify expiration dates and times to initial or pending requests. Learn how to add an expiration date and time to your signature requests.

How to edit a pending signature request with Sign Web

When you edit and resend a signature request, signers who already signed will get a new email notifying them of the changes. They’ll be prompted to re-sign, with all unchanged fields automatically pre-populated.

To edit a pending signature request:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com
  2. Click Documents in the left sidebar.
  3. Click “…” (more options) on the pending signature request you’d like to edit.
  4. Select Edit and resend from the dropdown menu.The editor opens with the same documents, signers, and fields pre-populated. 
  5. Update recipients, adjust fields in real time, and edit your email message. You can also modify parts of your document.
  6. Click Save when finished.

How to edit a pending signature request with Sign API

Sign API customers have the flexibility to quickly edit pending signature requests. Through the following API endpoints they can edit signatures based on whether they are individual signature requests or signature requests from eSignature templates.

Requests Sign through Dropbox Sign UI

  • -/signature_request/edit/{signature_request_id}
  • -/signature_request/edit_with_template/{signature_request_id}

Requests Sign through embedded UI

  • -/signature_request/edit_embedded/{signature_request_id}
  • -/signature_request/edit_embedded_with_template/{signature_request_id}

Additional details:

  • Signers who have signed must carefully review their responses and complete any new or changed fields. Dropbox Sign isn’t responsible for any errors in repopulated data.
  • Signers removed from the request will receive an email notifying them their signature is no longer required.
  • Signer access codes don’t automatically repopulate.
  • The audit trail records all changes, including:
    • Signature request edited
    • Signer reassignment
    • Signer added or removed
    • Resent with expiration date added or edited
    • Resent without expiration date

How to edit video and audio files in Dropbox

You can edit the video and audio files you store in your Dropbox account, including trimming, cropping, flipping, rotating, and generating transcripts.

How to edit video and audio files

To edit video and audio files:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click All files in the left sidebar.
  3. Click the name of your video or audio file to open its preview. Learn how to preview files.
  4. Click Edit at the top of the preview or use the editing features in the toolbar.
  5. Make your edits:
    • For video files only:
      • Rotate: Click the rotate icon (square with an arrow) at the top of the player to rotate left or right.
      • Flip: Click the flip vertically icon (square split by a horizontal line) at the top of the player to flip the video vertically. Click the flip horizontally icon (square split by a vertical line) at the top of the player to flip the video horizontally.
      • Crop: Click and drag the frame around your video.
    • For video and audio files:
      • Trim: Click and drag the beginning or end of the clip in the bar at the bottom of the player.
      • Click Transcript to generate a transcript for videos and audio files. Learn how to create transcripts and closed captions for video and audio files.
      • Click Dropbox AI to quickly summarize content and get answers about your files. Learn how to use Dropbox AI in a file preview.
  6. When you’re done, click Save.
    • To save a new copy and keep the original version, click Save a copy. Then, add a name for your copy, choose the folder you’d like to save it in, and click Save copy to confirm.
    • To overwrite the original version, click Replace original. To confirm, click Replace original.

How to edit your signature in Dropbox Sign

You can edit your signature in three ways: drawing, typing, or uploading a new signature.  

To add a new signature:

  1. Log in to your Dropbox Sign account.
  2. Hover over your email address in the top-right corner.
  3. Select Edit signature.
  4. Choose a method to create your signature. You can draw or type your name, or upload an image of your signature.
  5. Add your signature and click Select.  

To delete a saved signature:

  1. Log in to your Dropbox Sign account.
  2. Hover over your email address in the top-right corner.
  3. Select Edit signature.
  4. Click the clock icon on the left side to see your saved signatures.
  5. Click the correct signature.
  6. Click the trash icon.

How to format text in a Dropbox Paper doc

To format text in a Paper doc, highlight the text you want to edit. A toolbar will appear that will let you format your text, including:

  • Bold
  • Strikethrough
  • Highlight
  • Create link
  • Large header
  • Medium header
  • Create bulleted list
  • Create to-do
  • Add comment

Not using Dropbox yet? See how Dropbox emojis add a dose of fun to projects.

Does Dropbox Paper have spell check?

Dropbox Paper does not have its own spell checker. If your browser has a built-in spell checker, you can use that. If you want to turn off spell checking, you’ll have to do so through your browser settings.

How to format a block of text

You can format a block of text by using keyboard shortcuts. For example, you can convert a bulleted list to a numbered list. For a full list of block formatting keyboard shortcuts, click the keyboard shortcuts button (it looks like a keyboard) at the bottom-right of your Paper doc.

How to format text on the Dropbox Paper mobile app

  1. Open the Paper mobile app.
  2. Open the Paper doc you want to format.
  3. Tap into a new line or tap Edit and the formatting options will appear above your keyboard.

How to get feedback with Dropbox Replay

You can get feedback on files with Dropbox Replay, including adding comments, pinning or labeling comments, adding quick reactions, commenting on a range of time, drawing on video and image files, and starting live review sessions. 

How to pin or label a comment

You can pin and label comments in your video, image, and audio files to call collaborator attention to something specific. 

To pin and label a comment:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Open the file you’d like to pin comments in.
  3. In the Comments sidebar, click the comment you’d like to pin.
  4. Click“⁝” (vertical ellipsis).
  5. Click Pin.
    • Note: Pinned comments will move to the top of the Comments sidebar and the All tab.
  6. Click Add a label at the top of the pinned comment.
  7. Select a label option from the dropdown: 
    • Final decision
    • Open question
    • Needs attention
    • Still exploring
    • Custom

You can filter comments in the sidebar by clicking Filter by under the tabs at the top and selecting Commenter name or Labels.

How to add quick reactions

You can comment with quick reactions when viewing audio and video files in Dropbox Replay. These are emoji reactions with a pre-filled text comment for specific frames. Collaborators don’t need to type a comment or have a Dropbox account to use quick reactions. 

To add quick reactions:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Open the file you’d like to comment on.
  3. Click on the specific place in the timeline you’d like to comment on.
  4. On the right side of the comment box, select a quick reaction comment. 
    • Note: To delete a quick reaction, hover over your reaction emoji on the timeline and click Delete.

How to view comments on previous versions of a file

You can view resolved or unresolved comments on current or previous versions of a Replay file. You can also filter comments by person.  

To filter comments on a file by version:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Open the Replay project with the comments you want to view.
  3. In the Comments panel on the right, select the Resolved, Unresolved, or All tab.
  4. Click the dropdown beside Current version/Previous versions. 
  5. Select one of the following options:
    • Check the box beside Current version to see comments on the current version. 
    • Check the box beside Previous versions to see comments from all previous versions.
    • Click Select all to see comments on both the current and previous versions.

How to draw on a video

If you’re reviewing a video, you can draw directly on the video and post your drawings as comments.  

To draw on an image or video:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Click the name or thumbnail to open your file for drawing.
  3. Drag the playhead or click on the timeline where you’d like to add a drawing.
  4. Hover over the video where you’d like to draw.
    • Your cursor will become a pencil icon.
  5. Hold and drag your cursor to start drawing.
  6. Click the airplane icon to post your drawing as a comment.
    • You can also undo your last drawing action by clicking the undo button (curved arrow pointing to the left), delete your drawing by clicking the trashcan icon, select a different color by clicking the color wheel icon, or change the stroke width by clicking the line icon.

Once you post your drawing, you’ll see a new comment appear at the specified timeframe on the timeline. The comment will be annotated with a pencil icon in the Comments section to signify that it’s a drawing.

How to add annotations to an image or PDF

If you’re reviewing an image or PDF, you can add drawings directly on the image or PDF.  

To draw on an image or PDF:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Click the name or thumbnail to open your file for drawing.
  3. Click the pencil icon below the comment box to bring up the annotation toolbar.
  4. Click the colored wheel icon to select the color of your drawing.
  5. Click the line icon to select the stroke width of your drawing.
  6. Click the pencil icon, then click on the image or PDF and drag your cursor to add a drawing.
    • Use the undo button (curved arrow pointing to the left) to undo your last drawing action.
    • Use the redo button (curved arrow pointing to the right) to redo your last drawing action.

Exporting comments from Replay

You can export comments in the following formats:

  • XML
  • FCP XML
  • JSON
  • CSV
  • CSV (condensed)
  • Plain text
  • Avid Media Composer text

To export comments from Replay:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Open the Replay project you’d like to export comments from.
  3. In the Comments panel on the right, click the Export comments dropdown beside Comments.
  4. Select the format you want to export the comments in.  

The Dropbox Replay and Avid Pro Tools integration also allows you to take comments from a review session and export them directly into your Pro Tools project.

Live review sessions

You can start a live review session to review audio and video files with collaborators in real-time. During a live review session, you can comment directly on the frame, as well as see what others are commenting.

If you start a live review session for a video file, you and your collaborators can also draw on the frame and see what others are drawing. Anyone in the live review session can control audio or video playback.

Learn more about live review sessions.

How to group checkboxes in Dropbox Sign

You can add checkboxes to a document or template, and group them together to choose how many boxes must be checked.

To group checkboxes, click and drag the selection box around the checkboxes you’d like to group and then click Group checkboxes in the right sidebar.               

Settings options for Grouped Checkboxes:

A. Align your checkboxes

B. Delete the group of checkboxes

C. Choose who fills out the checkboxes

D. Pre-check the boxes for the signers as default

E. Set maximum and minimum requirements for the group

F. Label the fields - Note, labeling checkboxes helps to set up conditional logic for the checkboxes. It’s not required to label them and the signer does not see the labels.

G. Make the checkbox required for signer*

*available for ungrouped checkboxes

How to insert emojis into a Dropbox Paper doc

To add an emoji, type “:” (the colon key) to show the available options. From there, you can click the emoji you want, or choose a category from the left panel. You can also find emojis by typing the emoji description, like “:panda”.

Not using Dropbox yet? Add a dose of fun to projects with Dropbox Paper.

How to locate a document in Dropbox Sign using the document ID

You can locate a specific document by searching for that document’s ID. To do this:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Click Documents in the left sidebar.
  3. Click the search bar in the top right.
  4. Type the document ID.
  5. Press the enter/return key on your keyboard or click the search icon (magnifying glass).

How to manage Dropbox Replay for your team

Admins have access to all Dropbox Replay files and projects in the team space. Admin controls allow admins to view, change or re-assign ownership, permanently delete, change password settings, and add and edit members to Replay files and projects. If a team member leaves, an admin can take ownership of their shared files or projects to prevent workflow disruption.

Dropbox Replay settings in the admin console

  • Open any file in a shared project created by a Dropbox team member

 

  • Rename projects
  • Take ownership of files or projects of team members or former team members
  • Permanently delete files
  • Change sharing settings from your Links page or the file itself
  • Change shared links passwords
  • Manage external access to files and folders
  • Allow or restrict sharing outside your team

How to edit access to a Dropbox Replay project

Once you add files or create projects in Dropbox Replay, you can share them with collaborators and team members by adding someone to a project.

Learn more about how to share files and projects.

If you’d like to collaborate on a project in real time, start a live review session instead.

Learn how to use live review in Dropbox Replay.

How to manage external link sharing in Replay

Admins can use the admin console to restrict external sharing in Replay by their team. This allows them to centrally control whether members can share links and files with:  

Anyone: Anyone with the link 

Team + approved: The team and a list of approved users

Team only: Only members of the team

To change team sharing settings:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Settings in the left sidebar.
  4. Click Replay.
  5. Click the dropdown next to Sharing links outside team.
    • Choose On (Anyone), On (Team + approved), or Off (Team only).  

How to manage external access to projects in Replay

Admins can use the admin console settings to manage whether team members can add people from outside of the team to projects.

  1. Log in to dropbox.com with your admin credentials.
  2. Click Admin console.
  3. Click Settings in the left sidebar.
  4. Click Replay.
  5. Click the dropdown next to Adding people outside team.
    • Choose On (Anyone), On (Team + approved), or Off (Team only).  

How to manage ownership of files and projects

Admins can control ownership of a shared file or project to prevent stalled workflow.   

Once an admin has taken over or reassigned ownership of a project, they’ll be able to take all of the actions that an owner can take, including: 

  • Edit, delete, or add password
  • Toggle downloads on or off 
  • Archive files 
  • Resolve comments 
  • Pin or label comments
  • Set deadlines
  • Manage sharing permissions outside the team
How to take ownership of a project

To take ownership for yourself:

  1. Log in to to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Open the project you’d like to take ownership of.
  3. Click manage people (the people icon) at the top.
  4. Click the dropdown next to Owner.
  5. Click Take ownership.
  6. Click the Can edit dropdown next to the member you took ownership from.
  7. Choose Can edit, Can comment, or Remove,depending on the permissions you’d like to grant.
How to reassign ownership of a file

To reassign ownership of a file:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.    
  2. Click Admin at the top.
  3. Hover over the file thumbnail or the row of the file you’d like to reassign ownership of.
  4. Click “…” (ellipsis) in the top right. 
  5. Select Transfer ownership.
  6. Click the dropdown next to the current owner’s name.
  7. Select the person you’d like to transfer ownership to.
  8. Click Save.
How to transfer ownership of a project

To change ownership of a project:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Open the project you’d like to transfer ownership of.
  3. Click manage people (the people icon) at the top.
  4. Click the permissions dropdown beside the person you want to take ownership and select Transfer ownership.

How to view the admin of a file or project

To view the team admin of a file or project:

  1. Log in to replay.dropbox.com.
  2. Click any avatar (profile picture or initials) at the bottom of the project thumbnail.
  3. Scroll down the list of team members to find the person with Admin beside their name.

How to monitor activities in Replay

Admins can use the admin console to view the following member activity in Replay:

  • Logging in or out of Replay
  • Linking Replay to their accounts
  • Adding or deleting files
  • Creating or modifying shared links
  • Adding or removing people from projects

Learn more about how to access team activity in the admin console.

Disbanding a team

If you choose to disband your team, all team member accounts become individual Dropbox accounts. The ownership of the team project moves to the admin, including Replay content. Team members will still be able to access to any Replay projects they previously had access to from their individual accounts. But they’ll lose access to any files that aren’t inside a project.

Learn more about disbanding a team.

How to manage saved signatures in Dropbox Sign

You can view, add, or delete the signatures you use in your Dropbox Sign account.

To do this:

1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.

2. Hover over your initials in the top-right corner.

3. Click Edit signature.

4. Select an option in the window.

  • To view your signatures: Click the saved icon (clock).
  • To add a new signature: Click the pen, keyboard, or camera icons to write, type, or take a picture of your new signature.
  • To delete a signature: Click the delete icon (trash can) in the top-right corner of the thumbnail.

5. When you’re done, click Save.

How to mask fields in a document with Dropbox Sign

If you need to request sensitive information from a signer, you can mask fields in a document to hide the signer’s information.

How to mask a field

To mask a field:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Navigate to the form you’d like to mask a field for.
  3. Click on the text box you’d like to mask.
  4. In the right sidebar, toggle Mask Typed Text to On.
    • To remove a masked field, toggle Mask Typed Text to Off.

What masked fields look like

Masked fields will be replaced by asterisks (e.g. *****) in the following locations:

  • On the signer page, except when the signer is directly editing that field.
  • On the final PDF copy that is sent to all parties.
    • This includes the requester, the signers, and any individuals who’ve been CC’d.
  • On the API Dashboard, under the Account Callback and App Callback tabs where the callback response is displayed.

How to request redacted values in the callback response objects

If you‘d like us to mask the payload to your callback URL by default, follow these steps:

  1. Navigate to the page to submit a request with Dropbox Support.
  2. Select Dropbox Sign API as the type of support you require. 
  3. Enter the email address for the account you’d like us to apply this update to.
  4. Include the subject: Masked Fields - mask callback URL payload.
  5. Enter a brief description of your request and the reason for the request.
  6. Select Dropbox Sign API as the product you would like help with.
  7. Under I have a question about, select The API.
  8. Click Submit.

Your request will be picked up by a member of Dropbox Support who’ll reach out about your request to the email address you provided.

Learn how to retrieve and view masked data.

How to open and edit Dropbox files with third-party apps

If the Open menu doesn’t appear

There are several reasons why the Open menu may not appear:

  • The file isn’t saved to your Dropbox account. This happens if someone shared the file with you, but you didn’t save it to your Dropbox account.
  • Your admin has disabled your ability to connect new applications. If you’re a member of a Dropbox team, you may not see the Open menu if your admin has disabled your ability to connect third-party applications to your Dropbox account.

How to play video and audio files in Dropbox

You can upload and share audio and video files on Dropbox, just like any other file. Learn how to add files and folders to your Dropbox account.

  1. Open the Dropbox mobile app.
  2. Tap the name of an audio or video file to view a preview. Learn more about how to preview files.
  3. Tap the preview to play it.     
    • Scrub backward and forward by dragging the playhead along the timeline.
    • Skip forward or backward by 15 seconds by tapping  (forward 15 seconds) or  (back 15 seconds). You can also double-tap the right or left side of the screen to skip forward or backward by 15 seconds.
    • Change the playback speed by tapping  (settings) in the lower left corner and choosing a playback speed. You can also tap and hold anywhere on the screen to watch at 2X speed.
    • Change the playback quality by tapping (settings) in the lower left corner, tapping Quality, then choosing a playback quality.
    • Put the video on repeat by tapping  (repeat) in the lower right corner.     

If you’re watching a video on iOS, you can also:

  • View the video in fullscreen by tapping the fullscreen icon (rectangle with two arrows) in the top right corner.
  • Minimize the video while you use other apps by tapping the picture-in-picture icon (two rectangles) in the top-right corner.
  • Cast your video to AirPlay by tapping the cast icon (rectangle with an up arrow) in the top-right corner.

Note: Your iOS device must be on the same network as the device you’d like to cast to.

How to add a video thumbnail

To choose a thumbnail for a video you’ve uploaded to Dropbox:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click All files in the left sidebar.
  3. Find and open the video you want to update.
  4. Drag the playhead to the frame you want to use as your thumbnail.
  5. Click the Set this frame as thumbnail icon (image with an arrow pointing upwards) in the lower right corner.

The thumbnail will update anywhere the video appears, including shared links.

How to preview a file in Dropbox Paper

Previews allow you to to view a snapshot of a file or link without opening it. You’ll see a file preview if Dropbox supports your file type and:

  • You paste a link to the file into a Paper doc 
  • You drag and drop a file from your file system into a Paper doc 
    • If you drag and drop a file from the web, Paper will write the file name with a link to the file
  • You insert files manually

How to customize previews in Paper docs

If you’ve added an Illustrator, PDF, or Powerpoint file into your Paper doc, you can customize how the file previews in Paper.

To customize the preview of the Illustrator, PDF, or Powerpoint file you’ve inserted:

  1. Click the existing preview of the file.
  2. A toolbar will appear at the top of the preview. Click the four rectangles icon on the left.
  3. From the gallery, select what you’d like to display in your preview.
  4. Click Add to doc.
  5. To select which part of the file displays, click the new preview. 
  6. From the editing toolbar that appears at the top of the preview, select the Select display area icon. 
  7. Click and drag to select the area you’d like to display. 
  8. Click Select.

How to add a caption to a preview in Paper docs

To add a caption to a preview:

  1. Click the preview image to select it.
  2. Click Write a caption at the bottom of the image.
  3. Type your caption.

What can I preview in Paper docs?

Paper supports all file types that you can preview in Dropbox, and:

  • Adobe XD

  • YouTube

How to replace signers in pending signature requests

You can replace the signer on a pending signature request if a signer is no longer available or valid. You can only do this after the request is sent and as long as no one has signed. If you’d like to make changes to a signature request that’s already been signed by someone, we recommend duplicating the request, making your desired changes, and then deleting the original request.

Everyone can edit their own pending signature requests. However, admins can also edit pending signature requests sent by team members. Learn more about what roles can replace signers on pending signature requests.

How to edit and replace signers

  1. Log in to hellosign.com
  2. Click Documents in the left side bar.
  3. Click “⁝” (vertical ellipsis) next to the signature request you’d like to replace signers for.
  4. Click Edit Signers.
    • You can only edit signers if no one has signed yet.
  5. Click the dropdown next to the signer you’d like to replace, then click Replace.
  6. Enter the name and email address of the new signer.
  7. You can’t edit the authentication method or signer settings for pending signature requests.
  8. Repeat steps 5 and 6 for any other signers you’d like to replace.
  9. Click Save.

The previous signer will receive an email notification that says the document no longer needs their signature. They will also no longer have access to the document via the link they were sent.

The new signer will receive an email requesting their signature.

How to retrieve and view masked data in Dropbox Sign

You can use masked fields to hide sensitive signer information. All masked field information will be hidden and replaced by asterisks (e.g. *****) on callback events displayed in the API Dashboard. This article explains how to retrieve and view this masked data.

How to view masked data

There are three ways to view masked data:

Download the document data as a CSV 

By downloading the document data as a CSV, you’ll receive an excel sheet with information about the signature request with values of all fields, including masked fields. Learn how to download documents as a CSV.

Execute a request to the Get Signature Endpoint

Executing a request to the Get Signature Request endpoint will return a response object with unmasked values. To do this:

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Navigate to the Get Signature Request endpoint page.
  3. Click Try it at the top of the page.
  4. Enter your API key under Security.
  5. Click Parameters.
  6. Enter the signature_request_id of the signature request with masked fields.
  7. Click Send.

View the callback response objects

You can view unmasked values for masked fields in the callback event response objects that report to any callback URLs set on your account. This option allows you to process the information within your workflow.

Viewing masked data from the API Dashboard: an example

Here’s a response body from a callback event posted on the API Dashboard where the data is masked with asterisks:

- “value”: “*********”

Below is the response body after executing the Get Signature Request endpoint using the correlated signature_request_id. This exposes the masked data.

- “value”: “123-45-6789”

How to search and explore your content in Dropbox Dash

With Dropbox Dash, you can quickly search across all of your content and connected apps. You can use Dash to find what you need, summarize content, and answer specific questions about files you have access to.

Not using Dropbox Dash yet? Discover universal search for work content.

How to search and explore your content with Dropbox Dash

You can find and create content from apps that you or your admin have connected to Dash. Learn how to connect apps to Dropbox Dash.

How does searching web content in Dash work?

Dash uses OpenAI’s web search API (gpt-5-mini) to search the internet and summarize relevant web content in your Dash Chat results.

Enter your query in the search bar to find specific items, or click one of the options below the search bar before entering your query to use that feature:

  •  Attach sources: Attach supported files or folders to include with your query.
  • Chat controls
    • Web search: Enable or disable web search by using the checkbox.
    • Model: Select the AI model you want to use, or leave it on “Best” to select the best option for your task.
    • Connect apps: Connect third-party apps to Dash.

Attach sources

Follow these steps to attach sources to your query:

  1. Log in to dash.ai.
    • If you’re using the desktop app, press control-shift-e (Windows) or command-shift-e (macOS) to open the app window.
  2. Click  (add) and select your desired files or folders.

Chat controls

Web search

You can use Dash to search the internet for answers to your questions from across the web and view them directly in Dash Chat.

Follow these steps to search the web from dash.ai.

  1. Log in to dash.ai.
  2. Click①(slider) All content at the bottom of the text box near the (Attach sources) button
  3. Check “Web search”
    • Note: Web search will be enabled by default. You can toggle between web search and searching your content and connected apps by checking or unchecking this box within the current or future chats.
  4. Enter your question in the text box.
  5. Click  (send) to generate your answer.

Dash Chat will generate answers based on its web search. You can ask follow-up questions and refine answers by typing instructions in the text bar.

Learn more about Dash Chat.

Sharing chats

You can share individual chats with others through a shareable link.

Follow the steps below to share your chat:

  1. Log in to dash.ai.
  2. Enter a question or message into the chat box.
  3. Click  (send) to generate your answer.
  4. Click Share.
  5. Click Copy link.
    • Note: Your chat link will be copied to your clipboard.
  6. Send the link to the intended recipient(s).

Manage shared chat links

You can manage shared chat links to control access or revoke them at any time. 

How to manage links directly after sharing

After you share your chat link, in the confirmation window:

  1. Click Manage links.
  2. Navigate to the chat link you want to manage.
  3. Select the action you want to take.

How to manage links from settings

  1. Log in to dash.ai.
  2. Click Account.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click General.
  5. Click Data & Security.
  6. Navigate to the chat link you want to manage.
  7. Select the action you want to take.

Model

You can select the AI model you want to use by browsing through the Model menu in the bottom left corner of the chat box.

By default, “Best” is selected and will automatically determine the most useful model for your query.

Learn more about choosing chat models in Dash.

Connect apps

Use this option to connect supported, third-party apps to Dropbox Dash. Connected apps allow you to access, search, and interact with content directly in Dash.

Learn how to connect apps to Dash.

You can search for your Paper docs, and any docs that have been shared with you by using the search bar in Dropbox Paper.

The search bar searches the full text of Paper docs. To find any available doc, you can search for:

  • The title or name of a doc

  • The content within a doc

  • The name of a team member, to see all the docs they’ve created

     

To access search:

  1. Click ☑ (search) in any doc.

  2. Begin typing in the search bar. All matching docs will be displayed.

     

To access Paper Home from dropbox.com:

To access Paper Home from any Paper doc, click < next to the document title in the top left of the page.

To find any available doc on Paper Home, you can filter by:

  • Docs created by you

You can start a new search by clicking Clear filters.

How to self-sign a document

You can self-sign a document on dropbox.com, then send the signed document to anyone who needs a copy. 

Learn how to self-sign a PDF on the Dropbox mobile app.

How to self-sign a document

To self-sign a document:

  1. Log in to dropbox.com.
  2. Click  New next to the search bar.
  3. Hover over Sign, and click Sign Yourself.
    • Note: You can also self-sign PDFs while previewing them.
  4. Check the box next to the file you’d like to use. You can use the search bar or find it in your Dropbox files if it doesn’t show up immediately.
    • Note: You can also upload a file by clicking Upload file in the lower left.
  5. Click Choose. 
  6. Add your signature:
    • Draw your signature. 
    • Type your signature. 
    • Upload a photo. 
    • Insert a recently Saved signature. 
  7. Click Insert. 
  8. Place the signer field where you want to add your signature. Learn more about using the Dropbox sign editor.
  9. Click Save in the top right corner.

The signed file will appear in your Dropbox files, with “(signed)” behind the filename.

How to self-sign a document in Dropbox Sign

You can self-sign a document on sign.dropbox.com or on the Dropbox mobile app.

Using this feature will link your Dropbox Sign and primary Dropbox accounts if both are under the same email address. If you don’t already have a Dropbox Sign account, self-signing a PDF will create a Basic account under the email affiliated with your Dropbox account.

On sign.dropbox.com

  1. Log in to sign.dropbox.com.
  2. Click Sign or send.
  3. Select the file(s) you’d like to sign.
    • To add files from your computer, click Upload file and follow the prompts, or drag and drop files where it says Drag and drop files here.
    • To add files from a third-party application, click the icon for the application where your files are located and follow the prompts.
  4. Once you’ve added all your files, click Next.
  5. Click I’m the only signer.
  6. Drag and drop the fields you’d like to add to your document. When you add a Signature or Initials field you’ll automatically be prompted to add your signature or initials. Learn more about the types of fields you can add.
  7. Click Next.
  8. You can download your signed document to your computer and/or send it via email.
    • To download your signed document, click Download document.
    • To send your signed document via email, type the email address of the person you’d like to send it to, add a document title and message, then click Send Document.

** On the Dropbox mobile app**

  1. Open the Dropbox mobile app.
  2. Navigate to the PDF you’d like to self-sign.
  3. Tap the PDF to open a preview.
  4. Tap Edit/Sign in the lower left.
  5. Choose Only you.
  6. Tap Add signature.
    • If you don’t have a saved signature, draw your signature under Sign your name.
    • If you have a saved signature, tap the desired signature under Select signature.
    • To add a saved signature, tap + (plus sign) next to Edit signature, draw your new signature, then tap Done.
    • To edit your saved signatures, tap Edit next to Select signature.
  7. Move and resize your signature to the desired area.
  8. Tap Save.

How to set the order of who signs in Dropbox Sign

When you’re setting up a document for someone to sign, whether from the Sign or Send tab or Create a Template tab:

  1. Click +Signer to add signers to the document.
  2. When you add signers, the Set signer order option will appear with a toggle next to it.
  3. Once you toggle Set signer order to on, you’ll notice that a grid of dots appears to the left of the signer role.  
  4. You can click and drag the grid of dots to rearrange the order of signers.

When Signer 1 has signed the document, Signer 2 will be prompted via e-mail that it’s his or her turn to sign, and so on.

How to set up and use your company directory in Dash

The company directory feature in Dash allows users to discover and view people profiles and team pages across their organization. Once an admin connects the company’s HR software, profile information and team structures become available, along with updated navigation and search functionality.

Connect your company directory to Dash (admins only)

To enable your company directory in Dash, an admin must connect it. Workday is currently the only supported company directory. 

To connect your company directory:

  1. Go to the Admin console in Dash.
  2. Click the Connectors tab.
  3. Select Workday from the list.
  4. Follow the prompts to authorize the connection.

What changes after connecting your company directory

When the connection with your company directory is active:

  • A People section appears in the left sidebar.
  • All people names across Dash become clickable and link to their profile.
  • People can be found using the Dash search bar.
  • Hovering over someone’s name in Dash will show you their role, which team they’re on, and their contact details. You can also visit their company profile by clicking View profile.

How to view and edit your profile

To view your own profile:

  1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner of Dash.
  2. Select View profile.  

To update your profile:

  1. On your profile page, click Edit in the top-right.
  2. Update the following:
    • Profile photo
    • About me

You can also choose a theme for your profile, whether to show a detailed location, your birthday, or an out of office notification on your profile. 

How to search for people and teams

Once your company directory is connected, you can search for anyone in your organization using the Dash search bar.  

You can search by:

  • Full name
  • Email
  • Display handle
